# OncoGemma v5 Code Audit

Repository: https://github.com/preshit-gupta/OncoGemma-v5 (commit `899d0e8`). Audited against the staged PRDs in `prd/00-overview.md` through `prd/07-stage-v4.6-validation.md`.

Date: 2026-09-04

## How this audit was done

1. The repo was cloned and the backend test suite and frontend type check were run locally to establish ground truth.
2. Twelve area and lens finders (worker, triage, mitosis, grading, report, API, frontend, lifecycle/concurrency, security, clinical constants) plus dependency, docs and test-suite checks and seven per-stage PRD conformance checks ran in parallel over the code.
3. A second completeness pass per area hunted for what the first pass missed.
4. Every candidate finding was then re-read by a skeptical verifier against the actual file. Refuted and duplicate claims were dropped and are listed in the appendix so nothing is hidden.
5. A cross-file duplicate merge folded the same defect reported from several places into one entry; the other locations are listed under "Also reported at".
6. A final synthesis pass grouped the verified findings into root causes and an ordered fix list.

Candidates raised: 768 · Refuted or merged by verifiers: 90 · Cross-file duplicates merged: 216 · Distinct findings in this document: 462

## Executive analysis

462 distinct verified findings (678 before merging duplicates reported from several files). The complaint "the code breaks down a lot" is accurate and has a small number of causes. Below: why it breaks, what is clinically unsafe, the fix order, PRD drift, and the refactors worth doing.

---

### 1. Why it breaks

### T1. It cannot be installed or started from a clean checkout
Nine of the fifteen test files fail at import because scipy, scikit-image, shapely, opencv, pandas, pyarrow, matplotlib, scikit-learn/joblib and google-cloud-aiplatform are imported unconditionally at module scope but absent from `requirements.txt`. Startup then dies a second way: `ensure_buckets_exist()` calls `get_gcs_client()` outside its own try block, so `DefaultCredentialsError` propagates out of the FastAPI lifespan on any machine without Google ADC. `USE_REAL_GCS` and `STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST` are declared in `config.py` and read by nobody, and the `fake-gcs-server` in `ops/docker-compose.yml` is never wired to anything, so there is no offline mode at all. Every dependency is a floor-only `>=` pin with no lockfile.
IDs: #381, #88, #395, #9, #4, #17, #387, #391, #386, #547

### T2. Every failure is swallowed and replaced with fabricated output
This is the single largest cause of "it breaks" being invisible until a clinician looks at a report. The pattern repeats in roughly forty places: a bare `except Exception` prints a note and returns invented data, then the stage completes normally. MedGemma failures return canned tubule 25 / pleomorphism 2 / IDC-NST for every patch. Vertex Path Foundation failures return `RandomState(42).randn` embeddings. OpenSlide failures produce procedurally drawn "histology" (pink squares, drawn glands and nuclei) that is fed to the detector, uploaded to the canonical GCS artifact path, and served forever as the real evidence patch. An unopenable slide becomes a flat 2048x2048 pink 13-level pyramid marked `done`. Missing hotspots become 24 fabricated ones on a diagonal. Missing HPFs become ten zero-count fields at [0,0]. Per-tile pyramid upload errors are `except Exception: pass`. Nothing anywhere sets a `needs_human` flag; the string appears only in a docstring.
IDs: #135, #13, #72, #71, #102, #103, #464, #136, #580, #144, #39, #325, #140, #730, #42, #431, #436, #548, #45, #91, #80, #263, #653, #466, #50, #597, #598, #599, #722

### T3. Fabricated clinical values are shipped as defaults, not as placeholders
ER 95%, PR 80%, HER2 1+, Ki-67 18%, 18 mm tumour, negative 5 mm posterior margin, laterality right, pT1c pNX Stage IA, and a diagnosis line asserting invasive carcinoma Grade 2 exist as SQLAlchemy column defaults, as Pydantic field defaults on `UpdateReportPayload`, as React `useState` initialisers, and again in `cap_elements.yaml`. `_ensure_report_record` fires on every GET, so simply opening the report tab creates a signable draft asserting biomarker results that were never measured. Because `PUT` applies any field that `is not None` and every field has a non-None default, a partial save resets tumour size to 18 mm and laterality to right. The PDF renderer adds its own layer of `.get(..., 95)` fallbacks.
IDs: #12, #249, #360, #182, #270, #621, #532, #166, #361, #677, #271, #684

### T4. The state machine has no locking, no status gates, and no attempt discipline
`poll_and_execute_single_task` does a plain ORM SELECT with no `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and no compare-and-set, so two replicas run the same stage row. Worker startup resets *every* `running` row globally, including rows another live replica owns. No confirm endpoint checks the current status, so a stage can be confirmed while `queued`, `running`, `failed` or already `confirmed`, and every confirm unconditionally re-queues the next stage. Three different attempt conventions coexist: triage confirm targets `attempt == 1`, `approve` creates `attempt + 1`, and mitosis/grading confirm use `.first()` with no ORDER BY. Uploads hard-code `attempt=1`, so the re-scan path after a QC failure violates `uq_stage_execution_attempt` and returns a 500. `GET /cases/{id}` orders stages by `started_at`, whose NULL placement differs between SQLite and Postgres, and the frontend takes the first row per stage, so a retried stage shows the old failed attempt forever.
IDs: #35, #36, #566, #703, #206, #279, #280, #567, #116, #625, #285, #535, #69, #60, #205, #207, #704, #47, #711

### T5. There is no authentication, no authorization, and no trustworthy audit actor
`MOCK_AUTH_ENABLED` is a Python literal `True`, not env-driven, so the Firebase branch is unreachable in every environment including production. The client picks its own identity and role via `X-User-Id` / `X-User-Role`, which is written verbatim into `AuditEvent.actor`. No endpoint anywhere consults `user.role`: grepping `.role` across the routers returns only the validity check in `auth.py`. Thirty of forty-two routes (all grading, mitosis, triage and report routes, the direct tile route, the case thumbnail) do not even declare `Depends(get_current_user)`, so fixing the mock alone leaves signing, amendment, grade confirmation and PHI tile serving open. `DELETE /api/v1/cases` wipes every case for any caller. CORS is `allow_origins=["*"]` with `allow_credentials=True`.
IDs: #1, #198, #529, #327, #255, #3, #77

### T6. Silent SQLite fallback, no migrations, no DB-level guarantees
`db.py` connects to Postgres at import time and, on any exception, permanently switches that process to a repo-root SQLite file with a printed warning. API and worker are separate processes, so one can land on Postgres and the other on SQLite. Schema comes from `Base.metadata.create_all` at startup; `alembic` is in requirements but there is no `alembic/` directory, so no column added since a DB was first created exists on that DB. Consequently none of the PRD's DB-level guarantees exist: no `trg_report_immutable`, no `REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ON audit_events`, and SQLite never enables `PRAGMA foreign_keys`, which is why the missing cascades below are invisible in tests. `Case` declares ORM cascades for slides, stages, grading and report but not for hotspots, detections or HPF sites, so `DELETE /cases/{id}` raises an unhandled IntegrityError on Postgres and orphans clinical rows on SQLite.
IDs: #6, #9, #7, #8, #495, #27, #10, #34, #496, #437

### T7. Clinical scoring is reimplemented six times with divergent formulas, and the config that owns the numbers is dead
The PRD locks the mitotic score to mitoses/mm2 via a CAP table in `configs/scoring.yaml`. Stage 4 implements that (unique mitoses / n_hpf * pi * r^2 against 3.65 and 7.30 per mm2). Stage 5 throws it away and re-derives the score from summed per-HPF counts against hard-coded 8/16 cut-offs, in four separate copies (`worker/grading.py:190`, `routers/grading.py:132`, `routers/grading.py:251` via `pipeline/grading.py:211`, plus a TypeScript reimplementation in `MitosisViewer.tsx:164`). `pipeline/grading.py` reads `cfg['mitosis']['cutoffs']`, a key that exists in no YAML file, so the config branch is dead and the literals always win. The two paths also disagree on the numerator: Stage 4 de-duplicates mitoses across overlapping HPFs, Stage 5 sums per-field counts and double-counts them. `stage_executions.config_hash` is never written by any handler, so no run is reproducible.
IDs: #357, #587, #356, #118, #227, #259, #483, #31, #478, #158, #764, #536, #153, #305, #626, #130

### T8. Frontend and backend disagree about the contract, and the frontend cannot be type-checked
`types/next-shim.d.ts` declares `next/link`, `lucide-react` and `openseadragon` as ambient `any`, shadowing the real `.d.ts` files, which is the only reason `tsc --noEmit` passes; `next.config.mjs` then sets `ignoreBuildErrors: true` and `ignoreDuringBuilds: true` with no ESLint config and no tests. The concrete drift: deleting a hotspot emits no `delete` op, so it reappears after confirm and is persisted; every save stamps untouched hotspots as `pathologist_modified`; the case page reads the first stage attempt while `StageRail` reads the latest; `isPreprocessDone` gates the Approve button, so QC is bypassable and `qc` has no rail entry at all; the grade cut-offs (5, 7) are recomputed client-side and the `/recompute` endpoint built for it is imported and never called; `type_confirmed: true` is hard-coded, so the server's histologic-type gate can never fire; missing slide metadata is rendered as `mpp_x || 0.25` and `width_px || 2048`, misplacing every overlay; `tile_url_template` is host-relative so tiles only resolve through a rewrite hard-coded to `localhost:8000`.
IDs: #268, #409, #448, #75, #205, #68, #38, #483, #142, #117, #360, #175, #270, #663, #637, #413, #250, #676, #655, #661, #256

### 2. Clinical-safety findings

Anything that changes a grade, score or stage, or lets a report be signed wrongly.

**Fabricated inputs to the grade**
- Any MedGemma or Vertex failure silently returns tubule 25 / pleo 2 / IDC-NST at confidence "high" for every patch, and the fallback always parses so the retry-exhaustion path is unreachable in the live config: #135, #13
- The triage "tumour probability" heatmap is thumbnail optical density; the Path Foundation probe output is computed and discarded, and the endpoint is fed a flat grey 224x224 image, never slide pixels: #71, #72
- Grading fabricates 24 hotspots on the slide diagonal when a case has none, then grades real tissue at those arbitrary coordinates and uploads the patches as evidence: #136
- Mitosis fabricates a 2x2 mm hotspot at slide centre when the pathologist excluded every hotspot, and falls back to unconfirmed triage output, resurrecting excluded hotspots: #580
- Ten zero-count HPFs at [0,0] are invented when no HpfSite rows exist, yielding mitotic score 1 and a complete grade: #144
- Detector and verifier weights are never loaded; a hand-tuned optical-density heuristic runs and is recorded as `midog22_yolov8x_sweep@v1.0`: #102, #129
- Synthetic drawn "histology" is served as evidence with HTTP 200 and cached into GCS as the real patch: #325, #140, #103
- Schema-retry exhaustion substitutes fabricated sub-scores and a made-up rationale; `needs_human` is never set: #141
- `HistologicTypeResponse` defaults every field, so any JSON validates as IDC-NST: #722

**Wrong scoring math**
- Stage 5 discards the confirmed density-based mitotic score and re-derives it from counts with 8/16 cut-offs; 5 fields with 8 mitoses is score 3 by the PRD and score 1 or 2 here: #357
- Overlapping HPFs are counted once by Stage 4 and twice by Stage 5; the area denominator assumes ten disjoint fields regardless: #587, #356, #764
- Pass 3 of HPF placement fabricates ten overlapping fields at 196 um separation when the density map is empty, inflating the denominator and under-scoring small tumours: #718, #123, #747
- `/recompute` accepts an arbitrary client-supplied HPF list, directly controlling the area denominator, with no count cap, no non-overlap check and no bounds check: #344
- Arbitrary label strings on `/recompute` are neither counted as mitosis nor seen as unreviewed, silently zeroing the count and bypassing the confirm gate: #115
- Empty evidence sets aggregate to tubule 3 and pleo 2 rather than failing: #366
- Detector caps at 6 candidates per tile, truncating counts exactly in highly mitotic tumours: #581

**Wrong stage / wrong QC**
- Missing MPP is silently replaced with 0.25 um/px in ingest and in six other call sites; a 20x scan is treated as 40x and mitotic density is off by 4x: #38
- Missing tumour size becomes 18.0 mm at every staging call site, so `pTX` is unreachable and a 0 mm entry stages as pT1c: #360
- `nodes_positive > nodes_examined` is never rejected; `validate_staging_invariants` is imported in two files and called nowhere: #175
- `pN1mi`, `pN0(i+)` and ITCs are unreachable because no caller passes `largest_meta_mm`; a 0.1 mm ITC stages as pN1a: #172, #363, #618
- Stage group defaults to "IA" for every unhandled pT/pN combination, including bare M1 and pN3b: #173
- Focus QC samples exactly one tile at the slide corner and returns "pass" when zero tiles were sampled: #45, #548
- Three of five configured QC checks (pen marks, folds, stain sanity) do not exist; thresholds are an order of magnitude more permissive than the PRD: #433, #48
- Approving `preprocess` re-opens a `needs_rescan` case and queues triage even when QC hard-failed, with no justification and no override audit: #68

**Reports signed wrongly**
- `POST /report/sign` checks only that the report is not already signed: no required-field check, no type-confirmed gate, no all-stages-confirmed gate, no role check, `password_or_pin` accepted and never read, NPI defaults to a fabricated number: #294, #498, #180
- The PDF substitutes a fabricated Nottingham grade (2/2/2, sum 6, tubules 45%) when grading is missing or any score is NULL, in four copy-pasted places: #532
- Draft PDFs print a fabricated signer, NPI and SHA-256 under "Electronically Signed By", with no DRAFT watermark: #169, #503
- The benign route is silently converted into an invasive-carcinoma Grade 2 / pT1c / Stage IA report because `run_report` never reads `input_ref.benign_flag`, and no benign template exists: #166, #506
- `no_invasive_tumor=True` is accepted while active hotspots remain; they are persisted as confirmed hotspots and the case is routed to a benign report: #569
- `/amend` mutates the signed row in place via unrestricted `setattr`, can overwrite `status`, `integrity_hash` and `signed_by`, does not recompute staging, does not re-hash, does not re-render: #496, #171
- Confirming grading re-queues the report stage even after signing; the worker then overwrites the signed narrative, staging and PDF at the same blob: #280, #170, #674
- The integrity hash omits the grade, sub-scores, LVI, DCIS, specimen type, attestation and the PDF bytes; the signed PDF is re-rendered after commit with failures swallowed, over the draft's blob: #178, #533, #622
- Signing does not persist unsaved form edits; the sealed document contains stale DB values while the screen shows the edited ones: #250
- ER/PR positivity uses `> 1` (1% reported negative) and Allred is hard-coded 8/7 regardless of percent: #258, #249
- Enter / "Approve Field & Next" silently relabels every unreviewed candidate in the field as `not_mitosis` with pathologist attribution and no audit event, and is bound to the global Enter key: #114, #126
- Every mitosis worker run deletes all Detection and HpfSite rows, destroying pathologist labels; triage re-confirm and stage approve both reach this path: #464, #279, #673
- Narrative guardrail checks only the grade digit and passes if the correct grade appears anywhere; the worker path never calls it at all: #176, #748
- Thumbnail endpoints fall back to an arbitrary slide from another case, then cache it under the requested case: #77

### 4. PRD drift summary

| Locked decision / stage requirement | PRD says | Code does | IDs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mitotic score basis | Mitoses/mm2 via configurable CAP table; no clinical numbers in code | Stage 5 uses summed counts with hard-coded 8/16 in four places; config key does not exist; TS copy in the UI | #357, #118, #227,  |
| HPF fallback | "If fewer than 10 legal positions, place as many as fit; scoring uses the actual counted area" | Pass 3 always fabricates 10 fields on a spiral at 196 um separation; the test asserts `len == 10` | #718, #133, #356 |
| Auth | Firebase ID-token verification, role column, signer role = pathologist | `MOCK_AUTH_ENABLED = True` literal; client picks its own role; no endpoint reads `.role`; 30/42 routes have no auth dependency | #1, #198, #529,  |
| Append-only audit log (non-negotiable) | `REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ON audit_events`; fixed event vocabulary incl. `stage_started`, `stage_rejected`, `report_signed` | `create_all` only, app connects as owner; invented names (`stage_6_report_signed`, `stage_5_grading_confirmed`); `stage_started` and `stage_rejected` never emitted; actor from request body | #27, #644, #305, #327 |
| Label/macro stripping (non-negotiable) | wsi-anon or tifftools before any other processing, then set `label_stripped_at` | No stripping tool anywhere in the repo; `label_stripped_at` stamped unconditionally; the Pillow fallback actually tiles the label and macro pages as pyramid levels | #37, #557 |
| Signed resumable uploads (non-negotiable) | Signed resumable session, 32 MiB chunks, Content-Range resume, localStorage session URI | Backend implements it; frontend never calls it and POSTs the whole WSI as one multipart request through FastAPI onto Cloud Run's 32 MiB limit | #413, #202,  |
| MPP handling | "Never guess MPP"; missing MPP means `status=needs_mpp` plus a manual entry field | Defaults to 0.25 in ingest and six other call sites; UI prints "MPP: 0.25 um/px, 40x Objective" as if measured | #38,  |
| Stain normalization | Macenko via tiatoolbox, one per-slide fit, persisted params reused for tiles | tiatoolbox absent, silent pure-NumPy fallback; `transform()` ignores the fitted params and re-fits per tile; `stain_params.json` is dead output; fit failures swallowed into hard-coded constants | #50, #436, #553 |
| DB / migrations | Postgres 16, SQLAlchemy 2 + Alembic, `backend/alembic/` | `create_all` at startup, no alembic tree, silent SQLite fallback on any Postgres error | #9, #6, #495 |
| Report versioning and immutability | `reports.id` PK, `version` int, `UNIQUE(case_id, version)`, amendment creates v+1, `trg_report_immutable` | `case_id` is the PK, no `version` column, amendment mutates the signed row via `setattr` | #496, #171, #495 |

| PDF rendering | WeasyPrint from a Jinja2 template, 3 pages, appendix with model versions and config hashes, DRAFT watermark on previews, sha256 of final bytes | ReportLab/Platypus, single flow, no appendix, no watermark, hash over a JSON metadata subset | #501, #502, #503, #178 |
| Benign path | Benign template, grade and mitosis sections omitted | `input_ref.benign_flag` never read; produces an invasive-carcinoma Grade 2 pT1c IA report | #166, #506 |
| Histologic type gate | Blocked until the pathologist confirms; `type_confirmed_by` server-side | Gate is a client boolean hard-coded `true`; no endpoint sets `type_confirmed_by` before confirm | #142, #294 |
| CAP elements | `configs/cap_elements.yaml` is the versioned compliance artifact, element class auto/manual/not_assessable, version printed on the report | File never loaded by anything; its `biomarker_defaults` were copy-pasted into code instead; value sets drift from the Pydantic Literal | #361, #480, #633 |
| QC checks | 5 checks (coverage, focus, pen marks, folds, stain sanity); focus VoL < 45, fail > 30% | Only coverage and focus; focus samples one corner tile and can never fail; thresholds 5.0 / 0.70 / 0.30 | #433, #48, #45, #548 |
| Triage embeddings | Real 224 px @ 1.0 um/px patches, batches of 64, concurrency 8, backoff, Parquet cache | 16 identical blank grey images sent, first embedding broadcast with noise, probe output discarded, no cache, `vertex_ai.*` config unread | #72, #452, #453, #86 |
| Hotspot extraction | Connected components >= `min_area_mm2`, marching-squares contours, simplify, dilate by `margin_um` | Peak-picking with fixed 600 um squares; `label`, `find_contours`, `Polygon` imported and unused; three config keys dead | #83, #81,  |
| Worker loop | `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, output keyed by execution id | Plain SELECT, no lock; all artifacts keyed by `case_id`, so retries overwrite the previous attempt | #35, #59,  |
| Coordinates | Conversions live in `pipeline/coords.py` and nowhere else; all geometry in base-level um | `coords.py` imported only by its own test; four inline reimplementations; grading persists patch centres in px | #64, #605, #243 |
| Tile reads | All downstream reads through `read_region_srgb` | Mitosis worker, preprocess and several routers call OpenSlide directly, bypassing ICC | #429, #465, #53 |
| Validation harness | `backend/cli/validate.py`, `cli.export_labels`, `report.html` with kappa and confusion matrices, override analytics views, `/analytics` page | None of it exists; no `cli` package, no `docs/` | #512, #516, #513, #514, #515 |
| Frontend stack | Next.js 15, Annotorious for polygon editing | Next 14, no Annotorious, hand-rolled SVG with no vertex editing or freehand draw | #393, #450, #468 |
| Region / naming | asia-south1 for PHI, `og-{env}-*` buckets | us-central1 default, `oncogemma-dev-*`, a foreign project number baked into defaults | #14, #422,  |

---

### 5. Structural improvements

- **One stage-transition module.** Attempt selection, status gating, next-stage queuing and audit emission are copy-pasted across `cases.py`, `triage.py`, `mitosis.py`, `grading.py` and `report.py` with three different attempt conventions and four different audit vocabularies. Collapse to one `advance_stage(case, stage, actor)` that owns the state machine, and delete the generic `approve_case_stage` second path entirely. #206, #285, #535, #644

- **One scoring module, config-driven, no duplicates.** Six implementations of the mitotic score, three of the Nottingham cut-offs (Python, a DB CHECK constraint, TypeScript), and hard-coded 262 um / 0.2157 mm2 / 2.157 mm2 in roughly a dozen places. Load `scoring.yaml` once, hash it into `config_hash`, and have the frontend call `/recompute` instead of reimplementing it. #357, #118, #227, #31, #478, #11, #158, #259

- **A single fallible-IO policy.** Roughly forty bare `except Exception` blocks currently return fabricated data. Replace with a small `stage_failure(reason)` helper plus the missing `needs_human` flag, and make "returned synthetic data" impossible to express. Every synthetic-image generator should be deleted, not gated. #135, #325, #103, #140, #141, #653

- **Delete the two-schema problem in the report.** `_ensure_report_record`, `render_and_upload_report_pdf` and `run_report` are three drifted copies of the same 60-line render-dict construction, with different fallbacks (`nottingham_sum` defaults to a literal 6 in one and to the actual sum in another). One builder, one caller. While there, add the `id`/`version` columns so amendments are rows rather than mutations. #629, #194, #169, #496

- **Make the tile path a real pyramid, not a fallback.** The 12-level cap plus per-tile full-WSI download plus a process-wide `threading.Lock` plus sync endpoints on a 40-thread pool is a four-way interaction that starves `/healthz`. Generate the full pyramid at ingest, make the tile endpoints async with a bounded executor, and drop the global lock (OpenSlide has been thread-safe per handle for years). Note the latent self-deadlock at `grading.py:572`: adding the two missing imports that finding #140 asks for will permanently wedge the endpoint on the non-reentrant lock. #635, #200, #636, #29, #541, #691

- **Put clinical value sets and constants in `configs/` and actually read them.** `cap_elements.yaml` has no reader at all; `mitosis.yaml` has ~15 dead keys; `triage.yaml` has 6; `qc.yaml` has 3 whole sections. Either wire them up or delete them, because a config file nobody reads is worse than a literal: it looks like a control that is not connected to anything. #361, #130, #83, #433, #480

- **Give the frontend a type system.** Delete `types/next-shim.d.ts`, turn off `ignoreBuildErrors` and `ignoreDuringBuilds`, add an ESLint config, and add a test runner. Most of the frontend drift in section T8 (dead imports, unused API fields, the never-called `recomputeGradingPreview`, `<button>` nested in `<Link>`) would be caught mechanically. Split the 1660-line `GradingReviewWorkspace` and 951-line `ReportWorkspace` while doing it. #268, #409, #273, #274, #266, #685

- **Move to a real queue claim and per-attempt artifacts.** `SKIP LOCKED` plus a `created_at` column for FIFO ordering (currently the tiebreak is `uuid4` order), plus GCS keys of the form `cases/{case_id}/{stage}/{execution_id}/...` so a retry cannot overwrite the attempt whose `output_ref` still points at it. #35, #66, #59, #703

- **Add the two CI tests the PRD already specifies.** The ingest test against `CMU-1-Small-Region.svs` and the `apply_edit_ops` idempotence property test are both cheap and both would have caught live classes of bug here (fabricated pyramid, missing delete op). The README's claim of "58/58 tests passing" names four test files that do not exist, and the suite cannot currently be collected. #417, #460, #386, #101, #405

- **Introduce `conftest.py` and stop hitting live GCS from tests.** Seven test files hand-roll identical in-memory-SQLite and dependency-override boilerplate, share DB state within a module, and several call real GCS or real Vertex by default (observed 403s). One fixture set with fakes makes the suite runnable offline, which is the precondition for any of the above being verifiable. #405, #101, #181, #399, #197

## All findings by area

### Backend: core / models / schemas (42)

#### 13. Default MedGemma endpoint ID is not a valid Vertex endpoint, and every failure silently becomes a canned grade

**Severity:** critical · **Category:** Clinical correctness · **Location:** `backend/app/core/config.py:29`

VERTEX_MEDGEMMA_ENDPOINT_ID defaults to the string 'medgemma-1-5-endpoint' (Vertex endpoint IDs are numeric or full resource names), so aiplatform.Endpoint(...) fails on default config. The consumer pipeline/medgemma.py:162-164 catches every exception and returns _mock_fallback_response(), which yields tubule_percent 25 / pleomorphism 2 / type IDC-NST regardless of the image, with only a print().

```
config.py:29-32  VERTEX_MEDGEMMA_ENDPOINT_ID: str = os.getenv(
        "VERTEX_MEDGEMMA_ENDPOINT_ID",
        "medgemma-1-5-endpoint"
    )
medgemma.py:162-164  except Exception as e:
            print(f"[MedGemma Vertex AI Note] Live endpoint call failed ({e}). Using deterministic fallback.")
            return self._mock_fallback_response(prompt)
```
**Impact:** With unset env (or any transient Vertex error) the grading stage stores identical fake sub-scores in gradings.machine and marks the stage awaiting_review as if a model had run; model_versions still records '1.5@2026.08'.

**Fix:** Remove the string default (require the env var, fail fast at startup when not USE_MOCK_VERTEX_AI); in medgemma.py only use the mock when settings.USE_MOCK_VERTEX_AI is true, otherwise re-raise so the stage goes to 'failed'.

*Verifier note:* Confirmed. config.py:29-32 defaults VERTEX_MEDGEMMA_ENDPOINT_ID to 'medgemma-1-5-endpoint'; medgemma.py:100 assigns it to self.endpoint_id and medgemma.py:120-125 passes it as endpoint_name to aiplatform.Endpoint, which requires a numeric id or full projects/.../endpoints/<digits> resource name and raises on this string. USE_MOCK_VERTEX_AI defaults false (config.py:43), so the default path is the live call, and the outer `except Exception` (actual lines 160-163, not 162-164 as quoted) swallows it and returns _mock_fallback_response — tubule_percent 25 / pleomorphism 2 / IDC-NST (medgemma.py:164-190) with only a print. Downstream is as described: worker/grading.py:270-271 stamps model_versions.medgemma = settings.VERTEX_MEDGEMMA_MODEL_VERSION ('1.5@2026.08'), writes the canned aggregate into gradings.machine (grading.py:410-437) and sets stage_exec.status = 'awaiting_review' (grading.py:457). Nothing distinguishes fallback output from a real model call. The same broad-except-to-fake-data pattern exists at triage.py:118-121.

#### 1. Mock auth is hard-coded on; any client picks its own identity and role via request headers

**Severity:** critical · **Category:** Security · **Location:** `backend/app/core/config.py:59`

MOCK_AUTH_ENABLED is a literal True (not read from env), so there is no deployment configuration that disables it. get_current_user() then trusts X-User-Id / X-User-Role / X-User-Email verbatim. The only validation is that role is one of three strings. PRD 00-overview §3 pins Firebase Auth + a role column in Postgres.

```
config.py:59  MOCK_AUTH_ENABLED: bool = True
auth.py:19-21  if settings.MOCK_AUTH_ENABLED:
        user_id = x_user_id or settings.DEFAULT_MOCK_USER_ID
        role = x_user_role or settings.DEFAULT_MOCK_ROLE
```
**Impact:** Anyone who can reach the API can act as any pathologist (sign reports, delete all cases, confirm stages) and forge the `actor` written into audit_events, which the PRD calls append-only evidence.

**Fix:** Read MOCK_AUTH_ENABLED from env, default False, and refuse to start with it on when ENV != dev/test; implement the Firebase token path in auth.py; stop deriving actor from a client header.

*Verifier note:* Location and quoted evidence are exact: config.py:59 `MOCK_AUTH_ENABLED: bool = True`, auth.py:19-22 takes id/role/email straight from X-User-* headers with the only check being role in [pathologist, technician, viewer] (auth.py:24-28). Those identities flow into audit rows as `actor=user.id` (routers/cases.py:48,151,202,287,355) and into the sign/amend paths, so header-chosen identity and role are authoritative. PRD 00-overview:47 does require Firebase Auth + a role column. One factual correction to the description: the field IS env-overridable — this is a pydantic-settings BaseSettings with no env_prefix (config.py:66-68), so field name MOCK_AUTH_ENABLED is populated from the env var of the same name; the os.getenv wrapper other fields use is redundant, not required. So 'no deployment configuration disables it' is wrong. It does not rescue the finding: auth.py:32-36 has no real auth path, so setting MOCK_AUTH_ENABLED=false makes every authenticated route return 401 — mock auth is the only working auth, and it is on by default. Critical stands.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/core/auth.py:19` (Mock auth is hard-coded on and trusts client-supplied X-User-Id/X-User-Role: audit actor is attacker-controlled); `backend/app/core/config.py:59` (MOCK_AUTH_ENABLED is hardcoded and role is fully client-controlled — no way to disable in any environment)

#### 12. Report model ships fabricated clinical results as column defaults (ER 95%, PR 80%, HER2 1+, Ki-67 18%, 18 mm tumour, negative margins, pT1c IA)

**Severity:** critical · **Category:** Clinical correctness · **Location:** `backend/app/models/report.py:39`

Every Report row is born with concrete biomarker, size, margin, node and AJCC values that were never measured. The same literals are repeated in worker/report.py:68-88, routers/report.py:66-69,78 (Pydantic defaults) and configs/cap_elements.yaml:113-127 (biomarker_defaults). Nothing marks them as placeholders; the PDF renderer prints whatever is in the row.

```
report.py:25  tumor_size_mm: ... default=18.0
report.py:42-46  default=lambda: {
            "er": {"status": "positive", "percent": 95, "allred_score": 8},
            "pr": {"status": "positive", "percent": 80, "allred_score": 7},
            "her2": {"ihc_score": "1+", "fish_status": "not_performed", "result": "negative"},
report.py:52  default=lambda: {"ajcc_version": "8th/9th Edition", "pt_stage": "pT1c", "pn_stage": "pNX", "pm_stage": "cM0", "stage_group": "IA"}
```
**Impact:** A pathologist who skips a field signs a CAP synoptic report containing invented receptor status and stage — the exact failure a synoptic report exists to prevent.

**Fix:** Make these columns/JSON keys nullable with default None / 'not_performed', render 'Not reported' in the PDF, and block sign-off (report.py sign route) while required CAP elements are unset. Delete biomarker_defaults from cap_elements.yaml.

*Verifier note:* Verified in full. models/report.py:22-27 (laterality='right', tumor_size_mm=18.0, lvi_status='absent'), :29-33 (margins negative / 5.0 mm / posterior), :39-48 (ER positive 95% Allred 8, PR positive 80% Allred 7, HER2 IHC 1+ negative, Ki-67 18%), :49-53 (pT1c / pNX / cM0 / IA). The literals are duplicated verbatim in backend/worker/report.py:80-87 and backend/app/routers/report.py:66-69 (BiomarkersPayload/MarginsPayload Pydantic defaults) and :134-143 (_ensure_report_record), plus configs/cap_elements.yaml:113-127 biomarker_defaults. Nothing marks them as placeholders: pipeline/report_pdf.py:233-245,260 reads margins/biomarkers straight out of the row and prints 'ER: POSITIVE (95%) | PR: ... | HER2: IHC 1+ (NEGATIVE) | Ki-67: 18%', and its own .get() fallbacks repeat the same fabricated values. sign_final_report (routers/report.py:576-620) has no required-field/checklist gate at all -- it hashes report.margins/report.biomarkers/report.staging as-is and seals. PRD 06 sec.2 classes margins and er/pr/her2/ki67 as not_assessable with explicit na_text, and sec.4 requires sign preconditions with a 422 missing-items list, neither of which exists. Critical is correct.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/report.py:124` (Report rows are auto-created with fabricated clinical values (tumor size, ER/PR/HER2/Ki67, margins, laterality, diagnosis line) and can be signed as-is); `backend/worker/report.py:77` (Fabricated clinical values (18 mm tumor, ER 95%, PR 80%, HER2 1+, Ki-67 18%, negative 5 mm margin, right UOQ) are written into the report and PDF as real findings)

#### 6. Silent import-time fallback to a shared local SQLite file when Postgres is unreachable

**Severity:** high · **Category:** Data integrity · **Location:** `backend/app/core/db.py:27`

db.py opens a Postgres connection at import time; any exception (DB briefly down, DNS blip, wrong password) permanently switches that process to backend/../oncogemma_local.db and merely prints a warning. API and worker are separate processes, so one can land on Postgres and the other on SQLite. PRD 00-overview §3 pins Postgres 16 with no fallback.

```
db.py:25-32  with engine.connect() as conn:
            pass
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"[DB Core Warning] Postgres connection failed ({e}). Falling back to shared local SQLite database at {sqlite_url}.")
        engine = create_engine(sqlite_url, ...)
```
**Impact:** Split-brain: cases/stage_executions written by the API into SQLite are never seen by the worker (or vice-versa), signed reports land in an unencrypted file in the repo directory, and the operator only learns from a stdout line. Data written during the outage is stranded when Postgres returns.

**Fix:** Delete the fallback. Create the engine lazily, honour DATABASE_URL only, and let a bad DB fail /healthz (add a SELECT 1 there) so orchestration restarts the process.

*Verifier note:* Code matches exactly. db.py:10 reads settings.DATABASE_URL (config.py:46-49 defaults to postgresql://...localhost:5432/oncogemma_db); db.py:18-26 builds the Postgres engine and probes it with `with engine.connect()` at import time; db.py:27-32 catches *any* Exception, prints a warning to stdout and rebinds `engine` to sqlite:///<repo>/oncogemma_local.db. This is genuinely per-process: backend/app/main.py:15 and backend/worker/main.py:13 both import from app.core.db independently, so one can land on Postgres and the other on SQLite. The fallback DB is fully functional, not inert: main.py:23 runs Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine) in lifespan, so the API creates tables and accepts writes into the file while the worker (worker/main.py polling StageExecution) polls a different store forever. PRD 00-overview.md:41 pins 'Postgres 16' and no SQLite tier appears anywhere in prd/. /healthz (main.py:50-56) does no DB check, so orchestration cannot detect it. Severity lowered critical -> high: the trigger is conditional (Postgres unreachable at import), nothing is corrupted or overwritten (data is stranded/diverged, not destroyed), and the file IS gitignored (.gitignore last line: oncogemma_local.db). Everything else in the impact claim holds.

#### 495. No DB trigger (or any mechanism) enforces signed-report immutability

**Severity:** high · **Category:** PRD deviation · **Location:** `backend/app/core/db.py:36`

PRD section 5 requires a Postgres trigger `trg_report_immutable` calling `reject_signed_update()` that raises on any UPDATE/DELETE of a row where `status = 'signed'`. There is no migrations directory, no alembic setup, and no trigger DDL anywhere in the repo (confirmed by grep for `reject_signed_update`/`trg_report_immutable`/`CREATE TRIGGER` — zero hits). db.py only defines SQLAlchemy's declarative Base and a plain engine/session factory with no schema-enforcement hooks, and the app also silently runs on SQLite (which doesn't support this trigger syntax) when Postgres is unreachable.

```
class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass

def get_db():
    db = SessionLocal()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()
```
**Impact:** Nothing at the database layer prevents a signed report from being altered — immutability, if it exists at all, depends entirely on the application code remembering to check `status == 'signed'` before every write, which the /amend endpoint (see separate finding) already fails to do correctly.

**Fix:** Add the migration creating reject_signed_update()/trg_report_immutable exactly as specified, and ensure it runs against whatever engine is actually deployed.

*Verifier note:* Evidence holds. prd/06-stage-v4.5-report.md:90-94 literally specifies CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION reject_signed_update() and CREATE TRIGGER trg_report_immutable BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON reports; grep for reject_signed_update / trg_report_immutable / CREATE TRIGGER over the whole repo returns hits only inside that PRD file, never in code. There is no migrations/ dir, no alembic.ini, no .sql file anywhere (find over the repo root returns nothing). Schema comes from Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine) at backend/app/main.py:23, which emits only tables/indexes from the ORM metadata — never triggers or functions — so the trigger can never exist in any deployed DB. db.py:27-32 additionally falls back to SQLite on any Postgres connect failure, where that PL/pgSQL trigger is not even expressible. Downgraded critical->high because the impact claim overstates the current state: application-layer guards DO reject direct writes to signed reports at report.py:348-351, 418-421, 492 and 588-591. What is genuinely missing is the DB-level backstop the PRD mandates, and it matters most for /amend (report.py:665-690), which by design UPDATEs the signed row in place (report.status = 'amended', report.amendments = ...) — exactly the statement the PRD trigger is meant to raise on, and it leaves no untouched v1 row. So this is a real PRD deviation with a real audit/regulatory consequence, but not 'nothing prevents alteration'. Cited location db.py:1 is acceptable for an absence-of-code finding; db.py:36 (class Base) is the closest concrete anchor.

#### 4. GCS client ignores STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST/USE_REAL_GCS and is built outside the try in ensure_buckets_exist, so the API cannot start without Google ADC

**Severity:** high · **Category:** Crash · **Location:** `backend/app/core/gcs.py:19`

config.py declares USE_REAL_GCS (line 12) and STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST (line 56) but neither is read anywhere (`grep -rn USE_REAL_GCS\|STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST backend` hits only config.py). get_gcs_client() always builds storage.Client(project=...) with default credentials. In ensure_buckets_exist(), that call sits on line 140 before the try/except that starts on line 142, so google.auth.exceptions.DefaultCredentialsError propagates out of the lifespan handler. Values placed in .env are loaded into `settings`, not os.environ, so even the library's own STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST support is bypassed for .env users.

```
gcs.py:19   _gcs_client = storage.Client(project=settings.GCP_PROJECT_ID)
gcs.py:140  client = get_gcs_client()
gcs.py:141-142  for bucket_name in [...]:
        try:
```
**Impact:** Local dev / CI without gcloud ADC: uvicorn startup raises in lifespan and the server never comes up; with ADC but no bucket access every API test hits real GCS (the observed HTTP 403s). The compose fake-gcs-server is unreachable by design.

**Fix:** In get_gcs_client(): if settings.STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST or not settings.USE_REAL_GCS -> storage.Client(project=..., credentials=AnonymousCredentials(), client_options={'api_endpoint': host}); move get_gcs_client() inside the try in ensure_buckets_exist or make lifespan tolerant.

*Verifier note:* Verified. gcs.py:19 builds storage.Client(project=settings.GCP_PROJECT_ID) with no credentials argument and no emulator handling. Repo-wide grep for USE_REAL_GCS|STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST returns only config.py:12 and config.py:56 — both settings are dead. main.py:20-26 defines lifespan and calls ensure_buckets_exist() with no try/except, and gcs.py:140 `client = get_gcs_client()` really does sit above the `try:` that begins at gcs.py:142, so google.auth.exceptions.DefaultCredentialsError from google.auth.default() propagates out of the lifespan and uvicorn never serves. The finder's subtle point is also correct: pydantic-settings loads .env into `settings`, not os.environ, so google-cloud-storage's own STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST anonymous-credentials path never triggers for a .env-only dev, and ops/docker-compose.yml's fake-gcs-server (port 4443) is unreachable by any code path. Severity kept high: total startup failure for any environment without ADC.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/core/gcs.py:140` (App startup crashes without Google credentials because get_gcs_client() runs outside the try in ensure_buckets_exist); `backend/app/core/config.py:12` (USE_REAL_GCS and STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST settings are defined but never consumed anywhere)

#### 9. Schema managed by create_all at startup; Alembic declared but absent

**Severity:** high · **Category:** Data integrity · **Location:** `backend/app/main.py:23`

main.py creates tables with Base.metadata.create_all; there is no backend/alembic directory or alembic.ini although alembic is in requirements.txt (line 4) and PRD §3/§4 pin 'SQLAlchemy 2 + Alembic' and a `backend/alembic/` tree. create_all never alters existing tables, so every column added since a DB was first created (e.g. gradings.type_confirmed_by, reports.amendments) is missing on that DB.

```
main.py:22-23  # Ensure database tables exist for dev
    Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)
requirements.txt:4  alembic>=1.13.1
```
**Impact:** After any model change, existing environments return HTTP 500 (UndefinedColumn / no such column) on the affected routes; there is no migration/rollback story for PHI tables.

**Fix:** Initialise Alembic, generate the baseline revision from current models, run `alembic upgrade head` in the entrypoint, and drop create_all outside tests.

*Verifier note:* Verified all three legs. (1) main.py:20-26 lifespan calls Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine) and nothing else touches schema — a repo-wide grep for create_all/drop_all/migrat found only main.py:23 plus test files (tests/test_grading_api.py:24, test_api_auth.py:20, etc.); zero migration code. (2) `find backend -iname '*alembic*'` returns nothing: no backend/alembic/, no alembic.ini, despite requirements.txt:4 `alembic>=1.13.1` and prd/00-overview.md:40 ('SQLAlchemy 2 + Alembic') and :62 (an `alembic/` tree in the prescribed layout). (3) The named columns exist and postdate v4.0: backend/app/models/grading.py:27 type_confirmed_by, backend/app/models/report.py:72 amendments. Severity stays high rather than being a dev-only nit because ops/docker-compose.yml pins postgres to a persistent named volume (`postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data`), so any environment that ran an earlier stage keeps the old schema across the upgrade and create_all silently no-ops on the existing tables — the grading/report routes then fail with UndefinedColumn. No forward or rollback path exists for a PHI database.

*Also reported at:* `backend/requirements.txt:4` (alembic declared in requirements.txt but never used anywhere in the codebase)

#### 529. Auth dependency is opt-in per endpoint; 30 of 42 routes (all grading/mitosis/triage/report routes, direct tile route, thumbnail) never call get_current_user

**Severity:** high · **Category:** Security · **Location:** `backend/app/main.py:43`

get_current_user is only wired as a per-endpoint Depends() in cases.py, audit.py and tiles.get_tile. The grading (6 routes), mitosis (8), triage (5) and report (9) routers plus tiles.get_tile_direct (tiles.py:222) and cases.get_case_thumbnail (cases.py:373) take only db and read the actor from the request body (payload.signed_by, payload.reviewed_by). main.py includes every router with no router-level dependencies list. So even after MOCK_AUTH_ENABLED is turned off and Firebase verification is added to auth.py, the 401 branch only protects case CRUD and audit; signing, amendment, grading confirmation, label toggles and PHI tile/crop serving remain unauthenticated.

```
app.include_router(cases_router) ... app.include_router(report_router)   # no dependencies=[Depends(get_current_user)]
backend/app/routers/report.py:577  def sign_final_report(payload: SignReportPayload, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
```
**Impact:** Anyone who can reach the API can sign or amend a clinical report, confirm grading, or pull slide tiles and crops for any case id, independent of the auth implementation.

**Fix:** Attach auth at router/app level (APIRouter(dependencies=[Depends(get_current_user)]) or include_router(..., dependencies=[...])), derive actor from CurrentUser rather than body fields, and add a test asserting every route except /healthz returns 401 without credentials.

*Verifier note:* Counts verified exactly. Route totals per router file: audit 1, cases 11, grading 6, mitosis 8, report 9, tiles 2, triage 5 = 42. Depends(get_current_user) appears only in audit.py:20, tiles.py:208 (get_tile), and ten places in cases.py (39, 60, 69, 84, 100, 172, 222, 307, 330, 431) = 12 protected, leaving 30 unprotected — matching the claim. Spot-checked the named ones: report.py:577 `def sign_final_report(payload: SignReportPayload, db: Session = Depends(get_db))`, cases.py:372-375 get_case_thumbnail (db only), tiles.py:216-222 get_tile_direct (db only). main.py:43-49 includes all seven routers with no `dependencies=` argument, and main.py has no auth middleware — only CORSMiddleware at 35-41 — so nothing enforces auth globally. High is correct: this is a structural gap, not a config toggle. Flipping MOCK_AUTH_ENABLED off or dropping Firebase verification into auth.py:32-36 hardens only case CRUD, audit and the one tile route; report signing/amendment, grading confirmation, mitosis label toggles, triage and PHI crop/thumbnail serving stay open. Note the finder's framing is slightly generous to the current state — today get_current_user grants a pathologist even with zero headers (auth.py:20-30 + config.py MOCK_AUTH_ENABLED=True), so the 12 'protected' routes are not actually protected either; the finding is about the latent design, and on that it is right.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/report.py:576` (Report router has no authentication or role dependency at all — anyone can read PHI PDFs, sign, and amend); `backend/app/routers/mitosis.py:618` (No authentication/role dependency on any mitosis endpoint; reviewed_by/actor is client-supplied); `backend/app/routers/triage.py:54` (No authentication or role check on any triage endpoint; reviewer identity taken from request body); `backend/app/routers/cases.py:373` (Case thumbnail endpoint has no authentication dependency); `backend/app/routers/tiles.py:216` (The tile URL actually served to the viewer points at an endpoint with no authentication at all); `backend/app/routers/tiles.py:217` (Direct tile route and case thumbnail have no auth dependency at all; tile response is marked public/immutable)

#### 10. Case relationships omit Hotspot/Detection/HpfSite; deleting a case violates FKs on Postgres

**Severity:** high · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/app/models/case.py:21`

Case declares ORM cascades only for slides, stage_executions, grading, report. hotspots.case_id, hotspots.stage_execution_id, detections.case_id and hpf_sites.case_id are FKs with no ondelete and no relationship, so DELETE /api/v1/cases/{id} (cases.py:80-93) and DELETE /api/v1/cases (cases.py:66-78) issue DELETE FROM cases / stage_executions while child rows still reference them.

```
case.py:21-24  slides = relationship("Slide", back_populates="case", cascade="all, delete-orphan")
    stage_executions = relationship("StageExecution", ...)
    grading = ...
    report = ...
hotspot.py:17-18  case_id = Column(GUID, ForeignKey("cases.id"), primary_key=True, index=True)
    stage_execution_id = Column(GUID, ForeignKey("stage_executions.id"), nullable=False)
```
**Impact:** On Postgres, deleting any case that reached triage confirmation raises psycopg2 ForeignKeyViolation -> HTTP 500; on SQLite (FKs off) it leaves orphaned clinical rows.

**Fix:** Add ondelete='CASCADE' to those three FKs (and hotspots.stage_execution_id) plus passive_deletes relationships on Case, or explicitly delete children in delete_case.

*Verifier note:* Evidence holds exactly as quoted. case.py:21-24 declares relationships/cascades only for Slide, StageExecution, Grading, Report. Hotspot (hotspot.py:17-18: case_id ForeignKey('cases.id') and stage_execution_id ForeignKey('stage_executions.id'), both with no ondelete), Detection (detection.py:18: case_id ForeignKey('cases.id'), no ondelete) and HpfSite (hpf_site.py:17: same) have no Case relationship anywhere — grep for 'Hotspot' shows it is only referenced in routers, never in a relationship(). By contrast Grading (grading.py:18) and Report (report.py:18) DO carry ondelete='CASCADE', which shows the omission is inconsistent rather than intentional. Delete path: routers/cases.py:80-93 delete_case does db.delete(case_obj); db.commit(), and cases.py:66-78 clear_all_cases loops db.delete(c) — the ORM emits DELETE on slides/stage_executions/gradings/reports then DELETE FROM cases, and nothing touches hotspots/detections/hpf_sites. Schema is created by Base.metadata.create_all (main.py:23) so the FKs really exist in the created DB, and the default DATABASE_URL (config.py:46-49) is postgresql://..., so on Postgres a case that reached triage confirm (triage.py:514-530 inserts Hotspot rows with stage_execution_id) raises ForeignKeyViolation — in fact it fires on the earlier DELETE FROM stage_executions via hotspots.stage_execution_id — surfacing as an unhandled IntegrityError -> HTTP 500. On the SQLite fallback (db.py:12-32) there is no 'PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON' anywhere in the codebase (grep found none), so FK enforcement is off and the delete silently leaves orphaned hotspot/detection/hpf_site clinical rows. Severity high is right: the delete endpoint is unusable for any post-triage case on the default backend, and the degraded path silently retains patient-derived data that the user asked to delete.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/models/hotspot.py:17` (Hotspot has no ORM relationship/cascade from Case; polygon column is plain JSON); `backend/app/routers/cases.py:91` (Deleting a case with hotspots/detections/HPF sites raises IntegrityError (500) on Postgres and orphans rows on SQLite); `backend/app/routers/cases.py:91` (Deleting a case fails with FK violation on Postgres once hotspots/detections/hpf_sites exist; on SQLite it leaves orphan rows and GCS blobs); `backend/app/routers/cases.py:91` (Deleting a case with hotspots/detections/HPFs fails on Postgres (FK without cascade) and never deletes GCS artifacts)

#### 18. Slide finalize accepts any gs:// URI — cross-case / cross-bucket PHI attachment

**Severity:** high · **Category:** Security · **Location:** `backend/app/schemas/case.py:33`

SlideFinalizeRequest.gcs_uri is an unconstrained string and cases.py:336-340 stores it as slides.gcs_uri_original and queues ingest on it. The worker then downloads whatever object the service account can read (parse_gcs_uri accepts any bucket). client_sha256 is stored but never compared with the object (ingest.py:261-262 overwrites it).

```
schemas/case.py:32-34  class SlideFinalizeRequest(BaseModel):
    gcs_uri: str
    client_sha256: str | None = None
cases.py:336-340  slide_obj = Slide(
        case_id=case_id,
        gcs_uri_original=req.gcs_uri,
        checksum_sha256=req.client_sha256
    )
```
**Impact:** Any caller can attach another patient's raw slide (gs://<raw>/cases/<other-id>/...) or any readable object to their case and view it through the tile endpoints.

**Fix:** Validate in the schema/route that gcs_uri == f'gs://{GCS_RAW_BUCKET}/cases/{case_id}/<uuid>.<ext>' (regex + case_id match), verify the blob exists, and reject when client_sha256 != computed checksum at ingest.

*Verifier note:* Holds up end to end. schemas/case.py:32-34 declares gcs_uri as a bare str with no validator. cases.py:325-341 (finalize_slide_upload) checks only that the Case row exists (line 332-334) and then writes req.gcs_uri verbatim into Slide.gcs_uri_original (line 338) and into the ingest StageExecution.input_ref (line 349) — no check that the URI is in settings.GCS_RAW_BUCKET, that its key is under cases/{case_id}/, or that the blob even exists (gcs.blob_exists is defined at gcs.py:81-85 and never called here). The worker then trusts it: ingest.py:243-257 does `raw_bucket_name, blob_name = parse_gcs_uri(gcs_uri_original)` and downloads it, and parse_gcs_uri (gcs.py:22-34) returns whatever bucket the string names. The same field is re-read for viewing at tiles.py:158-163 and cases.py:385-398, so the fetched object is served back to the caller as tiles/thumbnail. The checksum claim is also correct: cases.py:339 stores client_sha256, and ingest.py:261-262 unconditionally recomputes and overwrites (`checksum = calculate_sha256(...); slide_obj.checksum_sha256 = checksum`) with no comparison, so the client value is decorative. Severity high stands for a PHI system — this is an arbitrary-read primitive over everything the GCS service account can read, not merely cross-case. Two aggravating facts the finder did not mention: auth is header-only mock (auth.py:19-30, MOCK_AUTH_ENABLED defaults True) so any caller is 'authenticated', and cases.py:372-375 (thumbnail) and tiles.py:216-227 (get_tile_direct) have no get_current_user dependency at all, so the attached object can be read back unauthenticated. Cited line 32 is the class statement; the unconstrained field is line 33.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/cases.py:336` (finalize trusts an arbitrary client-supplied gs:// URI and never verifies the object exists or the client checksum); `backend/app/routers/cases.py:336` (finalize_slide_upload trusts a client-supplied gcs_uri; the worker then downloads any object the service account can read)

#### 541. DB pool (10+20) is smaller than FastAPI's 40 sync worker threads and sessions are held across the OpenSlide global lock and full-slide GCS downloads

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Performance · **Location:** `backend/app/core/db.py:22`

Every tile/thumbnail/patch endpoint takes db: Session = Depends(get_db) and then blocks on OPENSLIDE_GLOBAL_LOCK and, in the fallback path (tiles.py:163, grading.py:546, mitosis.py:284), downloads the entire raw WSI to a temp dir while holding the pooled connection. OpenSeadragon issues dozens of tile requests per viewport change; with anyio's default 40-thread pool, more than 30 concurrent sync requests exhaust pool_size+max_overflow and the 31st waits pool_timeout (30 s) then raises TimeoutError -> HTTP 500. Because the lock serialises tile generation, requests pile up exactly in this state.

```
pool_size=10,
max_overflow=20
```
**Impact:** Viewer stalls and intermittent 500s under normal panning/zooming once the DZI pyramid is missing for a layer.

**Fix:** Release the session before slow I/O (query slide metadata, db.close(), then generate), or size the pool to the thread pool and serve tiles without a DB dependency (cache slide metadata per slide id).

*Verifier note:* Confirmed at the cited line. db.py:19-24 creates the Postgres engine with pool_size=10, max_overflow=20 (30 connections max, default pool_timeout 30s). Both tile endpoints are plain sync `def` (tiles.py:202 get_tile, tiles.py:217 get_tile_direct), so FastAPI runs them in anyio's threadpool (default 40 tokens) — 40 potential concurrent holders against 30 connections. Each takes db: Session = Depends(get_db) (tiles.py:207, 222) and issues a query immediately (db.scalars(select(Slide)...).first() at tiles.py:210; db.get(Slide, slide_id) at tiles.py:224), which checks out a pooled connection into an open transaction that is only released by db.close() in get_db's finally (db.py:39-44) — i.e. after the whole response is built. stream_slide_tile then does GCS blob fetches (tiles.py:136-147), and on the pyramid-miss path downloads the entire raw WSI with download_blob_to_filename (tiles.py:163) and renders under OPENSLIDE_GLOBAL_LOCK (tiles.py:47), a process-wide threading.Lock (app/core/openslide_lock.py:5) that serialises every tile, thumbnail and patch render. So sessions are demonstrably held across the lock and the full-slide download, and the same pattern repeats at grading.py:546/572, mitosis.py:284/289 and 472/475, cases.py:398/402. Under OpenSeadragon's burst of tile requests with a missing DZI pyramid, the 31st concurrent request waits pool_timeout then raises TimeoutError -> HTTP 500. Medium is right: it needs the pyramid-missing fallback path plus concurrency, and the serialising lock means the user-visible symptom is usually a stall before it is a 500. Worth noting the SQLite fallback engine (db.py:29-32) has an even smaller default pool (5+10), so the same exhaustion arrives sooner there.

#### 19. Signed upload URL pins Content-Type to octet-stream and ignores size_bytes/content_type from the request

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/app/core/gcs.py:103`

SlideUploadUrlRequest carries content_type and size_bytes but generate_signed_upload_url hard-codes content_type='application/octet-stream' and adds no size/extension constraint. A V4 signature includes Content-Type, so a browser PUT with the file's real MIME (e.g. image/tiff) fails with 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch. The filename extension at cases.py:314 is also unvalidated.

```
gcs.py:99-104  url = blob.generate_signed_url(
            version="v4",
            expiration=timedelta(minutes=expiration_minutes),
            method="PUT",
            content_type="application/octet-stream"
        )
schemas/case.py:23-26  class SlideUploadUrlRequest(BaseModel):
    filename: str
    size_bytes: int
    content_type: str = "application/octet-stream"
```
**Impact:** Direct-to-bucket uploads fail unless the client happens to send octet-stream; no upload size ceiling; arbitrary extensions accepted.

**Fix:** Pass req.content_type into the signature (and echo it in the response), add headers={'content-length': str(size_bytes)} or a max size check, and allowlist WSI extensions.

*Verifier note:* Verified. gcs.py:99-104 hard-codes content_type="application/octet-stream" into a v4 signature and takes no size or extension argument (signature at gcs.py:94 is bucket_name, blob_name, expiration_minutes only). schemas/case.py:23-26 does declare filename/size_bytes/content_type, and cases.py:308-318 uses only req.filename for the extension (`req.filename.rsplit('.',1)[-1].lower()`, falling back to "svs") and never passes req.content_type or req.size_bytes to the signer. Because Content-Type is part of a V4 signed-header set, a browser PUT with the real MIME type fails SignatureDoesNotMatch; there is no size ceiling and no WSI extension allowlist. Distinct from index 5 (that is the swallowed-exception fallback; this is the signature contents). Severity medium is defensible but note the practical blast radius is currently latent — no frontend caller uses this route yet (index 20).

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/core/gcs.py:94` (Signed upload URL ignores requested content_type/size and silently falls back to an unsigned public URL)

#### 5. Signed-URL failure silently returns an unauthenticated public GCS URL

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Security · **Location:** `backend/app/core/gcs.py:106`

Any exception from generate_signed_url (missing private key with user ADC, wrong scopes, network) is swallowed and the handler returns https://storage.googleapis.com/{bucket}/{blob}. The API responds 200 with a URL that either fails the browser PUT with 401/403 (misconfiguration hidden from the operator) or, if the raw bucket is ever made writable, accepts unauthenticated PHI uploads.

```
gcs.py:106-108  except Exception as e:
        # Fallback to direct GCS endpoint if signed URL generation credentials lack private key (e.g. ADC user token)
        return f"https://storage.googleapis.com/{bucket_name}/{blob_name}"
```
**Impact:** Upload path fails late in the browser instead of at the API, and the fallback encourages opening the PHI bucket to public writes to 'make it work'.

**Fix:** Remove the fallback: raise HTTPException(503, 'signed URL unavailable') from the caller (cases.py:318), and use IAM signBlob (service_account_email/access_token args) when running on ADC without a private key.

*Verifier note:* Code confirmed exactly as quoted: gcs.py:106-108 catches bare Exception (binding an unused `e`) and returns f"https://storage.googleapis.com/{bucket_name}/{blob_name}", and cases.py:318-322 returns that string as SlideUploadUrlResponse.upload_url with a 200. So a signing failure (ADC user token with no private key, wrong scopes, transient error) is silently converted into a non-signed URL — real defect, real masked misconfiguration. Downgrading high->medium: the second half of the impact claim is speculative rather than a property of this code. The returned URL is not writable — a default GCS bucket rejects anonymous PUT — so no unauthenticated PHI write exists today; that only materialises if someone separately makes the raw bucket public. And nothing calls this endpoint: grep over frontend/app, frontend/lib, frontend/components finds no reference to upload-url or slide/finalize (see index 20), so today's blast radius is a misleading 200 on a dead route, not a live PHI exposure.

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Security · **Location:** `backend/app/core/gcs.py:144`

On every API start the process creates any missing bucket with client.create_bucket(name, location=settings.GCP_REGION) — default us-central1, default (non-uniform) ACLs, no lifecycle rule. Any error (permission denied, wrong project) is discarded, so a misconfigured deployment appears healthy.

```

PRD backing checked and holds: 00-overview.md:43 ('GCS, uniform bucket-level access, asia-south1 | PHI residency') and 00-overview.md:158 ('All asia-south1, UBLA, no public access, 30-day lifecycle rule on raw scratch prefix only'). #### 3. CORS allows every origin with credentials

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Security · **Location:** `backend/app/main.py:37`

allow_origins=['*'] combined with allow_credentials=True makes Starlette reflect the request Origin on credentialed requests, so any web page can issue authenticated cross-origin calls. Combined with header-based mock auth, any third-party page in a user's browser can drive the API.

```
main.py:37-38  allow_origins=["*"],
    allow_credentials=True,
```
**Impact:** Cross-site request forgery / data exfiltration of PHI (tiles, patches, reports) from any origin.

**Fix:** Read an ALLOWED_ORIGINS list from settings (default http://localhost:3000) and drop allow_credentials unless cookies are actually used.

*Verifier note:* Code is exactly as quoted: main.py:35-41 add CORSMiddleware with allow_origins=["*"], allow_credentials=True, allow_methods=["*"], allow_headers=["*"]. Verified the reflection behaviour in the installed starlette 1.2.1 (/opt/homebrew/lib/python3.13/site-packages/starlette/middleware/cors.py:167-168: `if self.allow_all_origins and self.allow_credentials: self.allow_explicit_origin(headers, origin)`), so the response carries Access-Control-Allow-Origin: <request Origin> + Allow-Credentials: true. main.py has no other middleware, so nothing narrows this elsewhere. Severity downgraded from high to medium: the load-bearing defect is allow_origins=["*"] + allow_headers=["*"] (which already lets any page preflight and send X-User-Id/X-User-Role and read the reply), not the credentials flag — there are no cookies or session tokens anywhere in the backend today (auth.py:10-30 reads only request headers), so allow_credentials leaks nothing extra yet. And because get_current_user defaults to a pathologist with no headers at all (config.py MOCK_AUTH_ENABLED=True, DEFAULT_MOCK_ROLE="pathologist") and 30 routes never call it (see index 529), the API is already open to any direct HTTP client; CORS only adds the drive-by-browser path to an otherwise unroutable host. Real, worth fixing, but not the primary control failure.

Confirmed at the worker: main.py:78-81 sets only status/output_ref/model_versions/completed_at, and the handler contract is `out_uri, model_versions = handler(...)` (main.py:76) -- a two-tuple with no slot for a hash, so no handler could persist one even if it computed it (qc.py:130 returns `output_ref, {"opencv": "4.13.0"}`). PRD 00-overview.md:150 is explicit: 'loaded once, hashed (sha256 of canonical JSON) into stage_executions.config_hash', and the schema at 00-overview.md:114 lists the column. So the column is dead and the config-discipline contract is unimplemented. Severity kept at medium, not raised: nothing reads the column either, so there is no runtime failure, and QC's own hash does survive in the AuditEvent payload -- but only for QC, and it is md5[:12] rather than the sha256 the PRD specifies, so triage/mitosis/grading/report thresholds remain entirely untraceable. Note the proposed fix understates the work: it needs the handler return signature widened (7 call sites in worker/) or a hash computed centrally in main.py.

*Also reported at:* `backend/pipeline/qc_checks.py:35` (config_hash never persisted to stage_executions.config_hash; hash is md5[:12] of raw text rather than sha256 of canonical JSON); `backend/worker/qc.py:129` (stage_executions.config_hash is never populated for preprocess or qc stages); `backend/worker/triage.py:556` (run_triage never computes or stores config_hash and returns a model_versions dict that disagrees with output.json)

#### 648. CurrentUser.email is synthesized from a spoofable header and never read anywhere

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Improvement · **Location:** `backend/app/core/auth.py:22`

get_current_user accepts X-User-Email and otherwise fabricates `{user_id}@oncogemma.health`; no router or worker reads `.email` (grep over app/ and worker/ finds no usage). The fabricated domain would leak into any future notification or report signature block.

```
app/core/auth.py:13  x_user_email: str | None = Header(None, alias="X-User-Email")
app/core/auth.py:22  email = x_user_email or f"{user_id}@oncogemma.health"
```
**Impact:** Dead field with a fake default that looks real; when Firebase auth is wired in, the fallback will mask a missing verified email.

**Fix:** Drop the header and the field until a verified identity provider supplies it, or make email Optional[str] = None.

*Verifier note:* Verified. auth.py:13 declares x_user_email (alias X-User-Email) and auth.py:22 fabricates `f"{user_id}@oncogemma.health"` when it is absent. `grep -rn email backend/ --include=*.py` returns hits only at auth.py:7, 13, 22, 30 — no router, worker, model, schema, test, or frontend file reads CurrentUser.email or sends the X-User-Email header (the only X-User-* headers used in tests and backend/pipeline/diagnose_system.py:249 are X-User-Role and X-User-Id). The synthesized address is a plausible-looking fake with no verifying authority behind it, which is the real hazard once report signature blocks or notifications start reading it. Low is right: today it is inert dead weight, not an exploitable path. The report.py sign path already ignores it entirely (report.py:639 uses payload.signed_by). Cheapest fix is deleting the field and the header, not making it Optional.

#### 391. No .env.example despite ~15 environment variables the app depends on, and README documents none of them

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Docs · **Location:** `backend/app/core/config.py:4`

config.py's Settings class reads over a dozen environment variables (GCP_PROJECT_ID, GCP_REGION, USE_REAL_GCS, VERTEX_PATH_FOUNDATION_ENDPOINT_ID/LOCATION/API_ENDPOINT, VERTEX_MEDGEMMA_ENDPOINT_ID/LOCATION/MODEL_VERSION, MEDGEMMA_TEMPERATURE/MAX_RETRIES, USE_MOCK_VERTEX_AI, DATABASE_URL, GCS_RAW_BUCKET/PYRAMIDS_BUCKET/ARTIFACTS_BUCKET, CDN_BASE_URL, STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST) and declares `env_file = ".env"` (config.py:67), but there is no `.env.example` anywhere in the repo (find for .env* under backend and root turns up nothing), and README.md never names a single one of these variables.

```
class Settings(BaseSettings):
    ENV: str = os.getenv("ENV", "dev")
    ...
    class Config:
        env_file = ".env"
        extra = "ignore"
```
**Impact:** A new developer has no discoverable list of what can/should be configured (e.g. USE_MOCK_VERTEX_AI to avoid needing live Vertex AI endpoints, or GCS bucket names) short of reading config.py source; they will hit hard-coded defaults pointing at a specific GCP project ('oncogemma') and specific Vertex endpoint IDs that are almost certainly not theirs.

**Fix:** Add a backend/.env.example enumerating every Settings field with a safe default/placeholder, and reference it from the README Quick Start.

*Verifier note:* Verified: `find . -name '.env*' -not -path './.git/*'` in the repo root returns nothing — there is no .env.example anywhere. .gitignore lines 40-45 ignore .env/.env.local/etc. but never whitelist an example. README.md's Quick Start (lines 177-215) names zero environment variables — the only 'env' hits in README.md are `python -m venv venv` / `source venv/bin/activate`. config.py really does read ~18 env vars (lines 5-64) and declares env_file='.env' at line 67, with defaults pointing at a concrete GCP project ('oncogemma', line 10) and concrete Vertex endpoint IDs (lines 17, 25). So the finding's facts all hold. Severity lowered medium->low: this is a pure documentation/onboarding gap with no functional break, and the full list is a single 70-line file away; the cited location (config.py:9) is a comment line, the Settings class starts at line 4.

#### 15. Dead/duplicated settings: USE_REAL_GCS, STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST, DEBUG, ENV vs ENVIRONMENT

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Improvement · **Location:** `backend/app/core/config.py:6`

ENV and ENVIRONMENT are two independent fields with the same meaning (only ENV is consumed, at worker/triage.py:282 and /healthz). DEBUG is never read. USE_REAL_GCS and STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST are never read (see GCS finding). Every field also duplicates pydantic-settings' own env loading with os.getenv defaults, and `class Config` is the deprecated pydantic-v1 style.

```
config.py:5-7  ENV: str = os.getenv("ENV", "dev")
    ENVIRONMENT: str = os.getenv("ENVIRONMENT", "dev")
    DEBUG: bool = True
config.py:12  USE_REAL_GCS: bool = os.getenv("USE_REAL_GCS", "true").lower() in ("true", "1")
config.py:66-68  class Config:
        env_file = ".env"
        extra = "ignore"
```
**Impact:** Operators set flags that do nothing (the documented way to run offline), and ENV/ENVIRONMENT can disagree.

**Fix:** Remove ENVIRONMENT/DEBUG, wire USE_REAL_GCS/STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST in gcs.py, drop the os.getenv wrappers, and use model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file='.env', extra='ignore').

*Verifier note:* Dead-field claims all hold on a repo-wide grep: ENVIRONMENT (config.py:6) has no reader anywhere; DEBUG (:7) has no reader; USE_REAL_GCS (:12) has no reader — gcs.py always builds a real storage.Client (gcs.py:12-20); STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST (:56) has no reader in the repo either. Only ENV is consumed (main.py:56 /healthz, worker/triage.py:282), so ENV and ENVIRONMENT can indeed disagree with no effect. `class Config` (:66-68) is the pydantic-v1 style, still honoured but deprecated in pydantic-settings 2.x (requirements.txt pins >=2.2.1), and the os.getenv wrappers do duplicate the settings loader. Two corrections that reduce severity: (a) STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST is read by google-cloud-storage itself from the environment, so an operator exporting it does reach ops/docker-compose.yml's fake-gcs-server even though gcs.py ignores the setting — the field is redundant rather than a broken switch; (b) nothing here causes a runtime failure, and there is no README/ops doc advertising USE_REAL_GCS as the offline path, so 'operators set flags that do nothing' is speculative. Cleanup, not medium — downgraded to low.

#### 544. Pydantic v2 class-based Config used in Settings and all schemas (deprecated, removed in v3) with unbounded pydantic pin

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Dependencies / environment · **Location:** `backend/app/core/config.py:66`

Settings uses 'class Config: env_file/extra', and schemas/audit.py:13, schemas/case.py:20 and :52 use 'class Config: from_attributes'. Pydantic 2.x emits PydanticDeprecatedSince20 warnings for these and pydantic 3 removes them; requirements.txt pins pydantic>=2.6.4 and pydantic-settings>=2.2.1 with no upper bound, so a fresh install after the v3 release will fail at import.

```
class Config:
    env_file = ".env"
    extra = "ignore"
```
**Impact:** Warning noise now; hard import failure once pydantic 3 resolves from the open pin.

**Fix:** Switch to model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file='.env', extra='ignore') and model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True); add an upper bound on pydantic.

*Verifier note:* All cited evidence checks out at the exact lines: config.py:66-68 `class Config: env_file/extra`; app/schemas/audit.py:13 and app/schemas/case.py:20 and :52 all use `class Config: from_attributes = True`; backend/requirements.txt pins `pydantic>=2.6.4` and `pydantic-settings>=2.2.1` with no upper bound. Class-based Config is deprecated in pydantic/pydantic-settings v2 and does emit PydanticDeprecatedSince20. The second half — 'a fresh install after the v3 release will fail at import' — is a forecast, not an observed failure, and pydantic-settings would carry its own pydantic bound; but the deprecated usage plus the unbounded pin are both real, and low is the right severity for warning noise plus future-upgrade risk.

#### 8. SQLite engine never enables foreign_keys, so FK/cascade bugs are invisible in tests and in the fallback DB

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Data integrity · **Location:** `backend/app/core/db.py:13`

Both SQLite create_engine calls omit a PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON connect listener. All API tests (test_api_auth.py:12-19 etc.) and the production fallback therefore run with FKs unenforced, which is why the missing cascades below never surface.

```
db.py:13-16  engine = create_engine(
        sqlite_url,
        connect_args={"check_same_thread": False, "timeout": 30}
    )
```
**Impact:** Orphan hotspots/detections/hpf_sites after case deletion on SQLite; Postgres raises IntegrityError for the same code path (see cascade finding).

**Fix:** @event.listens_for(engine, 'connect') def _fk(dbapi_conn, _): dbapi_conn.execute('PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON') for sqlite engines.

*Verifier note:* Core claim holds: neither SQLite create_engine call (db.py:13-16 and db.py:29-32) registers a connect listener issuing PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON, and SQLite defaults to FKs off. The downstream impact is real and I verified it: cases.py:80-92 delete_case does db.delete(case_obj); Case (models/case.py:21-24) declares delete-orphan cascades only for slides, stage_executions, grading and report, while Hotspot (models/hotspot.py:17), Detection (models/detection.py:18) and HpfSite (models/hpf_site.py:17) hold ForeignKey("cases.id") with no ondelete and no relationship on Case -> orphans on SQLite, IntegrityError on Postgres. clear_all_cases (cases.py:66-78) has the same shape. But the evidence sentence is misattributed: test_api_auth.py:12-19 does not get its engine from db.py, it constructs its own at line 13, so db.py:13 is not why tests run without FKs (those test engines independently omit the PRAGMA). Severity lowered medium -> low: db.py's SQLite engines are reached only via an explicit sqlite DATABASE_URL or the outage fallback, so this compounds finding 6 rather than standing alone; the cascade gap itself lives in the models/routers, not here.

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/app/core/db.py:14`

When DATABASE_URL starts with 'sqlite', the engine is created from the module-level `sqlite_url` (repo-root oncogemma_local.db) instead of `db_url`, so `DATABASE_URL=sqlite:///:memory:` or `sqlite:////tmp/ci.db` is silently replaced.

```

    engine = create_engine(
        sqlite_url,
```
