**Fix:** Use `db_url` in that branch (drop the `sqlite_url` constant).

*Verifier note:* Real bug as described: db.py:12 branches on `db_url.startswith("sqlite")` but db.py:14 passes the module-level `sqlite_url` (built at db.py:7-8 from the repo root) instead of `db_url`, so DATABASE_URL=sqlite:///:memory: or sqlite:////tmp/ci.db is silently rewritten to the shared repo file. Severity lowered medium -> low because the stated impact largely does not apply: no test uses db.py's engine. test_api_auth.py:13-18 builds its own in-memory engine with StaticPool and overrides get_db at line 32; test_triage_worker.py:16, test_mitosis_api.py:26, test_grading_api.py:24, test_cap_reporting.py:51 and test_triage_api.py:24 all do the same. Real victims are limited to backend/pipeline/diagnose_*.py, backend/tools/diagnostics.py, the API and the worker when someone points DATABASE_URL at an isolated sqlite file. The defect is at line 14 (wrong variable), not line 12.

#### 23. Dead GCS helpers with latent bugs: upload_directory_to_gcs_and_purge / delete_blob have no callers

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/app/core/gcs.py:110`

Neither function is referenced outside gcs.py. upload_directory_to_gcs_and_purge additionally references blob_path in the except before it is assigned (UnboundLocalError if relpath fails), guesses application/json for every non-image (e.g. .dzi XML), skips extension-less files (glob '*.*'), and rmtree()s the source even when uploads failed.

```
gcs.py:118-126  def _upload_one(local_file: str):
        try:
            rel_path = os.path.relpath(local_file, local_dir).replace("\\", "/")
            blob_path = f"{dest_prefix.strip('/')}/{rel_path}"
 ...
        except Exception as err:
            print(f"[GCS Directory Upload Warning] {local_file} -> {blob_path}: {err}")
```
**Impact:** Maintenance trap: a future caller would silently lose pyramid tiles.

**Fix:** Delete both functions (or fix: propagate failures, mimetypes.guess_type, glob '**/*').

*Verifier note:* Verified dead: `grep -rn 'upload_directory_to_gcs_and_purge\|delete_blob' OncoGemma-v5` returns hits only inside backend/app/core/gcs.py (87-92, 110-136). The only gcs.py symbols imported elsewhere are ensure_buckets_exist (main.py:14), generate_signed_upload_url/get_gcs_tile_template_url (cases.py:17-18), get_gcs_artifact_direct_url (triage/mitosis/grading), plus the low-level upload/download/parse helpers. The real pyramid upload uses a near-copy in worker/ingest.py:191 upload_dzi_tree_to_gcs, so upload_directory_to_gcs_and_purge is duplicated dead code. Sub-claims all hold: blob_path (line 121) is assigned inside the try yet referenced in the except at line 126, so a failure in os.path.relpath (e.g. Windows cross-drive ValueError) raises UnboundLocalError out of the worker; line 123 falls back to content_type='application/json' for anything not .png/.jpg (a .dzi is XML); glob at line 116 uses '**/*.*' so extension-less files are skipped; line 134 rmtree's local_dir unconditionally because _upload_one swallows every failure into a print. Severity low is right - it is unreachable today.

#### 29. Global OpenSlide lock serialises every tile/thumbnail/patch request in the API process

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Performance · **Location:** `backend/app/core/openslide_lock.py:5`

A single process-wide threading.Lock wraps slide open + region read in tiles.py:47, cases.py:402, triage.py:389, mitosis.py:289, grading.py:572. OpenSlide has been thread-safe per handle since 3.x, the lock only exists in one process (the worker's copy is a different object, so the stated cross-endpoint guarantee does not hold), and the tile fallback path downloads the whole WSI inside the request before taking the lock.

```
openslide_lock.py:3-5  # Unified global lock across all endpoints (tiles, thumbnails, patches)
# to guarantee 100% thread-safety for OpenSlide native C library on Windows.
OPENSLIDE_GLOBAL_LOCK = threading.Lock()
```
**Impact:** OpenSeadragon issues dozens of concurrent tile requests; they queue behind one lock, so the viewer's throughput collapses to one tile at a time per API instance.

**Fix:** Drop the global lock; keep a per-slide LRU of open OpenSlide handles (each handle is safe for concurrent read_region) and remove the per-tile full-slide download.

*Verifier note:* The artifact exists as quoted: openslide_lock.py:1-5 is exactly `import threading` + the two comment lines + `OPENSLIDE_GLOBAL_LOCK = threading.Lock()`. All five cited call sites are real and hold the lock across open+read: tiles.py:47 (inside generate_tile_on_the_fly, wrapping openslide.OpenSlide at :50 and read_region_srgb), cases.py:402-405 (thumbnail), triage.py:389-393, mitosis.py:289-293 (and a second site at :475), grading.py:572-573. API endpoints are sync `def` (tiles.py:201 get_tile, :217 get_tile_direct), so FastAPI runs them in the anyio threadpool and the lock really does serialise them within the one uvicorn process (backend/run_server.py starts a single-process uvicorn, no --workers). The two supporting sub-claims also hold: (a) the worker is a separate process, so worker/grading.py:76,210,259 and worker/mitosis.py:170,192,241,354,396 take a *different* Lock object — the module comment's 'unified across all endpoints' is only true inside the API process, and in the worker the lock is a pure no-op since worker/main.py:47-57 is a single-threaded sequential poll loop; (b) libopenslide has been thread-safe for concurrent read_region on the same handle since 3.x, so the stated Windows safety rationale does not justify a process-wide lock.

Severity downgraded medium -> low because the stated impact is overstated. stream_slide_tile serves the normal case from the pre-generated GCS pyramid at tiles.py:132-149 and returns before ever touching the lock; the lock is only reached in fallback step 2 (tiles.py:151-177). So an OpenSeadragon viewer against a slide with a built pyramid never contends on it — throughput does not 'collapse to one tile at a time' in the normal path. And on the fallback path the lock is not the dominant cost: download_blob_to_filename at tiles.py:163 pulls the entire WSI and sits OUTSIDE the lock (the finder states this correctly), so dozens of concurrent tile requests each download a full slide in parallel — removing the lock alone would change nothing measurable. The finder's own proposed fix names the real problem ('remove the per-tile full-slide download'); the lock is the smaller half of it. Thumbnail (cases.py:402) and patch (grading.py:572, mitosis.py:289) endpoints are low-frequency, so contention there is negligible.

#### 546. /healthz is a liveness stub that reports healthy even when the API silently fell back to SQLite or GCS is unreachable

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Improvement · **Location:** `backend/app/main.py:51`

health_check returns a constant dict. It does not touch the engine, so it cannot distinguish 'connected to Cloud SQL' from 'fell back to oncogemma_local.db' (db.py:27-32), and it does not check GCS or that a worker has polled recently. Cloud Run/compose health checks would keep routing traffic to an instance writing PHI to a local file.

```
return {
    "status": "healthy",
    "version": app.version,
    "env": settings.ENV
}
```
**Impact:** Misconfiguration in prod is invisible to orchestration.

**Fix:** Execute SELECT 1 on the engine and report engine.dialect.name; return 503 when the dialect is sqlite in non-dev ENV; optionally include last worker heartbeat.

*Verifier note:* Code matches exactly. main.py:51-57 is `@app.get("/healthz")` returning a constant dict {status, version, env}; it never touches `engine`, GCS, or any worker state. The silent degradation it fails to surface is real: db.py:17-32 wraps create_engine + `with engine.connect(): pass` in try/except and on ANY exception prints a warning and rebinds `engine` to `sqlite:///<repo>/oncogemma_local.db`, and gcs.py:142-149 wraps the bucket exists/create loop in `except Exception: pass` (the comment 'Bucket exists or already accessible' is wrong — it swallows auth, network and permission errors too). config.py:46-49 defaults DATABASE_URL to a Postgres URL, so a bad/unreachable DATABASE_URL in any env falls back silently. Grepped the backend: nothing HTTP-facing exposes engine.dialect.name or runs SELECT 1 — the only place that does is the standalone diagnostic script pipeline/diagnose_system.py:91, not the API. Kept at low/improvement, with two caveats on the framing: (a) the repo contains no orchestration that actually consumes /healthz — ops/docker-compose.yml defines only postgres and fake-gcs-server (no API service, no healthcheck on it) and there is no Cloud Run manifest, so 'orchestration keeps routing traffic' is prospective rather than an observed wiring; (b) the genuinely dangerous half of this is the silent fallback in db.py:27-32, which is a defect of db.py, not of the health endpoint. As scoped (endpoint is a liveness stub with no readiness probe) low is the right severity.

**Impact:** The weekly pilot review ritual (section 3) has no qualitative signal to complement the quantitative override views, since the feedback channel it depends on was never built.

**Fix:** Add a thumbs/comment widget to each stage viewer component (TriageViewer, MitosisViewer, GradingReviewWorkspace, ReportWorkspace) posting to a new audit endpoint with event_type='feedback'.

*Verifier note:* Factually correct. `grep -rhon 'event_type="..."'` across backend reproduces exactly the 18 event types listed (the finder said 17; the set includes stage_confirmed and stage_approved) and 'feedback' is absent. Frontend: components/viewer/ contains TriageViewer, MitosisViewer, MitosisGallery, GradingReviewWorkspace, ReportWorkspace, StageRail, OpenSeadragonViewer; the only case-insensitive 'thumb' hit is TriageViewer.tsx:517 `thumbSrc` (a hotspot thumbnail URL), so no widget exists. Downgrading to low for scope: the requirement lives in prd/07-stage-v4.6-validation.md:81 under '5. Pilot onboarding assets', and NONE of v4.6 is built — no v_override_rates/v_detection_toggles/v_score_overrides views, no cli/export_labels, no docs/pilot-runbook.md, no shadow-mode config, no RUO banner (all greps empty) — while the app ships as v4.5 (main.py:31). This is an unreached stage, not a defect in delivered code, and models/audit.py:1 is a proxy location: the model already stores arbitrary event_type/payload, so nothing there needs changing.

#### 26. Missing indexes/constraints vs PRD DDL: audit_events.case_id (text, unindexed), slides.case_id, stage_executions.case_id, hotspots.stage_execution_id; poll index not partial

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Performance · **Location:** `backend/app/models/audit.py:15`

audit_events.case_id is String (PRD §5.3: uuid) with no index, yet the audit endpoint filters and counts on it per page. slides.case_id and stage_executions.case_id are looked up on nearly every request and have no index; hotspots.stage_execution_id is an FK with no index. ix_stage_poll is a full (status, stage) index where the PRD specifies `WHERE status='queued'`.

```
audit.py:15  case_id: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String, nullable=True) # UUID string
slide.py:13  case_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(GUID, ForeignKey("cases.id"), nullable=False)
stage_execution.py:40  Index("ix_stage_poll", "status", "stage"),
```
**Impact:** Sequential scans on audit_events (append-only, grows forever) and stage_executions for every case page; on PG a uuid=text join needs casts.

**Fix:** Make audit_events.case_id GUID + index; add index=True to slides.case_id, stage_executions.case_id, hotspots.stage_execution_id; use Index(..., postgresql_where=text("status='queued'")).

*Verifier note:* Core claims hold. audit.py:15 `case_id: Mapped[str|None] = mapped_column(String, nullable=True)` — text, not uuid (PRD 00-overview.md:122 `case_id uuid`), and no index anywhere: models/audit.py has no __table_args__, no Index(...) exists outside stage_execution.py:40 (grep 'Index(' returns exactly one hit), and there is no migrations/alembic dir and no .sql file — schema comes solely from Base.metadata.create_all (main.py:23), so nothing adds indexes out of band. routers/audit.py:28-31 filters `AuditEvent.case_id == str(case_id)` plus a COUNT over the same subquery on every page = two seq scans on an append-only table. slide.py:13 case_id is FK-only (PG does not auto-index FKs) — confirmed unindexed. hotspot.py stage_execution_id is FK-only (case_id does have index=True) — confirmed unindexed. stage_execution.py:40 ix_stage_poll is indeed non-partial vs PRD 00-overview.md:110 `WHERE status='queued'`. Two sub-claims are wrong and pull severity down: (a) stage_executions.case_id is NOT unindexed — UniqueConstraint('case_id','stage','attempt') at stage_execution.py:39 is implemented in PG as a unique btree whose leading column is case_id, so per-case lookups are already served; (b) 'on PG a uuid=text join needs casts' — no such join exists; the router compares text to a stringified uuid, and no query joins audit_events to cases. Combined with pilot scale (PRD acceptance target is ~30 archive cases) the performance impact is negligible today; this is really a schema-hygiene/PRD-conformance nit, so low rather than medium.

#### 25. GUID type returns str while columns are annotated Mapped[uuid.UUID]; routers compensate with ad-hoc to_uuid helpers

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Improvement · **Location:** `backend/app/models/base.py:24`

process_result_value always str()s the value, so Case.id/Slide.case_id are strings at runtime on both dialects despite the uuid.UUID annotations, and the ORM identity key differs from the uuid passed to db.get (extra SELECT, never a cache hit). Routers therefore carry to_uuid() shims (triage.py:37-43) and mix `case_id: str` and `case_id: uuid.UUID` signatures.

```
base.py:24-27  def process_result_value(self, value, dialect):
        if value is None:
            return value
        return str(value)
```
**Impact:** Type confusion across routers/tests; comparisons like Slide.case_id == case_uid rely on dialect coercion.

**Fix:** Use SQLAlchemy 2's built-in sqlalchemy.Uuid(as_uuid=True) (native on PG, CHAR(32) elsewhere) and delete the GUID class and to_uuid shims.

*Verifier note:* Evidence is exact. base.py:24-27 is `def process_result_value(self, value, dialect): if value is None: return value; return str(value)` verbatim, and load_dialect_impl (13-17) yields PG_UUID(as_uuid=True) on Postgres / CHAR(36) elsewhere — so on BOTH dialects the loaded attribute is a str, despite Mapped[uuid.UUID] on case.py:12, slide.py:12-13, stage_execution.py:15-16. The compensation the finder describes is real and present four times: identical `def to_uuid(val) -> uuid.UUID` shims at triage.py:37-43, grading.py:110, mitosis.py:41, report.py:106 (each silently returning the original value on parse failure), and the runtime type split is visible in the router signatures — cases.py/tiles.py/audit.py take `case_id: uuid.UUID` while triage.py:97/160/268, grading.py:120/346/519 and report.py:330/486 take `case_id: str`. The identity-map claim also holds: the identity key is built from the processed (str) PK, so `db.get(Case, <uuid.UUID>)` can never hit the map — and the code visibly knows it, e.g. triage.py:297 and mitosis.py:83 both read `db.scalars(select(Case).where(Case.id == case_uid)).first() if isinstance(case_uid, uuid.UUID) else db.get(Case, case_id)`, a branch that exists only because the runtime type is unpredictable. Severity stays low / improvement, not raised: no incorrect result is produced, because process_bind_param (19-22) str()s the bind value too, so `Slide.case_id == case_uid` matches whether the RHS is a UUID or its string form on either dialect. It is type-hygiene and a lost identity-map cache, not a defect. Note for whoever takes the fix: switching to sqlalchemy.Uuid(as_uuid=True) flips every one of these attributes from str to uuid.UUID at once, so it is a cross-router/test change, not a drop-in edit of base.py.

#### 11. Nottingham grade thresholds hard-coded in a DB CHECK constraint; NULL semantics force grade=3

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Clinical correctness · **Location:** `backend/app/models/grading.py:45`

The CHECK duplicates the 5/7 cut-offs that configs/scoring.yaml:21-22 (grade1_max_sum/grade2_max_sum) and pipeline/grading.py:187 also define — PRD §5.5 says 'No clinical numbers in code'. It also ignores nottingham_sum, and because a NULL sub-score makes the CASE fall to ELSE 3, any row with grade set and one sub-score NULL is rejected unless grade == 3.

```
grading.py:45-48  CheckConstraint(
            "grade = CASE WHEN tubule_score + pleo_score + mitotic_score <= 5 THEN 1 "
            "WHEN tubule_score + pleo_score + mitotic_score <= 7 THEN 2 "
            "ELSE 3 END",
```
**Impact:** Changing the YAML thresholds makes every grading INSERT fail with IntegrityError (HTTP 500); partial-score rows (e.g. mitotic_score NULL before the mitosis stage) can only be stored as grade 3.

**Fix:** Drop the constraint (validate_grading_invariants already enforces it in code from config) or make it NULL-safe and include nottingham_sum = t+p+m.

*Verifier note:* Evidence is real: grading.py:44-51 emits CheckConstraint("grade = CASE WHEN tubule_score+pleo_score+mitotic_score <= 5 THEN 1 WHEN ... <= 7 THEN 2 ELSE 3 END", name="check_nottingham_grade_calc"), and it is actually applied to the live schema (no alembic in the repo; backend/app/main.py:23 does Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine); tests do the same). The 5/7 duplication of configs/scoring.yaml:20-22 (grade1_max_sum/grade2_max_sum) does violate PRD 00-overview.md:149-150 ("No clinical numbers in code"). The NULL analysis is also correct SQL semantics: with a NULL sub-score both WHEN predicates are UNKNOWN so the CASE yields ELSE 3, and `grade = 3` is then a real comparison that rejects any row with grade 1 or 2 (grade NULL still passes, since NULL = 3 is UNKNOWN). Severity lowered from medium to low for two reasons. (1) The partial-score failure is unreachable today: every writer sets all four fields in one flush - backend/worker/grading.py:415-436 and backend/app/routers/grading.py:740-746 are the only non-test writers, and grep for `.grade = ` / `.tubule_score = ` etc. finds nothing else. It is a latent hazard from the columns being nullable, not a live bug. (2) The stated impact chain is wrong about which layer fails first: backend/pipeline/grading.py:186 hard-codes the same cut-offs (`expected_grade = 1 if expected_sum <= 5 else (2 if expected_sum <= 7 else 3)`) and is called at pipeline/grading.py:299 and routers/grading.py:649/731 before any DB write, so tuning scoring.yaml raises ValueError from validate_grading_invariants (HTTP 400 on /confirm, ValueError in the worker) long before an IntegrityError. That also refutes the proposed fix's premise - validate_grading_invariants does NOT read the config, so dropping the constraint alone leaves a second hard-coded copy of the same constant.

#### 704. stage_executions.stage and .status accept arbitrary strings, so a typo creates a permanently unpollable row

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Data integrity · **Location:** `backend/app/models/stage_execution.py:18`

Both columns are plain String with the legal values written only in a comment; there is no CHECK constraint, Enum type, or application-level validation. POST /cases/{id}/stages/{stage_name}/retry takes stage_name straight from the URL path with no whitelist (backend/app/routers/cases.py:191-197) and inserts it. The worker only polls stages in HANDLERS (backend/worker/main.py:58), so the row is never picked up and never fails.

```
stage: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String, nullable=False) # ingest|preprocess|qc|triage|mitosis|grading|report
    attempt: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer, nullable=False, default=1)
    status: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String, nullable=False, default="queued")
```
**Impact:** A single mistyped retry ('mitoses', 'Triage') returns HTTP 202 and creates a queued row that never runs and never errors; the case detail view shows a stage stuck at 'queued' forever with no way to diagnose it. Same for any code path that writes an unexpected status.

**Fix:** Add a CHECK constraint (or SQLAlchemy Enum) for both columns -- this is the root cause that also fixes the retry endpoint accepting arbitrary stage names.

*Verifier note:* Mechanism verified end to end. Line 18 `stage` and line 20 `status` are plain `String` with legal values only in trailing comments; __table_args__ (lines 38-41) has no CHECK, and there is no SQLAlchemy Enum or validator. cases.py:167 declares POST /{case_id}/stages/{stage_name}/retry with status_code=202 and `stage_name: str` as a bare path param (line 170); lines 183-197 use it only to find the prior attempt and then insert `stage=stage_name` with status='queued' -- no membership test against any handler list. The worker's poll query filters `StageExecution.stage.in_(list(HANDLERS.keys()))` (main.py:52-57), so a row with 'mitoses' or 'Triage' is provably never selected, never transitions out of 'queued', and never records an error. cases.py:438 then renders it in the case detail response. Severity lowered medium->low: the only user-controlled stage string in the codebase is this one path param (every other enqueue -- cases.py:139/278/348, triage.py:565, mitosis.py:666, grading.py:773, worker/ingest.py:325, worker/preprocess.py:244 -- passes a hardcoded literal), the caller is an authenticated user, nothing gates case progression on the count of queued rows, and the blast radius is one cosmetic phantom row in one case's detail view with no data corruption and no way to affect a real stage. The status-column half of the claim is currently unreachable: no code path writes an unlisted status value.

#### 24. AuditEventResponse lacks the UTC serializer that CaseResponse has — naive timestamps leak on SQLite

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/app/schemas/audit.py:11`

case.py:14-18 and 46-50 normalise naive datetimes to UTC ISO strings because SQLite's DateTime(timezone=True) returns naive values. audit.py copies the model without that serializer, so /cases/{id}/audit emits '2026-09-03T10:00:00' with no offset on the SQLite fallback/test DB while other endpoints emit '+00:00'.

```
schemas/audit.py:11  created_at: datetime
schemas/case.py:14-18  @field_serializer("created_at")
    def serialize_created_at(self, dt: datetime, _info) -> str:
        if dt.tzinfo is None:
            dt = dt.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
```
**Impact:** Browsers parse offset-less ISO strings as local time, shifting audit timestamps by the user's UTC offset.

**Fix:** Move the serializer to a shared base schema (or a TZDateTime TypeDecorator in models/base.py) used by every response model.

*Verifier note:* Structural claim holds exactly as cited. audit.py:11 declares `created_at: datetime` with no serializer (the module imports only `datetime`, not `timezone`), while case.py:14-18 and 46-50 contain the quoted UTC-normalising `field_serializer` verbatim; case.py is the ONLY file in app/schemas/ with a field_serializer. models/audit.py uses DateTime(timezone=True) just like models/case.py, and SQLAlchemy's SQLite dialect drops the offset on store and returns naive datetimes, so /cases/{id}/audit (routers/audit.py:14, 33-38) really does emit '...T10:00:00' while /cases emits '...+00:00' on the same DB. SQLite is reachable: core/db.py:12-16 for an explicit sqlite:// URL and 27-32 as a silent fallback when the Postgres connect at line 25 raises. Severity lowered from medium to low because the claimed impact does not occur: frontend/lib/utils.ts:5-8 (formatISTDateTime, the only consumer of any created_at in the UI) explicitly appends 'Z' when no offset is present, and a grep for '/audit' across frontend/ excluding node_modules finds no caller of this endpoint at all. So nothing currently shifts by the user's UTC offset — what remains is a genuine but latent API-contract inconsistency for a future or third-party consumer. Proposed fix (shared base schema, or better a TZDateTime TypeDecorator alongside the existing GUID decorator in models/base.py) is the right root-cause shape, since every other datetime-bearing response model would otherwise need its own copy.

#### 136. Worker fabricates 24 hotspots at fixed slide coordinates when no confirmed hotspots exist

**Severity:** critical · **Category:** Clinical correctness · **Location:** `backend/worker/grading.py:178`

If the case has no non-excluded Hotspot rows (e.g. pathologist excluded all, or triage never ran), run_grading synthesises 24 HotspotItems at (5000+i*1500, 5000+i*1500) px with tumor_probability 0.95-i*0.02, extracts patches from those arbitrary locations, sends them to MedGemma and persists a full grading. Same pattern at line 170: a hotspot with empty polygon_um is centred at (5000,5000) um.

```
if not hotspots:
            hotspots = [
                HotspotItem(f"hs_{i+1:02d}", 5000 + i * 1500, 5000 + i * 1500, 0.95 - i * 0.02)
                for i in range(24)
            ]
```
**Impact:** A Nottingham grade is computed from tissue that was never triaged as tumour (possibly glass/background) and shown as evidence with fake 0.95 tumour probabilities. PRD 05 section 2 requires sampling from confirmed hotspots only.

**Fix:** Raise ValueError('no confirmed hotspots') so the stage lands in failed/needs_human; never invent coordinates or probabilities.

*Verifier note:* Confirmed verbatim at worker/grading.py:178-182: when every Hotspot row is excluded or none exist, 24 HotspotItems are synthesised at (5000+i*1500, 5000+i*1500) px with tumor_probability 0.95-i*0.02, and those go straight into sample_stratified_patches (line 202), extract_10x_patch (line 220) and the MedGemma calls; the fabricated probability is even persisted into the evidence panel as `tumor_probability` (line 254). Line 170 confirms the second half: `poly = np.array(h.polygon_um) if h.polygon_um else np.array([[5000, 5000]])`, centring an empty-polygon hotspot at 5000/5000 um. Reachability checked: app/routers/triage.py:500-530 has no zero-hotspot guard - the GCS load is wrapped in a bare except that just prints (lines 507-508), so a failed artifact read yields machine_hotspots=[] and zero persisted Hotspot rows, and excluding every polygon without ticking no_invasive_tumor confirms the same way and still queues mitosis -> grading. Coordinates are level-0 pixels up to 39500 (~10 mm at 0.25 mpp); OpenSlide read_region past the bounds returns blank tissue rather than raising, so the stage completes and lands in awaiting_review (line 458) with a full Nottingham grade over glass. PRD 05 section 2 requires sampling 'From confirmed hotspots'. Critical stands.

#### 635. Pyramid is only pre-generated to DZI level 11, so every tile at diagnostic zoom is a guaranteed miss that triggers a full-WSI download

**Severity:** critical · **Category:** Performance · **Location:** `backend/worker/ingest.py:105`

Ingest (and preprocess for the 'norm' layer) writes DZI levels 0..11 only, but the tile router and the OpenSeadragon viewer serve/request levels up to max_level = ceil(log2(max_dim)) (17 for a 100k px slide) and cap 'norm' at max_level-2 (tiles.py:119-124, OpenSeadragonViewer.tsx:254-265). Level 11 is a ~2048 px overview, i.e. roughly 1x magnification; every tile the pathologist looks at above that (levels 12..17, the 5x-40x range where mitoses are counted) does not exist in GCS, so stream_slide_tile falls into step 2 and downloads the entire raw WSI into a fresh tempdir for each 256 px tile, under OPENSLIDE_GLOBAL_LOCK. The already-recorded 'missing tile downloads whole WSI' finding treats misses as exceptional; this shows they are the norm for the whole diagnostic zoom range by construction.

```
worker/ingest.py:105  max_pregen_level = min(12, dz.level_count)
worker/preprocess.py:46  max_norm_pregen_level = min(12, dz.level_count)
app/routers/tiles.py:123  if layer == "norm" and z > cap_10x_level:
app/routers/tiles.py:163  download_blob_to_filename(raw_bucket_name, blob_name, local_slide_path)
```
**Impact:** Viewer is unusable above overview zoom on any real slide: an OSD viewport of ~40 tiles at 20x means 40 sequential multi-GB downloads (serialized by the global lock), each deleted immediately after (shutil.rmtree at tiles.py:178) so nothing is reused. Cloud Run request timeouts (default 300 s) will kill most of them.

**Fix:** Generate the full DZI tree at ingest (PRD 01 §2.3 step 5: pyvips dzsave of all levels) and the full norm tree at preprocess, or at minimum cache the downloaded raw slide per slide_id (keyed tempdir + LRU) and serve on-the-fly tiles from that instead of re-downloading per tile. Validate 0 <= z <= max_level in the router before any GCS access.

*Verifier note:* Every cited line checked and exact. ingest.py:105 max_pregen_level = min(12, dz.level_count) with the loop at 106 being range(0, max_pregen_level), so DZI levels 0..11 only; preprocess.py:46 is identical for the norm layer. tiles.py:119 slide_max_level = ceil(log2(max_dim)) and :120 cap_10x_level = slide_max_level - 2, :123 the norm->orig demotion; frontend/components/viewer/OpenSeadragonViewer.tsx:253-254 maxLevel = Math.ceil(Math.log2(maxDim)) and :265 the same maxLevel-2 rule, with getTileUrl emitting z up to maxLevel. For a 100k px slide dz.level_count == 18 and the router/viewer max_level == 17, so levels 12..17 are requested and were never written. The upload key at ingest.py:208 ({slide_id}/orig/{z}/{c}_{r}) matches the router's lookup at tiles.py:135, so this is a genuine miss and not a naming mismatch - step 1 falls through to step 2 at tiles.py:151-168, which mkdtemps, downloads the entire raw WSI at :163, renders one 256px tile under OPENSLIDE_GLOBAL_LOCK (generate_tile_on_the_fly:46), and rmtrees the whole tempdir at :178 with no caching or reuse anywhere. There is also no z bounds validation before the GCS access. This is not a duplicate of 559: 559 is about non-pyramidal inputs inside the generator, this is about the pregen ceiling. Critical stands - it makes the diagnostic zoom range structurally uncached for every slide, not just pathological ones. PRD 01 section 2.3 step 5 does require a full pyvips dzsave tree, confirming the intent.

**Severity:** critical · **Category:** Data integrity · **Location:** `backend/worker/ingest.py:176`

#### 38. Missing MPP is silently replaced with 0.25 um/px (PRD: never guess MPP)

**Severity:** critical · **Category:** Clinical correctness · **Location:** `backend/worker/ingest.py:266`

When OpenSlide reports no openslide.mpp-x/y (common for generic TIFFs, some NDPI/MRXS exports, and every file that falls into the Pillow fallback) the ingest handler stores 0.25 as the slide MPP and proceeds. Every downstream micrometre computation (tissue mask, HPF area, mitoses/mm2, hotspot polygons) uses slide_obj.mpp_x, so a 0.5 um/px 20x scan is treated as 40x.

```
slide_obj.mpp_x = meta.get("mpp_x") or 0.25
slide_obj.mpp_y = meta.get("mpp_y") or 0.25
slide_obj.base_mag = meta.get("base_mag") or 40.0
slide_obj.width_px = meta.get("width_px") or 1024
```
**Impact:** Wrong clinical result: mitotic density (mitoses/mm2, the locked PRD scoring input) would be off by 4x for a 20x scan, silently changing the mitotic score and Nottingham grade. Violates 01-stage-v4.0 §2.3 step 4 ('If MPP missing ... mark slide status=needs_mpp ... never guess MPP').

**Fix:** If mpp_x/mpp_y are None, leave them NULL, set a needs_mpp state on the slide/case, and make preprocess/qc/triage refuse to run until a pathologist enters MPP; remove all `or 0.25` fallbacks in the workers/routers.

*Verifier note:* Verified at ingest.py:266-267 `slide_obj.mpp_x = meta.get("mpp_x") or 0.25` (same for mpp_y). extract_openslide_metadata leaves mpp None whenever openslide.mpp-x/y is absent (lines 56-61) and always leaves it None on the Pillow fallback path (lines 74-83), so the 0.25 substitution is reachable for generic TIFFs and any file OpenSlide cannot open. PRD 01-stage-v4.0 section 2.3 step 4 states verbatim that a missing MPP must set slide status=needs_mpp and 'never guess MPP'; grep shows no needs_mpp state anywhere in backend/ or frontend/. The value is then persisted and re-read by the um->px math (pipeline/tiles.py:142+ extract_patch_from_pyramid, routers/mitosis.py:258-268, routers/triage.py:358), so field area and mitotic density scale with the guess. Critical stands.

*Also reported at:* `backend/worker/ingest.py:266` (Missing MPP is silently guessed as 0.25 instead of blocking the slide); `backend/worker/ingest.py:266` (Ingest fabricates mpp (0.25) and dimensions (1024) when slide metadata is missing, corrupting every micrometre/mm2 computation downstream); `backend/worker/mitosis.py:83` (Missing slide MPP silently defaults to 0.25 um/px, corrupting every um coordinate and HPF size on 20x scans); `frontend/app/cases/[id]/page.tsx:336` (Fabricated MPP (0.25) and dimensions (2048 px) fed to viewers when slide metadata is missing — PRD 'never guess MPP')

#### 580. Worker fabricates a 2x2 mm hotspot at slide centre when the pathologist excluded every hotspot (or triage was never confirmed)

**Severity:** critical · **Category:** Clinical correctness · **Location:** `backend/worker/mitosis.py:127`

If no non-excluded Hotspot rows exist, run_mitosis first silently falls back to the unreviewed triage output.json (bypassing the pathologist's confirmed hotspot set), and if that also yields nothing it invents a default 2000x2000 um box around the slide centre with prob_mean 0.85 / source 'model' and sweeps it for mitoses. Width/height default to 20000 px if the slide row lacks dimensions, so the box may not even be on tissue. Detections are persisted with hotspot_id 'hs_01' that has no Hotspot row.

```
if not hotspots:
    center_x_um = (width_px * mpp_x) / 2.0
    ...
    hotspots.append({"id": "hs_01", "polygon_um": default_poly, "area_mm2": 4.0, "prob_mean": 0.85, "prob_max": 0.95, "source": "model"})
```
**Impact:** A benign slide, or one where the pathologist deliberately excluded all hotspots, still produces a mitotic count and Nottingham mitotic score from an arbitrary region; the invented hotspot is indistinguishable from a model-proposed one downstream (detections carry hotspot_id 'hs_01').

**Fix:** Raise ValueError('no confirmed hotspots') (stage fails visibly) or set the stage to awaiting_review with zero candidates and n_hpf=0; never fall back to unconfirmed triage output or a synthetic polygon. Remove lines 127-153.

Lines 104-109 select only non-excluded Hotspot rows; if that is empty, lines 127-133 fall back to the raw triage artifact cases/{case_id}/triage/output.json filtering on h.get('excluded', False). But exclusions are never written into that artifact — per PRD 00-overview 5.2 'machine output is never mutated'; routers/triage.py:84-86 applies the 'exclude' op only in memory via apply_edit_ops, and the excluded flag is persisted solely to the DB Hotspot row (triage.py:527) and to stage_exec.review_edits. So the fallback silently resurrects precisely the hotspots the pathologist excluded, with the same ids, and sweeps them. Second half also confirmed: lines 136-153 synthesize a hotspot with r_box=1000.0 um, i.e. a 2000x2000 um / 4 mm^2 box (area_mm2=4.0 matches; the inline comment '# 1 mm box' is wrong), stamped prob_mean 0.85 / prob_max 0.95 / source 'model' so it is indistinguishable from a model proposal downstream; centre derives from width_px/height_px whose defaults are 20000 at lines 85-86 when the Slide row lacks dimensions. Detections carry hotspot_id 'hs_01' (line 419) and Detection.hotspot_id is a plain nullable String with no FK (app/models/detection.py), so the dangling reference raises nothing. Upgrading high -> critical: this path produces a full Nottingham mitotic score (lines 402-409) from a region the pathologist explicitly rejected, or from an arbitrary slide-centre box that may be off-tissue, with no signal to the reviewer that either happened.

#### 102. Detector weights never loaded: config weights_path ignored, heuristic OD-threshold sweep is recorded as 'midog22_yolov8x_sweep@v1.0'

**Severity:** critical · **Category:** Clinical correctness · **Location:** `backend/worker/mitosis.py:156`

run_mitosis constructs the detector and verifier without ever passing the configured weights paths (configs/mitosis.yaml detector.weights_path / verifier.weights_path are read by nobody). YoloMitosisDetector therefore always has self.model=None and every tile goes through _detect_hyperchromatic_features, a hand-tuned optical-density contour heuristic (detect.py:71-136). The same is true for HoVerNetMitosisVerifier (verify.py:66-67). Yet model_version is hard-coded to a MIDOG YOLOv8x string (detect.py:31) and 'hovernet_fast_mitosis@v1.2' (verify.py:34) and persisted to stage_executions.model_versions and output.json (worker/mitosis.py:443-455). models/detector/ contains only EVAL.md — no weights exist anywhere in the repo. The PRD (prd/04-stage-v4.3-mitosis.md §2, §9) requires published MIDOG weights with a documented F1 >= 0.70 floor; 'below floor -> escalate, don't ship silently'.

```
detector = YoloMitosisDetector(conf_threshold=det_thresh)
verifier = HoVerNetMitosisVerifier(threshold=ver_thresh)
# detect.py:31  self.model_version = "midog22_yolov8x_sweep@v1.0"
# detect.py:67-69  # Algorithmic optical density ... fallback
#   return self._detect_hyperchromatic_features(tile_rgb)
```
**Impact:** Every production case is 'detected' by an unvalidated dark-blob heuristic while the audit trail, output.json and UI attribute the result to a validated MIDOG model. Mitotic counts and the resulting Nottingham score are clinically meaningless, and the provenance record is false.

**Fix:** Pass det_cfg['weights_path'] / ver_cfg['weights_path'] (resolved against repo root) into the constructors; if the file is missing, fail the stage (raise) instead of falling back, and set model_version to the actual engine (e.g. 'od_heuristic@dev') so the record is truthful. Gate the fallback behind mock.use_mock_detector and ENV != prod.

*Verifier note:* Verified line-by-line. mitosis.py:156-157 construct YoloMitosisDetector(conf_threshold=...) and HoVerNetMitosisVerifier(threshold=...) with no weights_path argument; both constructors default weights_path=None (detect.py:26, verify.py:29) and only load a model when `weights_path and os.path.exists(weights_path)` (detect.py:33, verify.py:36), so self.model stays None. `grep -rn weights_path backend/ configs/` returns only the two constructor bodies and configs/mitosis.yaml:5,20 — nothing in the repo reads those config keys (worker reads det_cfg/ver_cfg only for tile_size_px, stride_px, det_threshold, review_threshold, nms_radius_um, ver_threshold, crop_size_px at lines 93-99). Therefore detect() always falls through to _detect_hyperchromatic_features (detect.py:69,71-136) and verify() to _morphometric_nuclear_analysis (verify.py:67). model_version is hard-coded at detect.py:31 ('midog22_yolov8x_sweep@v1.0') and verify.py:34 ('hovernet_fast_mitosis@v1.2') and is persisted to stage_executions.model_versions and output.json at mitosis.py:443-446, 455, 469. `find models -type f` returns only models/detector/EVAL.md, models/probe/probe_v1.json, models/probe/probe_v1.joblib — no .pt weights exist. Worse than the finder states: models/detector/EVAL.md contains a fabricated MIDOG++ results table (YOLOv8x P=0.724/R=0.892/F1=0.799, HoVer-Net F1=0.832) asserting the pipeline 'comfortably exceeds' the F1>=0.70 floor that prd/04-stage-v4.3-mitosis.md:117 requires, for models that do not exist. configs/mitosis.yaml:41 has mock.use_mock_detector: false, which is also read by nobody. Critical stands: false provenance on a clinical number.

*Also reported at:* `backend/worker/mitosis.py:156` (Mitosis detection never loads a trained model — production always runs the pixel-heuristic fallback)

#### 103. Synthetic tissue tiles/crops are generated and fed to the detector when OpenSlide fails, producing fake detections persisted as real model output

**Severity:** critical · **Category:** Data integrity · **Location:** `backend/worker/mitosis.py:198`

If the WSI download or OpenSlide open fails (any exception at 167-174 is only printed), openslide_slide stays None and every tile is replaced by a procedurally generated pink image with 15 random dark squares (198-205). The detector then finds those squares, they are NMS'd, 'verified' on a synthetic 128x128 crop (247-252), uploaded as crop PNGs, written to the detections table with label_source='model', scored, and the stage transitions to awaiting_review exactly like a real run. The same happens for the 10 HPF patches (361-364, generate_synthetic_microscopic_patch). Nothing in output.json, the DB, or the audit event marks the run as synthetic.

```
if tile_rgb is None:
    # Generate realistic synthetic high-power H&E tile for dev/mock environments
    np.random.seed(int(abs(tx_um * 17 + ty_um * 31)) % 10000)
    tile_rgb = np.full((tile_size_px, tile_size_px, 3), (235, 215, 230), dtype=np.uint8)
```
**Impact:** A transient GCS/OpenSlide error (network blip, missing blob, unsupported format) silently yields a fabricated mitotic count and score for a real patient that the pathologist is then asked to 'review'. Data-integrity failure with no signal to the user.

**Fix:** Raise when the slide cannot be opened (the worker loop already marks the stage failed with the traceback). Move the synthetic generators behind an explicit settings.USE_MOCK_SLIDES flag that is refused when ENV=='prod', and stamp output_payload['synthetic']=True whenever it is used. Also stop mutating the global numpy RNG (np.random.seed) — use np.random.default_rng(seed).

*Verifier note:* Confirmed and distinct from 102 (that one is a fake model, this one is fake pixels). mitosis.py:165-174: any exception from download_blob_to_filename or openslide.OpenSlide is only printed, leaving openslide_slide=None; there is no re-raise and no status flag. Lines 198-205 then synthesise a (235,215,230) tile with fifteen 16x16 blocks of (60,20,90). I checked these actually detect: h_od for the block = -ln(60/255) - 0.15*(-ln(20/255)) - 0.15*(-ln(90/255)) = 0.909 > detect.py's chromatin_thresh 0.85, and block area 256 px sits inside the 200-3500 px window (detect.py:99), so every synthetic tile yields exactly 15 contours, top 6 returned (detect.py:120). These flow through apply_global_nms (226), the synthetic 128x128 crop at 247-252, verifier.verify (255), crop upload (283-294), Detection rows with label_source='model' (415-428), scoring (402-409), and stage_exec.status='awaiting_review' (467) — identical to a real run. Same for HPF patches at 361-364 via generate_synthetic_microscopic_patch (stain.py:337). output_payload (448-456) and the AuditEvent (472-482) carry no synthetic marker. Note the trigger is broader than the finder says: even with the slide open, a per-tile read_region failure (195-196) or per-crop failure (244-245) silently substitutes synthetic data for that tile/crop. The np.random.seed(...) at line 200 mutating global RNG state is also real.

#### 464. Every mitosis worker run wipes all prior Detection rows, destroying pathologist review edits that are the product's training-data moat

**Severity:** critical · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/worker/mitosis.py:412`

PRD section 7 states explicitly: 'Every label toggle → audit_events(...). These toggles are the future training set — they are the product's moat; never lose one.' `run_mitosis` unconditionally deletes every existing Detection and HpfSite row for the case before inserting freshly-generated candidates (all reset to label='unreviewed'), with no check for whether prior pathologist-confirmed labels exist.

```
# worker/mitosis.py:412-413
        db.execute(delete(Detection).where(Detection.case_id == case_obj.id))
        db.execute(delete(HpfSite).where(HpfSite.case_id == case_obj.id))
```
**Impact:** Per the shared state machine (00-overview 5.2), 'awaiting_review -> rejected -> (stage re-queued with edits applied)' means the mitosis stage can legitimately re-run after a pathologist has already toggled dozens of labels. On any re-run (rejection re-queue, retry after failure, or manual re-trigger), all of those human labels — the exact data the PRD calls the moat — are permanently deleted and replaced with fresh model-only 'unreviewed' detections, with no migration/merge of prior labels by spatial proximity or id.

Nothing in the file inspects existing rows first — there is no select(Detection) anywhere in worker/mitosis.py. The re-run path is real and reachable, not hypothetical: app/routers/cases.py:174-214 is a retry endpoint that creates a new StageExecution(stage=<name>, attempt=n+1, status='queued'), and worker/main.py:28 dispatches 'mitosis' to run_mitosis. What gets destroyed is exactly what PRD 04 section 7 calls the moat: rows where routers/mitosis.py:373 set label_source='pathologist', :555 set 'pathologist_bulk', and :508 created pathologist_added detections (those have no machine counterpart at all, so they cannot even be regenerated). Partial mitigation the finder did not mention: routers/mitosis.py:376-390 writes an AuditEvent(event_type='review_edit', payload={detection_id, from, to}) per toggle, so labels are in principle reconstructable from the audit trail — but only for toggles sent with audit_toggle, and nothing in the codebase ever replays them. Critical stands.

#### 72. Vertex AI client never sends real patches; 16 dummy calls are replicated with noise, any error silently returns random embeddings

**Severity:** critical · **Category:** Clinical correctness · **Location:** `backend/worker/triage.py:80`

`predict_embeddings` builds a single flat grey 224x224 PNG and sends it `chunk_len` times (lines 80-95); no slide pixels ever reach the endpoint. run_triage then calls it for at most 16 'patches' (line 275-276), takes `sample_embs[0]` and repeats it for every grid cell plus Gaussian noise (277-280). On any exception (auth, quota, wrong endpoint host) the client prints a note and returns `RandomState(42).randn` (118-121), so the stage always 'succeeds'. `api_endpoint` (the dedicated `*.prediction.vertexai.goog` host from config) is stored but never passed to `aiplatform.init`, so a dedicated endpoint will fail and hit the random fallback. No retry/backoff/concurrency despite `configs/triage.yaml` vertex_ai section and PRD 03 §2.2.

```
dummy_png = Image.new("RGB", (224, 224), color=(200, 200, 200))
...
base_emb = sample_embs[0]
embeddings = np.repeat(base_emb[np.newaxis, :], patch_count, axis=0) + noise
...
except Exception as e:
    print(f"[Vertex AI Path Foundation Note] Offline / Endpoint error ({e}). Falling back to deterministic embeddings.")
    return rng.randn(patch_count, 384).astype(np.float32)
```
**Impact:** Model invocation is fake; audit `model_invocation` events and cost estimates describe calls that carry no clinical content. Silent fallback means production cannot distinguish a real run from an offline one.

**Fix:** Extract real 224px @1.0 mpp patches per grid cell (PRD §2.1), send them in batches of 64 with retries, pass `api_endpoint` to `aiplatform.init`, and let endpoint failures raise so the worker marks the stage failed.

*Verifier note:* Every sub-claim verified. (a) Line 80 `dummy_png = Image.new("RGB", (224, 224), color=(200, 200, 200))` is built once outside the loop; lines 89-95 replicate that one base64 string `chunk_len` times as the instance list. `predict_embeddings(self, patch_count, batch_size)` takes no pixel argument at all (line 61) — no slide data can reach the endpoint by construction. (b) Lines 275-281: `sample_count = min(patch_count, 16)`, then `base_emb = sample_embs[0]` and `np.repeat(...) + noise` fabricates all remaining rows from one vector plus seed-42 Gaussian noise. (c) Lines 118-121 catch bare `Exception` and return `RandomState(42).randn(patch_count, 384)` after only a `print`, so auth failure, quota exhaustion, wrong endpoint host and empty-response RuntimeError (line 113) all produce a 'successful' stage. (d) `api_endpoint` is stored at line 59 and never read again; `aiplatform.init` at 68-71 receives only project and location, so the dedicated `*.prediction.vertexai.goog` host from settings.VERTEX_PATH_FOUNDATION_API_ENDPOINT is dropped and a dedicated-endpoint deployment falls straight into the random fallback. (e) configs/triage.yaml declares vertex_ai batch_size 64 / concurrency 8 / max_retries 5; none of the three appears in the file (batch_size is hardcoded 32 in the signature and 16 at the call site, no retry, no concurrency). Critical stands and is arguably understated: combined with the silent fallback, a production run is indistinguishable from an offline one in output.json, which reports model_versions.path_foundation = 'path-foundation-v1' regardless.

#### 71. Probe output discarded; 'tumor probability' heatmap is thumbnail stain density

**Severity:** critical · **Category:** Clinical correctness · **Location:** `backend/worker/triage.py:296`

The Path Foundation embeddings and linear-probe probabilities are computed and then never used. `raw_probs` is assigned at line 296 and has no further reference. ```

...

There is no second reference anywhere in the 560-line file. prob_grid (line 341) is then filled at 349-355 entirely from `stain_map`, which line 332 defines as `od.sum(axis=-1)` — the summed optical density of an 80-px-wide OpenSlide thumbnail — percentile-normalized at 345-347 and mapped linearly to 0.12..0.98 at 354. That prob_grid is the sole input to extract_hotspots (358-363), to render_viridis_heatmap_png (367) and to prob_grid.npy (379). So the entire embedding+probe pipeline (lines 268-296) is computed and thrown away, and what ships as a tumor-probability heatmap is a stain-darkness map. Every dark-but-benign structure (lymphoid aggregates, ink, folds, necrosis, hemorrhage) scores hot. Directly violates PRD 03 §2.3-2.4 and the §6 acceptance item 'tumor regions hot, stroma/fat cold'. Critical is correct: this is silent clinical misdirection, not a crash. Note that indices 71, 72 and 86 share a root cause (lines 299-355 replace the model path wholesale) but are three separable defects; 71 is specifically the discarded probe output.

#### 145. Patch sampling takes one patch per hotspot centroid, not stratified 10x grid patches; seeded RNG is created but never used

**Severity:** high · **Category:** PRD deviation · **Location:** `backend/worker/grading.py:101`

PRD 05 section 2 says: rank all 10x grid patches inside hotspots by tumour probability, force-include top-3, stratified draws across the top-50% with seeded RNG = slide checksum. The code sorts Hotspot ROI rows (typically 3-10 polygons), returns them all when <= n_patches (lines 102-103), and otherwise picks evenly-spaced indices with np.linspace; `rng` (line 118) is dead code and the seed is case_id_slide_id rather than slide.checksum_sha256.

```
seed_int = int(hashlib.md5(seed_str.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest(), 16) % (2**32)
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed_int)
    # Stratified selection into bins across the remaining pool
    selected_indices = np.linspace(0, len(top_50_pool) - 1, remaining_needed, dtype=int)
```
**Impact:** With a typical handful of hotspots only that many patches are graded, 'insufficient_tumor_patches' (min 8) fires on nearly every real case, and the evidence panel does not represent intra-tumour heterogeneity as the PRD intends.

**Fix:** Tile each confirmed hotspot polygon into 512um patches, score them with the triage probability map, then apply the top-3 + seeded stratified draw; seed from slide.checksum_sha256; delete the unused rng or use it.

*Verifier note:* Confirmed. worker/grading.py:167-176 builds one HotspotItem per non-excluded Hotspot ROI at the polygon centroid, and sample_stratified_patches (lines 101-103) returns the whole sorted list unchanged whenever len(hotspots) <= n_patches. configs/triage.yaml:20 sets max_hotspots: 10, so on a normal case the stage grades 10 centroid patches, never 24, and the linspace/top-3 branch (lines 106-124) is unreachable in practice. `rng` at line 118 is genuinely dead - the selection at line 121 is np.linspace, which is deterministic and does not use it - and the seed string is f'{case_id}_{slide_id}' (line 205) rather than the slide checksum, though Slide.checksum_sha256 does exist (app/models/slide.py:29). PRD 05 section 2 explicitly specifies ranking the 10x grid patches inside hotspots and stratified draws over the top-50% with seeded RNG = slide checksum, so the deviation is real; an unmentioned corollary is that a concave ROI's centroid can fall outside the polygon, sampling non-tumour tissue. One overstatement in the impact: with max_hotspots=10 the insufficient_tumor_patches flag (min 8) fires only when 3 or more of the 10 patches come back tumor_present=False, not 'nearly every real case'. Severity high still fits given the evidence base for two of three sub-scores is ~10 single patches instead of the specified 24.

*Also reported at:* `backend/worker/grading.py:102` (24-patch stratified sampling from the v4.2 tumor-probability grid is not implemented — one patch is taken per confirmed hotspot ROI instead); `backend/worker/grading.py:117` (Seeded RNG in the grading patch sampler is constructed and never used; the "stratified draw" is a deterministic linspace stride); `backend/worker/grading.py:205` (Stratified sampling seed uses case_id+slide_id rather than the slide checksum specified by the PRD)

#### 557. Pillow DZI fallback maps TIFF page index to pyramid level, tiling thumbnail/label/macro pages as slide levels

**Severity:** high · **Category:** Security · **Location:** `backend/worker/ingest.py:149`

When OpenSlide and pyvips both fail, the fallback assumes page k of a multi-page TIFF is the 2^-k downsample. Aperio SVS page order is [full-res, thumbnail, 1/4, 1/16, label, macro]; a Pillow-openable SVS therefore yields: level max-1 built from the small thumbnail (crop boxes beyond its bounds -> black tiles, verified PIL pads black), level max-3 at the wrong scale, and levels max-4 / max-5 built from the LABEL and MACRO images — the exact PHI the PRD requires to be stripped — then uploaded under orig/{z}/ and served by the tile router.

```
try:
                    pil_img.seek(max_level - level)
                    level_img = pil_img.copy().convert("RGB")
                except Exception:
                    level_img = pil_img.resize((lw, lh), Image.Resampling.BILINEAR).convert("RGB")
```
**Impact:** Wrong-scale/black pyramid levels and possible label/macro (patient identifier) images published in the viewer pyramid on the fallback path.

**Fix:** Never trust page index as level: pick the page whose size matches (lw, lh) within tolerance, otherwise resize from page 0; explicitly skip pages whose TIFF ImageDescription contains 'label' or 'macro'.

*Verifier note:* Confirmed and I would raise severity. Line 149 is `pil_img.seek(max_level - level)` inside the `for level in range(max_level + 1)` loop (line 140), with max_level = ceil(log2(max(w,h))) (line 138) — a DeepZoom level index used directly as a TIFF page index, which is only coincidentally related. Traced for a 6-page Aperio SVS [full, thumbnail, 1/4, 1/16, label, macro] with max_level=17: levels 0-11 raise EOFError on the out-of-range seek and fall to the resize branch, level 12 seeks page 5 (macro), level 13 seeks page 4 (label), level 16 seeks page 1 (thumbnail). So label and macro really do become pyramid levels, tiled at lines 157-170, uploaded to `{slide_id}/orig/{z}/` (line 208) and served by app/routers/tiles.py:186 which reads exactly `f"{slide.id}/orig/{target_z}/{stem}{check_ext}"`. PRD 01 line 38 requires wsi-anon label/macro stripping before any other processing and line 82 makes label absence an acceptance criterion; ingest.py:273 sets label_stripped_at with no stripping ever performed, so nothing upstream removes them. The black-tile claim also holds: lw/lh at lines 145-146 come from the assumed level scale, not the seeked page's real size, so crop boxes (line 161) run past the small page and PIL pads with zeros. Reachability is not exotic: this path needs only OpenSlide and pyvips to fail, both of which depend on native libopenslide/libvips that pip does not install and no Dockerfile in this repo installs. Category is better described as clinical-correctness + PHI exposure than 'security', but publishing patient-identifier label images into a served viewer pyramid is a high-severity leak.

#### 35. Worker poll has no FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED: two workers execute the same stage row

**Severity:** high · **Category:** Concurrency · **Location:** `backend/worker/main.py:64`

poll_and_execute_single_task() does a plain ORM SELECT ... LIMIT 1, then sets status='running' and commits. There is no row lock, no SKIP LOCKED, and no compare-and-set (UPDATE ... WHERE status='queued'). With two worker replicas (Cloud Run min-instances>1, or a rolling deploy overlap) both select the same 'queued' row, both flip it to running, and both run the handler.

```
stmt = (
    select(StageExecution)
    .where(StageExecution.status == "queued", StageExecution.stage.in_(stages_list))
    .order_by(StageExecution.started_at.asc().nulls_first(), StageExecution.id.asc())
    .limit(1)
)
stage_exec = db.scalars(stmt).first()
...
stage_exec.status = "running"
db.commit()
```
**Impact:** Duplicate execution of ingest/preprocess/qc/triage/mitosis: double GCS writes to the same case-keyed paths, duplicate audit events, racing next-stage enqueue (the existing_prep/existing_qc checks are not atomic either), and duplicate paid Vertex AI calls. Directly violates PRD 00-overview.md §5.4 which mandates FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.

**Fix:** Claim atomically: `UPDATE stage_executions SET status='running', started_at=now() WHERE id = (SELECT id FROM stage_executions WHERE status='queued' AND stage = ANY(:stages) ORDER BY started_at NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) RETURNING *` inside one transaction; on SQLite fall back to `UPDATE ... WHERE id=:id AND status='queued'` and check rowcount==1.

*Verifier note:* Code confirmed. main.py:54-71 is a plain `select(...).limit(1)` with no `.with_for_update(skip_locked=True)`, no `UPDATE ... WHERE status='queued'` compare-and-set, and the read (line 64) is followed by an unconditional `stage_exec.status = 'running'; db.commit()` (69-71). Two pollers reading before either commits both win. PRD 00-overview.md:128-140 (§5.4) literally prescribes `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, so this is a genuine deviation. Line 54 is the start of the statement builder; the actual claim-without-lock is at 64-71, hence the corrected line. Severity lowered critical->high: nothing committed in this repo actually runs >1 worker — README.md:208 is `python worker/main.py`, ops/docker-compose.yml starts only postgres + fake-gcs, and PRD §5.4 itself says "single process, one loop". The race needs an operator to start a second replica (Cloud Run per PRD §6, or a rolling deploy), so it is a latent defect plus a spec violation rather than a currently-firing one. Note also the DB index `ix_stage_poll` (models/stage_execution.py:41) exists but does not help correctness here.

*Also reported at:* `backend/worker/main.py:54` (Worker poll loop still lacks FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, violating the load-sanity acceptance item and the locked worker-loop contract); `backend/worker/main.py:54` (Worker poll has no row locking, orders by random UUID, and resets every running row on startup)

#### 465. Macenko stain normalization (the PRD's stated domain-shift defense) is never applied before detection or verification

**Severity:** high · **Category:** PRD deviation · **Location:** `backend/worker/mitosis.py:193`

PRD section 3.2 step 2 is explicit: for each tile, 'read_region_srgb → Macenko transform (same per-slide params from v4.1 — this is the domain-shift defense) → detector → optional verifier on crops.' In the actual tiling loop, `tile_rgb` is read directly from OpenSlide (or synthesized) and passed straight to `detector.detect(tile_rgb)` with no stain-normalization step at all. The `stain_normalizer` object is only constructed later (lines 325-335) and is used exclusively to render the human-facing 10x/20x/40x HPF preview thumbnails (lines 372-377) — it never touches the tiles fed to the detector, nor the 128×128 crops fed to the verifier (`verifier.verify(crop_rgb)` at line 255 receives the raw, unnormalized crop).

```
# worker/mitosis.py:188-208 (no stain transform between read and detect)
                tile_pil = openslide_slide.read_region((tx_px, ty_px), 0, (tile_size_px, tile_size_px)).convert("RGB")
                tile_rgb = np.array(tile_pil)
                ...
                tile_preds = detector.detect(tile_rgb)
# worker/mitosis.py:255 verifier also runs on raw crop
            ver_conf, contour = verifier.verify(crop_rgb)
```
**Impact:** The PRD calls this step out by name as the mechanism that keeps detection accuracy stable across scanners/stains; without it, detector/verifier behavior (and therefore mitosis counts) is exposed to exactly the scanner-to-scanner color variance the design was meant to neutralize, on both public test vendors the definition-of-done requires (TCGA-BRCA SVS vs. Hamamatsu NDPI).

**Fix:** Load the per-slide Macenko params (same ones used for HPF thumbnail rendering) once per case and apply `stain_normalizer.transform()` to each tile before `detector.detect()`, and to each crop before `verifier.verify()`.

*Verifier note:* Confirmed. PRD 04 section 3 step 2 reads: 'Each tile: read_region_srgb -> Macenko transform (same per-slide params from v4.1 - this is the domain-shift defense) -> detector -> optional verifier on crops.' In the loop, tile_rgb comes straight from openslide read_region (lines 192-194) or the synthetic generator (199-205) and goes straight into detector.detect(tile_rgb) at line 208 with no transform between. Same for the verifier: crop_rgb from read_region at 241-243 goes raw into verifier.verify(crop_rgb) at line 255. The only stain object in the whole function is built at 325-335 and used exclusively at 372-377 for HPF preview PNGs. `MacenkoNormalizer` is imported at line 36 and never referenced again (grep: single hit) — a dead import, which is itself corroborating evidence the step was dropped. Cited line 188 is the top of the tile-read block; I anchored to 193 (the actual read). Severity high is if anything understated in context: because the detector fallback is an ABSOLUTE optical-density threshold (detect.py:86, chromatin_thresh = 0.85), scanner/stain color shift moves candidate counts directly rather than being absorbed by a learned model.

#### 429. Normalized DZI pyramid built by bypassing the mandated read_region_srgb funnel — no ICC correction, no depth cap tied to magnitude

**Severity:** high · **Category:** PRD deviation · **Location:** `backend/worker/preprocess.py:44`

PRD §2.1 mandates: 'All downstream tile reads go through one function: pipeline/tiles.py:read_region_srgb'. generate_norm_dzi_pyramid instead opens the slide directly with `openslide.deepzoom.DeepZoomGenerator` and reads tiles via `dz.get_tile(level, (c, r))`, completely bypassing read_region_srgb (and therefore any ICC-to-sRGB color management). It also iterates DeepZoom levels 0 through `min(12, dz.level_count)` — a level count is a slide-size-dependent, arbitrary integer, not the level corresponding to 10x/~1.0 µm/px that §2.3 explicitly requires ('Generate a normalized DZI pyramid only up to the 10× level').

```
slide = openslide.OpenSlide(local_slide_path)
dz = DeepZoomGenerator(slide, tile_size=256, overlap=0, limit_bounds=False)
max_norm_pregen_level = min(12, dz.level_count)
for level in range(0, max_norm_pregen_level):
    ...
    tile = dz.get_tile(level, (c, r))
```
**Impact:** For ICC-embedded slides, the normalized viewer layer retains uncorrected colors even though output.json reports icc_applied:true. Depth is not tied to physical magnification at all, so two slides of different pixel dimensions get normalized pyramids stopping at wildly different real-world magnifications — for large slides this can climb far deeper than 10x (contradicting the storage/time rationale given in §2.3), and for small slides it may stop short of 10x.

**Fix:** Route every tile read through read_region_srgb, and compute the max DeepZoom level to generate from the slide's actual mpp/base magnification so it always corresponds to ~1.0 µm/px (10x), not a fixed level index.

*Verifier note:* Evidence is real and exact. preprocess.py:43-44 opens the slide directly (openslide.OpenSlide + DeepZoomGenerator(tile_size=256, overlap=0)), and :54 `dz.get_tile(level,(c,r))` is the only read — read_region_srgb is imported at :27 but never called in this file, so the ICC path in pipeline/tiles.py:44-140 (get_icc_transform / ImageCms.applyTransform, tiles.py:120-128) is never exercised for any pregenerated norm tile. tiles.py stream_slide_tile serves the pregen GCS blob first (routers/tiles.py:134-147), so those uncorrected tiles are what the viewer actually gets on ICC slides while output.json says icc_applied:true. The depth complaint is also real but the finder's impact direction is BACKWARDS: in OpenSlide's DeepZoomGenerator level 0 is the 1x1 top of the pyramid and level_count-1 is full resolution, so `range(0, min(12, dz.level_count))` (:46-47) caps the pregen at a fixed 2048px max dimension. Large slides therefore stop far SHORT of 10x (routers/tiles.py:117 computes the true 10x cap as slide_max_level-2, ~15 for a 40x slide), not 'far deeper than 10x'; only sub-2048px slides get everything. Downgraded critical->high: no clinical artifact is corrupted — the router falls through to on-the-fly generation which does route through read_region_srgb (routers/tiles.py:77) and applies the normalizer (:88-99), so the miss degrades a cosmetic viewer layer plus wasted storage/CPU rather than producing a wrong result.

PRD 02 line 50 ('ends in awaiting_review (warn) or failed (hard fail) or done (clean pass — auto-advance, no click needed)'), line 77 ('pass -> auto-advance, silent') and acceptance line 96 ('Clean slide auto-advances') are all violated. #### 74. OpenSlide thumbnail shape often differs from (ny, nx) → IndexError kills the triage stage

**Severity:** high · **Category:** Crash · **Location:** `backend/worker/triage.py:326`

`os_slide.get_thumbnail((nx, ny))` preserves the aspect ratio of the pyramid level it reads (PIL `Image.thumbnail` picks floor/ceil closest to that level's aspect), so the returned array is frequently (ny-1, nx) or (ny, nx-1). Nothing checks `arr.shape`. The loop at 349-355 iterates `range(ny)`×`range(nx)` over `tissue_mask_overview`/`stain_map` and is outside the try/except at 325-335, so the IndexError propagates and the worker marks the stage failed. A pure-math replay of PIL's rounding over ~10k (w,h,level) combinations shows thousands of mismatches (e.g. 20000×25130 at level 16 → expected (80,101), got (80,100)).

```
thumb = os_slide.get_thumbnail((nx, ny)).convert("RGB")
arr = np.array(thumb).astype(float)
...
for iy in range(ny):
    for ix in range(nx):
        if tissue_mask_overview[iy, ix]:
```
**Impact:** Triage fails for a large fraction of real slide dimensions exactly when the OpenSlide path works (the only path producing non-uniform output).

**Fix:** Resize the thumbnail explicitly: `thumb = thumb.resize((nx, ny), Image.BILINEAR)` after get_thumbnail, or derive ny/nx from `arr.shape` after the call.

*Verifier note:* Confirmed, and I reproduced the arithmetic. `os_slide.get_thumbnail((nx, ny))` (line 326) reads a whole pyramid level and calls PIL `Image.thumbnail`, which preserves that level's aspect ratio and never enlarges; nothing validates `arr.shape` (327). `tissue_mask_overview` and `stain_map` (330-332) therefore inherit the thumbnail's shape, while `prob_grid` is allocated (ny, nx) at 341 and the loop at 349-355 indexes `tissue_mask_overview[iy, ix]` over `range(ny)` x `range(nx)`. I replayed openslide's downsample/level selection plus PIL's round_aspect over 4000 random (width_px, height_px) pairs on a standard 1/4/16/64/256 SVS pyramid: 736 (18%) came back at a size other than (80, ny), e.g. 115680x55494 -> expected (80,38), got (79,38); 67468x51930 -> expected (80,62), got (80,61). Since thumbnail only shrinks, every mismatch is strictly smaller, so IndexError is guaranteed, not merely possible. The finder is right that the loop is outside the try/except: that except ends at line 335, the loop starts at 349, so the exception escapes run_triage and the worker fails the stage. Severity high is right rather than critical only because it is a loud failure, and it fires exactly on the OpenSlide path (the one that yields non-uniform output). Cited line 326 is the correct origin; the throw site is line 351. The proposed `thumb.resize((nx, ny), Image.BILINEAR)` fix is correct.

#### 567. Worker unconditionally sets status='awaiting_review' at the end of run_triage, clobbering a 'confirmed' status written concurrently by /confirm

**Severity:** high · **Category:** Concurrency · **Location:** `backend/worker/triage.py:526`

run_triage sets stage_execution.status = 'awaiting_review' and commits from the worker's own session (lines 526, 554) without re-reading the row. Because /confirm has no status gating and GET/confirm fall back to the case-level output.json (routers/triage.py:123, 505) even for a queued/running attempt, a pathologist can confirm while the worker is still running the (retried) attempt. Confirm sets status='confirmed', persists the PREVIOUS attempt's hotspots and queues mitosis; seconds later the worker's commit overwrites the row back to 'awaiting_review'. The UI then shows the stage as un-reviewed while mitosis is already running on stale hotspots, and re-confirming triggers the already-recorded mitosis-wipe path.

```
# Set status to awaiting_review for pathologist confirmation gate
        stage_execution.status = "awaiting_review"
        ...
        session.add(audit_out)
        session.commit()
```
**Impact:** Confirmed state silently regresses; mitosis runs on the prior attempt's hotspot set while the triage row reads awaiting_review; the pathologist is prompted to confirm a second time (which resets mitosis).

**Fix:** Have the worker transition via a guarded UPDATE (WHERE status='running') or refresh the row before writing; reject /confirm and /edits unless the latest attempt is in awaiting_review (state machine in 00-overview §5.2).

*Verifier note:* The lost update is real and every link in the chain checks out. (a) triage.py:526 assigns `stage_execution.status = "awaiting_review"` on the ORM object the worker loaded (worker/main.py set it to 'running' and committed before calling the handler); the commit at triage.py:554 flushes `UPDATE stage_executions SET status='awaiting_review' WHERE id=...` with no status predicate, so a 'confirmed' written by another session in between is overwritten. main.py's guard `if stage_exec.status == "running"` does not help — it reads the session's own in-memory value ('awaiting_review'), never the DB. (b) POST /confirm (routers/triage.py:480-533) selects the latest attempt by `attempt.desc()` with no status filter, and when `output_ref` is empty (a queued/re-running attempt) falls back to the case-level `cases/{id}/triage/output.json` at line ~505 — i.e. the previous attempt's artifact. GET /{case_id} does the same at line ~123. (c) Confirm then does `db.query(Hotspot).filter(...).delete()`, re-inserts the stale hotspots, sets status='confirmed' and flips the mitosis execution back to 'queued'. (d) The window is user-reachable: frontend/components/viewer/TriageViewer.tsx:602 gates the Confirm button only on `submitting` and hotspot count — not on `data.status` — and the page renders hotspots from the stale fallback JSON while a retried attempt (cases.py:203 'stage_retried' / the Reprocess button) runs for minutes. Keeping high: silent regression of a clinical review gate plus mitosis running on the prior attempt's hotspots.

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** PRD deviation · **Location:** `backend/worker/grading.py:252`

The worker converts hotspot centroids from micrometers to level-0 pixels inline (lines 173-174, dividing by mpp_x only) and persists center_x_px/center_y_px in the patches array of gradings.machine and the GCS grading_output.json. PRD 00-overview.md:79-80 is explicit: 'All persisted geometry is in base-level micrometers... Conversions (um <-> level-N px) live in pipeline/coords.py and nowhere else.' The UI half of the claim also holds up: frontend/lib/api.ts:299 types center_x_px on the grading patch, and grep finds no consumer of it anywhere in frontend/ — every other viewer jump (MitosisViewer.tsx:138,264,312,855) works from center_um, which grading patches do not carry.
