#### 624. PDF prints a closest-margin distance even when margin status is 'positive' or 'cannot_be_assessed'

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Clinical correctness · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/report_pdf.py:257`

MarginsPayload defaults closest_margin_mm to 5.0 and the renderer always appends '(Closest margin: X mm)'. PUT margins {"status": "positive"} therefore renders 'Positive (Closest margin: 5.0 mm)', and {"status": "cannot_be_assessed"} renders 'Cannot Be Assessed (Closest margin: 5.0 mm)'. No cross-field validation exists in MarginsPayload (line 51-55).

```
margin_status = margins.get("status", "negative").replace("_", " ").title()
margin_dist = margins.get("closest_margin_mm", 5.0)
...
Paragraph(f"{margin_status} (Closest margin: {margin_dist} mm)", body_style)
```
**Impact:** A positive margin (tumor at ink, distance 0) is reported with a 5 mm clearance; a not-assessable margin is given a numeric distance. Both are clinically contradictory statements on the final document.

**Fix:** Only print the distance when status == 'negative'; in MarginsPayload use a model_validator that forces closest_margin_mm to None (and requires positive_margins) for the other statuses.

*Verifier note:* Confirmed exactly as quoted: report_pdf.py:234-235 reads status and `closest_margin_mm` with a 5.0 fallback, and line 257 unconditionally renders `{margin_status} (Closest margin: {margin_dist} mm)` with no branch on status. MarginsPayload (report.py:51-55) is a bare BaseModel: `closest_margin_mm: Optional[float] = Field(default=5.0, ge=0.0)` with no model_validator, and update_report_data stores it verbatim (`report.margins = payload.margins.model_dump()`, report.py:370-371), so PUT {'status':'positive'} really does persist closest_margin_mm=5.0 and render 'Positive (Closest margin: 5.0 mm)'. One additional wrinkle the finder missed: an explicit `closest_margin_mm: null` dumps to None and the renderer's `.get(..., 5.0)` returns None, printing 'Closest margin: None mm' — so the guard is needed for the null case too, not only the positive/not-assessed case. Medium is appropriate for a self-contradictory statement on a signed clinical document.

#### 183. Unbalanced markup in narrative or free-text fields raises ValueError inside ReportLab -> /pdf 500 and silent save-time failures

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Crash · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/report_pdf.py:327`

Paragraph() parses its text as XML-ish markup; text is inserted raw (no escape()). Verified: microscopic_findings 'Closest margin <2 mm, focal DCIS <b>unclosed' -> ValueError 'Parse error: saw </para> instead of expected </b>'. Narrative is free-form (PUT narrative Dict[str,str], LLM output), procedure/histologic_type/etc. are also unescaped (lines 174, 206, 249). update_report_data swallows the error (router 403-404) so the user never learns the PDF is stale; get_report_pdf then returns 500 (router 563).

```
[Paragraph(micro_text, body_style)],
...
[Paragraph(corr_text, body_style)],
```
**Impact:** PDF generation breaks on ordinary pathology text containing '<' + letter or stray tags; error hidden at save time.

**Fix:** xml.sax.saxutils.escape() every user/LLM string before Paragraph; surface render failures from PUT/sign as a warning field instead of print().

*Verifier note:* Confirmed by execution. Ran generate_clinical_cap_pdf with narrative={'microscopic_findings': 'Closest margin <2 mm, focal DCIS <b>unclosed'}: ValueError "paragraph text '<para>...' caused exception Parse error: saw </para> instead of expected </b>". No xml.sax.saxutils.escape() anywhere in the file; micro_text/corr_text go raw into Paragraph at lines 327 and 329, and procedure/histologic_type/etc. are likewise unescaped (lines 174, 249). narrative is free-form (UpdateReportPayload.narrative: Optional[Dict[str,str]], routers/report.py:83) and is also MedGemma output. Error handling as described: routers/report.py:401-404 swallows the render exception with print(), and routers/report.py:563 turns a render failure into HTTP 500 (though only when no prior blob exists — otherwise the stale PDF is served, which is the worse silent case). One narrowing of the finder's claim, verified: '<' followed by a digit or space ('Closest margin <2 mm from the inked posterior margin.') and a bare '&' both render fine; the crash needs '<' immediately followed by a letter (a tag-like token) or an unbalanced tag. So the trigger is LLM/pasted markup rather than any '<' in ordinary prose — medium is the right severity, not higher. Secondary unreported effect: valid markup in user text (e.g. '<i>') is silently interpreted as formatting.

#### 184. Long narrative (> ~1 page in one table cell) raises reportlab LayoutError -> 500

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Crash · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/report_pdf.py:339`

Narrative sections are single Table cells wrapped in KeepTogether; a cell cannot split across pages. Verified: a 16 kB microscopic_findings string raises LayoutError 'Flowable <Table ...> too large on page'. No length limit exists on UpdateReportPayload.narrative or the LLM output.

```
story.append(KeepTogether([narr_table]))
```
**Impact:** A detailed microscopic description makes the report un-renderable; sign succeeds but PDF upload silently fails (router 657-660).

**Fix:** Render narrative as plain Paragraphs (splittable) instead of table cells, drop KeepTogether, and cap narrative length in the API.

*Verifier note:* Confirmed by execution. A ~18 kB microscopic_findings string raises reportlab LayoutError: 'Flowable <Table ...> with cell(0,0) containing ...' — the narrative is a single-cell Table row (lines 325-330) wrapped in KeepTogether at line 339, and a table cell cannot split across pages. No length cap exists on UpdateReportPayload.narrative (routers/report.py:83, Optional[Dict[str,str]]) nor on the MedGemma output. Same swallow/500 handling as index 183 (routers/report.py:401-404, 563). Distinct root cause from 183 (layout vs markup), so not a duplicate. Minor precision point: removing KeepTogether alone would not fix it — the Table row itself is unsplittable, so the fix must be plain Paragraphs as the finder proposes.

#### 622. PDF prints a hard-coded attestation sentence instead of the attestation_statement the pathologist actually signed

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Data integrity · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/report_pdf.py:351`

SignReportPayload requires attestation_statement (min_length=15) and it is stored on Report.attestation_statement, but render_and_upload_report_pdf never puts it in render_dict and the PDF attestation block prints a fixed sentence. ```
**Impact:** The signed PDF misrepresents the attestation the pathologist made; a signer who edited the statement (e.g. to add a limitation) has that edit silently dropped from the legal document.

#### 619. pT categories ignore the AJCC 8th edition millimetre-rounding rule at every boundary

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Clinical correctness · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/staging.py:49`

AJCC 8th edition (Breast, chapter 48) instructs that tumor size be rounded to the nearest millimetre before assigning pT (e.g. 20.4 mm -> 20 mm -> pT1c, 20.5 mm -> 21 mm -> pT2), with the special rule that 1.0-1.9 mm is reported as 2 mm (pT1a, not pT1mi). The code compares the raw float against the cut-offs, so 20.4 mm -> pT2, 50.4 mm -> pT3, 10.2 mm -> pT1c, 1.0 mm -> pT1mi. Statically verified: calculate_ajcc_pt_stage(20.4) == 'pT2'. test_cap_reporting.py:98 locks in the wrong behaviour ('assert calculate_ajcc_pt_stage(20.1) == "pT2"').

```
elif tumor_size_mm <= 20.0:
    return "pT1c"
elif tumor_size_mm <= 50.0:
    return "pT2"
```
**Impact:** Tumors measured with sub-millimetre precision near a boundary are up-staged (e.g. 20.3 mm reported as pT2 / Stage IIA instead of pT1c / IA), which changes the stage group printed on the signed report.

**Fix:** Round to the nearest mm first (round-half-up), map 1.0-1.9 mm to 2 mm, then apply the cut-offs; add boundary tests for 20.4/20.5 and 1.0-1.9.

*Verifier note:* Verified by execution: calculate_ajcc_pt_stage(20.4) == 'pT2' and calculate_ajcc_pt_stage(1.0) == 'pT1mi'. Lines 43-54 compare the raw float against 1.0/5.0/10.0/20.0/50.0 with no rounding step, so any sub-millimetre measurement in (20.0, 20.5) is up-staged to pT2 and then to a higher stage group by calculate_ajcc_stage_group (pT1c/pN0 -> IA vs pT2/pN0 -> IIA at line 119). AJCC 8th ed. does direct rounding to the nearest millimetre before T assignment, with the 1.0-1.9 mm -> report as 2 mm carve-out, so the deviation is real. tests/test_cap_reporting.py:98 does assert calculate_ajcc_pt_stage(20.1) == 'pT2', pinning the current behaviour. Reachability is genuine but narrow: tumor_size_mm is a free float on UpdateReportPayload (report.py:77, ge=0.0), so a pathologist entering 20.4 hits it; the seeded default is 18.0. Medium is right — real but requires sub-mm entry near a cut-off.

calculate_ajcc_pn_stage checks nodes_examined <= 0 before looking at nodes_positive, so {examined_count: 0, positive_count: 3} returns 'pNX'. validate_staging_invariants deliberately exempts the same case ('and nodes_examined > 0', line 164), so even if it were called the contradiction is accepted. #### 173. Stage-group fallback returns 'IA' for every unhandled combination (pN1b/pN2b/pN3b/pN3c, bare 'M1', pTX)

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Clinical correctness · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/staging.py:149`

Any pN outside {pN0,pNX,pN1mi,pN1a,pN2a,pN3a} falls to the default chain and ends at 'IA'.     return "IIIC"
...

```
**Impact:** Silently under-stages advanced disease to Stage IA instead of failing loudly or returning 'Cannot be determined'.

Line number is correct. Severity lowered high->medium on reachability, not on correctness: all four call sites (routers/report.py:277-279, 384-386, 439-441; worker/report.py:99-101) call calculate_ajcc_pt_stage(tumor_size) with `tumor_size = report.tumor_size_mm or 18.0` (never None/0) and calculate_ajcc_pn_stage(n_exam, n_pos) with no largest_meta_mm/is_micrometastasis and always pm_stage='cM0'. That restricts today's reachable inputs to pT1mi..pT3 x {pNX,pN0,pN1a,pN2a,pN3a}, every one of which the explicit matrix at 105-139 handles, so the fallback is currently unreachable in production. It is a real latent wrong-answer path that finding 196 (passing pT4/pTis inputs) and 363 (passing largest_meta_mm) would immediately expose, and the fix proposed is right.

*Also reported at:* `backend/pipeline/staging.py:149` (AJCC stage group defaults to 'IA' for every unrecognised pT/pN combination)

#### 52. Full-mosaic SVD / lstsq on up to 13M x 3 float64 rows — hundreds of MB to GBs per fit

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Performance · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/stain.py:50`

_get_stain_params runs np.linalg.svd(od_tissue, full_matrices=False) on the concatenated 50 x 512 x 512 patch mosaic (13.1M rows). LAPACK allocates U (N x 3 float64 ~ 315 MB) plus workspace, and lstsq(stain_matrix.T, od.T) at line 73 builds another 3 x 13M system and a 2 x 13M concentration array before np.percentile copies it again. transform() repeats an SVD for every tile.

```
_, _, V = np.linalg.svd(od_tissue, full_matrices=False)
...
concentrations = np.linalg.lstsq(stain_matrix.T, od.T, rcond=None)[0]
```
**Impact:** Multi-GB transient memory on an 8-vCPU/32 GiB worker that is simultaneously holding a scratch slide in tmpfs; slow fits.

**Fix:** Use the 3x3 covariance eigendecomposition (np.linalg.eigh(od.T @ od)) for the principal plane and solve concentrations with a precomputed pseudo-inverse (2x3 @ 3xN).

*Verifier note:* Arithmetic checks out. mosaic = np.concatenate(valid_patches, axis=0) at 307 over up to 50 512x512x3 patches -> (25600, 512, 3) = 13,107,200 px; _rgb_to_od(...).reshape(-1,3) at 43 is 13.1M x 3 float64 = 315 MB, and od_tissue (45) is that minus background. np.linalg.svd(od_tissue, full_matrices=False) at 50 makes gesdd allocate U at N x 3 (~315 MB) plus an input copy; lstsq(stain_matrix.T, od.T) at 73 needs a Fortran copy of od.T (315 MB) and returns 2 x 13.1M (210 MB), then np.percentile at 74 sorts a further copy. Peak transient is ~1-1.5 GB per fit, on a worker that also holds a scratch slide. Worse than the finding says: on the NumPy path this entire computation is thrown away, since stain_matrix_src/max_conc_src set at 128 are never read (see index 50) and transform() re-does an SVD per tile anyway. Related to 50 but a distinct defect (cost, not correctness), so not a duplicate. Medium stands.

#### 551. Slide dimensions read from non-existent width_px/height_px attributes; PIL-opened slides get a 2048 px corner as 'thumbnail'

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/stain.py:256`

fit_macenko_stain receives an OpenSlide or PIL.Image object (preprocess.py:147-149, qc.py:63-65), neither of which has `width_px`/`height_px`. Only the OpenSlide `.dimensions` branch works; for the PIL fallback (plain TIFF/PNG uploads, or any slide OpenSlide cannot open) the size silently defaults to 2048x2048, so thumb_w_um = 2048*mpp and the 'whole-slide thumbnail', Otsu tissue mask, tissue_area_mm2, coverage QC and patch sampling all cover only the top-left 2048x2048 px of the image.

```

    slide_h_px = float(getattr(slide_obj, "height_px", 2048) or 2048)

        slide_w_px, slide_h_px = float(slide_obj.dimensions[0]), float(slide_obj.dimensions[1])
```
**Impact:** For non-OpenSlide inputs the tissue mask is wrong (likely near-empty), coverage QC fails or passes on a corner, and stain sampling never touches most of the tissue.

**Fix:** Use `slide_obj.size` for PIL images (`elif hasattr(slide_obj, 'size')`) and pass the Slide ORM dims explicitly; raise if neither is available.

*Verifier note:* Confirmed at lines 256-259, quoted accurately. Both call sites pass the image handle, not the ORM row: backend/worker/preprocess.py:146-152 does `slide = openslide.OpenSlide(local_slide_path)` / `except: slide = Image.open(local_slide_path)` then `fit_macenko_stain(slide, ...)`; backend/worker/qc.py:61-72 is identical. Neither OpenSlide nor PIL.Image exposes `width_px`/`height_px` (the ORM Slide does — backend/app/models/slide.py, set in ingest.py:267-268 — but that object is never passed here), so getattr falls to 2048.0, and PIL has `.size`, not `.dimensions`, so the guard at 258 does not rescue it. Result for the PIL path: thumb_w_um = thumb_h_um = 512 um, and read_region_srgb's PIL branch (backend/pipeline/tiles.py:102-111) crops box (0,0,2048,2048) clamped to the image, then resizes to 512x512 — i.e. the top-left 2048x2048 px only. tissue_mask_1bit, tissue_area_mm2 (preprocess.py:160-161), the coverage QC check, and the patch-sampling window (max_x_um/max_y_um at 286-287) all inherit that corner. backend/tests/test_stain.py:29-40 exercises exactly this path with a 1024x1024 PIL image. Medium is right: it degrades, rather than crashes, and only for non-OpenSlide inputs.

#### 49. Otsu threshold is computed then overridden by hard-coded 215..235 clamp and saturation>12 rule (clinical constants in code)

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** PRD deviation · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/stain.py:279`

The between-class-variance Otsu at lines 267-276 is correct, but its result is immediately clamped into [215,235] and OR-ed with a fixed saturation gate, so the 'Otsu tissue mask at 1.25x' is really a fixed-threshold mask. The same file also embeds W_target, maxC_target=[1.85,1.05], scale clip [0.75,1.35], beta 0.12/0.15 and fallback stain vectors in transform()/_get_stain_params (lines 144-147, 167, 179, 184, 186). None of these live in configs/ or contribute to a config_hash.

```
effective_thresh = max(215.0, min(235.0, otsu_thresh))
tissue_mask_1bit = (gray_thumb <= effective_thresh) | (sat_thumb > 12)
```
**Impact:** Tissue mask quality on dark-background or lightly stained slides is unpredictable and untunable; PRD 00 §5.5 'No clinical numbers in code' violated; changing any of these silently changes outputs with no hash change.

**Fix:** Move thresholds to configs (e.g. configs/stain.yaml), hash them into stage_executions.config_hash, and either trust Otsu or remove the dead computation.

*Verifier note:* Evidence exact at stain.py:279-280: `effective_thresh = max(215.0, min(235.0, otsu_thresh))` then `tissue_mask_1bit = (gray_thumb <= effective_thresh) | (sat_thumb > 12)`. The Otsu computation (267-276) is real but its output only survives inside [215,235]; on any thumbnail whose true Otsu falls outside that band (dark background, faded stain) the mask is a fixed threshold, and the `| sat_thumb > 12` OR-gate can override it entirely. The other constants are all present as claimed: W_target 144-147, W_src fallback 167, maxC_target [1.85,1.05] 179, maxC_src floor 0.15 at 184, scale clip [0.75,1.35] at 186, beta defaults 0.15 (41) / 0.12 (131). configs/ contains cap_elements/mitosis/pricing/qc/scoring/triage.yaml and stain_reference.png but no stain.yaml; the only config_hash producer in the repo is qc_checks.py:35-36 (qc.yaml), consumed at worker/qc.py:124 — nothing hashes any stain constant into stage_executions.config_hash (model at app/models/stage_execution.py:27). PRD 00 line 150 states verbatim that every clinical constant lives in configs/*.yaml, hashed into stage_executions.config_hash, 'No clinical numbers in code'. Deviation is real. Medium is right: it is a tunability/provenance defect, not an incorrect output on the common case. Minor overstatement in the title only — the Otsu result is not universally dead, just clamped.

#### 553. Stain-fit patch sampling ignores the tissue mask; falls back to the whole thumbnail as the 'mosaic'

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** PRD deviation · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/stain.py:289`

PRD 02 §2.2 step 2: 'sample up to 50 random 512x512 tissue patches'. Candidate positions are drawn uniformly over the slide footprint, not from tissue_mask_1bit computed 9 lines earlier; the only filter is saturation-mean >= 0.05. On a low-coverage slide most of the 100 candidates land on glass, valid_patches can be empty, and the code then fits on the stretched 512x512 thumbnail (mostly background) while reporting patches_sampled = 1.

```
candidate_xs = rng.uniform(0, max_x_um, size=100)
    candidate_ys = rng.uniform(0, max_y_um, size=100)
    ...
    if not valid_patches:
        valid_patches.append(thumb_arr)
```
**Impact:** Persisted stain params (and the PRD stain-sanity check, if implemented) are fitted on background; determinism holds but the fit is meaningless.

**Fix:** Sample candidate centres from np.argwhere(tissue_mask_1bit) (seeded rng.choice), convert mask px -> um using the mask scale, and fail the stage (or mark stain_params 'degenerate') when fewer than N tissue patches are found instead of substituting the thumbnail.

*Verifier note:* Verified end to end. PRD prd/02-stage-v4.1-preprocess-qc.md:25-28 specifies 'tissue mask at 1.25x' then 'sample up to 50 random 512x512 tissue patches at 10x'. stain.py:280 builds tissue_mask_1bit = (gray_thumb <= effective_thresh) | (sat_thumb > 12), and that array is then used ONLY as a return value (line 334) -- it is never consulted by the sampler. Candidates are drawn uniformly over the whole footprint at lines 289-290 (rng.uniform(0, max_x_um/max_y_um, size=100), with max_*_um derived from thumb_w_um/thumb_h_um at 286-287), and the sole acceptance test is the per-patch saturation mean at line 301. So on a low-coverage slide (needle core, small biopsy on a large glass footprint) the 100 candidates can all fail, and lines 304-305 then push thumb_arr -- the 512x512 stretched thumbnail of the ENTIRE slide including all background -- into valid_patches, making it the whole 'mosaic' at line 307, with stain_params_dict reporting patches_sampled = 1 (line 330). Determinism holds (seed from checksum, line 251-252) but the fit is on background. Two notes on impact: (a) it is not only the empty case -- even with 50 accepted patches the sampling is mask-blind and biased toward whatever passes a loose 0.05 mean-saturation gate; (b) the *current* blast radius is damped by the separate 'transform ignores fit' defect: backend/app/routers/tiles.py:97-98 and backend/worker/triage.py:391-397 load stain_params.json and assign stain_matrix_target/max_conc_target, but PureNumpyMacenkoNormalizer.transform (lines 131-199) re-derives everything from the source tile and never reads those attributes, so today the bad params mostly pollute the persisted audit record rather than pixels. Keeping medium: it is a real PRD deviation on a persisted clinical artifact, and it becomes a pixel-level defect the moment the transform bug is fixed. Also worth noting the fallback is silent -- no degenerate marker, no stage failure -- exactly as the finder says.

#### 53. ICC profile detection never works for OpenSlide slides; icc_applied is always False

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/tiles.py:33`

check_icc_profile looks for a properties key 'openslide.color-profile'. OpenSlide exposes no such property (the C library publishes openslide.icc-size and openslide-python >= 1.3 exposes the profile as OpenSlide.color_profile / embeds it in read_region() output). The second branch requires `.info`, which OpenSlide objects do not have. So for every real WSI icc_bytes is None, has_icc False, and read_region_srgb never applies a transform; preprocess.py:164 records icc_applied=false for every slide.

```
if hasattr(slide, "properties"):
    icc_bytes = slide.properties.get("openslide.color-profile")
    if isinstance(icc_bytes, str):
        icc_bytes = icc_bytes.encode("utf-8")
```
**Impact:** PRD 02 §2.1 ICC handling is silently a no-op; scanner colour casts pass into stain fitting and models, and output.json misreports the reason ('assume sRGB') as absent profile.

**Fix:** Use `profile = getattr(slide, 'color_profile', None)` (ImageCmsProfile) or read `slide.read_region(...).info.get('icc_profile')`; build the transform from that.

*Verifier note:* Line 33 reads slide.properties.get("openslide.color-profile"). No such OpenSlide property exists — the C library publishes openslide.icc-size, and openslide-python >= 1.3 exposes the profile as OpenSlide.color_profile / attaches it to read_region() output. The fallback at line 38 requires .info, which OpenSlide objects do not have (only PIL Images do), so for any OpenSlide input check_icc_profile returns (None, False), has_icc at line 121 is False, and the ImageCms branch at 121-128 never runs. worker/preprocess.py:164 then writes icc_applied=false for every WSI. Independent corroboration that the approach is wrong: line 34-35 utf-8-encodes a str property, and raw ICC binary cannot round-trip through OpenSlide's string property map anyway. Mitigating context (worth flagging to the author, not a refutation): prd/02-stage-v4.1-preprocess-qc.md:19 itself names `openslide.color-profile`, so the code faithfully implements a mistaken PRD line — the fix belongs in both. Severity medium is right: the ICC path is dead, but stain fitting is done on the same uncorrected pixels so the pipeline is at least self-consistent. Note the PIL-Image fallback path (line 38-39) does work, so it is not universally dead.

#### 54. read_region_srgb has no guard for non-pyramidal slides: whole-slide thumbnail read at level 0

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Performance · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/tiles.py:97`

fit_macenko_stain requests the full slide (w_um = slide width) at out_px 512. read_region_srgb picks best_level via get_best_level_for_downsample; for a single-level TIFF (allowed by 'generic OpenSlide' support) best_level=0 and it calls slide.read_region((0,0), 0, (100000, 80000)) — a 32 GB RGBA allocation — then resizes. There is also no cap on w_px_lvl/h_px_lvl.

```
best_level = slide.get_best_level_for_downsample(target_downsample)
level_ds = slide.level_downsamples[best_level] if hasattr(slide, "level_downsamples") else 1.0
w_px_lvl = max(1, int(round(w_px_0 / level_ds)))
h_px_lvl = max(1, int(round(h_px_0 / level_ds)))
...
pil_tile = slide.read_region((safe_x, safe_y), best_level, (w_px_lvl, h_px_lvl))
```
**Impact:** OOM in preprocess/qc for any slide whose pyramid has too few levels; also the origin clamp at lines 95-96 shifts (rather than pads) regions that start off-slide, so edge HPF/hotspot patches are spatially displaced relative to their stored um coordinates.

**Fix:** Cap the level-N read size (e.g. tile the read when w_px_lvl*h_px_lvl > 16M px, or use slide.get_thumbnail for overview requests) and pad out-of-bounds regions instead of moving the origin.

*Verifier note:* Real, though the cited line 86 is the `best_level = 0` initializer; the defect is the uncapped level-N size at 92-93 and the read at 97. Traced: stain.py:262-264 calls read_region_srgb(slide, 0, 0, thumb_w_um, thumb_h_um, out_px=(512,512)) with thumb_w/h_um = min(50000, dim*mpp), i.e. the whole slide. At mpp 0.25 that is w_px_0 = 200000, target_downsample = 200000/512 = 390 (line 88). get_best_level_for_downsample returns the deepest level with ds <= 390; for a single-directory generic TIFF that is 0, level_ds = 1.0, and line 97 asks OpenSlide for a 200000x200000 RGBA buffer. Nothing between lines 92 and 97 bounds w_px_lvl*h_px_lvl. This is not limited to single-level files: an SVS with only downsamples {1,4} yields a 50000x50000 read (~10 GB), which is enough to OOM the preprocess worker. Four-level SVS (ds 32) lands at ~156 MB, which survives — so the failure is slide-structure dependent, and medium (not high) is the right severity. I judged only the read-size claim here; the origin-clamp sentence in the impact paragraph is finding 554/729's defect.

#### 554. read_region_srgb pads out-of-bounds regions with black (and shifts negative-origin regions)

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/tiles.py:99`

For regions that extend past the slide edge, OpenSlide returns RGBA (0,0,0,0); `.convert('RGB')` turns that into solid black (verified). The PIL branch and the fully-OOB branch pad with near-white, so behaviour is inconsistent. Black pixels have OD = -log10(1/255) = 2.4 in the stain code (rgb is clamped to 1.0), dominating the 99th-percentile concentration and SVD in fit/transform for edge patches, and they create a high-variance edge that makes an edge tile look 'sharp' in the Laplacian check. Additionally safe_x/safe_y clamp the origin without reducing width, so a region with x_um < 0 is shifted rather than cropped.

```
safe_x = max(0, min(dim_w - 1, x_px_0))
            safe_y = max(0, min(dim_h - 1, y_px_0))
            pil_tile = slide.read_region((safe_x, safe_y), best_level, (w_px_lvl, h_px_lvl))
            if pil_tile.mode != "RGB":
                pil_tile = pil_tile.convert("RGB")
```
**Impact:** Wrong stain concentrations and false-sharp focus at slide borders; on-the-fly viewer tiles at the right/bottom edge render black.

**Fix:** Composite the RGBA tile over white (`Image.alpha_composite(Image.new('RGBA', size, (255,255,255,255)), tile)`) before convert, and clip the region to slide bounds then pad to target size.

*Verifier note:* The black-fill half is confirmed and reachable. OpenSlide returns (0,0,0,0) outside the slide and line 98-99 does a plain .convert('RGB'), which drops alpha and yields solid black (verified locally: Image.new('RGBA',(2,2),(0,0,0,0)).convert('RGB') -> (0,0,0)). The inconsistency claim also holds: line 84 fills (245,240,245) and line 112 fills (240,235,240). Reachable path: app/routers/tiles.py:66-87 computes x_px_0 = c*w_px_0 for the last DeepZoom column/row, so the region overhangs the right/bottom edge, safe_x is unchanged (it only clamps negatives), and the viewer gets a black band on edge tiles — where the pre-generated DeepZoomGenerator tiles are not black, so the on-the-fly fallback visibly differs. The QC edge argument is weaker but sound: qc_checks.py:110 skips flat tiles via np.std > 5.0, so a fully-black tile is excluded, but a part-black tile passes and its black/tissue boundary inflates the Laplacian variance. The 'additionally ... shifted rather than cropped' clause is correct as written but currently unreachable — see index 729. Medium is right; the fix (alpha_composite over white before convert) is one line and covers all three callers.

#### 730. Pyramid patch stitcher returns a mosaic with missing tiles left as flat pink

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Clinical correctness · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/tiles.py:221`

extract_patch_from_pyramid pre-fills the mosaic with (240, 230, 235) and only bails out when not a single tile was fetched. If some of the up-to-16 tiles are missing from GCS — the normal case at high zoom, since ingest only pre-generates DeepZoom levels up to 11 — the remaining area stays the flat placeholder colour and the crop is returned as a real patch.

                        found_any = True
...

            return None
```
**Impact:** The hotspot and HPF thumbnail endpoints (routers/triage.py:358, routers/mitosis.py:258) serve, cache into GCS and display a partly synthetic microscopy field as clinical evidence; a pathologist counting mitoses in that field sees blank tissue-coloured area where the slide was never read.

In the edge case the pink filler stands in for genuinely off-slide area, which is misleading but not fabricated tissue. Medium is fair; coverage tracking rather than found_any is the right fix.

#### 475. Batched fp16 tile inference from config is never implemented — detector runs one tile at a time with no batching

**Severity:** low · **Category:** PRD deviation · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/detect.py:51`

PRD section 2 serving spec: 'same worker container... PyTorch 2.x, fp16 inference, batch 16 tiles.' configs/mitosis.yaml declares `batch_size: 16` and `fp16: true`, but `YoloMitosisDetector.detect()` only ever accepts a single tile (`img_t = torch.from_numpy(tile_rgb)...unsqueeze(0)`), and `worker/mitosis.py`'s tiling loop (line 208) calls `detector.detect(tile_rgb)` once per tile inside a plain Python for-loop — there is no batching path and `batch_size`/`fp16` are never referenced anywhere in detect.py or worker/mitosis.py.

```
# detect.py:50-52
                img_t = torch.from_numpy(tile_rgb).permute(2, 0, 1).float() / 255.0
                img_t = img_t.unsqueeze(0).to(self.device)
# worker/mitosis.py:208 (inside `for tile in tiles:`)

```
**Impact:** Even if real weights were wired in (see the fabricated-model finding), inference would run at batch size 1 on every tile, not the batch-16 fp16 throughput the PRD sizes the ≤8-minute-per-case / L4 GPU budget around — the runtime target in section 3.5 ('50 mm² ≈ 800 tiles → ≤8 min') would not be met at the documented serving configuration.

#### 583. Per-contour full-tile mask allocation makes the detector O(n_contours x tile_pixels); lymphocyte-rich tiles cost seconds each

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Performance · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/detect.py:106`

For every contour in the size window, the code allocates a fresh 1024x1024 uint8 mask, rasterises the contour into it, and boolean-indexes h_od over the whole tile just to get a 95th percentile of the contour's pixels. Inflammatory or necrotic tiles routinely yield hundreds of dark blobs in the 200-3500 px2 window.

```
mask_cnt = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=np.uint8)
cv2.drawContours(mask_cnt, [cnt], -1, 255, -1)
p95_od = float(np.percentile(h_od[mask_cnt > 0], 95))
```
**Impact:** ~3-5 ms per contour x hundreds of contours x 800 tiles pushes a full case well past the PRD's <= 8 min budget on CPU, and the worker holds the case in 'running' the whole time.

**Fix:** Use cv2.boundingRect(cnt) and rasterise/percentile only inside the bounding box, or replace findContours+moments with cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats and compute per-label percentiles once via np.bincount / sorted labels.

*Verifier note:* Code and line are exact: detect.py:106-108 allocates a fresh full-tile np.zeros((h,w)) per in-window contour, rasterises into it, then does h_od[mask_cnt > 0] over the whole 1024x1024 array just for one percentile. That is genuinely O(n_contours x tile_pixels) and the boundingRect+offset rewrite the finder proposes is correct and trivial. It is also on the live path, not a dead branch: worker/mitosis.py:156 constructs YoloMitosisDetector(conf_threshold=det_thresh) with no weights_path, and no config anywhere supplies one (grep for weights_path finds only detect.py:26 and verify.py:29), so self.model is always None and _detect_hyperchromatic_features runs for every tile. PRD 04-stage-v4.3-mitosis.md:32 does state the ~800 tiles / <=8 min target the finder cites.

Severity dropped medium -> low because the impact arithmetic is roughly 10x overstated. Measured on this machine, the quoted allocate + boolean-mask + fancy-index + percentile sequence on a 1024x1024 float32 h_od costs ~0.33 ms per contour, not 3-5 ms (cv2 was not installed so drawContours was simulated with a slice fill; drawContours cost scales with the fill area, not the canvas, so it adds little). At 300 in-window contours that is ~100 ms/tile, ~80 s over 800 tiles - real waste worth the one-line fix, but nowhere near 'pushes a full case well past the 8 min budget' on its own. Two further mitigations the finder missed: the expensive block sits inside `if 200 <= area <= 3500` (detect.py:99), so contours outside the window never allocate a mask; and in the densest lymphocytic tiles RETR_EXTERNAL tends to merge adjacent nuclei into blobs above 3500 px2, which are then skipped - the pathological case is moderate density, not maximum density. No correctness impact.

        return float(values[len(values) // 2])

Reachability is exactly as stated and narrow: weights come from weights_map.get(...,1.0) at :267/:282, so total_weight<=0 requires a scoring.yaml whose grading.confidence_weights are all 0 (or negative). #### 761. weighted_mode's zero-weight fallback reports perfect agreement and biases to the worst sub-score

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/grading.py:97`

When every weight is zero or negative the function returns `tie_breaker(values), 0.0`. tie_breaker defaults to max, so the returned pleomorphism score is the worst observed value, and the disagreement ratio of 0.0 asserts unanimous agreement -- so aggregate_grading_findings never raises the pleo_high_variance flag (line 295) for the one case where the evidence weighting collapsed. This mirrors the weighted_median zero-weight path (line 60), but with an additional wrong-direction clinical consequence.

```
total_weight = sum(weights)
    if total_weight <= 0:
        return tie_breaker(values), 0.0
```
**Impact:** A patch set whose confidences all map to weight 0 yields pleomorphism = max(observed), typically 3, presented as a unanimous result -- one point of Nottingham sum awarded on degenerate input, with the variance flag suppressed.

**Fix:** Return the mode over unweighted counts with disagreement_ratio 1.0 (so pleo_high_variance fires), or raise so the stage lands in needs_human as PRD section 3 requires.

*Verifier note:* Code and behaviour are as described: grading.py:96-98 is `total_weight = sum(weights); if total_weight <= 0: return tie_breaker(values), 0.0`, tie_breaker defaults to max (signature line 76) and aggregate_grading_findings passes tie_breaker=max explicitly at 286, so the returned pleo_score is the worst observed value and the 0.0 dispersion suppresses the pleo_high_variance flag at 295-296 (max_disp 0.30). Both halves of the claim are accurate, including the asymmetry with weighted_median:59-60, which at least returns the middle value rather than the worst. Severity downgraded from medium to low on reachability: every weight the two production callers construct is either the literal 1.5 (pathologist override, lines 267/282) or weights_map.get(..., 1.0), so a zero total requires an operator to set grading.confidence_weights.{low,medium,high} to 0 in configs/scoring.yaml — a plausible edit ('don't count low-confidence patches') but not the shipped state, and it must additionally be true that every patch in the case falls in the zeroed bucket. No current code path reaches it. Fix as proposed (unweighted mode with disagreement_ratio 1.0) is sound; note the empty-values path at line 90 already returns (2, 1.0), so returning a non-zero ratio here is the consistent choice.

#### 728. prob_mean and prob_max are both single-cell values, not region statistics

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/hotspots.py:93`

Both statistics are read at the single grid cell (r, c) of the local maximum: prob_mean is the Gaussian-smoothed value there and prob_max the raw value there. Neither aggregates over the 600x600 um polygon that is persisted. PRD section 2.4 step 6 asks for stats over the returned polygon.

```
"prob_mean": round(float(smoothed[r, c]), 3),
                "prob_max": round(float(prob_filled[r, c]), 3),
```
**Impact:** prob_mean is systematically higher than the true regional mean (it is measured at the peak) and prob_max is systematically lower than the true regional max (it is a smoothed-peak neighbour). The values drive the hotspot tooltips and the pathologist's ranking of which ROIs to keep, and are persisted on hotspots.prob_mean/prob_max as if they were region statistics.

**Fix:** Compute both from the grid cells inside the polygon (mean and max of prob_filled over the box) rather than from the seed cell.

*Verifier note:* The core claim is correct and the lines are exact: prob_mean = smoothed[r,c] (line 93, repeated at 131) and prob_max = prob_filled[r,c] (line 94, repeated at 132) are both read at the single seed cell, never aggregated over the 600x600 um polygon that is persisted, contrary to PRD 03 section 2.4 step 6 ('return polygons in um + stats'). Severity lowered from medium to low because the finder's directional reasoning is wrong on both counts: prob_max is not 'a smoothed-peak neighbour', it is the RAW grid value at the seed cell (a 5x5 maximum_filter on the smoothed field almost always lands on or beside the raw peak — my corner test gave prob_max=0.99, the true regional max, while prob_mean=0.466), so the systematic-underestimate story does not hold. What survives is a labelling/contract defect: two columns named as region statistics carry point samples. Ranking behaviour is unaffected since both are monotone in the seed's probability, and on the degenerate stain-density grid (index 447) the values are meaningless regardless.

#### 596. Density map splats 'unreviewed' candidates weighted by ver_conf, so HPFs are steered by candidates the verifier did not confirm

**Severity:** low · **Category:** PRD deviation · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/hpf.py:64`

PRD 04 §4.1 says only 'confirmed candidates (post-verifier threshold, pre-human)' are splatted. The code also adds every 'unreviewed' candidate with weight ver_conf (or det_conf). With the heuristic verifier the unreviewed class is the majority (ver_conf in [0.40,0.65) or det_conf>=0.70 & ver_conf>=0.35), so field placement is dominated by sub-threshold candidates and not by the figures that will actually be counted.

```
if label == "unreviewed":
    weight = cand.get("ver_conf", cand.get("det_conf", 0.5))
point_grid[gy, gx] += float(weight)
```
**Impact:** Fields are placed over clusters of likely-false candidates; after review the counted density inside them can be lower than in unplaced regions, under-scoring the tumour unless the pathologist re-places manually.

**Fix:** Splat only label == 'mitosis' (weight 1.0) as the PRD specifies; if a soft prior is wanted, make the unreviewed weight a config value defaulting to 0.

*Verifier note:* Quoted evidence exists verbatim: lines 54-66 skip only label == 'not_mitosis' and splat 'unreviewed' with weight = ver_conf (fallback det_conf, then 0.5). PRD 04 4.1 says 'confirmed candidates (post-verifier threshold, pre-human) splatted as points', so including sub-threshold candidates is a real deviation. The label bands the finder cites are correct: worker/mitosis.py:258-262 assigns 'mitosis' at ver_conf >= ver_thresh (0.65 default, line 97) and 'unreviewed' at ver_conf >= review_threshold (0.40, line 96) or det_conf >= 0.70 and ver_conf >= 0.35. The claim that unreviewed is 'the majority' is an empirical assertion I cannot check statically, but the verdict does not depend on it. Severity low is right: the weighting is a soft prior, confirmed figures still carry weight 1.0, and mis-steering the fields is recoverable via re-place / manual drag.

#### 586. greedy_place_hpfs never enforces the PRD 'circle fully inside slide' constraint and is not given slide dimensions

**Severity:** low · **Category:** PRD deviation · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/hpf.py:103`

PRD 04 §4.2 requires each HPF centre c to satisfy 'circle(c, r) fully inside slide, center in mask'. The placement loop only checks the tumour mask and pairwise separation; the function signature has no slide width/height, and the grid origin can be negative (bbox minus 1.5r padding), so centres within 262 um of the slide edge, or with negative coordinates in pass 3, are accepted.

```
while len(placed_hpfs) < count:
    masked_density = working_density * tumor_mask
    max_val = np.max(masked_density)
    ...
    gy, gx = np.unravel_index(np.argmax(masked_density), masked_density.shape)
```
**Impact:** HPFs overhanging the slide boundary count off-slide area in the mm2 denominator (deflating density) and their thumbnails/patches are partly black; pass-3 fields can have negative centre coordinates that the viewer cannot navigate to.

**Fix:** Add slide_w_um/slide_h_um parameters and AND a boundary mask (origin+g*stride within [r, W-r] x [r, H-r]) into tumor_mask before the argmax; drop any fallback that places centres outside that mask.

*Verifier note:* Code fact holds. greedy_place_hpfs signature (lines 103-111) takes density_map, grid_meta, hotspot_polygons_um, count, radius_um and the two separation params only - no slide extent. The only spatial predicate is tumor_mask (lines 124-134, hotspot polygons) plus the pairwise separation check (155, 209); nothing anywhere enforces PRD 04 4.2's 'circle(c, r) fully inside slide'. The grid origin really is bbox - 1.5*radius (lines 40-44), so origin_um can be negative. Severity lowered from medium to low because the impact is overstated for passes 1-2: argmax is taken over working_density*tumor_mask and the loop breaks at max_val <= 0 (144-146, 199-201), and density is nonzero only within radius_um of a splatted candidate (fftconvolve with the disk kernel, line 71), so a pass-1/2 centre can never land in the empty padded margin - it can only approach the slide edge if a real detection sits within ~262 um of that edge. The genuinely unbounded coordinates (negative / arbitrary centres) come from pass 3 (lines 233-251), which is finding 718. Fix direction (boundary mask ANDed into tumor_mask) is right.

#### 609. Strict int/Literal schemas turn benign model outputs (25.5, "2", "25%") into schema-retry exhaustion and fallback scores

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/medgemma.py:24`

TubuleResponse.tubule_percent is int and PleoResponse.pleomorphism_score is Literal[1, 2, 3]. Pydantic v2 rejects 25.5 for an int field ('got a number with a fractional part') and rejects the string '2' for the Literal. Since temperature is 0 the same answer is returned on all three attempts, so any such response is guaranteed to exhaust retries and be replaced by the worker's fabricated 20% / score 2 with confidence 'low'. No coercion (round, strip '%', int()) is attempted before validation.

```
tubule_percent: int = Field(ge=0, le=100, ...)
...
pleomorphism_score: Literal[1, 2, 3] = Field(...)
```
**Impact:** Valid clinical estimates are discarded and silently replaced by placeholder values that then enter the weighted median/mode.

**Fix:** Add field validators that coerce numeric strings/percent strings and round floats before the range check, and count the coercion in the model_invocation audit.

*Verifier note:* Verified against the installed pydantic 2.13.3: TubuleResponse(tubule_percent:int, line 24) rejects 25.5 ('int_from_float') and '25%' ('int_parsing'); PleoResponse.pleomorphism_score: Literal[1,2,3] (line 30) rejects the string '2'. ('25' as a plain numeric string IS accepted in lax mode, and 25.0 coerces to 25 — the finder's three examples are the ones that actually fail.) With MEDGEMMA_TEMPERATURE defaulting to 0.0 (config.py:41) and each retry re-sending a byte-identical prompt+image, the retry loops at lines 196-203 / 212-219 cannot produce a different answer, so any such response deterministically raises SchemaRetryExhaustedError and worker/grading.py:290-291 / 298-299 substitute tubule_percent=20 / pleomorphism_score=2 with confidence='low', which then feed aggregate_grading_findings. No coercion is attempted anywhere. Severity low is right — it is a robustness gap contingent on model output the prompt explicitly asks to be an int, not a defect that fires on well-formed responses. Worth folding into the note: the retry loops are useless for ALL deterministic failures at temperature 0, and `except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValidationError, Exception)` (lines 201/217/233) is just `except Exception` — it also swallows asyncio.CancelledError-class programming errors.

#### 561. Missing qc.yaml silently falls back to hard-coded thresholds and a fake 'default_hash'

**Severity:** low · **Category:** PRD deviation · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/qc_checks.py:23`

If the config file cannot be resolved (e.g. worker started from a directory where the ../../configs walk-up fails), load_qc_config returns an in-code threshold dict and the literal config_hash 'default_hash', and QC proceeds. PRD 00-overview §5.5: 'No clinical numbers in code'; a missing config should be a hard error, not a silent default, and the hash written to audit is meaningless.

```
if not os.path.exists(config_path):
        # Fallback default configuration dictionary
        default_cfg = {
            "tissue_coverage": {"fail_threshold": 0.02, "warn_threshold": 0.05},
            "focus": {"vol_threshold": 5.0, "fail_blurry_ratio": 0.70, "warn_blurry_ratio": 0.30, "sample_max_tiles": 400}
        }
        return default_cfg, "default_hash"
```
**Impact:** QC verdicts can be produced with unversioned thresholds and an audit trail that cannot be tied to a config.

**Fix:** Raise FileNotFoundError; resolve via settings.CONFIGS_DIR (config.py:64) instead of CWD-relative walk-ups.

*Verifier note:* The quoted code exists verbatim at qc_checks.py:23-29: missing file -> in-code threshold dict -> `return default_cfg, "default_hash"`, and load_qc_config's caller (147) passes that straight into run_all_qc_checks' returned config_hash (168), which backend/worker/qc.py:124 writes into the AuditEvent payload. Hard-coded clinical thresholds plus a non-hash audit value do contradict prd/00-overview.md:150. Correcting the finding's stated trigger: the failure scenario as written is wrong. resolve_config_path's walk-up at line 14 is `os.path.dirname(__file__)/../../` — relative to the module file, not the CWD — so it resolves to <repo>/configs/qc.yaml regardless of where the worker was started; no CWD can make it fail. The fallback is therefore only reachable if configs/ is genuinely absent from the deployment (there is no Dockerfile in the repo to confirm what gets packaged, so that is not currently demonstrable). Low is right; the proposed fix (raise, and resolve via settings.CONFIGS_DIR, which does exist at backend/app/core/config.py:64) is still the correct one.

#### 439. config_hash computed with MD5 over raw YAML text instead of SHA256 over canonical JSON

**Severity:** low · **Category:** PRD deviation · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/qc_checks.py:35`

PRD §00 overview §5.5 specifies configs are hashed as 'sha256 of canonical JSON'. load_qc_config instead computes `hashlib.md5(content.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:12]` over the raw YAML file text (not the parsed/canonicalized structure).

```
config_dict = yaml.safe_load(content) or {}
config_hash = hashlib.md5(content.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:12]
return config_dict, config_hash
```
**Impact:** Hash values are neither the specified algorithm nor representation, and are sensitive to irrelevant whitespace/comment changes in the YAML file (since it hashes raw text, not canonical JSON of the semantic config) — any tooling built against the PRD's documented sha256-canonical-JSON contract would be incompatible.

**Fix:** Hash json.dumps(config_dict, sort_keys=True) with hashlib.sha256, matching the contract used by other stages.

*Verifier note:* Code and PRD both check out. qc_checks.py:35 is literally `config_hash = hashlib.md5(content.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:12]` over the raw file text, while prd/00-overview.md:150 says every clinical constant config is 'hashed (sha256 of canonical JSON) into stage_executions.config_hash'. So the deviation is real. Severity lowered from medium to low: the impact is contract/audit-hygiene only. Grep shows qc_checks.py is the ONLY producer of a config_hash in the repo (backend/worker/qc.py:124 drops it into an AuditEvent payload; StageExecution.config_hash at backend/app/models/stage_execution.py:27 is never written), and no consumer parses or re-derives it, so the claimed incompatibility with 'tooling built against the contract' and 'the contract used by other stages' is hypothetical — no other stage computes one. The whitespace-sensitivity complaint is also weak (hashing exact file bytes is a defensible audit choice); the substantive points are MD5 vs SHA-256 and truncation to 48 bits.

#### 549. Focus tissue gating uses np.std > 5 instead of the tissue mask, systematically dropping blurred tiles

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Clinical correctness · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/qc_checks.py:110`

The tissue mask is passed in but only its shape is used; whether a tile counts as 'tissue' is decided by a hard-coded RGB std > 5.0. Heavy defocus reduces local contrast, so the very tiles the check is supposed to catch (low-contrast blurred tissue) can fall under the std gate and are excluded from the denominator, while textured background (dust, pen, black OOB padding) passes the gate. The 5.0 constant is a clinical threshold living in code (PRD 00-overview §5.5).

```
if np.std(tile_rgb) > 5.0:
                gray = cv2.cvtColor(tile_rgb, cv2.COLOR_RGB2GRAY)
                vol = cv2.Laplacian(gray, cv2.CV_64F).var()
```
**Impact:** Blurry-ratio is biased toward 'sharp'; non-tissue tiles dilute the metric; threshold cannot be recalibrated via configs/qc.yaml.

**Fix:** Select sample positions from tissue_mask_1bit (map mask px -> um using the mask's real scale) and drop the std gate, or move it into qc.yaml as `focus.min_tile_std`.

*Verifier note:* The two verifiable claims hold. (a) tissue_mask_1bit is used only for its shape — qc_checks.py:89 `thumb_h, thumb_w = tissue_mask_1bit.shape` is the sole reference in check_focus_sharpness; nothing indexes the mask when choosing positions (97-100). prd/02-stage-v4.1-preprocess-qc.md §3.1 specifies the focus check runs 'on <= 400 sampled tissue tiles', so selecting positions on a blind grid and gating with pixel statistics is a real deviation. (b) The 5.0 at line 110 is a literal, not read from cfg — configs/qc.yaml has no focus.min_tile_std key, so it cannot be recalibrated, which contradicts prd/00-overview.md:150 ('No clinical numbers in code'). Severity lowered from medium to low because the headline mechanism is not supported: np.std over a whole 512x512 H&E tile is dominated by the tissue-vs-background dynamic range, which defocus barely touches (blur is a local high-frequency operation and leaves global std largely intact); a tile with std <= 5/255 is essentially uniform, i.e. blank, not 'blurred tissue'. So the claimed systematic bias of the blurry-ratio toward 'sharp' is speculative. The dilution direction is also arguably backwards from the claim — the std gate is what currently keeps flat glass out of the denominator. Note the same class of in-code clinical constant exists at lines 81-84 as cfg.get() defaults and at 26-27.

#### 630. PDF header stamps render time as 'Report Date', so re-renders of a signed report carry a different date than signed_at

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Data integrity · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/report_pdf.py:150`

The header prints datetime.now() at render. GET /pdf re-renders whenever the blob is missing (line 553-556) and sign re-renders after hashing, so the signed PDF's 'Report Date' is whatever time the last render happened, not the sign time, and two renders of the same signed record produce different bytes (also defeating the PRD 06 section 7 golden-file / byte-identical requirement, which asks for no timestamps in the body).

```
Paragraph(f"Report Date: {datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC')}", body_style)
```
**Impact:** A regenerated copy of a signed report shows a date after the signature, and PDF bytes are non-deterministic so a pdf_sha256 could never be re-verified.

**Fix:** Print report_data['signed_at'] (or created_at for drafts) and pass the timestamp in from the caller; never call now() inside the renderer.

*Verifier note:* Line 150 is exactly `Paragraph(f"Report Date: {datetime.now(timezone.utc)...}", body_style)` — the only 'Report Date' on the document, stamped at render time. Both re-render paths are real: sign_final_report re-renders after sealing (report.py:651-654) and GET /pdf re-renders whenever the GCS blob download fails (report.py:551-556), so a regenerated copy of a signed report shows a date later than the signature (signed_at is separately printed at report_pdf.py:359, so the two visibly disagree). PRD 06 section 7 does require the golden PDF to be byte-identical with 'no timestamps in body, timestamp only from fixture', so this is a stated-requirement violation. Two corrections to the impact wording: (a) there is no pdf_sha256 anywhere in this implementation — Report only has integrity_hash (models/report.py:71), computed over canonical JSON (report.py:613-614), never over PDF bytes — so 'a pdf_sha256 could never be re-verified' describes a field that does not exist; (b) removing now() alone will not make bytes deterministic, since ReportLab's SimpleDocTemplate stamps /CreationDate and a random /ID unless invariant is set. Low severity stands.

...

Low is correct — 8 hex chars is practically unique for lookup, so this is a traceability/faithfulness annoyance rather than a safety defect.

#### 764. Area normalisation uses only the first HPF's radius while counting uses each field's own radius

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Clinical correctness · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/scoring.py:78`

calculate_hpf_mitosis_counts reads `hpf.get("radius_um", 262.0)` per field, so containment is tested against each field's own radius. compute_nottingham_mitotic_score, by contrast, takes a single radius_um scalar, and every caller passes `hpfs[0]["radius_um"]` (routers/mitosis.py:151, 425) or the config default (worker/mitosis.py:407). Since /recompute accepts a per-HPF radius_um from the client (line 404, `h.get("radius_um", 262.0)`), a mixed-radius set is counted correctly but normalised as if every field had field 1's radius.

```
r = float(hpf_copy.get("radius_um", 262.0))
        r_sq = r * r
```
**Impact:** Any HPF set with non-uniform radii produces a wrong area_mm2 and therefore a wrong mitoses/mm2 and possibly a wrong mitotic score, with no warning. The two functions disagree about whether radius is a per-field or a global property.

**Fix:** Have compute_nottingham_mitotic_score take the HPF list (or a list of radii) and sum pi*r_i^2 over the actual fields, rather than n_hpf * pi * r_0^2.

*Verifier note:* Real inconsistency, accurately described. calculate_hpf_mitosis_counts tests containment against each field's own radius (scoring.py:29, inside the per-hpf loop), while compute_nottingham_mitotic_score normalises with a single scalar: line 77-78, `single_hpf_area_mm2 = math.pi * ((radius_um/1000)**2)` then `area_mm2 = n_hpf * single_hpf_area_mm2`. All three callers pass field 1's radius or a config scalar (routers/mitosis.py:151 `hpfs[0]["radius_um"]`, :425 `updated_hpfs[0]["radius_um"]`, worker/mitosis.py:407 config `radius_um`). Mixed radii ARE storable: RecomputePayload.hpfs is `List[Dict[str, Any]]` with no validation (routers/mitosis.py:52) and :404 writes `h.get("radius_um", 262.0)` per row into HpfSite.radius_um (per-row Float column). Cited line 29 is where the quoted evidence lives and the quote is verbatim; I point corrected_line at 78 where the wrong normalisation actually happens. Downgraded medium -> low on likelihood, not on logic: nothing in the repo emits a non-uniform set — the worker places all fields at one config radius, and the frontend round-trips whatever it received. The only trigger is a hand-rolled API client sending per-field radii, and such a client would already see a wrong area from the frontend too, which hard-codes 262.0 in its own area formula (MitosisViewer.tsx:162, `Math.PI * Math.pow(262.0/1000.0, 2)`) rather than using hpf.radius_um that line 140 uses for counting — the same defect mirrored client-side. Proposed fix (sum pi*r_i^2 over actual fields) is correct and would also need MitosisViewer.tsx:162.

#### 363. pN logic mislabels isolated tumour cells (<=0.2 mm) as pN1a and applies an inconsistent node-count cap for micrometastases

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Clinical correctness · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/staging.py:79`

With nodes_positive=1 and largest_meta_mm=0.1 the micrometastasis branch fails (0.2 < 0.1 is false) and the function returns pN1a; AJCC 8th classifies ITC-only nodes as pN0(i+) (the docstring at line 67 even says so, and validate_staging_invariants lists 'pN0(i+)' as valid, but nothing produces it). The explicit is_micrometastasis flag returns pN1mi for any node count, whereas the size-based branch requires nodes_positive <= 3 - two code paths for the same concept with different rules.

```
if is_micrometastasis or (0.2 < largest_meta_mm <= 2.0 and nodes_positive <= 3):  |      return 'pN1mi'  |  if 1 <= nodes_positive <= 3:  |      return 'pN1a'
```
**Impact:** Once callers start passing largest_meta_mm (previous finding) an ITC-only case would be up-staged to pN1a / Stage IIA instead of pN0(i+) / Stage IA.

**Fix:** Add `if largest_meta_mm <= 0.2: return 'pN0(i+)'` before the pN1mi test, drop the redundant is_micrometastasis flag, and cover both boundaries in tests.

*Verifier note:* Both halves reproduced. calculate_ajcc_pn_stage(nodes_examined=12, nodes_positive=1, largest_meta_mm=0.1) returns 'pN1a': line 79's guard is `0.2 < largest_meta_mm <= 2.0`, so an ITC-sized deposit falls through to line 82 and is graded as a macrometastasis, even though the docstring at line 67 and validate_staging_invariants:176 both name 'pN0(i+)' - grep confirms no code path anywhere emits that string. The two-path inconsistency is real too: (12, 5, is_micrometastasis=True) -> 'pN1mi' while (12, 5, largest_meta_mm=1.0) -> 'pN2a', i.e. the explicit flag bypasses the nodes_positive <= 3 cap that the size branch enforces. Severity lowered medium->low for the same reason as 173: no caller passes largest_meta_mm or is_micrometastasis (routers/report.py:278/385/440 and worker/report.py:100 all call calculate_ajcc_pn_stage(n_exam, n_pos)), so this is latent and the finding itself says so. The proposed `if largest_meta_mm <= 0.2: return 'pN0(i+)'` needs a guard for the default largest_meta_mm=0.0 case, otherwise every existing caller with positive nodes would start returning pN0(i+).

#### 565. transform() and fit() use different beta and different hard-coded H&E vectors (copy-paste drift)

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/stain.py:131`

_get_stain_params (fit path) uses beta=0.15 and fallback vectors [0.65,0.70,0.29]/[0.07,0.99,0.11]; transform() uses beta=0.12, a different W_target [0.644,0.717,0.267]/[0.093,0.954,0.283], a different degenerate guard (adds dot(v1,v2) > 0.95), fixed maxC_target [1.85,1.05] vs fit default [1.95,1.10], and a bg_mask cutoff of 0.10. None of these clinical constants come from configs/ and the two halves of the same class disagree, so a slide 'fitted' with one set is transformed with another.

```
def transform(self, source_rgb: np.ndarray, beta: float = 0.12) -> np.ndarray:
        ...
        W_target = np.array([
            [0.644, 0.717, 0.267],   # Hematoxylin (deep royal violet/purple)
            [0.093, 0.954, 0.283]    # Eosin (rich vibrant pink/magenta)
```
**Impact:** Unreproducible normalization behaviour; impossible to hash into config_hash; hard to reason about when the recorded 'transform ignores fit' bug is fixed.

**Fix:** Single source of constants (module-level or configs/stain.yaml) shared by fit and transform; remove the duplicated angle/SVD code from transform once it honours the fitted matrices.

*Verifier note:* Confirmed in substance -- transform() at 131-199 carries a second, independent copy of the Macenko angle/SVD estimation that _get_stain_params (41-77) already implements, with divergent hard-coded constants and none of them sourced from configs/ (I listed configs/: cap_elements.yaml, mitosis.yaml, pricing.yaml, qc.yaml, scoring.yaml, triage.yaml, stain_reference.png -- no stain config, and stain.py imports no config loader). Verified divergences: beta default 0.15 (lines 41, 123) vs 0.12 (line 131); tissue-pixel floor len<10 (line 47) vs len<50 (line 152); percentile bounds parameterised by alpha (56-57) vs hard-coded 1.0/99.0 (160-161); degenerate guard np.abs(max_angle-min_angle) < 0.25 (line 62) vs the same test PLUS np.dot(v1,v2) > 0.95 (line 166). Two of the finder's sub-claims are wrong and should not survive into the writeup: (1) the fallback H&E vectors do NOT drift -- line 167 W_src = [[0.65,0.70,0.29],[0.07,0.99,0.11]] is byte-identical to lines 63-64; the W_target at 144-146 ([0.644,0.717,0.267]/[0.093,0.954,0.283]) is a different thing (a hard-coded re-projection target that replaces the fitted stain_matrix_target), not a drifted copy of the fallback. (2) '[1.95,1.10] fit default' is a misread: line 324 is inside fit_macenko_stain, and is only reached when getattr(normalizer,'max_concentrations') is None -- for PureNumpyMacenkoNormalizer that property (25-26) is always populated after fit(), so it is a tiatoolbox-shim fallback, not fit's default. Likewise the bg_mask cutoff 0.10 (line 196) has no counterpart in fit, so it is not a disagreement. The finder's closing claim 'a slide fitted with one set is transformed with another' is true but is a restatement of the separate transform-ignores-fit defect (transform never touches self.stain_matrix_target / self.max_conc_target, despite tiles.py:97-98 and triage.py:394-397 setting exactly those). Low severity is right: this is duplication/reproducibility debt, not a live wrong-output path on its own.

#### 70. Non-hex client-supplied checksum crashes the stain fit seed derivation

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Crash · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/stain.py:251`

seed_int = int(checksum_sha256[:8], 16) assumes hex. finalize_slide_upload stores req.client_sha256 verbatim (cases.py:339) with no validation; if ingest failed before overwriting it (or a caller retries preprocess before ingest completes), preprocess/qc call fit_macenko_stain with that string and raise ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 16.

```
seed_int = int(checksum_sha256[:8], 16) if checksum_sha256 and checksum_sha256 != "default_checksum" else 42
```
**Impact:** Stage failure with a confusing traceback; edge path.

**Fix:** Validate client_sha256 with a ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ regex at the API, and in stain.py seed from hashlib.sha256(checksum.encode()) so any string works.

*Verifier note:* Line 251 is verbatim as quoted: `seed_int = int(checksum_sha256[:8], 16) if checksum_sha256 and checksum_sha256 != "default_checksum" else 42`. The trust-boundary gap is real: backend/app/schemas/case.py:34 declares `client_sha256: str | None = None` with no validator, and backend/app/routers/cases.py:339 stores it verbatim into Slide.checksum_sha256. Both callers of fit_macenko_stain read that column back (backend/worker/preprocess.py:143 and backend/worker/qc.py:69) and pass it straight in. Normally backend/worker/ingest.py:261-262 (`checksum = calculate_sha256(...); slide_obj.checksum_sha256 = checksum`) overwrites it before preprocess/qc run, so the crash requires ingest to have failed or not yet committed past line 262 — a narrow but genuinely reachable window (retry/out-of-order stage execution). Failure mode is exactly `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 16`. Note the None case is already safe (falsy -> seed 42); only a non-empty non-hex string crashes. Severity low is correct — edge path, hard fail with a confusing traceback, no silent corruption.

#### 62. Hard 50 mm cap on the thumbnail/tissue-mask footprint silently truncates long slides

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/stain.py:261`

thumb_w_um/thumb_h_um are capped at 50,000 um. Scan areas longer than 50 mm (large-format or whole-mount slides) are cropped: the mask, tissue coverage ratio, tissue_area_mm2 and the random patch sampling all ignore tissue beyond 50 mm.

```
thumb_w_um = min(50000.0, slide_w_px * mpp_x)
thumb_h_um = min(50000.0, slide_h_px * mpp_y)
```
**Impact:** Coverage/area under-reported and tissue outside the window never QC'd or normalised on large slides.

**Fix:** Remove the cap (the read is downsampled to 512 px anyway) or make it a config value with a warning.

*Verifier note:* Lines 261-262 are exactly as quoted, and the capped values propagate: they are the w_um/h_um passed to read_region_srgb at 264 (so the 512x512 thumbnail and tissue_mask_1bit only cover the first 50 mm) and they bound the patch sampling window at 286-290 (max_x_um/max_y_um), so no patch is ever drawn beyond 50 mm. Real but narrow — a standard 25x75 mm slide scanned at 0.25 mpp is typically 15-25 mm of scan area, so only large-format/whole-mount scans hit it. One correction to the impact claim: tissue_area_mm2 (worker/preprocess.py:160-161) is already mis-scaled independently of this cap — it multiplies the always-512x512 mask's nonzero count by a fixed (8*mpp) px area, so it does not track slide size at all; the cap changes which tissue is counted, not the (already wrong) scale. Low is correct.

*Also reported at:* `backend/pipeline/stain.py:261` (Thumbnail/Otsu tissue-mask analysis window capped at 50mm from the top-left origin, truncating most standard slides)

#### 595. HoVerNetMitosisVerifier stores threshold but never uses it; the worker's ver_threshold appears wired but has no effect inside verify()

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Improvement · **Location:** `backend/pipeline/verify.py:31`

The constructor accepts threshold (worker passes ver_thresh from mitosis.yaml) and saves it on self, but verify()/_morphometric_nuclear_analysis return a raw probability and never consult self.threshold. The actual decision thresholds live in worker/mitosis.py:258-263. The parameter creates the impression that the verifier's operating point is configured here.

```
self.weights_path = weights_path
self.threshold = threshold
self.device = device
```
**Impact:** Misleading API; a future caller relying on the verifier to gate by threshold gets unfiltered output.

**Fix:** Remove the threshold parameter (and model_version pretence) or return (p_mitosis, p_mitosis >= self.threshold) and have the worker use that.

*Verifier note:* Verified. verify.py:29 `def __init__(self, weights_path=None, threshold=0.50, device='cpu')` and verify.py:31 `self.threshold = threshold`; `grep -n threshold backend/pipeline/verify.py` returns ONLY those two lines — neither verify() (lines 43-67) nor _morphometric_nuclear_analysis (68-201) ever consults self.threshold. Every return path yields a raw probability (0.05/0.10/0.12/0.15/0.20/0.28 early rejects, or the clipped weighted score at the end). The caller worker/mitosis.py:157 constructs `HoVerNetMitosisVerifier(threshold=ver_thresh)` with ver_thresh read from mitosis.yaml:23 (0.65) at mitosis.py:97, then at mitosis.py:255-263 calls `verifier.verify(crop_rgb)` and does its own gating (`if ver_conf >= ver_thresh` / `elif ver_conf >= review_thresh or ...`); `grep -n 'verifier\.' backend/worker/mitosis.py` shows only .verify() and .model_version are ever touched, so the constructor arg is genuinely dead. So the claim is exactly right and low/improvement is the correct severity: no behavioral defect today (the operating point in effect is the worker's 0.65, and the constructor's 0.50 default is inert), only a misleading API for a future caller. One correction to the finder's proposed fix, not the claim: model_version is NOT a pretence — it is consumed at worker/mitosis.py:445 (`"verifier": verifier.model_version`) and surfaced through stage_exec.model_versions (mitosis.py:469, routers/mitosis.py:171), so it must stay. Only the unused threshold parameter is dead.

### Backend: API routers (125)

#### 198. No role-based authorization on any endpoint: a 'viewer' can wipe every case with DELETE /api/v1/cases

**Severity:** critical · **Category:** Security · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/cases.py:66`

Every mutating endpoint (create case, delete one case, clear ALL cases, upload slide, retry stage, approve stage, finalize) only depends on get_current_user, which merely validates that the role string is one of three values. No endpoint in the whole app checks user.role (grep for 'user.role' across backend/app returns only the validity check in auth.py:24). clear_all_cases is an unauthenticated-in-practice bulk destructive endpoint on a clinical system.

```
@router.delete("", status_code=status.HTTP_200_OK)
def clear_all_cases(
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
    user: CurrentUser = Depends(get_current_user)
):
    cases = db.scalars(select(Case)).all()
    for c in cases:
        db.delete(c)
```
**Impact:** Any request with X-User-Role: viewer (or no headers at all, see mock-auth finding) can delete every case, slide, stage execution, grading and report in the database, approve stages, or upload slides. PRD 01 section 2.5 defines role in {pathologist, technician, viewer} for a reason; nothing enforces it.

**Fix:** Add a require_role(*roles) dependency and apply it: pathologist for approve/retry/finalize/delete, pathologist|technician for upload, everyone for reads. Remove DELETE /api/v1/cases entirely (or gate behind ENV != prod) and emit case_deleted audit events.

*Verifier note:* Confirmed. `grep -rn 'user\.role|require_role' backend/` returns zero hits - user.role is never read after construction; the only role logic in the codebase is the membership check at backend/app/core/auth.py:24 ('if role not in [pathologist, technician, viewer]'), which validates the string and nothing else. Every mutating endpoint in this file depends only on get_current_user. It is in fact worse than the finding states: config.py:59 sets MOCK_AUTH_ENABLED=True as a hardcoded default with no env override anywhere in the repo (grep for MOCK_AUTH finds only auth.py:19 and config.py:59), and auth.py:20-22 falls back to DEFAULT_MOCK_USER_ID / DEFAULT_MOCK_ROLE='pathologist' when headers are absent - so DELETE /api/v1/cases (cases.py:66-78) is reachable with a bare, header-less curl and deletes every Case, plus (via cascade='all, delete-orphan' on models/case.py:21-24) every slide, stage_execution, grading and report. Keeping critical: the undefended bulk-destroy endpoint lives in this file, has no confirmation, no audit event, and no environment gate. The proposed require_role dependency is the right fix but is secondary to deleting or gating that endpoint, since role headers are self-asserted under mock auth anyway.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/core/auth.py:24` (No endpoint enforces roles — a 'viewer' can sign reports and wipe the database); `backend/app/routers/cases.py:66` (No endpoint checks role or case ownership; a viewer can wipe every case); `backend/app/routers/report.py:577` (No role enforcement on any clinical transition; stage routers do not even depend on get_current_user; DELETE /cases wipes all cases)

#### 140. Patch image endpoint serves a synthetic drawn 'histology' image as 200 image/png; on-demand path is dead due to missing imports

**Severity:** critical · **Category:** Clinical correctness · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/grading.py:601`

When the GCS patch blob cannot be read, the handler falls into an on-demand WSI extraction path that references `Hotspot` (line 553) and `OPENSLIDE_GLOBAL_LOCK` (line 572) - neither is imported in this module (imports at lines 9-45 contain no Hotspot / openslide_lock). The resulting NameError is swallowed by `except Exception as e: print(...)`, and the function proceeds to draw random ellipses ('glands' and 'nuclei') with PIL and return them as the evidence patch.

```
# Fallback to high-definition histological synthetic patch
    rng = np.random.RandomState(hash(f"{case_id}_{patch_id}") % (2**32))
    ...
    draw.ellipse([gx - gr, gy - gr, gx + gr, gy + gr], fill=(250, 245, 248), outline=(90, 40, 110), width=3)
```
**Impact:** Missing/unauthorised GCS (the established 403 state) yields fake H&E images with HTTP 200, indistinguishable from real evidence in the UI; the on-demand extraction can never succeed. hash() is also process-randomised so the image differs per API process.

**Fix:** Return 404 when the artifact is missing; delete the synthetic drawing; either import Hotspot and OPENSLIDE_GLOBAL_LOCK or delete the on-demand branch (see separate perf finding).

*Verifier note:* Both halves verified. (a) Dead branch: grep for 'Hotspot' in grading.py returns exactly one hit — the use at line 553 — with no import; imports are lines 9-45 plus the function-local imports at 534-536 (extract_10x_patch, PureNumpyMacenkoNormalizer, openslide). Same for OPENSLIDE_GLOBAL_LOCK at 572: it lives in backend/app/core/openslide_lock.py and is correctly imported by tiles.py:26, mitosis.py:27, cases.py:21, triage.py:28 and worker/grading.py:33, but not here. Line 553 executes unconditionally inside `if os.path.exists(local_slide_path)`, so even a fully successful multi-GB download always dies on NameError, swallowed by `except Exception as e: print(...)` at 596-597. (b) The handler then always reaches 601-632 and returns PIL-drawn ellipses as image/png with HTTP 200; the frontend renders these as the evidence patch (GradingReviewWorkspace.tsx:960-961, 1377, 1592) and its onError placeholder never fires because the response is a valid 200 PNG. hash() on a str is PYTHONHASHSEED-randomised, so the same patch differs across API processes — the 'evidence' is not even stable. Critical is right: a pathologist approves patch-level tubule/pleomorphism against fabricated imagery, and those approvals are what unlock the confirm gate at 703-707.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/grading.py:553` (Synthetic microscopy images are generated when extraction fails and then cached into GCS as the real patch; grading on-demand extraction always fails due to missing imports); `backend/app/routers/grading.py:553` (On-demand patch image re-extraction path uses undefined names (Hotspot, OPENSLIDE_GLOBAL_LOCK) and always silently falls back to a fabricated synthetic image)
