```
**Impact:** Scenario: sign report -> pathologist re-opens grading, changes a score, confirms grading again (PRD 05 'reopen stage' flow). Report worker rewrites narrative/staging/PDF of a report whose status is still 'signed' and whose integrity_hash was computed over the old narrative; the hash no longer matches the content, and the signed PDF blob in GCS is overwritten. PRD 06 §4 requires signed rows to be immutable and amendments to create version+1.

**Fix:** In run_report: if report_record.status in ('signed','amended') create a new draft version row (or fail the stage) instead of mutating; in confirm_grading refuse to re-queue report when report.status == 'signed'.

*Verifier note:* Verified end to end. confirm_grading_stage (grading.py:666-780) has no precondition on report state: gates 1-3 check type_confirmed and patch/HPF review flags only, and those remain satisfied after signing (overrides persist, type_confirmed_by stays set, case.status='done' is never consulted). Lines 776-780 unconditionally reset the existing report StageExecution to status='queued' with started_at/completed_at/error cleared. worker/main.py:53-71 polls exactly `status == 'queued'` and dispatches HANDLERS['report'] = run_report (main.py:23-31). worker/report.py:66-83 loads the existing Report row and never inspects report_record.status, then overwrites report_record.staging (100-106), report_record.narrative (140), uploads a fresh PDF to the same blob `cases/{case_id}/report/{pdf_filename}` (208-215) and sets report_record.pdf_path (218). report.py's own write endpoints DO guard on signed (routers/report.py:348, 418, 492, 588), which makes the worker path the only unguarded mutation of a signed report - confirming this is an oversight, not intent. Damage is exactly as described: integrity_hash (routers/report.py:598-614) is computed over narrative + staging, both of which run_report rewrites, so a report whose status is still 'signed' now carries a hash that does not match its content, and the signed PDF blob in GCS is replaced. Critical severity stands.

#### 532. PDF renderer substitutes a fabricated Nottingham grade (2/2/2, sum 6, tubules 45%) when grading is missing or any score is 0/None

**Severity:** critical · **Category:** Clinical correctness · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/report.py:164`

render_and_upload_report_pdf builds ng_data with 'x if grading and grading.x else 2' fallbacks. This is called from update_report_data (report.py:402) and from sign_final_report (report.py:658), so a report can be drafted and signed before the grading stage exists or when the Grading row has NULL scores (the CheckConstraint allows all-NULL rows). The same fallback pattern is copy-pasted at lines 261, 426 and 497 so the JSON API also reports grade 2. This is distinct from the biomarker/margin column defaults already recorded: it fabricates the primary histologic grade in the signed PDF.

```
"grade": grading.grade if grading and grading.grade else 2,
"tubule_score": grading.tubule_score if grading and grading.tubule_score else 2,
"tubule_percent": grading.tubule_percent if grading and grading.tubule_percent is not None else 45.0,
```
**Impact:** A signed clinical PDF can state Nottingham Grade 2 (6/9) for a case that was never graded.

**Fix:** Render 'Not assessed' / block signing when Grading is missing or any component score is NULL; remove all four copies of the fallback and centralise grade lookup in one helper that raises.

*Verifier note:* Verified at report.py:164-169 (render path), 261-266 (GET/JSON), 426-431 (resynthesize) and 497-502 (regenerate) - four identical copies. models/grading.py:20-25 makes tubule_percent/tubule_score/pleo_score/mitotic_score/nottingham_sum/grade all nullable, and the CheckConstraint at grading.py:45-50 evaluates to NULL (i.e. passes) when any operand is NULL, so an all-NULL Grading row is legal; a case with no Grading row at all is equally reachable because _ensure_report_record (line 113) creates the Report on demand and sign_final_report (577-664) has NO preconditions whatsoever - no grading-exists check, no confirmed-stages check, contrary to prd/06-stage-v4.5-report.md:64. pipeline/report_pdf.py:202 and :250 then print 'NOTTINGHAM HISTOLOGIC GRADE 2' and 'Grade 2 (Elston-Ellis Sum: 6/9)' into the signed PDF, plus 'Tubule Formation ... 45%'. Critical stands: fabricated primary histologic grade in a signed clinical document. Two refinements to the finding: (a) the falsy-0 half of the claim is theoretical - 0 is not a producible Nottingham score, the real trigger is missing/NULL; (b) there is a FIFTH copy the finder missed at report.py:144, and it is worse - 'GRADE {grading.grade if grading else 2}' has no None guard, so a Grading row with NULL grade writes the literal string 'NOTTINGHAM HISTOLOGIC GRADE None.' into report.narrative.diagnosis_line.

#### 294. POST /report/sign has no preconditions: signs before pipeline confirmation, ignores password_or_pin, and enforces no role

**Severity:** critical · **Category:** Clinical correctness · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/report.py:588`

sign_final_report only refuses if the report is already signed. It does not check that the report StageExecution is awaiting_review, that grading is confirmed/type_confirmed, that manual fields are filled, or the caller's role; the router has no get_current_user dependency at all. SignReportPayload.password_or_pin (line 92) is accepted and never read.

```
if report.status == "signed":
    raise HTTPException(...)
now_utc = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
...
report.status = "signed"
```
**Impact:** Scenario: create case, upload slide, immediately POST /stages/report/sign with any name -> _ensure_report_record fabricates a grade-2 invasive carcinoma report (previous finding), it is sealed with an integrity hash, case.status becomes 'done'. PRD 06 §4 line 64 requires: all required manual fields filled, histologic type confirmed, all stages confirmed, signer role = pathologist, else 422.

**Fix:** Implement the precondition checklist and return 422 with missing items; require role == 'pathologist' via get_current_user; either verify password_or_pin or remove it.

*Verifier note:* Verified. sign_final_report (577-662) contains exactly one guard — `if report.status == "signed"` at 588-592 — then hashes and seals (594-622), sets case.status='done' (624-625), and force-marks the report StageExecution 'confirmed' (628-635) without ever reading its prior status. No check that grading exists or is type_confirmed (grading is fetched at 586 but used only for the PDF re-render at 658), no check of other stages, no required-field check. The router has no auth dependency at all: every handler's signature is `(..., db: Session = Depends(get_db))` (330, 339, 410, 486, 534, 567, 577, 666), whereas cases.py/tiles.py/audit.py do use `get_current_user`, and main.py:43-49 adds no global dependency — so `CurrentUser.role` ('pathologist' | 'technician' | 'viewer', auth.py:5-8) is never consulted here. `password_or_pin` is declared at line 92 and sent by the frontend (api.ts:629) but grep finds zero reads of it in backend/. The stated attack path holds: _ensure_report_record fabricates the row (index 293), so POST /sign on a fresh case produces a sealed grade-2 invasive-carcinoma report. PRD 06 §4 requires 422 with a missing-items list on any of these violations. Critical confirmed; not a duplicate of 293 — that one is the fabricated content, this one is the absent gate.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/report.py:588` (Sign-off gate enforces none of the PRD preconditions; PIN ignored, NPI defaults to a hard-coded number); `backend/app/routers/report.py:577` (POST /report/sign has none of the PRD's required preconditions — no required-field check, no type-confirmed gate, no all-stages-confirmed check, no role check); `backend/app/routers/report.py:588` (Sign has none of the PRD preconditions: no required-field check, no histologic-type confirmation gate, no stage-confirmed gate; password_or_pin ignored); `frontend/components/viewer/ReportWorkspace.tsx:326` (Report can be signed with no pipeline output and no precondition gate (client or server))

#### 496. /report/amend mutates the existing (single) report row in place instead of creating a new version+1 draft

**Severity:** critical · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/report.py:688`

PRD section 5: 'Amendment path: new row version+1 referencing the same case (status draft), original stays signed.' amend_signed_report instead appends a note to an `amendments` JSON array on the same row, sets `report.status = "amended"`, and then directly `setattr`s arbitrary fields from `payload.updated_fields` onto that same signed row — overwriting the original signed content that was supposed to remain immutable and downloadable.

```
current_amendments.append(amendment_entry)
report.amendments = current_amendments
report.status = "amended"

# Apply updated fields if provided
for k, v in payload.updated_fields.items():
    if hasattr(report, k):
        setattr(report, k, v)
```
**Impact:** The original signed report is destroyed the moment an amendment is submitted — v1 is no longer downloadable as-signed (the PRD acceptance criterion 'v1 stays downloadable' is unmet), and `payload.updated_fields` lets a caller overwrite any attribute on the ORM object by name (e.g. `status`, `signed_by`, `integrity_hash`, `pdf_path`) with no allow-list, since `hasattr(report, k)` is true for essentially every column.

**Fix:** Create a new Report row with `version = old.version + 1`, `status='draft'`, copying forward the relevant fields, and never write to a row once `status == 'signed'`; validate `updated_fields` against an explicit allow-list of editable field names.

*Verifier note:* Verified. report.py:665-712 amend_signed_report loads the single existing row via _ensure_report_record (line 672), appends an entry to report.amendments (688-689), sets report.status='amended' (690), then does an unrestricted `for k, v in payload.updated_fields.items(): if hasattr(report,k): setattr(report,k,v)` (693-695). No new row is created and none can be: app/models/report.py declares `case_id ... primary_key=True` with no `version` column, so the schema physically allows exactly one report row per case — the PRD's 'new row version+1' (06-stage-v4.5-report.md:96, DB DDL lines 79-88 with `version int` + `UNIQUE(case_id, version)`) is unimplemented, as is the reject_signed_update trigger (PRD 90-94). The setattr loop is a genuine unfiltered write: hasattr is true for status, signed_by, signed_at, integrity_hash, pdf_path, case_id, so `updated_fields={"status":"signed"}` re-seals the row after the amendment marker was written 3 lines earlier. Two aggravators the finder did not name, both strengthening it: (a) after amend flips status to 'amended', update_report_data (348), resynthesize_narrative (418) and regenerate-narrative (492) all guard only on `== "signed"`, so the whole draft-edit surface reopens on the signed row; (b) render_and_upload_report_pdf writes to a version-less deterministic blob `cases/{case_id}/report/CAP_Report_{case_id[:8]}.pdf` (231, 542), so any post-amendment re-render overwrites the signed v1 PDF in GCS. The acceptance criterion 'amendment flow produces v2 while v1 stays downloadable' (PRD:118) is unmet on both the DB and the artifact. Critical stands. Line 692 is the comment line; the defect spans 688-695.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/models/report.py:17` (reports table uses case_id as primary key with no version column — the required amendment/versioning model is architecturally impossible); `frontend/components/viewer/ReportWorkspace.tsx:222` (Amendment flow is a no-op that mutates the signed row instead of creating v+1)

#### 325. Synthetic microscopy images are served as clinical evidence and cached into GCS as if real

**Severity:** critical · **Category:** Clinical correctness · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/triage.py:430`

When extraction fails, get_hotspot_thumbnail generates a procedurally drawn patch and then uploads it to the canonical patch key, so every later request returns the fake as the real thumbnail. Same pattern: mitosis.py:196-203 (crop), mitosis.py:332-345 (HPF, cached), grading.py:601-632 (evidence patch with drawn glands), worker/mitosis.py:198-205 (synthetic tiles fed to the detector, producing fake candidates), worker/triage.py:434-441. No response header or flag marks them synthetic.

```
if extracted_bytes is None: extracted_bytes = generate_synthetic_microscopic_patch(mag, stain, ...) ... upload_blob_from_bytes(settings.GCS_ARTIFACTS_BUCKET, patch_blob, extracted_bytes, "image/png")
```
**Impact:** A pathologist may grade tubules/pleomorphism or verify mitoses on drawings; once cached the fake permanently replaces the real artifact for the case.

**Fix:** Return 404/503 on extraction failure; never persist fallbacks; restrict synthetic generators to ENV=test.

*Verifier note:* Confirmed. triage.py:429-430 `if extracted_bytes is None: extracted_bytes = generate_synthetic_microscopic_patch(mag, stain, f"{case_id}_{hotspot_id}_{mag}_{stain}")` and then 433-441 uploads that same buffer to the canonical `patch_blob` = `cases/{case_id}/triage/patches/{hotspot_id}_{mag}_{stain}.png` (280) — the identical key the cache-hit path at 281-283 reads first, so the drawing permanently displaces the real artifact for that case and is served with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400` and no marker of any kind. The generator (175-263) deliberately draws glands, nuclei, karyorrhectic dots and explicit 'mitotic figures' (251-258), i.e. it fabricates exactly the features being scored. Corroborating sites check out with one correction: routers/mitosis.py:332-345 does generate synthetic and cache it to hpf_blob (same defect); worker/mitosis.py:198-205 does feed synthetic tiles to detector.detect (207) producing fabricated candidates; worker/triage.py:433-441 does substitute flat synthetic patches. But routers/grading.py:601-632 only *returns* the drawn-gland patch — it is never uploaded — so the 'cached' half of that one sub-claim is wrong; the serving-as-evidence half holds. routers/mitosis.py:196-203 likewise returns without caching. The main finding at the cited location is unaffected. Critical stands for a clinical-grading system.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/mitosis.py:193` (API endpoints return fabricated histology images with HTTP 200 on storage errors and cache them permanently); `backend/app/routers/cases.py:413` (Case thumbnail returns HTTP 200 with a synthetic pink square when the slide cannot be decoded)

#### 279. confirm_triage unconditionally re-queues mitosis attempt 1; a second confirm (or a confirm after mitosis review) wipes pathologist mitosis labels

**Severity:** critical · **Category:** Data integrity · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/triage.py:570`

confirm_triage does not check stage_exec.status, so it can be called on a stage that is already 'confirmed'. It then finds the existing mitosis attempt 1 row and resets it to 'queued' regardless of whether that row is running, awaiting_review or confirmed. The mitosis worker starts with `db.execute(delete(Detection)...)`/`delete(HpfSite)` (worker/mitosis.py:412-413), so every pathologist label, bulk-reject, add_candidate row and HPF placement is destroyed and replaced by fresh model output.

```
else:
    next_exec.status = "queued"
    next_exec.input_ref = input_data
    next_exec.started_at = None
    next_exec.completed_at = None
    next_exec.error = None
```
**Impact:** Scenario: pathologist confirms triage, reviews 200 mitosis candidates, then double-clicks Confirm on the triage page (or the UI retries a timed-out POST). Mitosis row goes back to queued, worker deletes all detections/hpf_sites and re-detects; all clinical review work is silently lost. If mitosis is currently running, the row is re-queued while the handler is still active -> double execution and IntegrityError on the Detection PK.

**Fix:** Guard the transition: reject with 409 unless stage_exec.status == 'awaiting_review'; never reset an existing next-stage row whose status is not queued/failed - create a new attempt instead (and make the mitosis handler refuse to delete rows with label_source='pathologist').

*Verifier note:* Verified end to end. confirm_triage (triage.py:479-595) selects the latest triage StageExecution with no status check (484-495) and unconditionally sets stage_exec.status='confirmed' (532), then at 544-558 looks up the mitosis row with attempt==1 and, if found, resets it to queued regardless of its current status (569-574: `else: next_exec.status = "queued"` ... started_at/completed_at/error=None). The queued row is genuinely consumed: worker/main.py:54-70 polls `status == "queued"` and dispatches HANDLERS['mitosis'] = run_mitosis; run_mitosis then executes `db.execute(delete(Detection).where(Detection.case_id == case_obj.id))` and the same for HpfSite at worker/mitosis.py:412-413, before re-inserting model rows with label_source default 'model' (424). Pathologist state really is destroyed: routers/mitosis.py:373 sets label_source='pathologist' on review, 456/508 create m_user_NNN rows with label_source='pathologist', 555 sets 'pathologist_bulk'. Nothing anywhere filters the delete by label_source. So a second POST /api/v1/stages/triage/confirm after mitosis review silently wipes all labels, user-added candidates and HPF placements. Cited line 569 is the `else:`; the reset begins at 570. One sub-claim is weaker than stated: the 'IntegrityError on Detection PK' from double execution is speculative — the worker deletes all detections at the start of each run, so a PK clash needs true concurrent handler execution; the re-queue-while-running race itself is real (worker/main.py:76-84 only writes status when its stale in-session copy reads 'running'), so the row can be left queued and re-run. Severity critical stands: silent, unrecoverable loss of clinical review work on an unauthenticated endpoint (no auth dependency on this router; main.py:46 includes it with no dependencies).

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/triage.py:532` (Confirm has no status gating and re-queues mitosis attempt 1 on every call); `backend/app/routers/mitosis.py:648` (Confirm endpoints never check the stage is awaiting_review; confirming while a worker is still running causes a lost update); `frontend/components/viewer/TriageViewer.tsx:602` (Triage 'Confirm & Move to Stage 4' stays enabled after confirmation; re-confirming re-queues mitosis and the worker wipes all detections/HPF review)

#### 202. Multipart upload spools the whole WSI to API-server local disk and blocks the event loop for the entire GCS transfer

**Severity:** high · **Category:** Performance · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/cases.py:115`

upload_slide_file is `async def` but calls the synchronous google-cloud-storage upload_from_file inline, so the asyncio event loop is blocked for the duration of a multi-GB upload (every other request, including tile serving, hangs). Starlette's multipart parser spools UploadFile to a SpooledTemporaryFile with spool_max_size = 1 MiB, so a 3 GB slide is written in full to the API server's temp directory before this line runs; the docstring's 'zero local persistence' is false. On Cloud Run /tmp is in-memory, so the container needs >3 GB RAM per concurrent upload. PRD 01 section 2.2 specifies signed resumable browser->GCS uploads in 32 MiB chunks precisely to avoid this; the frontend (frontend/lib/api.ts:96) uses this endpoint, not upload-url/finalize.

```
async def upload_slide_file(
    ...
    await file.seek(0)
    upload_blob_from_file(
        bucket_name=settings.GCS_RAW_BUCKET,
        blob_name=blob_name,
        file_obj=file.file,
```
**Impact:** Uploading one slide freezes the API for all users for minutes; large slides OOM the container; a dropped connection loses the whole upload with no resume (PRD acceptance: 'survives one forced disconnect, resumes').

**Fix:** Either make the endpoint `def` (thread pool) as a stopgap, or implement PRD 2.2: blob.create_resumable_upload_session(origin=FRONTEND_ORIGIN, size=size_bytes) in get_slide_upload_url and have the browser PUT chunks directly to GCS, then call finalize.

*Verifier note:* Confirmed on all three limbs. (1) Event-loop block: upload_slide_file is `async def` (cases.py:96) and calls upload_blob_from_file at cases.py:115, which is plain synchronous blob.upload_from_file (app/core/gcs.py:41-46) - no run_in_threadpool, no asyncio.to_thread - so the whole loop stalls for the transfer. Note the endpoint has no await-able reason to be async other than `await file.seek(0)`, so the `def`-instead-of-`async def` stopgap the finder proposes really is a one-word fix. (2) Local spooling: Starlette's MultiPartParser spools UploadFile to SpooledTemporaryFile with spool_max_size = 1 MiB, so the docstring's 'zero local persistence' (cases.py:102) is false for any real WSI; file.file passed at 118 is that spooled temp file. (3) The unused-path claim holds: frontend/lib/api.ts opens POST .../slide/upload (xhr.open at api.ts:96) - get_slide_upload_url/finalize_slide_upload (cases.py:302-364) are dead in the UI, and generate_signed_upload_url is a plain signed PUT, not create_resumable_upload_session, so PRD 01 line 80's 'survives one forced disconnect, resumes' acceptance criterion is unmet. Severity high stands.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/cases.py:115` (Async upload endpoint blocks the event loop with a synchronous multi-GB GCS upload; no size or type validation); `backend/app/routers/cases.py:96` (Slide upload endpoint is `async def` but performs a blocking multi-GB GCS upload on the event loop)

#### 206. approve_case_stage ignores the state machine: confirms any status, sets no reviewer, and re-queues the next stage on every call

**Severity:** high · **Category:** PRD deviation · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/cases.py:241`

PRD 00 section 5.2 allows only awaiting_review -> confirmed, and the DDL has reviewed_by/reviewed_at for exactly this. The endpoint marks the latest attempt 'confirmed' regardless of whether it is queued, running, failed or already confirmed, never sets reviewed_by/reviewed_at (grep shows neither is written anywhere in cases.py), unconditionally sets case_obj.status = 'open' at line 283, and every invocation creates a fresh queued StageExecution for the next stage (attempt+1). The audit event_type is 'stage_approved' whereas the PRD minimum set and triage.py:579/mitosis.py:678 use 'stage_confirmed'.

```
current_stage = db.scalars(stmt).first()
if current_stage:
    current_stage.status = "confirmed"
...
new_stage = StageExecution(
    case_id=case_id, stage=next_stage_name, attempt=next_attempt, status="queued",
```
**Impact:** Double-clicking Approve (or a retried POST) queues duplicate triage/mitosis/grading runs that overwrite each other's GCS artifacts and Vertex spend; a failed or still-running preprocess can be 'confirmed' with no output; the audit trail cannot say who approved (only the forgeable actor).

**Fix:** Require current_stage.status == 'awaiting_review' (409 otherwise), set reviewed_by=user.id and reviewed_at, refuse if a queued/running next-stage row already exists, and use event_type='stage_confirmed'.

*Verifier note:* Every sub-claim checks out. cases.py:236-243: the query orders by attempt.desc() and sets `current_stage.status = "confirmed"` with no status check at all — a queued/running/failed/already-confirmed row is confirmed just the same. `grep -n 'reviewed_by\|reviewed_at' backend/app/routers/cases.py` returns nothing, while the column exists (models/stage_execution.py:32-33) and siblings do write it (triage.py:533-534, mitosis.py:649-650, grading.py:758-759, report.py:634-635). Line 283 is `case_obj.status = "open"` unconditionally. Lines 261-281: the next-stage block computes next_attempt = existing_next.attempt + 1 and inserts a fresh queued row on EVERY call, with no check for an already queued/running next stage — worker/main.py:75-88 polls status=='queued' one row at a time, so two clicks = two real executions of triage/mitosis writing the same cases/{case_id}/<stage>/ GCS prefix. Line 288 emits event_type='stage_approved'; PRD 00 line 153 lists 'stage_confirmed' in the minimum audit set and triage.py:579 / mitosis.py:678 use it, so the audit stream is genuinely inconsistent. PRD 00 section 5.2 is explicit: 'awaiting_review -> confirmed'. Reachable from the UI: frontend/lib/api.ts:112 approveStage, called at frontend/app/cases/[id]/page.tsx:115 and :158 with no client-side debounce. High is right — it is a state-machine bypass plus a duplicate-Vertex-run bug plus a missing attribution field on a clinical audit record.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/cases.py:241` (approve_case_stage confirms any status and queues the next stage even when QC failed or the next stage is running); `backend/app/routers/cases.py:243` (Generic approve endpoint confirms any stage regardless of state and bypasses stage-specific persistence)

The QC handler sets stage 'failed' and case.status='needs_rescan' on a hard fail (qc.py:110-114). **Fix:** Compute next attempt as in retry_case_stage (max(attempt)+1), or key ingest executions by slide_id.

*Verifier note:* Confirmed at both cited sites: cases.py:344-350 (finalize_slide_upload) and cases.py:135-145 (upload_slide_file) both hardcode attempt=1 for stage='ingest'. StageExecution declares UniqueConstraint('case_id','stage','attempt', name='uq_stage_execution_attempt') (backend/app/models/stage_execution.py:39). A UNIQUE table constraint is enforced on SQLite too (unlike the FK issue in index 201), so the second upload to the same case raises IntegrityError on db.commit() on both backends; no try/except and no IntegrityError handler exists anywhere in the router or in app/main.py, so it surfaces as an unhandled 500 and the Slide row added at 336-342 rolls back with it. This is the exact needs_rescan recovery path from PRD 02 line 75. Note the fix already exists two functions up: retry_case_stage computes next_attempt = max(attempt)+1 (cases.py:176-181), so the inconsistency is clear. Severity high is fair - it is a guaranteed 500 on a documented workflow, not a data-corruption bug.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/cases.py:348` (Slide finalize/upload always creates ingest attempt=1, so a second slide on a case violates uq_stage_execution_attempt and returns HTTP 500)

#### 205. GET /cases/{id} orders stages by started_at, so the frontend picks the oldest attempt and never shows retried stages progressing

**Severity:** high · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/cases.py:438`

stages are ordered by started_at ASC. Queued rows have started_at NULL (set only when the worker starts them, worker/main.py:67-68). Postgres sorts NULLs last for ASC, SQLite sorts them first, so ordering differs by backend, and in either backend an older attempt that already ran sorts before a retried attempt once it starts. frontend/app/cases/[id]/page.tsx:69-73 and 92-95 use stages.find(s => s.stage === X), i.e. the FIRST row per stage, so after 'Retry' the UI keeps rendering attempt 1's 'failed' status while attempt 2 runs and completes (StageRail.tsx:39 sorts by attempt desc, page.tsx does not).

```
stages = db.scalars(select(StageExecution).where(StageExecution.case_id == case_id).order_by(StageExecution.started_at.asc())).all()
```
**Impact:** Retry appears to do nothing on the case workspace page: the auto-advance logic and isIngestFailed/isPreprocessDone flags stay pinned to the stale attempt, blocking the pathologist's workflow.

**Fix:** Order by (stage, attempt DESC) or return only the latest attempt per stage (or order by attempt.desc() and have the frontend rely on that); at minimum add a deterministic tiebreak.

*Verifier note:* Confirmed, line-accurate. cases.py:438 orders by StageExecution.started_at.asc() with no tiebreak, and started_at is nullable and set only when the worker picks the row up (worker/main.py:68-69 sets status='running' and started_at=now). NULL ordering does differ (Postgres NULLS LAST for ASC, SQLite NULLS FIRST) - and worker/main.py:59 itself uses an explicit .nulls_first(), showing the author knew the default is backend-dependent. Independently of NULL handling, once the retried attempt starts, its started_at is greater than the old attempt's, so attempt 1 always sorts first. frontend/app/cases/[id]/page.tsx:68-72 and 89-91 use stages.find(s => s.stage === X), i.e. the first matching row, so isIngestFailed / isPreprocessDone / the auto-advance chain stay pinned to the stale attempt - while StageRail.tsx:39 does sort by attempt desc and picks sorted[0], producing two components disagreeing about the same stage on the same screen. Retry is reachable from both handleRetryIngest (page.tsx:104) and StageRail's handleRetry, so the user-visible 'Retry does nothing' symptom is real. Severity high is fair: workflow-blocking UI bug with no data loss.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/cases.py:438` (Case detail sorts stage rows by started_at; NULL ordering differs between SQLite and Postgres and the UI picks the first matching row, so a retried stage shows the old attempt on Postgres); `frontend/app/cases/[id]/page.tsx:91` (Case page reads the FIRST stage attempt, StageRail reads the LATEST: stale failed state after retry)

#### 600. Unvalidated override score values are persisted and make every later GET of the case 500

**Severity:** high · **Category:** Crash · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/grading.py:277`

ConfirmGradingPayload.overrides is Dict[str, Any]; the confirm handler only checks len(justification) (lines 717-725) and then merges the whole dict into grading_record.overrides (line 752). _build_grading_stage_data_dict later does overrides.get('tubule', {}).get('score', ...) and feeds it straight into calculate_nottingham_grade (line 282) with no type or 1-3 range check. A payload override of {'tubule': {'score': 'three', 'justification': 'long enough text here'}} passes confirm, and every subsequent GET /api/v1/stages/grading/{case_id} (and both review endpoints, which call the same builder) raises TypeError -> HTTP 500 for that case permanently. An integer like 7 passes silently and produces current.nottingham_sum=11 with grade 3 (no invariant check on the 'current' block). The same applies to overrides['mitotic']['score'] and overrides['tubule']['percent'].

```
eff_tubule_score = overrides.get("tubule", {}).get("score", dyn_agg["tubule_score"])
...
eff_sum, eff_grade = calculate_nottingham_grade(eff_tubule_score, eff_pleo_score, eff_mitotic_score, scoring_cfg)
```
**Impact:** A malformed or malicious confirm bricks the case page; out-of-range overrides are displayed as a valid 'current' grade.

**Fix:** Type the override entries with a Pydantic model (score: int ge=1 le=3, percent: float 0-100, justification: str min_length=10) and reject unknown component keys; in the builder run validate_grading_invariants on the effective values and surface a flag instead of raising.

*Verifier note:* Verified end to end. ConfirmGradingPayload.overrides is `Dict[str, Any]` (line 93) — Pydantic validates nothing inside it, unlike the sibling scalar fields which carry ge=1/le=3. The confirm handler's only override gate is the justification-length loop at 717-725, which skips 'patches'/'hpfs' and otherwise reads `override_info.get('justification','')`; the whole dict is then merged verbatim at 751-753. The builder consumes it unguarded at 277-282: eff_tubule_score/eff_pleo_score/eff_mitotic_score come straight from overrides.get(...).get('score', ...) and go into calculate_nottingham_grade, whose first act is `tubule_score + pleo_score + mitotic_score` (pipeline/grading.py:149). A stored score of 'three' therefore raises TypeError inside _build_grading_stage_data_dict, which is called unprotected from GET /{case_id} (line 363), POST /patches/review (line 434), POST /hpfs/review (line 519) and from confirm itself (line 699) — so the case is bricked for every one of those endpoints, including any retry of confirm, matching the claim. The out-of-range case is also real: nothing calls validate_grading_invariants on the 'current' block (contrast lines 727-735 which validate only the payload's own scalar scores), so score=7 yields current.nottingham_sum=11, grade=3 rendered as a valid grade. Additional nearby hazard the finder did not mention: a non-dict override value (e.g. 'tubule': 5) makes line 720's .get() raise AttributeError -> 500 at confirm time. High is correct.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/grading.py:720` (Malformed override entries in the confirm payload raise AttributeError -> HTTP 500)

#### 138. Confirm/sign-off endpoint has no authentication, no role check and no stage-state gating; double sign-off silently overwrites signed values

**Severity:** high · **Category:** Security · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/grading.py:667`

No endpoint in this router depends on get_current_user (grep: only Depends(get_db)). The signer is taken from the request body (`reviewed_by`, default 'user_pathologist_001', lines 65/79/94). confirm_grading_stage never checks stage_exec.status (works while 'running', 'failed' or already 'confirmed'), runs even when stage_exec is None (`if stage_exec:` at line 756), and on a second call overwrites the already-signed Grading row and re-queues the report stage (line 777). A worker still 'running' will later set status back to awaiting_review, clobbering the confirmation.

```
@router.post("/confirm")
def confirm_grading_stage(payload: ConfirmGradingPayload, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    ...
    grading_record.type_confirmed_by = payload.reviewed_by
```
**Impact:** Any caller (viewer/technician role, or unauthenticated once mock auth is off) can sign a Nottingham grade under any name; signed rows are mutable; audit attribution is client-controlled.

**Fix:** Add Depends(get_current_user), require role == 'pathologist', use user.id as actor; require stage_exec exists and status == 'awaiting_review'; reject if already confirmed (409).

*Verifier note:* Every fact checks out. grep 'Depends(' in grading.py returns only Depends(get_db) at lines 346/368/441/519/637/667 — no get_current_user, although that dependency exists (backend/app/core/auth.py:10) and IS used by cases.py, tiles.py:208 and audit.py:20. Actor comes from the body: reviewed_by defaults at lines 65, 79, 94 and is written straight to grading_record.type_confirmed_by (748), stage_exec.reviewed_by (759) and every AuditEvent.actor (804). confirm_grading_stage never reads stage_exec.status, so it runs on 'running'/'failed'/already-'confirmed'; `if stage_exec:` (756) means a case with no grading StageExecution row still signs the Grading row and queues report (768-780) — mitosis.py:630 by contrast 404s when stage_exec is missing, so this laxity is grading-specific. Re-confirm is unguarded: a second POST overwrites the signed sub-scores (740-748) and re-queues report (777-780). The worker-clobber path is real too (backend/worker/grading.py:458 sets status back to 'awaiting_review' after commit). Downgraded critical->high only because the missing auth dependency is a repo-wide pattern for the stage routers (mitosis.py:618, triage.py also take reviewed_by from the body) rather than a regression unique to this endpoint, and MOCK_AUTH_ENABLED=True (config.py:59) means no router currently enforces role anyway; the missing state gating / idempotency half, however, is unique to this file and is what makes the finding actionable.

#### 142. Histologic-type confirmation gate is a client-supplied boolean; no server-side confirm-type action exists

**Severity:** high · **Category:** PRD deviation · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/grading.py:682`

The only gate is `payload.type_confirmed`, which the frontend hard-codes to true (frontend/components/viewer/GradingReviewWorkspace.tsx:374 `type_confirmed: true`). The server never checks grading_record.type_confirmed_by or review_summary.can_confirm. PRD 00-overview.md locked decision 3 and PRD 05 section 5 require the field to be blocked until the pathologist acts.

        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST,
            detail="Clinical Confirmation Gate: Histologic Type must be explicitly confirmed ..."
```
**Impact:** The mandatory confirm is a no-op; a report can be generated with a never-reviewed histologic type.

Repo-wide grep for type_confirmed shows the only writer of grading_record.type_confirmed_by is grading.py:748 inside /confirm itself (worker/grading.py:433 seeds it to 'unconfirmed'); there is no confirm-type endpoint. So is_type_confirmed (284) and therefore can_confirm (285, surfaced at 301) are necessarily False for any case that has not already been confirmed, making the server's own gate flag useless — and the frontend indeed ignores it (grep for can_confirm/is_type_confirmed in GradingReviewWorkspace.tsx returns nothing) while hard-coding type_confirmed: true at line 374. The server checks only that client boolean (682-686) and never grading_record.type_confirmed_by, so the gate is a no-op, contradicting PRD 00-overview.md decision 3 ('field blocked until pathologist acts') and PRD 05 line 74 ('Blocked state by design'). Note for the fix: the histologic type is still user-selectable in the UI (dropdown at GradingReviewWorkspace.tsx:1190, default 'IDC-NST'), so the practical exposure is an unchanged default silently counting as a confirmation, not a wholly unseen field — high, not critical.

*Also reported at:* `frontend/components/viewer/GradingReviewWorkspace.tsx:374` (Histologic-type confirmation gate is client-only; `type_confirmed: true` is always sent)

#### 139. Confirm trusts client-supplied sub-scores; overriding without an 'overrides' entry needs no justification and emits no score_override audit

**Severity:** high · **Category:** Clinical correctness · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/grading.py:740`

The endpoint validates that payload.tubule_score/pleo_score/mitotic_score/nottingham_sum/grade are internally consistent (validate_grading_invariants) but never compares them with the server-derived `current_data['current']` values computed at line 697. The 10-char justification check (lines 715-725) and score_override audit rows (lines 800-815) iterate only over keys the client chose to put in payload.overrides. A client can send pleo_score=1 while the reviewed value is 3 with overrides={} and the row is signed with no justification and no override audit.

```
grading_record.tubule_score = payload.tubule_score
    if payload.tubule_percent is not None:
        grading_record.tubule_percent = payload.tubule_percent
    grading_record.pleo_score = payload.pleo_score
    grading_record.mitotic_score = payload.mitotic_score
```
**Impact:** PRD 05 section 5 (overrides require justification and score_override audit events) is bypassable; the persisted grade can differ from the reviewed evidence with no trace.

**Fix:** Derive final scores server-side from current_data['current']; treat any payload score that differs from the derived value as an override that must carry a justification; emit score_override for each diff; ignore client nottingham_sum/grade and recompute.

*Verifier note:* Accurate. current_data is built at 699 and only review_summary is consulted (700-714); current_data['current'] (the server-derived eff_tubule_score/eff_pleo_score/eff_mitotic_score computed at 277-282) is never compared with the payload. validate_grading_invariants (729-735) is fed exclusively payload fields, so it only proves payload self-consistency — pipeline/grading.py's check cannot detect divergence from the reviewed evidence. The justification loop (717-725) and the score_override AuditEvents (799-814) both iterate payload.overrides only, so overrides={} plus arbitrary tubule/pleo/mitotic scores is signed with no justification and no score_override row, defeating PRD 05 line 71 ('requires 10-char min justification') and line 77 ('score_override audit events {component, from, to, justification}'). Kept at high rather than critical: it requires a client that deviates from the shipped UI (GradingReviewWorkspace.tsx:376-381 sends the derived activeTubuleScore/activePleoScore values), and exploiting it grants no capability a signer does not already hold — the harm is a silently untraceable grade, not privilege escalation.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/grading.py:740` (Grading confirm trusts client-supplied scores; override justification gate is only applied to keys the client chooses to send); `backend/app/routers/grading.py:740` (Grading confirm gate persists the client-supplied Nottingham grade without ever comparing it to the server's own aggregate)

#### 114. Audit trail loses toggles: only the last client-supplied audit_toggle per 300 ms debounce is logged, auto-rejects log nothing, and the server never derives events from actual label changes

**Severity:** high · **Category:** Data integrity · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/mitosis.py:376`

recompute applies the whole candidate_labels map (367-373) but records one review_edit only if the client passed audit_toggle, with client-supplied from/to values. The frontend debounces recompute with clearTimeout (MitosisViewer.tsx:192-205); pressing m/x on several cards within 300 ms drops all but the last audit_toggle. handleApproveFieldAndNext auto-rejects every unreviewed candidate in the field and calls syncWithServer with no audit_toggle (MitosisViewer.tsx:274-291). PRD §7 requires `review_edit` with {detection_id, from, to} for every toggle.

```
if payload.audit_toggle:
    toggle = payload.audit_toggle
    audit = AuditEvent(... payload={"detection_id": toggle.get("id"), "from": toggle.get("from"), "to": toggle.get("to")})
```
**Impact:** The 'product moat' training labels and the legal audit trail are incomplete and forgeable; PRD §9 'All toggles present in audit trail with before/after' fails.

**Fix:** In recompute, emit one review_edit per detection whose label actually changed (compare d.label before assignment) and ignore the client's audit_toggle; keep actor from the auth dependency.

*Verifier note:* Confirmed, and distinct from 113 (that one is authn/actor identity; this one is event completeness). recompute_scoring applies the entire candidate_labels map at 367-373 - including flips it detects via `if d.label != new_label` - but emits at most one AuditEvent, only when payload.audit_toggle is present, using the client's own id/from/to values (376-389); the server never derives events from the labels it actually changed, even though it has the pre-assignment value in hand at 371. Frontend confirms both loss paths: syncWithServer clears the pending timer before rescheduling (MitosisViewer.tsx:192-196, 300ms), so several m/x presses inside one window collapse to a single POST carrying only the last auditToggle while candidate_labels still carries every flip; and handleApproveFieldAndNext auto-rejects every unreviewed candidate in the field and calls syncWithServer(currentCandidates, updatedHpfs) with no third argument (MitosisViewer.tsx:274-291), so bulk auto-rejects are labelled in the DB with zero audit rows. PRD backs the requirement: prd/04-stage-v4.3-mitosis.md:105 'Every label toggle -> audit_events(event_type=review_edit, payload={detection_id, from, to}) ... never lose one', and the §9 checklist line 'All toggles present in audit trail with before/after'. High stands.

*Also reported at:* `frontend/components/viewer/MitosisViewer.tsx:192` (Debounced recompute drops the audit_toggle of any label change made <300 ms before the next one); `frontend/components/viewer/MitosisViewer.tsx:280` (Enter / 'Approve Field & Next' silently relabels all unreviewed candidates in the field as not_mitosis with pathologist attribution and no audit event); `frontend/components/viewer/MitosisViewer.tsx:274` (Bulk auto-reject on 'Approve Field & Next' changes candidate labels without logging any audit_toggle event)

#### 109. add_candidate and thumbnail fallback download the entire WSI synchronously per request while holding the global OpenSlide lock

**Severity:** high · **Category:** Performance · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/mitosis.py:472`

Every 'Add missed mitosis' click calls download_blob_to_filename on the full SVS (multi-GB) to cut one 128x128 crop, inside the request thread; get_hpf_thumbnail does the same on a cache miss (284) — and the fast path rarely hits for 40x because preprocess only pre-generates the norm pyramid up to level 12 (worker/preprocess.py:46 `max_norm_pregen_level = min(12, dz.level_count)`) while extract_patch_from_pyramid asks for z = max_level (~15-17) (tiles.py:163-170). The read_region is done under OPENSLIDE_GLOBAL_LOCK (475, 289), which is shared with the tile-serving endpoint.

```
download_blob_to_filename(raw_bucket_name, blob_name, local_slide_path)
if os.path.exists(local_slide_path):
    import openslide
    with OPENSLIDE_GLOBAL_LOCK:
        oslide = openslide.OpenSlide(local_slide_path)
```
**Impact:** Minutes of latency and gateway timeouts on a single click; concurrent viewers are blocked from loading tiles while the lock is held; repeated multi-GB egress.

**Fix:** Cut crops from the DeepZoom pyramid (extract_patch_from_pyramid at level 0, already present) or from a worker-side cached slide; if raw access is unavoidable, do it in the worker via a queued job and return 202. Never take the global lock around a network download.

*Verifier note:* Core defect confirmed, headline partly wrong. mitosis.py:466-480: every /add_candidate call does `download_blob_to_filename(raw_bucket_name, blob_name, local_slide_path)` on the full SVS in the request thread just to cut one 128x128 crop; same shape at 284 for the thumbnail fallback. The pyramid-fast-path gap is real for the default norm layer: extract_patch_from_pyramid (pipeline/tiles.py:163-172) computes z = max_level + level_offset, which for mag=40x is field_um=128/out 512 -> crop_mpp 0.25 == mpp_x -> level_offset 0 -> z = ceil(log2(max_dim)) (~15 for 20000px), while worker/preprocess.py:46 only pregenerates norm levels 0..min(12,level_count)-1, and tiles.py's on-the-fly generation (routers/tiles.py:150-175) never writes tiles back to the pyramid bucket. CORRECTION to the title/proposed fix: the download is NOT inside the lock at either site - 472 precedes `with OPENSLIDE_GLOBAL_LOCK` at 475, and 284 precedes the `with` at 289; only OpenSlide open + read_region are under it. The lock IS process-global and shared with tile serving (app/core/openslide_lock.py:5; routers/tiles.py:47, cases.py:402, triage.py:389, grading.py:572), so slide-open contention is real but bounded. Also note get_hpf_thumbnail normally short-circuits at 218-221 on the worker-prerendered blob, so the multi-GB path there is a miss-only cost; /add_candidate pays it on every click, which alone justifies high.

#### 110. Pathologist-added mitoses and re-placed HPFs never update HpfSite.mitotic_count, which grading later reads

**Severity:** high · **Category:** Clinical correctness · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/mitosis.py:608`

HpfSite.mitotic_count is only persisted by the worker and by recompute_scoring (430-434). re_place_hpfs writes new rows with mitotic_count=0 and returns get_mitosis_stage_data, which recomputes counts in memory only (147). add_pathologist_mitosis inserts the Detection (500-512) without touching HPF counts, and the frontend does not call syncWithServer after an add (MitosisViewer.tsx:240-254 — only computeClientScore). bulk_action likewise never persists counts. worker/grading.py:188 and routers/grading.py:131 sum HpfSite.mitotic_count.

```
hpf_row = HpfSite(
    case_id=case_id, seq=h["seq"], center_um=h["center_um"], radius_um=h["radius_um"],
    mitotic_count=0,
    source="model")
...
return get_mitosis_stage_data(case_id, db)
```
**Impact:** A pathologist who re-places HPFs (or adds missed mitoses) and then confirms sees a correct live score, but grading/report compute the grade from mitotic_count = 0 (or the pre-add count).

**Fix:** Factor a single persist_hpf_counts(case_id, db) that runs calculate_hpf_mitosis_counts against DB detections and writes HpfSite.mitotic_count; call it from re_place_hpfs, add_candidate, bulk_action and recompute. Better: have grading read the confirmed Stage-4 summary (see grading finding).

*Verifier note:* Confirmed on all three paths. HpfSite.mitotic_count is persisted only by the worker (worker/mitosis.py:429-438, from calculate_hpf_mitosis_counts) and by recompute_scoring (430-434). re_place_hpfs writes mitotic_count=0 at 608, commits at 612, then returns get_mitosis_stage_data, whose recount at 147 is in-memory only. add_pathologist_mitosis inserts the Detection (500-512) with no HPF-count update, and the client does not resync (MitosisViewer.tsx:240-254 calls only computeClientScore - no syncWithServer, unlike handleToggleCandidate:237). bulk_reject_unreviewed (549-568) likewise persists labels but not counts. Consumers read the stale column: routers/grading.py:131 and worker/grading.py:188 both `sum(getattr(h, 'mitotic_count', 0) ...)` and derive mitotic_score from that sum. Concrete failure: pathologist pins a missed mitosis inside field 3 and confirms without touching any other card -> live UI shows the incremented score, DB HpfSite counts still exclude it, grading computes a lower mitotic score. pipeline/scoring.py:33 counting only label=='mitosis' means the bulk-reject path is usually benign (unreviewed was never counted), but the add and re-place paths are real. High stands - it is a silent grade-changing divergence.

#### 360. Missing tumour size is silently replaced by 18.0 mm, fabricating pT1c on the report

**Severity:** high · **Category:** Clinical correctness · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/report.py:131`

Every staging call site substitutes 18.0 mm when tumor_size_mm is None or 0 (routers/report.py:272, 379, 434; worker/report.py:94), and worker/report.py:77 creates the report row with tumor_size_mm=18.0 outright. staging.py:40-41 already has the correct behaviour for a missing size (return 'pTX'), but no caller can ever reach it.

```
tumor_size = report.tumor_size_mm or 18.0  |  pt_stage = calculate_ajcc_pt_stage(tumor_size)
```
**Impact:** A signed report can carry pT1c / Stage IA-IIA for a case in which the pathologist never entered a size. PRD 06 s2 defines tumor_size_gross as a required manual element that 'blocks signing while ... empty'.

**Fix:** Remove the `or 18.0` defaults and the seeded 18.0 in worker/report.py:77; let staging.py return pTX and have the sign-off gate refuse to sign while the element is empty.

*Verifier note:* Fabrication is real, but the operative line is not the one cited. The `or 18.0` fallbacks do exist at report.py:272, 379, 434 and worker/report.py:94 as quoted, yet they are nearly dead code: tumor_size_mm can essentially never be None because app/models/report.py:25 declares the column default 18.0 and both creation paths hardcode it (report.py:131 in _ensure_report_record, worker/report.py:77), while the PUT guard at 363 skips assignment when a client sends null. The root cause is therefore the seeded 18.0 at report.py:131 (corrected anchor) plus the two siblings, which is why staging.py:40-41's correct pTX branch is unreachable — GET on a brand-new case returns pT1c/IA with no pathologist input, exactly as tests/test_cap_reporting.py:314 asserts. Severity lowered from critical to high on two grounds: (1) PRD 06 section 2 marks tumor_size_gross 'required-if specimen_type != core_biopsy', and the seeded specimen_type is core_biopsy, so the PRD's own gate would not fire on the default row; (2) this is one instance of a repo-wide fabricated-defaults pattern (ER 95% positive, HER2 1+, margins negative at 5.0 mm, LVI absent, Nottingham grade 2 — report.py:134-147, 260-269) and there is no sign-off precondition check of any kind in sign_final_report (576-662), so the missing gate, not this constant alone, is what lets a signed report carry invented values.

#### 499. Narrative is not regenerated automatically on element change, and there is no narrative_edited flag to freeze it after a manual edit

**Severity:** high · **Category:** PRD deviation · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/report.py:375`

PRD section 3.2 (locked behavior): narrative is 'Regenerated automatically whenever any element value changes (debounced); pathologist can edit the paragraph freehand — post-edit, regeneration stops (their text wins; flag narrative_edited).' update_report_data (the endpoint that mutates specimen_type/laterality/margins/lymph_nodes/biomarkers/etc.) recalculates AJCC staging and re-renders the PDF, but never calls narrative regeneration at all — narrative only changes via the separate, must-be-explicitly-called /resynthesize-narrative or /{case_id}/regenerate-narrative endpoints. There is also no `narrative_edited` column anywhere on the Report model, so even if auto-regeneration were wired in, a freehand pathologist edit could never be detected and protected from being overwritten.

```
if payload.narrative is not None:
    report.narrative = payload.narrative
...
report.status = "in_review"

db.commit()
db.refresh(report)

# Re-render and upload PDF to GCS
try:
    render_and_upload_report_pdf(str(payload.case_id), report, grading, db)
```
**Impact:** Element edits silently leave a stale narrative on screen/in the PDF until someone remembers to hit a separate regenerate button, and because there is no `narrative_edited` flag, any future auto-regeneration hookup would clobber a pathologist's freehand edits with a new MedGemma call — the exact behavior the PRD explicitly locks against.

**Fix:** Add a `narrative_edited` boolean column; have update_report_data trigger a debounced narrative regeneration whenever any element field actually changes, unless `narrative_edited` is true; set `narrative_edited=True` whenever the pathologist edits the narrative text directly.

Narrative regeneration lives solely in /resynthesize-narrative (409) and /{case_id}/regenerate-narrative (485), both of which must be invoked explicitly. `narrative_edited` does not exist: grep over the repo returns zero hits, and app/models/report.py has no such column (PRD 06 §5 line 85 requires `narrative, narrative_edited bool DEFAULT false`; §3.2 line 59 locks the debounce-regenerate/stop-after-edit behaviour). High is right rather than merely a spec nit, because the stale narrative is printed: render_and_upload_report_pdf passes report.narrative into render_dict (186) alongside the freshly recomputed report.staging (184). Change tumor_size_mm 18→60 and the PDF's staging table updates while the seeded narrative still reads 'consistent with Stage IA invasive carcinoma' (_ensure_report_record:146). validate_narrative_consistency is imported (39) but called only inside regenerate-narrative (522), so nothing catches the divergence on the edit path.

#### 178. Integrity hash omits the Nottingham grade/sub-scores, tumor_site, LVI, DCIS, specimen_type, attestation and PDF bytes; not verifiable from stored data

**Severity:** high · **Category:** Data integrity · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/report.py:598`

canonical_payload hashes only a subset of columns; the clinical core (grade, T/P/M scores, histologic subtype confirmation) and the rendered PDF are excluded. PRD 06 §4.3 specifies sha256 of the final PDF bytes stored as pdf_sha256. There is no verify endpoint, and signed_at is hashed as now_utc.isoformat() (microseconds + '+00:00') while SQLite DateTime(timezone=True) stores a naive value, so re-serialising report.signed_at from the DB cannot reproduce the string. The PDF prints the hash with a literal '...' appended (report_pdf.py:360).

```
canonical_payload = {
    "case_id": str(payload.case_id),
    "procedure": report.procedure,
    "laterality": report.laterality,
    "histologic_type": report.histologic_type,
    "tumor_size_mm": report.tumor_size_mm,
```
**Impact:** Tampering with grade, LVI, DCIS or the PDF is undetectable; the hash cannot be recomputed later for audit.

**Fix:** Hash the full element JSON (including grading snapshot) AND the final PDF bytes; store both; persist the exact signed_at string used; add GET /{case_id}/verify.

*Verifier note:* Confirmed with one sub-claim narrowed. canonical_payload (598-612) covers case_id, procedure, laterality, histologic_type, tumor_size_mm, margins, lymph_nodes, biomarkers, staging, narrative, signed_by, npi, signed_at — and genuinely omits specimen_type, tumor_site, lvi_status, dcis_present, attestation_statement, the whole Nottingham block (grade/tubule/pleo/mitotic/nottingham_sum come from the gradings table at 260-269 and are never hashed) and the PDF bytes. That matters because /amend can silently rewrite exactly those unhashed columns (finding 171). Slight overstatement: the grade is indirectly pinned via narrative.diagnosis_line, which is hashed (608) and carries 'NOTTINGHAM HISTOLOGIC GRADE n' (144) — the structured sub-scores are not. PRD 06 §4.3 requires sha256 over the final PDF stored as pdf_sha256; `grep pdf_sha256 backend/` returns nothing and Report has no such column (models/report.py:63-71). No verify endpoint exists (only /pdf 533, /json 566). report_pdf.py:360 does print `SHA256: {integrity_hash}...` with a literal trailing ellipsis on the full 64-char digest, so the printed value never matches the stored one by string comparison. The signed_at round-trip claim is config-dependent, not universal: DATABASE_URL defaults to postgresql (config.py:46-48) where timestamptz round-trips tz-aware and isoformat() would reproduce the '+00:00' string; it holds only on the SQLite path (db.py:8-31, including the silent fallback when Postgres is unreachable), where DateTime(timezone=True) comes back naive. Core defect stands regardless.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/report.py:598` (Report immutability and hash contract diverge from PRD: hash omits fields and PDF bytes, event names differ); `backend/app/routers/report.py:598` (pdf_sha256 is never computed over the actual PDF bytes; the stored 'integrity_hash' only hashes report metadata JSON)
