#### 533. Signed PDF is re-rendered after commit with failures swallowed, overwrites the draft at the same unversioned blob, and no pdf_sha256 is stored

**Severity:** high · **Category:** Data integrity · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/report.py:656`

sign_final_report commits status='signed' first, then calls render_and_upload_report_pdf inside try/except that only prints. render_and_upload_report_pdf writes to cases/{case_id}/report/CAP_Report_{id8}.pdf (report.py:231) - the same key the draft used - so the draft is destroyed and there is no per-version PDF. The integrity_hash (line 614) is a sha256 over the JSON payload computed before the PDF exists; nothing hashes the PDF bytes. PRD 06-stage-v4.5 sign steps 3-4 require sha256 of the final PDF bytes stored in DB + audit, uploaded as artifacts/{case}/report/v{n}.pdf, and the reports table has pdf_gcs_uri and pdf_sha256 columns; models/report.py has only pdf_path.

```
try:
    render_and_upload_report_pdf(str(payload.case_id), report, grading, db)
except Exception as e:
    print(f"[Final PDF Render Note] {e}")
```
**Impact:** If GCS or ReportLab fails during signing, the report is 'signed' while pdf_path still points at the unsigned draft (or at nothing); the served PDF can never be verified against the stored hash; a later amendment silently overwrites the signed PDF.

**Fix:** Render and hash the PDF inside the same transaction before flipping status; write to report/v{n}.pdf; add pdf_sha256 (and version) columns to Report; fail the sign request (HTTP 500 with rollback) if the render/upload fails.

*Verifier note:* All three sub-claims hold. (1) Ordering: report.status='signed' plus the audit row are committed at report.py:656 (db.commit()); the render call at 657-660 is wrapped in 'except Exception as e: print(...)', so a ReportLab or GCS failure leaves a report row marked signed with pdf_path still pointing at the draft (or NULL if no draft was ever rendered) and returns HTTP 200. (2) Same key: gcs_blob_name at report.py:231 is f'cases/{case_id}/report/CAP_Report_{id8}.pdf' with no version segment - identical to the draft key used by update_report_data (402) and by worker/report.py:211, so the signed render destroys the draft and any later amend/update re-render would destroy the signed PDF. Note amend_signed_report never re-renders at all, so after an amendment the served bytes are the pre-amendment signed PDF. (3) No PDF hash: integrity_hash at report.py:604-614 is sha256 over a JSON dict only; grep for sha256 across app/ and worker/ shows no hashing of pdf_bytes anywhere. models/report.py:66 has only pdf_path - no version, no pdf_gcs_uri, no pdf_sha256, against prd/06-stage-v4.5-report.md:71-72 ('sha of final bytes stored in DB + audit event', 'Upload artifacts/{case}/report/v{n}.pdf') and the reports DDL at 06-stage-v4.5-report.md:86. High is right; I keep it below critical only because it corrupts provenance rather than the clinical content itself (that is index 532). Corrected line: the defect anchors at the commit on 656 that precedes the swallowed render on 657-660; 658 is the render call inside it.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/report.py:231` (Single PDF blob path is overwritten by every render and never versioned; amendment does not re-render, so the served PDF can be stale or a pre-sign draft); `backend/worker/report.py:150` (Every report version and re-render writes the same PDF object name, so the signed PDF is overwritten)

#### 171. /amend mutates the signed row in place and lets updated_fields overwrite any attribute (status, integrity_hash, signed_by, case_id)

**Severity:** high · **Category:** Security · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/report.py:693`

updated_fields is applied via hasattr/setattr with no whitelist, no re-validation, no staging recompute, no new hash, and no PDF re-render. PRD 06 §5 requires amendments to create a new version row while the original stays signed.

```
for k, v in payload.updated_fields.items():
    if hasattr(report, k):
        setattr(report, k, v)
```
**Impact:** {"integrity_hash": "x"}, {"status": "draft"}, {"signed_by": "..."} or {"case_id": ...} rewrite the sealed record; {"tumor_size_mm": 60} leaves staging at pT1c; {"margins": null} 500s on commit (nullable=False) and on next PDF render (report_pdf.py:234 None.get). The stale signed PDF stays in GCS.

**Fix:** Whitelist amendable fields (reuse UpdateReportPayload minus case_id), recompute staging, compute a new hash chained to previous_hash, re-render PDF as v{n}, and store as a new version row.

*Verifier note:* Confirmed. Lines 693-695 are exactly `for k, v in payload.updated_fields.items(): if hasattr(report, k): setattr(report, k, v)` with no whitelist. AmendReportPayload.updated_fields is `Dict[str, Any]` (99), so any mapped column on Report is reachable: status, integrity_hash, signed_by, npi, signed_at, attestation_statement, pdf_path, case_id (the PK, models/report.py:17-19) and amendments itself. Ordering makes it worse than described: `report.amendments = current_amendments` (689) and `report.status = 'amended'` (690) both run BEFORE the loop, so {"amendments": []} erases the amendment trail and {"status": "draft"} unlocks the report for /update again — and the audit event (697-707) records only version/reason/amended_at, never the field values, so the erasure leaves no record of what changed. Also confirmed: no re-staging (contrast 378-394 in update_report_data), no new integrity hash, and no render_and_upload_report_pdf call anywhere in amend_signed_report (665-712), so report.pdf_path (239) still points at the stale signed PDF. margins/lymph_nodes/biomarkers/staging/narrative are nullable=False (models/report.py:29-57), so {"margins": null} raises on commit at 709; report_pdf.py:233-234 (`margins.get(...)`) would also fail on None. PRD 06 §5 requires a new version+1 row with the original staying signed; this mutates in place. Severity high as claimed (not critical only because it presupposes reaching /amend, which finding 168 covers).

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/report.py:693` (/report/amend lets the client overwrite any Report column (status, integrity_hash, signed_by) and never re-hashes or re-renders); `backend/app/routers/report.py:693` (Amendment mutates staging inputs without recomputing staging)

#### 200. Every missing tile downloads the entire raw WSI from GCS and holds a process-wide lock

**Severity:** high · **Category:** Performance · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/tiles.py:152`

stream_slide_tile tries up to three GCS blob fetches (ext, .png, .jpg), and on a miss falls back to download_blob_to_filename of the ORIGINAL multi-gigabyte slide into a fresh mkdtemp directory, opens it with OpenSlide under OPENSLIDE_GLOBAL_LOCK, renders one 256px tile, then rmtree's the download. No caching of the download. OpenSeadragon issues dozens of tile requests per pan; before the pyramid is fully uploaded, or for any z/x/y outside the pyramid, each request re-downloads the whole slide. z is never bounded against max_level, so z=2000 also triggers the full download before failing with OverflowError at line 66 (256 / 2**1989).

```
download_blob_to_filename(raw_bucket_name, blob_name, local_slide_path)
if os.path.exists(local_slide_path):
    tile_bytes = generate_tile_on_the_fly(
    ...
    shutil.rmtree(scratch_dir, ignore_errors=True)
```
**Impact:** A single viewer session can pull hundreds of GB of egress and saturate the API server's disk (tmpfs on Cloud Run = RAM) and event loop; the global lock (openslide_lock.py:5) serializes all tile/thumbnail/patch rendering across every request in the process, so one slow download stalls all other users' tiles.

**Fix:** Return 404 immediately for tiles absent from the pyramid bucket (validate 0 <= z <= max_level, and x/y within grid). If on-the-fly rendering is required, cache the downloaded slide per slide_id on local disk with an LRU and open it once, and drop the global lock in favour of a per-slide lock.

*Verifier note:* Core defect is real. tiles.py:152-178: on any pyramid miss the router mkdtemp's a scratch dir, calls download_blob_to_filename(raw_bucket, blob, local_slide_path) (line 163) for the WHOLE original slide (gcs_uri_original, default .svs), renders one 256px tile, then rmtree's it in the finally at 178 — no cache, per request. Nothing bounds z or x/y: get_tile/get_tile_direct take `z: int` and an arbitrary {filename}, and stem only has to be `<digits>_<digits>` (line 155). Two parts of the impact claim do not hold: (1) the download is NOT under the global lock — OPENSLIDE_GLOBAL_LOCK is taken inside generate_tile_on_the_fly (line 47), after the download returns, so a slow download does not serialize other renders (the lock does serialize all rendering, but that is a separate issue); and both endpoints are sync `def`, so FastAPI runs them in the threadpool, not on the event loop. (2) z=2000 does not raise OverflowError: CPython evaluates 256 / 2**1989 to 0.0 (verified), so w_um=h_um=0, and read_region_srgb's guard at pipeline/tiles.py:83-84 ((x_px_0+w_px_0) <= 0) returns a blank (245,240,245) tile — i.e. an out-of-range z downloads the entire slide and returns HTTP 200 with a fake blank tile, which is worse than the claimed 404. Severity lowered from critical to high because the lock/event-loop amplification claim is wrong; the unbounded per-tile multi-GB egress and disk (tmpfs=RAM on Cloud Run) blowup is real.

#### 636. Synchronous tile/thumbnail handlers block anyio worker threads for the duration of multi-GB downloads, starving the whole API including /healthz

**Severity:** high · **Category:** Performance · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/tiles.py:202`

get_tile, get_tile_direct and get_case_thumbnail are plain `def` endpoints, so FastAPI runs each in the shared anyio threadpool (default 40 tokens). Each fallback holds a token for the full WSI download (tiles.py:163, cases.py:398) plus the OPENSLIDE_GLOBAL_LOCK wait. One OpenSeadragon viewport (~40 tiles) exhausts the pool; every other sync endpoint — GET /cases, the stage polling at 3 s intervals, and /healthz (main.py:52, also sync) — then queues behind the downloads.

```
app/routers/tiles.py:202  def get_tile(
app/routers/tiles.py:163  download_blob_to_filename(raw_bucket_name, blob_name, local_slide_path)
app/main.py:52  def health_check():
```
**Impact:** A single user opening the viewer makes the API unresponsive for every other user; Cloud Run health checks time out and the instance is recycled mid-download, losing all in-flight work.

**Fix:** Bound z and layer, return 404 immediately for tiles outside the pre-generated pyramid instead of falling back, and move any remaining heavy IO to a bounded dedicated executor (or the worker) so the request pool is never held by WSI downloads. Make /healthz `async def`.

*Verifier note:* Verified. tiles.py:202 get_tile, tiles.py:217 get_tile_direct and cases.py:373 get_case_thumbnail are all plain `def`, so Starlette runs each in the anyio worker threadpool (default 40 tokens); main.py:52 health_check is also plain `def` and therefore queues behind them. The worst part of the claim is accurate and is the load-bearing one: when the pyramid blob is missing, stream_slide_tile falls through to tiles.py:152-178, which downloads the ENTIRE source WSI (line 163) into a fresh tempdir per tile request and then serializes rendering behind OPENSLIDE_GLOBAL_LOCK (tiles.py:47) — a whole-slide download per 256px tile, times ~40 tiles for one viewport. get_case_thumbnail does the same full download at cases.py:398. Note the fallback also runs for out-of-range z, since nothing bounds z or layer before the fallback. Keeping high rather than critical: on the happy path (pyramid present) each thread only holds a short GCS blob fetch, so the pool exhaustion needs the fallback path to be hit, which happens on any slide whose ingest pyramid is incomplete rather than on every request.

#### 77. Thumbnail endpoint falls back to an arbitrary slide from another case → cross-patient image leakage, cached under the wrong case

**Severity:** high · **Category:** Security · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/triage.py:302`

If no slide is found for `case_id` (nonexistent case, typo, or any unauthenticated probe) the endpoint picks `db.scalars(select(Slide)).first()` — whichever slide sorts first in the table — reads a real 512 µm region from that patient's WSI (pyramid tiles or full OpenSlide download), returns it with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400`, and uploads it to `cases/{case_id}/triage/patches/...` under the bogus case (line 434-439). The router has no auth dependency at all (compare `cases.py` where every route takes `Depends(get_current_user)`).

```
if not slide_obj:
    slide_obj = db.scalars(select(Slide)).first()
```
**Impact:** Any client can enumerate tissue from an unrelated patient's slide; PHI is written into another case's artifact prefix.

**Fix:** Return 404 when the case has no slide; add `Depends(get_current_user)` to the router; drop the global-first-slide fallback.

*Verifier note:* Real and the worst item in the batch. triage.py:301-302 `if not slide_obj: slide_obj = db.scalars(select(Slide)).first()` with no case scoping and no 404. slide_obj then drives both extraction paths: line 355 `slide_id = str(slide_obj.id)` is passed to extract_patch_from_pyramid, which reads pipeline/tiles.py:205 `f"{slide_id}/{layer}/{z}/{c}_{r}{ext}"` from the pyramids bucket, and line 378 uses that slide's own gcs_uri_original for the OpenSlide download. So a request for a nonexistent/typo'd case really does return a 512 um field of an unrelated patient's tissue, with Cache-Control public max-age=86400 (line 443), and lines 433-439 then persist that PHI at cases/{bogus_case_id}/triage/patches/. There is no case-ownership check anywhere in the endpoint (case_obj is fetched at line 297 but only used for centroid lookup, never to authorize). Confirmed at high; the leak is independent of the auth gap in index 78 - even a properly authenticated user of case A gets patient B's pixels.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/triage.py:301` (Thumbnail endpoints fall back to an arbitrary slide from any case (cross-patient image leakage)); `backend/app/routers/mitosis.py:241` (HPF thumbnail falls back to ANY slide in the database and a fixed (1000,1000) µm centre, then caches the result under this case)

#### 80. Confirm swallows GCS read failure and then deletes all confirmed hotspots

**Severity:** high · **Category:** Data integrity · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/triage.py:507`

If output.json cannot be fetched (403, transient network, bucket misconfig) the exception is printed and `machine_hotspots=[]`. The code proceeds to `db.query(Hotspot)...delete()` and persists only user-added hotspots, marks the stage confirmed and queues mitosis with `confirmed_hotspots_count` possibly 0.

```
except Exception as e:
    print(f"[Triage Confirm Note] Could not load hotspots from GCS: {e}")

edits = stage_exec.review_edits or []
effective_hotspots = apply_edit_ops(machine_hotspots, edits)

# Delete any prior confirmed hotspots for this case
db.query(Hotspot).filter(Hotspot.case_id == payload.case_id).delete()
```
**Impact:** Transient storage error becomes a silently wrong confirmation snapshot; previously confirmed rows are lost.

**Fix:** Raise HTTPException(502/503) when machine output cannot be loaded; only delete/replace inside the same transaction after successful load.

*Verifier note:* Confirmed, and distinct from index 79. triage.py:499-508 wraps the whole GCS load in try/except with only a print; machine_hotspots stays []. Control then falls through unconditionally to 511 apply_edit_ops([], edits) - which, for the frontend's op set, yields only the 'add' ops since 'modify'/'exclude' branches require `hid in hotspots_dict` (lines 68, 86) - and to 514 `db.query(Hotspot).filter(Hotspot.case_id == payload.case_id).delete()`. The string case_id binds fine against the GUID column (models/base.py process_bind_param does str(value)), so the delete really does remove the prior confirmed rows. The stage is then marked confirmed (532) and mitosis queued with confirmed_hotspots_count possibly 0 (541), all in one commit at 588. A transient 5xx/403 from GCS therefore converts a valid confirmed snapshot into an empty or user-adds-only one. High is right. (The same swallow exists at line 125-126 in get_triage_data, but that path is read-only and non-destructive.)

#### 738. Case deletion writes no audit event and orphans the existing trail

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Data integrity · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/cases.py:66`

clear_all_cases (and delete_case at line 91) delete Case rows without emitting an AuditEvent, and audit_events rows are not deleted either — they have no FK and store case_id as a plain string. The docstring claims otherwise. Because GET /cases/{case_id}/audit 404s when the Case row is gone (routers/audit.py:22), the surviving events become unreachable through the API.

```
"""Clear all diagnostic cases and audit logs."""
    cases = db.scalars(select(Case)).all()
    count = len(cases)
    for c in cases:
        db.delete(c)
```
**Impact:** The most destructive operation in the system leaves no trace of who invoked it or what was destroyed, and the audit history of every deleted case becomes invisible while still occupying the table — the opposite of the append-only, queryable trail the PRD requires.

**Fix:** Emit a case_deleted audit event (actor, case id, counts of dependent rows) before deleting, and either keep the audit endpoint reachable for deleted cases or archive the events explicitly.

*Verifier note:* Verified end to end. cases.py:66-78 (clear_all_cases) and 80-93 (delete_case) call db.delete(...) + db.commit() and return; neither constructs an AuditEvent — contrast create_case at cases.py:45-52 which does. `grep -rn "case_deleted|cases_cleared" backend/` returns nothing, and `grep -rn "listens_for|before_delete|after_delete" backend/` returns nothing, so no ORM event hook covers it either. The orphaning claim also holds: models/audit.py declares `case_id: Mapped[str|None] = mapped_column(String, nullable=True)` — a plain String, no ForeignKey — and models/case.py's relationships cascade only to slides/stage_executions/grading/report, so audit_events rows survive the delete; routers/audit.py:22-24 does `case_obj = db.get(Case, case_id)` / `raise HTTPException(404)` before ever querying AuditEvent, so those surviving rows are unreachable via GET /cases/{id}/audit. The docstring at line 71 ("Clear all diagnostic cases and audit logs") is doubly wrong: audit logs are not cleared, and no audit of the clearing is written. Two calibrations on the finder's framing, neither changing the verdict: (1) retaining the audit rows is actually PRD-correct, not a bug — prd/00-overview.md:34 requires an append-only audit log and line 125 does `REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ON audit_events`; so the 'still occupying the table' phrasing and the proposed 'archive the events explicitly' half of the fix are misdirected. The real defects are the missing deletion event and the 404 gate that hides retained history. (2) 'most destructive operation leaves no trace' is accurate for the DB but the actor is still authenticated (user: CurrentUser dependency), so this is a lost-audit-record issue, not anonymous access. Medium is right — no data loss beyond what was asked for, but a compliance/traceability gap on the one endpoint that wipes every case.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/cases.py:71` (clear_all_cases claims to delete audit logs but leaves them, and wipes cases with stages mid-run)

#### 213. Multiple slides per case are silently allowed and picked non-deterministically with .first() and slides[0]

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Data integrity · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/cases.py:127`

upload_slide_file and finalize_slide_upload always insert a new Slide and a new attempt-1 'ingest' StageExecution; a second upload to the same case violates uq_stage_execution_attempt (case_id, stage, attempt) and raises IntegrityError -> 500, or if the first ingest row was already retried, succeeds and leaves two slides. Every consumer then selects one with no ORDER BY: retry (line 179), approve (line 231), thumbnail (line 380), get_tile (tiles.py:210) and slides[0] at line 472 — Postgres does not guarantee row order without ORDER BY, so tiles and pipeline stages can come from different slides.

```
slide_obj = Slide(
    case_id=case_id,
    gcs_uri_original=gcs_uri
)
db.add(slide_obj)
db.flush()
```
**Impact:** Second upload 500s with an opaque UNIQUE violation, or the case ends up with mixed slides where the viewer shows one and grading ran on another.

**Fix:** Reject upload/finalize with 409 when the case already has a slide (or explicitly model multi-slide cases with an ordered 'primary' flag) and order slide queries by created_at.

*Verifier note:* Confirmed. upload_slide_file (cases.py:127-145) and finalize_slide_upload (cases.py:336-350) both unconditionally insert a Slide plus a StageExecution hardcoded to stage='ingest', attempt=1, with no check for an existing slide. models/stage_execution.py:40 declares UniqueConstraint('case_id','stage','attempt'), so a second upload to the same case raises IntegrityError on commit -> unhandled -> opaque 500; if ingest had already been retried (index 207's endpoint bumps attempt), attempt=1 is free again and the insert succeeds, leaving two Slide rows. Every consumer then picks one with no ORDER BY: retry cases.py:179 .first(), approve cases.py:231 .first(), thumbnail cases.py:380 `.limit(1)` + .first(), tiles.py:210 .first(), and get_case_detail cases.py:472 `slides[0]` from an unordered select at line 437 — Postgres guarantees no order without ORDER BY, so the tile stream and the stage input_ref can legitimately resolve to different slides. Slide has a created_at column (models/slide.py:32-36) so the ordering fix is available. Reachable from the UI: api.ts:96 posts to /slide/upload with no client-side guard against re-upload. Medium is right — 500 is annoying, the split-slide case is silent and worse.

#### 207. retry_case_stage accepts any stage name and any current status, creating rows the worker never picks up or duplicate concurrent runs

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/cases.py:191`

stage_name is an unvalidated path string. worker/main.py:56-59 only polls stages in HANDLERS, so POST /stages/foo/retry inserts a StageExecution that stays 'queued' forever and pollutes GET /cases/{id}. There is also no check that the latest attempt is 'failed' (or 'rejected'), so retrying a running stage starts a second concurrent execution of the same stage.

```
new_stage = StageExecution(
    case_id=case_id,
    stage=stage_name,
    attempt=next_attempt,
    status="queued",
```
**Impact:** Junk permanently-queued rows and duplicate concurrent runs writing to the same cases/{case_id}/<stage>/ GCS prefix.

**Fix:** Validate stage_name against the known stage list (400 otherwise) and require existing_stage.status in ('failed', 'rejected') (409 otherwise).

*Verifier note:* Confirmed on both halves. `stage_name: str` is an unvalidated path parameter (cases.py:170) and is written straight into the new row at cases.py:193. worker/main.py:56-63 defines HANDLERS = {ingest, preprocess, qc, triage, mitosis, grading, report} and worker/main.py:75-84 filters the poll with `StageExecution.stage.in_(stages_list)`, so POST /cases/{id}/stages/foo/retry inserts a row the worker can never claim; get_case_detail (cases.py:438) selects all StageExecution rows for the case with no stage filter, so the junk row does surface in the API response. Separately, cases.py:183-189 reads the latest attempt only to compute next_attempt and never inspects existing_stage.status, so retrying a 'running' or 'queued' stage starts a second concurrent execution of the same stage against the same GCS prefix. Note the second half is reachable from the UI even without hand-crafted requests: StageRail.tsx:47 and TriageViewer.tsx:116 both call retryStage with no guard on current status. Distinct from index 206 (different endpoint, and 206's duplicate-run path is the *next* stage, not the same one). Medium is appropriate.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/cases.py:189` (retry_case_stage creates a new attempt while the previous attempt may still be queued/running, and accepts arbitrary stage names); `backend/app/routers/cases.py:191` (Retry endpoint accepts arbitrary stage names and re-queues stages already running)

#### 282. No 'rejected' transition exists anywhere: awaiting_review -> rejected -> re-queued is unreachable

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** PRD deviation · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/cases.py:217`

PRD 00-overview.md §5.2 defines `awaiting_review → rejected → (stage re-queued with edits applied)` and §5.6 requires a `stage_rejected` audit event. The only transitions implemented are approve/confirm/retry; grep of backend/app and backend/worker finds the word 'rejected' only in the StageExecution status comment (models/stage_execution.py:20) and mitosis candidate labels. The frontend has no reject call either.

```
@router.post("/{case_id}/stages/{stage_name}/approve", status_code=status.HTTP_202_ACCEPTED)
def approve_case_stage(
```
**Impact:** A pathologist who disagrees with a QC/triage/mitosis/grading output has no way to reject it; their only options are to confirm (advancing bad output) or hit 'retry', which creates a new attempt without carrying edits and leaves the old row in awaiting_review forever. The 'rejected' state and audit event required by the PRD are dead.

The only stage-transition endpoints are cases.py:167 retry, cases.py:217 approve, and per-stage /confirm (triage.py:479, mitosis.py:617, grading.py:666). No frontend reject call (frontend/lib/api.ts has only retryStage/approveStage). So the state and audit event are genuinely dead. Downgraded from high to medium because the stated impact overstates it: a disagreeing pathologist is not limited to confirm-or-retry, since each review stage stores review_edits and applies them at confirm (triage.py:511 apply_edit_ops over stage_exec.review_edits; mitosis add_candidate/bulk_action; grading recompute/overrides), so bad machine output can be corrected and then confirmed. What is truly missing is the named 'rejected' status, the stage_rejected audit record, and an edit-carrying re-queue.

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** PRD deviation · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/cases.py:288`

PRD 00-overview §5.6 fixes the minimum vocabulary: case_created, slide_uploaded, stage_started, stage_output, stage_confirmed, stage_rejected, review_edit, score_override, report_signed, model_invocation; PRD 01 §5 acceptance line 83 requires 'case_created → slide_uploaded → stage_started → stage_output'. cases.py emits 'stage_approved' (approve) and 'stage_retried' (retry), triage.py/mitosis.py emit 'stage_confirmed' for the same semantic action, and no code path (worker/main.py:69 marks running without an audit row) emits stage_started. ```

```
app/routers/cases.py:203  event_type="stage_retried",
worker/main.py:69  stage_exec.status = "running"  # no AuditEvent emitted
```
**Impact:** GET /cases/{id}/audit cannot be filtered or validated against the contract; the same clinical action (stage confirmation) appears under three different names depending on which router handled it, and the audit log has no record of when a stage began running or which attempt.

A repo-wide grep of event_type= shows cases.py:288 'stage_approved' and cases.py:203 'stage_retried', while triage.py:579 and mitosis.py:678 emit 'stage_confirmed' for the same confirm-and-queue-next action (triage.py:576-583 is literally the approve path), and grading.py:786 'stage_5_grading_confirmed', report.py:640 'stage_6_report_signed'/700 'stage_6_report_amended' add more ad-hoc names. 'stage_started' appears nowhere except the comment in app/models/audit.py:17; worker/main.py:68-70 sets status='running' + started_at and commits with no AuditEvent, so the PRD acceptance sequence can never be satisfied. #### 415. Upload validation (extension whitelist, 20GB size cap) required before issuing an upload URL is entirely absent

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** PRD deviation · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/cases.py:314`

PRD §2.2: 'Validation before issuing URL: extension ∈ {.svs, .ndpi, .mrxs, .tif, .tiff, .dcm}, size ≤ 20 GB.' `get_slide_upload_url` accepts `SlideUploadUrlRequest` (backend/app/schemas/case.py:23-26, which carries `size_bytes` and `content_type`) but never reads `req.size_bytes` or `req.content_type` anywhere, and performs no extension whitelist check — any filename extension is accepted verbatim as the object's ext. The same is true of the live `/slide/upload` multipart endpoint (cases.py:95-124), which likewise performs no extension or size check before uploading to GCS and queuing ingest.

```
def get_slide_upload_url(
    case_id: uuid.UUID,
    req: SlideUploadUrlRequest,
    ...
):
    ...
    ext = req.filename.rsplit(".", 1)[-1].lower() if "." in req.filename else "svs"
    # req.size_bytes and req.content_type are never referenced
```
**Impact:** A client can request an upload URL (or directly upload) for an arbitrarily large file of any type; the worker will attempt to ingest it via OpenSlide/PIL regardless, wasting scratch disk/CPU on non-WSI files and providing no early, friendly rejection for oversized files as the PRD intends.

**Fix:** Validate `req.filename`'s extension against the allowed set and reject `req.size_bytes > 20*1024**3` with a 4xx before calling generate_signed_upload_url; apply the same checks to the `/slide/upload` direct-upload path using `Content-Length`/filename.

*Verifier note:* Confirmed factually. SlideUploadUrlRequest carries filename/size_bytes/content_type (backend/app/schemas/case.py:23-26), but get_slide_upload_url (cases.py:302-323) references only req.filename at line 314 to derive ext; grep confirms req.size_bytes and req.content_type appear nowhere in the router. No extension whitelist on either path — upload_slide_file (cases.py:108) does the identical unchecked rsplit. PRD 01-stage-v4.0-walking-skeleton.md:33 explicitly requires 'extension in {.svs,.ndpi,.mrxs,.tif,.tiff,.dcm}, size <= 20 GB' before issuing the URL, so the gap is genuine. Downgraded high->medium: the impact is a missing early rejection and wasted worker scratch/CPU (worker/ingest.py opens it regardless), not a security hole — the derived ext is only concatenated into a GCS object key (cases.py:110, 316) and GCS object names are flat literals, so '..' segments give no traversal, and the object path already contains no filename per PRD line 31.

#### 210. Case thumbnail downloads the full raw WSI on every request and 500s when the blob is missing

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Performance · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/cases.py:398`

get_case_thumbnail re-downloads gcs_uri_original (the multi-GB original) into a temp file each call, opens it under the global OpenSlide lock, and deletes it. MitosisViewer.tsx:465 uses this URL as an <img> src, so every viewer mount triggers a full slide download. download_blob_to_filename is outside the inner try, so a missing blob raises google.api_core.exceptions.NotFound -> unhandled -> 500 instead of 404. Meanwhile preprocess already writes cases/{case_id}/preprocess/thumbnail.png to the artifacts bucket (worker/preprocess.py:172) which is never used here.

```
download_blob_to_filename(bucket_name, blob_name, temp_file)

try:
    import openslide
    with OPENSLIDE_GLOBAL_LOCK:
        oslide = openslide.OpenSlide(temp_file)
        thumb = oslide.get_thumbnail((256, 256)).convert("RGB")
```
**Impact:** Gigabytes of egress and minutes of latency for a 256px image; blocks all other OpenSlide work via the shared lock; hard 500 on missing object.

**Fix:** Serve the preprocess thumbnail.png artifact (or generate once at ingest and store it), and catch NotFound -> 404.

*Verifier note:* Confirmed. cases.py:373-421: every GET /cases/{id}/thumbnail mkstemps a file, calls download_blob_to_filename(bucket, blob, temp_file) on gcs_uri_original — the full multi-GB original — then opens it under OPENSLIDE_GLOBAL_LOCK for a 256px PNG and deletes it; no caching, no Range read, and no auth dependency on this route either. The download at line 398 sits in the outer `try:` whose only clause is `finally:` (line 416) — there is no `except` — so google.api_core.exceptions.NotFound from blob.download_to_filename (core/gcs.py:74-79) propagates to an unhandled 500, not a 404. The inner try/except at lines 400-414 wraps only openslide/PIL. Frontend usage confirmed: MitosisViewer.tsx:465 builds the URL and MitosisViewer.tsx:950 uses it as an <img src>, so it fires on every viewer mount. One correction to the proposed fix, not the defect: worker/preprocess.py:172 only *builds* the string thumbnail_uri and puts it in output.json — `grep -rn 'thumbnail.png' backend/worker backend/app` shows no upload_blob_* call for it, so cases/{case_id}/preprocess/thumbnail.png is never actually written and cannot simply be served; the thumbnail has to be generated and stored first (e.g. during ingest). Medium is right.

The grading router selects the stage row with no ordering and no limit, taking whatever the database returns first. ...

**Impact:** Post-sign-off review edits with no lock and no value-level audit; review_summary can show all_patches_reviewed=False on a confirmed stage.

*Verifier note:* Confirmed. review_grading_patches (grading.py:368-437) and review_grading_hpfs (441-515) fetch Case (375/448) and Grading (379/452) only; the StageExecution is loaded at 433-435 / 511-513 AFTER the mutation and commit, purely to render the response — nothing reads stage_exec.status before writing. reset_all wipes the dict unconditionally (401, 481). Grep across backend/app/routers/*.py shows no post-confirm lock anywhere (only writes of status='confirmed' at grading.py:757, mitosis.py:648, triage.py:532, report.py:632), so this is not handled elsewhere. Divergence is real: worker/report.py:57-65 reads the persisted gradings columns, which review never touches, while GET's 'current' block is recomputed live from dyn_agg (grading.py:277-320) — e.g. eff_mitotic_score falls back to calc_mitotic_score whenever overrides has no 'mitotic' key, so a post-confirm HPF edit changes the displayed mitotic score and mitotic_summary (332-336) but not the signed PDF; reset_all flips all_patches_reviewed to False on a confirmed stage. Audit payload (424-427, 502-505) records only action + count, no before/after values. Systemic across stages rather than grading-specific, but accurate as written. Medium stands.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/grading.py:368` (Grading patch/HPF review endpoints have no stage-status gate)

#### 154. review_edits never used; pathologist edits stored only in gradings.overrides with non-standard audit event names and no values

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** PRD deviation · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/grading.py:422`

PRD 00-overview section 5.2 stores pathologist edits as an RFC-6902 diff in stage_executions.review_edits and section 5.6 names the events review_edit / score_override / stage_confirmed. The grading router never touches review_edits (triage does), emits 'patches_reviewed' / 'hpfs_reviewed' with only {action, reviewed_count} (no patch ids, no from/to values) and 'stage_5_grading_confirmed' instead of stage_confirmed; score_override payload uses from_score/to_score keys (line 809) rather than the PRD's {component, from, to, justification}.

```
event_type="patches_reviewed",
        stage="grading",
        payload={
            "action": payload.action,
            "reviewed_count": len(payload.reviews) if payload.action == "update" else len(machine_patches)
```
**Impact:** Per-patch edits (e.g. tubule 25 -> 60 on p_007) are not recoverable from the append-only audit log; downstream stages that read review_edits (report) see none.

**Fix:** Write the diff to stage_exec.review_edits, log one review_edit per changed patch/HPF with before/after, and use the PRD event vocabulary.

*Verifier note:* Verified against PRD 00-overview line 88 (pathologist edits stored as an RFC-6902-style diff in review_edits) and line 153 (event vocabulary includes review_edit / score_override / stage_confirmed). grep for review_edits across backend/ hits only triage.py (128, 154, 327-328, 464, 510) and the model — grading.py never writes it. The grading router emits patches_reviewed (422) / hpfs_reviewed (500) with payload {action, reviewed_count} only — no patch ids, no from/to values — and stage_5_grading_confirmed (786) where triage.py:579 and mitosis.py:678 both use the PRD's stage_confirmed; score_override at 805-812 uses from_score/to_score rather than the PRD's {component, from, to, justification} (05-grading line 77). Two corrections: current per-patch edits are not unrecoverable — they persist as latest state in gradings.overrides['patches'] (415-416) — what is missing is the append-only history, which is the real audit defect; and "downstream stages that read review_edits (report) see none" is wrong, no report code reads review_edits at all. Medium stands on the audit-trail gap.

#### 601. Grading stage silently rewrites the confirmed Stage 4 mitotic result without writing back to HpfSite or reopening mitosis

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** PRD deviation · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/grading.py:487`

POST /hpfs/review with action=update accepts mitotic_count per HPF and stores it only in gradings.overrides['hpfs']; the builder then recomputes calc_mitotic_score from those counts (lines 247-251) and additionally honours a top-level overrides['mitotic']['score'] (line 280). Nothing updates the HpfSite rows or the mitosis stage. PRD 05-stage-v4.4-grading.md section 5 specifies the mitotic card as 'read-only summary from v4.3 ... + reopen stage link (re-enters mitosis review; grading re-runs on re-confirm)'. Downstream, worker/report.py:55-63 reads HpfSite rows (Stage 4 counts) for evidence and grading.mitotic_score for the score, and routers/mitosis.py:105 keeps showing the Stage 4 counts.

```
hpf_overrides[h_seq] = {
    "status": r.status,
    "mitotic_count": r.mitotic_count,
...
eff_mitotic_score = overrides.get("mitotic", {}).get("score", calc_mitotic_score)
```
**Impact:** The signed report can carry a mitotic score derived from counts that differ from the HPF evidence it prints; the Stage 4 record and the grading record disagree with no audit of the changed values.

**Fix:** Make the mitotic card read-only in grading (drop mitotic_count from SingleHpfReview and the 'mitotic' override key); expose a 'reopen mitosis' action that sets the mitosis stage back to awaiting_review and re-queues grading on re-confirm, as the PRD specifies.

*Verifier note:* Core claim confirmed, downstream impact partly overstated. SingleHpfReview carries mitotic_count (line 69) and /hpfs/review action=update writes it into overrides['hpfs'][seq] only (lines 485-491, 493-494); grading.py touches HpfSite exclusively via SELECT (lines 130, 196, 460) — no UPDATE anywhere in the file, and `grep -rn reopen app/routers/` returns nothing, so there is no reopen-mitosis affordance. The builder then recomputes calc_mitotic_score from those overridden counts (lines 245-251) and additionally honours overrides['mitotic']['score'] at line 280, and confirm persists the client's mitotic_score to gradings (line 743). prd/05-stage-v4.4-grading.md:73 does specify 'Mitotic card: read-only summary from v4.3 (count, mm2, score) + reopen stage link (re-enters mitosis review; grading re-runs on re-confirm)', so the PRD deviation is real, as is the Stage-4/Stage-5 divergence (routers/mitosis.py:104-106 keeps serving the untouched HpfSite rows) and the weak audit trail (the 'hpfs_reviewed' event at 497-506 records only action + count, never the from/to values — no score_override event is emitted for HPF count edits). Correction to the impact statement: worker/report.py:55 fetches HpfSite rows into `hpfs` but never uses them (grep for hpf/mitotic in that file: only lines 23, 55, 63-64, 128, 165-169; the report's mitotic evidence image is a fixed crop path, not HPF counts), so the report does not print HPF counts that could contradict the score. Severity lowered high -> medium: the signed mitotic score reflects counts the pathologist actually entered and confirmed, so the harm is stale Stage-4 records plus a missing per-value audit, not a wrong signed grade.

*Also reported at:* `frontend/components/viewer/GradingReviewWorkspace.tsx:1490` (Stage 5 HPF count editor creates a second source of truth for the mitotic count, diverging from Stage 4)

#### 147. On-demand patch fallback downloads the entire WSI per image request

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Performance · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/grading.py:546`

Whenever the 512x512 PNG is missing in GCS, each /patches/{id}/image request creates a scratch dir and downloads the whole slide (multi-GB) before extracting one patch. The review screen requests 24 patch images at once, so a single page load can trigger 24 concurrent full-slide downloads on the API container - and, because of the NameError described in the synthetic-image finding, every download is thrown away.

```
download_blob_to_filename(raw_bucket_name, slide_blob, local_slide_path)
```
**Impact:** API disk/network exhaustion and multi-minute image loads on any case whose patches were not uploaded (e.g. the GCS 403 state).

**Fix:** Remove the on-demand branch from the request path; return 404 and have the worker (which already has the slide open) be the only producer of patch PNGs.

*Verifier note:* Mechanism confirmed: any GCS read failure at 526 falls through `except Exception: pass` (528-529) into mktemp + download_blob_to_filename of the whole slide at 546, inside the request handler, with no cache and no concurrency limit. The 24-request fan-out is real — worker/grading.py:256 stores image_url='/api/v1/stages/grading/{case}/patches/{id}/image' per patch and GradingReviewWorkspace.tsx:960 renders one <img> per patch in the grid. Downgraded high->medium on two grounds the finder overstates: (1) in the specific GCS-403 state cited, download_blob_to_filename fails immediately with the same permission error, so no bytes are transferred and no disk fills — the exhaustion case needs the raw bucket readable while the artifact patch is missing; (2) the wasted-work framing is right but means the observable symptom is bandwidth/latency, not corrupted output, since the request already always ends at the synthetic-image path (see index 140). Overlaps index 140 in remediation — deleting the on-demand branch fixes both — but it is a distinct defect (cost vs. fabricated output), not a duplicate.

#### 691. Latent self-deadlock: on-demand patch extraction re-acquires the non-reentrant global OpenSlide lock

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Concurrency · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/grading.py:572`

get_patch_image holds OPENSLIDE_GLOBAL_LOCK and then calls worker.grading.extract_10x_patch, which acquires the same lock again (backend/worker/grading.py:76). OPENSLIDE_GLOBAL_LOCK is a plain threading.Lock (backend/app/core/openslide_lock.py:5), not an RLock, so the second acquire blocks the thread that already owns it -- forever. Today this is masked because the same function also references two names the module never imports (Hotspot at line 553 and OPENSLIDE_GLOBAL_LOCK itself -- `grep -c openslide_lock app/routers/grading.py` returns 0), so a NameError is raised at line 553 and swallowed by the except at line 596. The moment someone applies the obvious fix for the already-reported 'undefined names' finding (adding the two imports), this endpoint permanently wedges the API.

```
with OPENSLIDE_GLOBAL_LOCK:
                oslide = openslide.OpenSlide(local_slide_path)
                raw_img = extract_10x_patch(     # -> worker/grading.py:76 `with OPENSLIDE_GLOBAL_LOCK:`
```
**Impact:** After the import fix, one GET /stages/grading/{case}/patches/{id}/image whose blob is missing deadlocks that worker thread while holding the process-wide lock. Every OpenSlide-backed endpoint (tiles, case thumbnail, hotspot thumbnail, HPF thumbnail, add_candidate) then blocks forever; the API must be restarted. No error is logged.

**Fix:** Make extract_10x_patch lock-free (document that callers hold the lock) or switch OPENSLIDE_GLOBAL_LOCK to threading.RLock(). Fix this before adding the missing imports, not after.

*Verifier note:* The deadlock is real as written: grading.py:572 takes OPENSLIDE_GLOBAL_LOCK, then 574 calls worker.grading.extract_10x_patch, which re-acquires the same object at worker/grading.py:76 (`with OPENSLIDE_GLOBAL_LOCK: rgba = slide_obj.read_region(...)`), and app/core/openslide_lock.py:5 is `threading.Lock()`, not an RLock. The masking claim also checks out: `grep -n 'Hotspot\|OPENSLIDE_GLOBAL_LOCK' app/routers/grading.py` returns only lines 553 and 572 — neither name is imported (imports end at line 45), so line 553 raises NameError first and the bare `except Exception` at 596 swallows it, and 572 is unreachable today. Downgrading high->medium: the failure cannot occur in the current tree; it only fires if someone adds the two imports without also making the lock reentrant. The trap is genuine and worth fixing (RLock is a one-line fix), but severity should reflect that it is latent, not live.

#### 602. Confirm merge lets the client overwrite or erase server-held patch/HPF review records

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Data integrity · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/grading.py:752`

The justification loop explicitly skips the 'patches' and 'hpfs' keys (line 718), but merged_overrides.update(payload.overrides) still merges them verbatim. A confirm payload containing 'overrides': {'patches': {}, 'hpfs': {}} passes all gates (they are evaluated from the pre-merge state at line 699) and then replaces the reviewed_by/reviewed_at/status records the review endpoints wrote, or substitutes forged ones.

```
merged_overrides = dict(grading_record.overrides or {})
merged_overrides.update(payload.overrides)
grading_record.overrides = merged_overrides
```
**Impact:** After confirmation the stored review evidence (who approved which patch/HPF, with what values) can be blanked or rewritten by the confirming client; a later GET shows 0/24 patches reviewed on a confirmed stage.

**Fix:** Reject payload.overrides keys other than the allowed component names (tubule, pleo) with 400, and never merge 'patches'/'hpfs' from the confirm payload.

*Verifier note:* Verified. The justification loop skips 'patches'/'hpfs' (line 718) but the merge is unconditional: `merged_overrides.update(payload.overrides)` at 752 — dict.update replaces whole sub-dicts, it does not deep-merge, so a payload key 'patches': {} wipes every per-patch record written by /patches/review (lines 391-410) and 'hpfs': {} wipes those from /hpfs/review (lines 476-491), including reviewed_by/reviewed_at/status. The gates cannot catch it: current_data is built at line 699 from grading_record.overrides as it stands *before* the merge, so all_patches_reviewed/all_hpfs_reviewed pass on the pre-merge state and the destructive write happens 53 lines later. Post-confirm GET therefore reports 0/24 patches reviewed on a confirmed stage, and forged reviewed_by values are equally accepted. Not a duplicate of 600: same root cause (overrides is an unvalidated Dict[str, Any]) but a distinct failure mode (silent evidence loss/forgery vs. type crash) and a distinct fix (key allowlist / never merging patches+hpfs from the confirm payload). Medium is right — it needs a hand-crafted confirm payload, and no clinical score is altered, only the audit/review evidence.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/grading.py:752` (Grading confirm payload can overwrite the entire patch/HPF review record after the gates were checked)

#### 115. recompute accepts arbitrary label strings and unvalidated HPF dicts: gate bypass, KeyError 500s, and no server-side non-overlap/radius validation

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Security · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/mitosis.py:53`

candidate_labels is Dict[str,str] with no enum: a label like 'reviewed' is persisted (367-373), is not 'unreviewed' so it passes the confirm gate (637), and is not 'mitosis' so it is silently excluded from the count. hpfs is List[Dict[str,Any]]: h['seq'] / h['center_um'] (398-399) raise KeyError -> 500; radius_um is accepted as sent (400) so a client can set radius_um=5000 and collapse the density; nothing checks the PRD §6 requirement 'non-overlap validated server-side on recompute' or that centres are inside the slide. seq duplicates hit the (case_id, seq) PK -> IntegrityError 500.

```
candidate_labels: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None # {"m_0001": "mitosis", ...}
hpfs: Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]] = None # [{"seq": 1, "center_um": [x, y], "radius_um": 262.0}]
```
**Impact:** Malformed or malicious payloads crash the endpoint or silently corrupt the clinical score; the safety gate can be bypassed without a bulk-reject audit entry.

**Fix:** Use Literal['mitosis','not_mitosis','unreviewed'] for labels and a pydantic HpfIn model (seq: conint(ge=1), center_um: tuple[float,float], radius_um fixed from config); reject overlapping centres (dist < 2r) with 422.

*Verifier note:* All sub-claims check out. (1) `candidate_labels: Optional[Dict[str,str]]` (line 53) has no enum, and recompute writes it straight through: lines 367-373 set `d.label = new_label` for any string. `Detection.label` (backend/app/models/detection.py:24) is a plain String with no CHECK constraint. (2) A label like 'reviewed' then (a) never matches the confirm gate's `Detection.label == "unreviewed"` (line 637) -> gate bypassed with no bulk-reject audit row, and (b) never matches `cand.get("label") != "mitosis"` in backend/pipeline/scoring.py:34 -> silently excluded from count_total. (3) `h["seq"]` / `h["center_um"]` at lines 398-399 are raw dict subscripts on `List[Dict[str,Any]]` -> KeyError -> unhandled 500. (4) `radius_um` is taken from the client at line 400 and flows into `compute_nottingham_mitotic_score(radius_um=updated_hpfs[0]["radius_um"])` at line 426, so radius_um=5000 inflates area_mm2 by ~364x and collapses the score to 1 - the clinical score is client-controllable. (5) HpfSite PK is composite (case_id, seq) (backend/app/models/hpf_site.py:18-19), so duplicate seq values in one payload flush as an IntegrityError -> 500. (6) prd/04-stage-v4.3-mitosis.md:84 explicitly requires 'non-overlap validated server-side on recompute'; there is no separation/bounds check anywhere in recompute_scoring. Note the router carries no auth dependency at all (only a cosmetic X-User-Role header from frontend/lib/api.ts), so these payloads are reachable. Severity medium is right: no data destruction, but score corruption + gate bypass + 500s.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/mitosis.py:372` (/stages/mitosis/recompute writes arbitrary label strings onto detections, silently zeroing the count and bypassing the confirm safety gate)

#### 592. Review mutates machine labels in place and never writes review_edits; confirm does not snapshot the reviewed summary, violating the PRD 'machine output is never mutated' contract

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** PRD deviation · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/mitosis.py:370`

PRD 00 §5.2: 'Pathologist edits are stored as an RFC-6902-style JSON diff in review_edits — machine output is never mutated. Confirmation snapshot = machine output + applied diff.' recompute overwrites Detection.label/label_source directly and confirm_mitosis_stage only sets status/reviewed_by/reviewed_at; StageExecution.review_edits is never populated and mitosis/output.json keeps the pre-review labels and score. Nothing persists the final count_total/area_mm2/per_mm2/mitotic_score at confirm time.

```
if d.label != new_label:
    d.label = new_label
    d.label_source = "pathologist"
```
**Impact:** The model's original label for a toggled detection survives only in the GCS artifact (and is lost entirely for pathologist-added rows), the v4.6 label exporter has no diff to join, the 'reject → re-queue with edits applied' transition has nothing to apply, and downstream stages must re-derive the score from mutable HPF rows.

**Fix:** On recompute, append {op:'replace', path:'/candidates/<id>/label', from, to} entries to stage_exec.review_edits; keep a model_label column (or leave label immutable and add pathologist_label); on confirm, compute and persist the final summary onto the stage execution and write a reviewed output_ref.

*Verifier note:* Verified against prd/00-overview.md:88 ('Pathologist edits are stored as an RFC-6902-style JSON diff in review_edits — machine output is never mutated. Confirmation snapshot = machine output + applied diff'). recompute_scoring mutates in place at mitosis.py:370-373 (d.label = new_label; d.label_source = 'pathologist'), bulk_reject_unreviewed does the same at 553-555, and confirm_mitosis_stage (618-676) sets only status/reviewed_at/reviewed_by plus the grading requeue — it writes neither stage_exec.review_edits nor any reviewed output_ref, and never persists count_total/area_mm2/per_mm2/mitotic_score. StageExecution.review_edits exists (app/models/stage_execution.py:34) and the triage router does populate it (app/routers/triage.py:464), so this is a gap in the mitosis path specifically, not a missing column. Detection has no model_label column (app/models/detection.py:23-24), so the pre-review label survives only in the GCS output.json artifact, which does not contain pathologist-added rows at all — the artifact+diff reconstruction the PRD specifies cannot be performed. prd/07-stage-v4.6-validation.md:45-46 queries review_edits for edit_rate/edits_per_case, so mitosis cases will read as zero-edit. Partial mitigation: an AuditEvent 'review_edit' is written per toggle (mitosis.py:376-389), but the 300 ms debounce collapses rapid toggles to one audit_toggle and it lands in audit_events, not review_edits. Medium is correct.

#### 344. recompute replaces all HPF sites from unvalidated client dicts with no overlap or count check

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/mitosis.py:394`

payload.hpfs is List[Dict[str, Any]]; the handler deletes every HpfSite row and re-inserts using h['seq'] / h['center_um'] (KeyError -> 500 after the delete has been issued in the same session), accepts any number of HPFs and any positions. PRD 04 (HPF editing) requires non-overlap validated server-side on recompute; nothing checks separation or count == hpf.count.

```
db.execute(delete(HpfSite).where(HpfSite.case_id == case_id))  for h in payload.hpfs:  hpf_row = HpfSite(case_id=case_id, seq=h["seq"], center_um=h["center_um"], ...)
```
**Impact:** Overlapping or off-tissue HPFs inflate/deflate the mitotic density; malformed payloads 500 mid-transaction.

**Fix:** Pydantic model for HPFs (seq 1..N unique, center pair), enforce min separation and count from configs/mitosis.yaml, reject otherwise.

*Verifier note:* Validation gap is real and PRD-backed: RecomputePayload.hpfs is List[Dict[str, Any]] (line 54), lines 394-405 delete every HpfSite for the case and re-insert from raw h['seq']/h['center_um'] with no count, separation, or bounds check, while prd/04-stage-v4.3-mitosis.md:84 explicitly requires 'non-overlap validated server-side on recompute' and configs/mitosis.yaml carries hpf.count=10 and hpf.min_separation_um=524.0 unused by this path. The KeyError->500 is also real (unhandled). But the 'malformed payloads 500 mid-transaction' impact is wrong: get_db (backend/app/core/db.py:38-42) never commits on the exception path and Session.close() rolls the transaction back, so the issued DELETE is discarded and no HPF rows are lost — it is a plain 500, not partial destruction. Severity stays medium on the missing overlap/count validation alone, since it directly moves the mitotic density.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/mitosis.py:392` (Server-side recompute accepts arbitrary HPF center edits with no non-overlap validation); `backend/app/routers/mitosis.py:392` (/stages/mitosis/recompute lets the client replace the HPF set with any number of unvalidated, overlapping fields, directly controlling the area denominator of the mitotic score)

#### 753. Pathologist-added mitosis crop uses mpp_x for the Y-axis conversion

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/mitosis.py:478`

add_candidate reads only mpp_x from the slide (line 461, mpp_y is never fetched) and converts both axes with it. On any scanner where mpp_x != mpp_y (common on NDPI and on some resampled TIFF pyramids) the vertical position of the extracted 128x128 crop is wrong by the mpp_y/mpp_x ratio. The same class of mistake appears at routers/grading.py:563 (`cy_px = int(np.mean([pt[1] ...]) / mpp_x)`) and worker/triage.py:230/303. Note the correct pairing exists a few hundred lines earlier in the same file (line 298-299 uses mpp_x/mpp_y).

```
px = int(cx_um / mpp_x - 64)
                        py = int(cy_um / mpp_x - 64)
```
**Impact:** The crop stored for a mitosis the pathologist clicked in the viewer shows a different piece of tissue than the one clicked, and that crop is what appears in the review gallery and in the report evidence panel.

**Fix:** Fetch mpp_y alongside mpp_x and use it for the Y conversion -- or better, route through pipeline/coords.um_to_px as PRD section 5.1 requires.

*Verifier note:* Verified line by line. add_candidate reads only mpp_x (line 461: `mpp_x = float(getattr(slide_obj, "mpp_x", 0.25) or 0.25)`); mpp_y is never fetched, and line 478 computes `py = int(cy_um / mpp_x - 64)`. The correct pairing does exist in the same file at 243-244 and 298-299 (get_hpf_thumbnail reads mpp_y and uses `cy_px = int(cy_um / mpp_y)`), which rules out 'intentional'. Cross-references check out too: grading.py:562 uses `cy_px = int(np.mean([pt[1] ...]) / mpp_x)` and worker/triage.py:230/303 derive height_um / stride_y_um from mpp_x. Impact is a systematic Y offset of cy_um*(1/mpp_x - 1/mpp_y), which grows with slide position — on an anisotropic scanner that is thousands of pixels, i.e. the wrong tissue in the stored crop that then feeds the gallery and report. Harmless only on the common mpp_x == mpp_y slide, so medium is right.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/mitosis.py:478` (add_candidate uses mpp_x for the y axis when cutting the crop)

#### 399. add_candidate endpoint makes two unguarded real GCS uploads, breaking test_add_candidate_endpoint offline

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/mitosis.py:497`

POST /api/v1/stages/mitosis/add_candidate (exercised by tests/test_mitosis_api.py::test_add_candidate_endpoint) calls upload_blob_from_bytes() twice against real GCS with no try/except, unlike other GCS reads in this same router which are defensively wrapped.

```
from app.core.gcs import upload_blob_from_bytes
    upload_blob_from_bytes(settings.GCS_ARTIFACTS_BUCKET, f"cases/{case_id}/mitosis/crops/{new_id}.png", crop_bytes, "image/png")
    upload_blob_from_bytes(settings.GCS_ARTIFACTS_BUCKET, f"cases/{case_id}/mitosis/crops/{new_id}_orig.png", crop_bytes, "image/png")
```
**Impact:** Without real, authorized GCS access, upload_blob_from_bytes() raises and the endpoint 500s, so the test's `assert res.status_code == 200` fails offline; in production, any transient GCS outage loses the pathologist-added candidate entirely (the Detection DB row is only created after these two calls succeed).

**Fix:** Wrap the uploads in try/except with a retry or a queued-upload fallback, and create the Detection record even if the crop image upload fails (mark crop_uri as pending) rather than making the whole request fail on GCS unavailability.

*Verifier note:* Evidence exists verbatim at mitosis.py:496-498 and the two uploads are unguarded, unlike every other GCS call in this router (192/220 wrapped in try/except, 337-345 wrapped, and even the slide download in this same handler at 471-482 is wrapped). upload_blob_from_bytes -> get_bucket -> get_gcs_client -> storage.Client (core/gcs.py:16-19, 46-51) with no fake/local backend; config.py has USE_REAL_GCS and STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST but nothing in this path honours them, and there is no conftest.py anywhere in the repo, so tests/test_mitosis_api.py::test_add_candidate_endpoint really does reach live GCS (the fixture creates no Slide row, so crop_pil is synthetic and execution falls straight through to the uploads). Without credentials the TestClient re-raises, so the test errors rather than even returning 500. Downgrading high -> medium: the uploads precede db.add(det)/db.commit (512, 525), so a GCS failure aborts cleanly with nothing half-written; the pathologist must re-pin, which is annoying but not silent data loss, and the offline-test breakage is a dev-environment gap, not a production defect.

#### 123. re_place_hpfs ignores mitosis.yaml and places fields in a fixed 5 mm box at the slide origin when no mitoses are confirmed

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/mitosis.py:593`

When there are zero confirmed detections the bounding box becomes (0,0,5000,5000) µm (slide top-left corner, typically glass); with hotspots present but outside that box the tumour mask is all-False, so pass 1-2 place nothing and pass 3 fabricates 10 HPFs around (2500,2500) µm. generate_mitosis_density_map/greedy_place_hpfs are called with library defaults (598) rather than hpf.radius_um / min_separation_um / density_grid_res_um from configs/mitosis.yaml that the worker uses (worker/mitosis.py:305-322) — copy-paste drift between the two placement call sites.

```
xs = [d.centroid_um[0] for d in confirmed_dets] or [0.0, 5000.0]
ys = [d.centroid_um[1] for d in confirmed_dets] or [0.0, 5000.0]
bbox = (min(xs), min(ys), max(xs), max(ys))
density_map, grid_meta = generate_mitosis_density_map(cands, bounding_box_um=bbox)
```
**Impact:** Clicking 'Re-place HPFs' before confirming any mitosis moves all ten fields to the slide corner; config changes are honoured by the worker but not the API.

**Fix:** Extract one place_hpfs_for_case(case, detections, hotspots, cfg) helper used by both worker and router; when no confirmed points exist, use the hotspot polygon bbox (or refuse with 409).

*Verifier note:* Evidence exact at lines 593-598. Traced the zero-confirmed path: `confirmed_dets` empty -> xs/ys fall back to [0.0, 5000.0] -> bbox=(0,0,5000,5000) at line 595; `cands` is empty so backend/pipeline/hpf.py:52-66 splats nothing and density_map is all zeros; greedy_place_hpfs pass 1 (hpf.py:141-144) and pass 2 (hpf.py:197-201) both break immediately on `max_val <= 0.0`; pass 3 (hpf.py:231-245) then fabricates all 10 fields on a circle around the grid centre, which with pad_um=393 and nx=ny=362 lands at ~(2503, 2503) um - the slide corner, as claimed. Pass 3 also ignores tumor_mask entirely, so the hotspot-outside-the-box variant is real too. The config-drift half is true but currently latent: hpf.py's defaults (grid_res 16.0, radius 262.0, min_sep 524.0, relaxed 393.0) happen to equal configs/mitosis.yaml exactly, while backend/worker/mitosis.py:305-322 reads them from hpf_cfg - so today there is no numeric divergence, only a second uncontrolled call site. Keeping medium on the strength of the placement bug alone.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/mitosis.py:593` (re_place_hpfs with zero confirmed mitoses uses a magic 5000 um bbox and clusters 10 overlapping HPFs at an arbitrary point)

#### 116. confirm picks an arbitrary mitosis StageExecution (no attempt ordering) and never checks it is awaiting_review

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/mitosis.py:626`

get_mitosis_stage_data orders by attempt desc (92) but confirm_mitosis_stage uses .first() with no order_by, so with multiple attempts (cases.py:268-276 creates attempt+1 on re-approval) it may mark an older/failed attempt 'confirmed' while the live attempt stays awaiting_review. It also does not verify status == 'awaiting_review' before setting 'confirmed' (648), so a 'running', 'failed' or already-'confirmed' stage can be confirmed and grading re-queued, violating the state machine in prd/00-overview.md §5.2.

```
stage_exec = db.scalars(
    select(StageExecution).where(StageExecution.case_id == case_id, StageExecution.stage == "mitosis")
).first()
```
**Impact:** Wrong attempt confirmed; grading can be queued on top of a still-running or failed mitosis stage, producing a grade from partial data.

**Fix:** Order by attempt desc and require status == 'awaiting_review' (409 otherwise); reuse one helper for both endpoints.

*Verifier note:* Evidence exact at lines 626-628: `select(StageExecution).where(case_id == case_id, stage == "mitosis")` with `.first()` and no order_by, versus the GET path which does `.order_by(StageExecution.attempt.desc()).limit(1)` at line 92. Multiple mitosis attempts are genuinely reachable: backend/app/routers/cases.py:265-275 computes `next_attempt = (existing_next.attempt + 1) if existing_next else 1` and inserts a new StageExecution for the next stage on every approval, and the model's unique constraint is (case_id, stage, attempt) so several mitosis rows coexist. Row order for an unordered SELECT is not defined, so the wrong attempt can be marked confirmed. Second half also confirmed: line 648 sets status='confirmed' with no check of the current status, so a 'running', 'failed', 'rejected' or already-'confirmed' row is overwritten, and lines 661-673 (re)queue grading regardless - contradicting the state machine in prd/00-overview.md:84-86 (awaiting_review -> confirmed). Note the grading lookup at lines 654-659 has the same missing order_by, so the fix belongs in both places. (I checked GUID coercion in backend/app/models/base.py:19-22 - `process_bind_param` str()s the value, so the un-uuid'd `case_id` string in the where-clause is not itself a bug.)

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/mitosis.py:626` (confirm_mitosis_stage picks an arbitrary attempt and hard-codes the 0.50 safety-gate threshold)

#### 117. Confirm safety gate disagrees between backend (det_conf OR ver_conf >= 0.5) and frontend (ver_conf || det_conf) and with the PRD (det_conf >= 0.5)

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Frontend / UX · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/mitosis.py:638`

Backend blocks if either confidence >= 0.50; the frontend counts pending items with `(c.ver_conf || c.det_conf || 0) >= 0.50` (MitosisViewer.tsx:452), i.e. ver_conf wins when present. A candidate with det_conf 0.9 / ver_conf 0.3 (the common 'strong detector, weak heuristic verifier' case — worker labels it unreviewed via the det>=0.70&&ver>=0.35 rule at worker/mitosis.py:260) shows 0 pending in the UI but the confirm POST returns 400. PRD §6 specifies det_conf >= 0.5 only. The 0.50 constant is duplicated in code on both sides instead of configs/mitosis.yaml (PRD §5.5).

```
(Detection.det_conf >= 0.50) | (Detection.ver_conf >= 0.50)
```
**Impact:** Reviewer sees 'all reviewed' yet cannot confirm, with no list of which candidates block; conversely a ver_conf 0.55 / det_conf 0.2 item blocks the gate although the PRD would not.

**Fix:** Put gate_threshold in mitosis.yaml, apply it to det_conf only on the server, and have the UI display the server's blocking list (return ids in the 400 detail) instead of re-implementing the rule.

*Verifier note:* Both sides verified. Backend line 638: `(Detection.det_conf >= 0.50) | (Detection.ver_conf >= 0.50)`. Frontend frontend/components/viewer/MitosisViewer.tsx:451-452: `c.label === 'unreviewed' && ((c.ver_conf || c.det_conf || 0) >= 0.50)` - ver_conf shadows det_conf whenever it is non-zero. PRD prd/04-stage-v4.3-mitosis.md:88 says 'requires zero unreviewed candidates above det_conf >= 0.5', so the backend's ver_conf arm is also out of spec. One correction to the finder's example: det_conf 0.9 / ver_conf 0.3 cannot be labelled 'unreviewed' by the worker, because backend/worker/mitosis.py:260 requires ver_conf >= 0.35 in that branch; the reachable case is det_conf 0.9 / ver_conf 0.35-0.49 (unreviewed via `det_conf >= 0.70 and ver_conf >= 0.35`), which shows 0 pending in the UI yet returns 400 on confirm. The 400 detail does carry a count and is surfaced (frontend/lib/api.ts:288-291), but names no ids, so the reviewer is stuck with a contradiction. 0.50 is hard-coded on both sides and absent from configs/mitosis.yaml (which defines det_threshold/review_threshold/ver_threshold only). Severity medium stands: it is a hard block on the review workflow, not merely cosmetic.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/mitosis.py:634` (Confirm gate blocks on ver_conf as well as det_conf, broadening the spec's review-completeness check beyond what the PRD defines)

#### 182. PUT partial update resets omitted fields to hard-coded defaults; specimen_type is always reset to core_biopsy

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/report.py:74`

UpdateReportPayload gives non-None defaults to every field, and the endpoint applies a field whenever it `is not None`. Any omitted field is therefore overwritten with the default. The frontend never sends specimen_type (0 occurrences in ReportWorkspace.tsx), so every save writes specimen_type='core_biopsy' regardless of the procedure text; tumor_size_mm/laterality/tumor_site behave the same for other clients. The path {case_id} on the PUT route (line 338) is ignored in favour of payload.case_id.

```
specimen_type: Optional[str] = "core_biopsy"
procedure: Optional[str] = "Core Needle Biopsy"
laterality: Optional[str] = "right"
tumor_site: Optional[str] = "upper_outer_quadrant"
tumor_size_mm: Optional[float] = Field(default=18.0, ge=0.0)
```
**Impact:** Data loss on partial updates; a mastectomy report is stored as core_biopsy (which also affects the required-if rules in PRD 06 §2).

**Fix:** Default every field to None; validate that path case_id == payload.case_id; derive/validate specimen_type against cap_elements.yaml.

*Verifier note:* Mechanism verified: lines 74-79 give non-None literal defaults to specimen_type/procedure/laterality/tumor_site/tumor_size_mm/lvi_status/dcis_present, and 355-368 apply each `if payload.X is not None`, so an omitted field is written with the default rather than left alone. Frontend confirmed: `specimen_type` appears in frontend/ only at lib/api.ts:517 (a type field) — ReportWorkspace.tsx's handleUpdate payload (128-159) sends procedure, laterality, tumor_site, tumor_size_mm, lvi_status, dcis_present, margins, lymph_nodes, biomarkers, narrative but never specimen_type, so every save writes 'core_biopsy'. Path-param claim also holds: `@router.put("/{case_id}")` at 338 with a handler signature taking only (payload, db), so the path id is ignored and payload.case_id decides which report is written. Downgraded high -> medium: the only in-repo client sends every other field, and specimen_type is not used by the PDF renderer (report_pdf.py never reads it) nor by staging — it surfaces only in the GET/JSON export, so the demonstrated loss is one wrong synoptic element in the export. The dangerous case (a partial PUT silently resetting tumor_size_mm to 18.0 and thereby recomputing pT/stage_group at 384-394) requires a client that omits it, which does not exist in this repo. The impact sentence about 'required-if rules in PRD 06 §2' is moot: configs/cap_elements.yaml is loaded by no backend or frontend code.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/report.py:74` (UpdateReportPayload defaults clobber clinical fields on partial updates; PUT path case_id is ignored)

#### 180. NPI is a hard-coded fabricated default ('NPI-1982347102') and never validated

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Clinical correctness · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/report.py:90`

SignReportPayload defaults npi to a made-up identifier; the frontend pre-fills the same value (ReportWorkspace.tsx:76) and report_pdf.py:344 falls back to it. No format check (NPI = 10 digits, Luhn with 80840 prefix).

```
npi: Optional[str] = Field(default="NPI-1982347102", description="National Provider Identifier or License")
```
**Impact:** Signed legal documents carry an invalid/unowned provider identifier by default.

**Fix:** Make npi required, validate r'^\d{10}$' plus Luhn(80840+npi), and source it from the authenticated user's profile.

*Verifier note:* Evidence verified verbatim at line 90; the same literal appears at frontend/components/viewer/ReportWorkspace.tsx:76 as the useState default (not merely a placeholder — line 851 is a separate placeholder attr), at backend/pipeline/report_pdf.py:344 as the fallback, and at backend/tests/test_cap_reporting.py:241. report_pdf.py:346-360 prints it as `Credentials:` inside the attestation/signature block, and 344-347 fabricates signer name, timestamp and hash the same way on unsigned renders. No format validation exists anywhere (grep for npi shows only assignment/passthrough at report.py:90, 610, 619, 645, and models/report.py's nullable String). Downgraded high -> medium: the string is prefixed 'NPI-' and non-numeric, so it cannot collide with any real provider's 10-digit NPI — the defect is a bogus credential on the record, not impersonation of a real clinician — and the sign modal lets the user overwrite it. The missing validation and the fabricated default are both real.

#### 189. Unknown case_id on PUT/sign/amend/pdf/regenerate creates orphan Report rows (SQLite) or 500s (Postgres); invalid UUID strings pass through to SQL

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/report.py:106`

to_uuid returns the raw string on parse failure, and _ensure_report_record inserts a Report without checking Case exists. Only GET /{case_id} checks the case (line 249). db.py sets no PRAGMA foreign_keys, so SQLite accepts the orphan insert; Postgres raises IntegrityError / DataError ('invalid input syntax for type uuid') -> 500.

```
try:
    return uuid.UUID(str(val))
except Exception:
    return val
```
**Impact:** Garbage rows and signed 'reports' for non-existent cases; unhelpful 500s instead of 404/422.

**Fix:** Raise HTTPException(422) on bad UUID; look up the Case in _ensure_report_record and 404 when missing.

*Verifier note:* Verified. to_uuid (106-112) returns the raw string on parse failure exactly as quoted. `_ensure_report_record` (115-153) never looks up Case; only `_build_report_response_dict` does (247-250), so only GET /{case_id} and /{case_id}/json are protected. PUT/update (345), /resynthesize-narrative (415), /{id}/regenerate-narrative (491), /{id}/pdf (539), /sign (584) and /amend (672) all call it directly. sign_final_report tolerates the missing case (`if case:` at 624) and still seals the orphan with an integrity hash and an AuditEvent. db.py has no `PRAGMA foreign_keys` and no event listener (whole file is 44 lines), so SQLite — the default and the fallback path at db.py:28-32 — accepts the orphan insert despite the FK on models/report.py:17-19. On Postgres the GUID TypeDecorator (models/base.py:19-22) just does `str(value)`, so a non-UUID string reaches a native `uuid` column and raises DataError -> 500 rather than 422. Medium is right; it is a robustness/garbage-data bug, not a clinical one on its own.

#### 188. Report histologic_type is snapshotted at row creation and never refreshed from the confirmed Grading

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Clinical correctness · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/report.py:122`

_ensure_report_record copies grading.histologic_type once (or 'IDC-NST' if no grading yet) and the GET endpoint creates the row as a side effect (line 151 db.commit inside a GET). If the report page is opened before grading confirm, or the pathologist later changes the type, report.histologic_type stays stale; UpdateReportPayload has no histologic_type field so it cannot be corrected. The API response even exposes both (ng_data.histologic_type vs report.histologic_type) which can disagree.

```
htype = grading.histologic_type if grading and grading.histologic_type else "IDC-NST"
```
**Impact:** Signed diagnosis line can name the wrong histologic subtype.

**Fix:** Treat histologic_type as an auto element read from Grading at render/sign time (PRD 06 §2 'auto' class), not a copied column.

*Verifier note:* Verified. report.py:117-153 `_ensure_report_record` returns early if a row exists (118-119) and otherwise snapshots `htype = grading.histologic_type ... else "IDC-NST"` (122) into `histologic_type=htype` (130) plus a baked diagnosis_line (144). The row is created as a side effect of a GET (254, then db.commit at 151). Grep for `histologic_type` over backend/ shows no writer to `Report.histologic_type` anywhere except that one constructor and the generic `setattr` loop in /amend (693-695): grading.py:747 sets `grading_record.histologic_type` on confirm but never touches the report row, and worker/report.py:68-89 only sets it on the create branch — an existing row is left untouched even though grading re-confirm re-queues the report stage (grading.py:764-780). UpdateReportPayload (72-84) indeed has no histologic_type field, so the pathologist cannot correct it pre-sign. The response really does expose two possibly-disagreeing copies: ng_data.histologic_type from grading (267) and report.histologic_type (298), and the signed integrity hash covers the stale copy (602). Severity medium is right: the divergence needs a type change after row creation, and the machine-proposed type is already on grading before confirm, so the common path agrees. Overlaps index 293 (same constructor) but is a distinct defect — 293's fix (nullable manual fields) would not create a refresh path for this `auto`-class element.

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Clinical correctness · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/report.py:205`

The evidence image embedded under the mitotic-count section is always cases/{case_id}/mitosis/crops/m_0001.png (also used for has_mitotic_hpf at line 310). m_0001 is simply the first detector candidate; it may have been toggled to not_mitosis by the pathologist (detections.label) or be an unreviewed low-confidence candidate. ```

On top of that mitosis.py:372 lets a pathologist set label directly and mitosis.py:550-554 (bulk_reject_unreviewed) flips every remaining unreviewed detection to not_mitosis - m_0001 included. pipeline/report_pdf.py:288 captions the embedded image '<b>Highest-Density Mitotic HPF</b>' and :294 subtitles it 'Score {m_score} Mitotic Hotspot (0.2157 mm2)', so a detector candidate the pathologist explicitly rejected is presented in the signed PDF as the evidence for the mitotic score. Detection.label exists (models/detection.py:23) and Detection.ver_conf (:21) is available for the proposed ordering, so the fix is straightforward. Medium is right - it misleads rather than mis-states a value, and when m_0001 was dropped by NMS the download simply raises and the panel falls back to a placeholder thumbnail (report_pdf.py:279 generate_evidence_thumbnail), which is a silent-degradation path rather than a wrong-evidence path.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/report.py:205` (Report PDF embeds hard-coded evidence images regardless of review outcome)
