#### 187. Reports whose status is 'amended' are freely editable via PUT/regenerate with no further amendment trail

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Data integrity · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/report.py:348`

All mutation guards test only `status == "signed"`; after the first /amend the status becomes 'amended' (line 691) and PUT / regenerate-narrative / resynthesize-narrative succeed, flipping status back to 'in_review' (line 396) and dropping the report out of the signed state entirely.

```
if report.status == "signed":
    raise HTTPException(
        status_code=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST,
```
**Impact:** One amendment unlocks unlimited unaudited edits of a signed report.

**Fix:** Guard on status in ('signed','amended') in all three endpoints; route all post-sign changes through /amend.

*Verifier note:* Verified. The three mutation guards are all `== "signed"` only: PUT/update 348, resynthesize-narrative 418, regenerate-narrative 492. amend_signed_report sets report.status='amended' at 690 (and its own precondition at 673 accepts both 'signed' and 'amended', so amendments can chain). After one amendment: PUT succeeds and sets status='in_review' at 395 while leaving signed_by/npi/signed_at/integrity_hash/attestation_statement populated (nothing clears them), so the row keeps a signature block whose integrity_hash no longer matches the content; resynthesize-narrative likewise sets 'in_review' at 478; regenerate-narrative rewrites report.narrative at 526 without even touching status, leaving a report displayed as 'amended' with silently swapped narrative text and a stale hash. can_sign (321) is `status in ('draft','in_review')`, so after that PUT the UI re-offers Sign, which then overwrites signed_by/signed_at with a new hash and no amendment entry. Distinct from index 186 (that one is about the PDF artifact; this one is about the DB row's mutability). Medium stands.

#### 625. Report stage_execution is fetched with an unordered .first(); with multiple attempts sign leaves later attempts unconfirmed and the worker re-runs on a signed report

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/report.py:628`

cases.py approve_stage creates a new StageExecution(stage='report', attempt=existing.attempt+1) each time grading is approved through that path (cases.py:271-280), so several report rows can exist. sign_final_report selects StageExecution where stage=='report' with no ORDER BY attempt and confirms whichever row the DB returns first; _build_report_response_dict does the same at line 256 for stage_status. If the newest attempt is the one still 'queued'/'awaiting_review', it remains so after signing, the UI shows the wrong stage_status, and the worker later picks the queued row and executes run_report against the signed report (which then overwrites narrative/staging/PDF, already noted as a separate issue).

```
stage_exec = db.scalars(
    select(StageExecution).where(StageExecution.case_id == case_uid, StageExecution.stage == "report")
).first()
if stage_exec:
    stage_exec.status = "confirmed"
```
**Impact:** Signed cases can remain in a 'queued' report stage, be re-processed by the worker, and report inconsistent stage_status in the API.

**Fix:** Order by attempt.desc() (a shared helper for both call sites) and, on sign, mark every non-terminal report attempt for the case as confirmed.

*Verifier note:* Confirmed; the quoted select spans report.py:628-630 with .first() and no ORDER BY, and the identical unordered query is at 255-257 feeding stage_status. Multiple 'report' StageExecution rows are reachable: cases.py approve_case_stage builds next_attempt = existing_next.attempt + 1 and unconditionally db.add(new_stage) (cases.py:265-280) with no check for an existing non-terminal report row, and cases.py retry (191-198) does the same for any stage. Note grading.py:762-780 takes the opposite approach - it reuses the existing report row - which is exactly why the two paths interleaving produces duplicates. The contrast with cases.py:236-241, which DOES .order_by(StageExecution.attempt.desc()) for the stage being approved, shows the omission in report.py is an oversight rather than intent. Downstream impact verified: worker/main.py:53-71 picks any queued row ordered by started_at nulls_first, and worker/report.py has no signed-status guard at all (grep for 'signed' in that file hits only field reads at 198-200), so run_report will overwrite report_record.staging (103-109), narrative (143) and the unversioned PDF blob (211-215) on an already-signed report, then set stage_exec.status='awaiting_review' (223). Medium is right - it needs a multi-attempt case plus nondeterministic row order, but the outcome (a signed report silently rewritten by the worker) is serious.

#### 739. On-the-fly tiles use 2048x2048 defaults when slide dimensions were never recorded

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/tiles.py:54`

generate_tile_on_the_fly (and stream_slide_tile at line 116) derive the DeepZoom max level from Slide.width_px/height_px, falling back to 2048 whenever the column is NULL — which is the state of every slide whose ingest stage failed or never ran. max_level then becomes 11 instead of the real value, so level_scale = 2**(z - max_level) and the derived x/y offsets address a completely different part of the slide.

```
slide_w = float(getattr(slide_obj, "width_px", 2048) or 2048)
            slide_h = float(getattr(slide_obj, "height_px", 2048) or 2048)
...
            max_level = int(math.ceil(math.log2(max_dim))) if max_dim > 0 else 11
```
**Impact:** The viewer receives HTTP 200 image tiles showing the wrong region of the slide at the wrong magnification, with no error surfaced; the same defaults also set the norm/orig cap level (cap_10x_level) so the stain layer switches at the wrong zoom.

**Fix:** Return 409/404 when width_px or height_px is NULL instead of substituting a default, and read the dimensions from the opened slide when the DB has none.

*Verifier note:* Confirmed at tiles.py:54-60 and again at 116-119. Because width_px/height_px exist on the model as nullable columns (slide.py:26-27), getattr returns None and `or 2048` substitutes the default, giving max_level=11 and cap_10x_level=9. NULL dims is a real state: ingest.py:269-270 is the only writer (`meta.get('width_px') or 1024`), so any slide whose ingest failed or never ran still has NULL, and the case page renders the viewer regardless. read_region_srgb clamps rather than erroring (pipeline/tiles.py:83-97, 104-112), so a wrong or blank region comes back as HTTP 200 with the 24 h immutable cache header — no error is surfaced, as claimed. Two refinements to the impact wording: the frontend uses the SAME 2048 default (app/cases/[id]/page.tsx:338/348/358 `slide?.width_px || 2048`, OpenSeadragonViewer.tsx:252-253), so client and server agree on the coordinate space rather than disagreeing — the concrete failure is that the entire viewer addresses only the top-left 2048x2048 pixels of a multi-GB WSI and presents that corner as the whole slide; and for the same reason the cap_10x_level part is self-consistent with the client's cap, so that half of the impact claim does not hold. Every such tile also re-downloads the full raw slide (line 163). Medium stands on the silent wrong-imagery grounds.

#### 640. On-the-fly 'norm' tiles are served unnormalized when stain_params.json is missing, but labelled and cached as the normalized layer

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/tiles.py:100`

generate_tile_on_the_fly wraps the stain-params download and transform in a bare except that only prints a note. Before preprocess has run (stain_params.json absent), or if the JSON keys change, the raw tile is returned. stream_slide_tile then sends it with X-Tile-Layer: norm and the 24 h immutable cache header. Because the norm pyramid is only pre-generated to level 11 (preprocess.py:46), this is the path every zoomed-in 'norm' request takes.

```
app/routers/tiles.py:100  except Exception as norm_err:
app/routers/tiles.py:101      print(f"[Tile Router Warning] On-the-fly norm transform note: {norm_err}")
app/routers/tiles.py:130  "X-Tile-Layer": target_layer,
```
**Impact:** The 'Normalized' toggle in the viewer shows original colours at diagnostic zoom while claiming to be normalized; the pathologist assesses pleomorphism/mitoses on a different colour space than the one the model saw, and the browser caches the wrong tiles for a day.

**Fix:** If stain params cannot be loaded, fall through to the 'orig' GCS lookup (step 3) and set X-Tile-Layer: orig, or return 404 for norm; never silently relabel.

*Verifier note:* Verified end to end. tiles.py:91-101: when layer=='norm' the stain-params download + Macenko transform sit in a bare `except Exception as norm_err: print(...)`, so on any failure tile_arr stays the RAW array and is returned at line 103-106. stream_slide_tile then returns it at line 174 with headers built at 128-132 ('Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400, immutable' and 'X-Tile-Layer': target_layer == 'norm'). The path is genuinely reachable at diagnostic zoom: preprocess.py:46 `max_norm_pregen_level = min(12, dz.level_count)` pre-generates norm levels 0..11 only, while tiles.py:120 sets cap_10x_level = slide_max_level - 2 (15 for a ~100k-px slide), so norm requests at z=12..15 miss step 1 and fall into on-the-fly generation. The frontend applies the identical cap (OpenSeadragonViewer.tsx:263) so it really does ask for /norm/ at those levels. stain_params.json is only written by preprocess (preprocess.py:170-177), so any case where preprocess has not run yields silently unnormalized tiles labelled norm. Also note step 3 (line 181-196) is a norm->orig GCS fallback that is never reached in this case because step 2 already returned 200. Medium is right: wrong-colour tiles are mislabelled and cached for a day, but no data loss or auth bypass.

#### 340. PHI tiles and patches are marked Cache-Control: public, immutable

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Security · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/tiles.py:129`

The dict is even named no_cache_headers but sets public caching for a day; triage.py:283/291/443 and mitosis.py:347 do the same for hotspot/HPF images. Shared proxies/CDNs may cache patient imagery, and a re-generated tile (e.g. after re-ingest) stays stale.

```
no_cache_headers = {"Cache-Control": "public, max-age=86400, immutable", ...}
```
**Impact:** PHI cached by intermediaries; stale imagery after regeneration.

**Fix:** Use private, max-age with Vary on auth (or no-store for PHI) and rename the variable.

*Verifier note:* Verified verbatim at tiles.py:128-132 — the dict is named no_cache_headers and sets 'Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400, immutable', and it is attached to every success path (lines 145, 174, 192). This is also a direct contradiction of the PRD, not just a judgement call: prd/01-stage-v4.0-walking-skeleton.md:46 specifies tile serving with 'Cache-Control: private, max-age=86400'. 'immutable' additionally suppresses revalidation, so a re-ingested slide keeps serving stale tiles at the same URL for a day. Same headers used for the hotspot/HPF images in triage.py and mitosis.py. Medium is appropriate — public caching is only exploitable where a shared cache sits in front of the API, and the response is served over the API origin, so this is an exposure-widening defect rather than a direct leak.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/mitosis.py:347` (HPF thumbnails are served with Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400 (PHI images cacheable by shared proxies) while the cached-blob branch says no-cache)

#### 641. z path parameter is unbounded; a single out-of-range z on the unauthenticated direct route costs 3 GCS round trips plus a full raw-WSI download

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Security · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/tiles.py:220`

z is an int with no range check. Nothing in stream_slide_tile rejects z < 0 or z > max_level before step 1 (three blob downloads) and step 2 (download the whole original slide). Only inside generate_tile_on_the_fly does `2 ** (z - max_level)` overflow for huge z, and that exception is swallowed into a 404 after the download already happened. get_tile_direct has no auth dependency at all (already recorded), so this is reachable anonymously.

```
app/routers/tiles.py:205  z: int,
app/routers/tiles.py:63  level_scale = 2 ** (z - max_level)
app/routers/tiles.py:163  download_blob_to_filename(raw_bucket_name, blob_name, local_slide_path)
```
**Impact:** Trivial resource-exhaustion: `GET /api/v1/cases/tiles/<slide_id>/orig/999999/0_0.png` in a loop forces the API to download the multi-GB WSI repeatedly, hold the global lock, and fill /tmp.

**Fix:** Compute max_level once from slide dimensions and `raise HTTPException(404)` when not 0 <= z <= max_level (and when c/r exceed the level's tile grid) before any storage access; validate layer against {orig, norm} the same way.

*Verifier note:* Claim holds; two corrections. (1) Line 205 is `z: int` in the AUTHENTICATED get_tile (202-213). The unauthenticated route's z is line 220 (get_tile_direct, 217-223, which indeed has only `db: Session = Depends(get_db)` and no get_current_user). The actual missing bound is in stream_slide_tile (112-132), which validates neither z, nor layer, nor c/r before step 1 (three blob.download_as_bytes attempts, 138-147) and step 2 (`download_blob_to_filename` of the full raw WSI, line 163). (2) The finder's 'overflow ... swallowed into a 404' is wrong in a way that makes it worse, not better: I checked in CPython that `256/(2**999982)` returns 0.0, not an exception, so for a huge z level_scale is a giant int, w_px_0/h_px_0 become 0.0, and read_region_srgb (pipeline/tiles.py:83) hits `(x_px_0 + w_px_0) <= 0` and returns a blank tile — so the request returns HTTP 200 with a blank PNG and the 24 h immutable cache header AFTER the multi-GB download. (Negative z does raise ZeroDivisionError and 404s, still after the download.) Note the same cost is incurred for any in-range z whose pyramid tile is missing, so the unbounded z is the trigger, not the root cause; the root cause is unauthenticated on-the-fly full-slide download. Medium is fair.

#### 343. Triage edits are unvalidated dicts persisted straight into review_edits and Hotspot.polygon_um

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/triage.py:48`

TriageEditsPayload.edits is list[dict[str, Any]]; apply_edit_ops copies op['polygon_um'] verbatim (line 70, 77) and confirm_triage writes it to the DB (522). An add op with polygon_um='abc' or [[1]] passes, and run_mitosis then calls enumerate_hotspot_tiles on it (pipeline/detect.py:188-200), which does p[0]/min() over malformed data and raises, failing the stage. New ids are f'user_{len+1:02d}' (line 74), which collides after a delete op.

```
edits: list[dict[str, Any]] # RFC-6902 style edit operations ... "polygon_um": op.get("polygon_um", []),
```
**Impact:** A bad client payload corrupts persisted geometry and crashes the downstream stage; id reuse silently overwrites a hotspot.

**Fix:** Define a Pydantic EditOp with Literal op, polygon as list of [float,float] with >=3 points, and generate ids with uuid/next-free-index.

*Verifier note:* Evidence holds exactly. triage.py:48 `edits: list[dict[str, Any]]` is the only typing on the payload; apply_edit_ops (57-93) copies op['polygon_um'] verbatim at :70 (modify) and :77 (add, defaulting to []), and confirm_triage :522 writes `hs['polygon_um']` into Hotspot.polygon_um, which is a plain `Column(JSON, nullable=False)` (backend/app/models/hotspot.py:19) — no shape check anywhere on the path. Downstream crash is real: worker/mitosis.py:181-182 does `poly_um = hs['polygon_um']` then enumerate_hotspot_tiles(poly_um); backend/pipeline/detect.py:189-190 computes `xs=[p[0] for p in poly]` / `ys=[p[1] for p in poly]` and :201 `int(curr_x/mpp)`. polygon_um='abc' survives the `if not hotspot_polygon_um` guard (:186) and dies at the division with TypeError; [[1]] dies at p[1] with IndexError; worker/main.py:86-98 catches it and flips the stage to status='failed'. Empty [] is the one malformed case that IS handled (the :186 guard). Id-generation collision at :74 also real (see 575). Medium is right: unvalidated trust boundary, persisted bad geometry, downstream stage failure — but not privilege/data loss.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/triage.py:330` (Malformed review_edits polygon → 500 in thumbnail endpoint; edits payload is never validated)

#### 75. 'modify' op flips source to pathologist_modified even when polygon unchanged; frontend sends modify for every hotspot

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Data integrity · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/triage.py:71`

`apply_edit_ops` marks any hotspot with a `modify` op as `pathologist_modified` without comparing the polygon to the machine polygon. `frontend/components/viewer/TriageViewer.tsx:179-185` regenerates the whole edit list on every save and emits `{op:'modify', polygon_um}` for every non-excluded model hotspot.     if "polygon_um" in op:
```
        hotspots_dict[hid]["polygon_um"] = op["polygon_um"]
        hotspots_dict[hid]["source"] = "pathologist_modified"
```
**Impact:** Provenance in the `hotspots` table (PRD 03 §4: model|pathologist_added|pathologist_modified) is wrong for every case; v4.6 override analytics and the review-edit flywheel (PRD §2.3) are built on this column.

Contradicts prd/03-stage-v4.2-hotspot-triage.md:84 (model|pathologist_added|pathologist_modified) and prd/03:66 ('edit ops appended' as the pathologist acts, not regenerated wholesale). Severity lowered from high to medium: geometry, area, probabilities and the effective hotspot set are all still correct, so no diagnostic output changes; the damage is confined to the provenance column and to the review-edit flywheel, which prd/03:34 explicitly defers ('deferred per decision #6'). #### 741. Triage 'add' edit op can overwrite an existing machine hotspot

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Data integrity · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/triage.py:74`

apply_edit_ops handles 'add' without checking whether the id already exists, so an op carrying an existing hotspot id replaces that entry wholesale with source='pathologist_added' and prob_mean/prob_max of 1.0. Auto-generated ids are derived from the current dict length, so after a 'delete' the next auto id can collide with an id already in use.

```
elif action == "add":
            new_id = hid or f"user_{len(hotspots_dict)+1:02d}"
            hotspots_dict[new_id] = {
                "id": new_id,
```
**Impact:** An edit list of [{'op':'delete','id':'user_01'}, {'op':'add', ...}] silently reuses user_01, and an 'add' quoting a machine id destroys that hotspot's model polygon and probabilities in both the GET response and the rows persisted by confirm_triage. The machine-vs-pathologist provenance the review gate exists to record is lost.

**Fix:** Reject 'add' for an id already present (400) and generate new ids from a monotonic counter or uuid rather than the collection length.

*Verifier note:* Code claim verified verbatim at triage.py:73-84: the 'add' branch does hotspots_dict[new_id] = {...} with no membership check, unlike 'modify' (68), 'exclude' (86) and 'delete' (90) which all gate on `hid in hotspots_dict`. An add op carrying an existing id replaces that entry wholesale with source='pathologist_added', polygon_um=op.get('polygon_um', []) and prob_mean/prob_max defaulting to 1.0. This propagates to both consumers, which replay the full stored edit list: get_triage_data (line 130) and confirm_triage (line 511), whose output is written to Hotspot rows at 517-530 right after db.query(Hotspot)...delete() at 514, so the clobbered version is what is persisted. The /edits endpoint (447) accepts `edits: list[dict[str, Any]]` unvalidated with no auth dependency (X-User-Role is a cosmetic header), so a crafted add quoting a machine id is accepted. Two corrections to the finder's framing, neither of which refutes the defect: (1) the literal repro [delete, add-without-id] is not producible by the only caller — frontend/components/viewer/TriageViewer.tsx:183 always sends `id` on add ops, and handleDeleteHotspot (line 143) only drops the row from local state and never emits an op:'delete' — so the len()+1 auto-id branch is only reachable via a hand-written API call; (2) a duplicate-id add IS reachable from the shipped UI by a different route: handleAddRoiFromClick (line 157) mints `user_${count of ids starting with 'user_' + 1}`, so add user_01, add user_02, delete user_01 locally, add again -> id user_02 a second time; two add ops with id user_02 are saved and the server dict silently keeps only the last, so a pathologist-drawn ROI vanishes from effective_hotspots and from the persisted Hotspot rows with no error. Medium is fair: silent loss of a reviewer ROI or of machine provenance in the very gate meant to record it, but the auto-id collision itself is not on a UI path.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/triage.py:73` ('add' op with an id that already exists silently overwrites the machine hotspot)

#### 95. 'add' op fabricates prob_mean/prob_max = 1.0 and accepts empty polygons; unknown-id ops silently ignored

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Data integrity · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/triage.py:79`

A pathologist-added ROI is persisted with `prob_mean: 1.0, prob_max: 1.0` unless the client supplies values, and `polygon_um` defaults to `[]` which then becomes a NOT NULL JSON `[]` row that `enumerate_hotspot_tiles` skips. `modify`/`exclude`/`delete` for an id not in the machine set are dropped without error, and `new_id = f"user_{len(hotspots_dict)+1:02d}"` collides after deletes.

```

```
**Impact:** Model probability columns contain human-invented 1.0s that downstream code (grading patch selection) cannot distinguish from model output.

*Verifier note:* Verified at apply_edit_ops lines 73-84. 'add' defaults prob_mean/prob_max to 1.0 (lines 79-80), area_mm2 to 1.0, and polygon_um to [] (line 77); confirm_triage persists these unchanged (517-530), and Hotspot.polygon_um is nullable=False so [] is stored as a valid empty polygon which pipeline/detect.py:185-186 then skips, silently contributing zero tiles. The impact claim is directly corroborated downstream: worker/grading.py:155 selects hotspots ordered by Hotspot.prob_mean.desc(), so a human-added ROI with the fabricated 1.0 sorts ahead of every real model hotspot for grading patch selection, and grading.py:175 falls back to 0.85 only when prob_* is None. modify/exclude/delete with an unknown id fall through every branch (68, 86, 90) with no error and no report to the caller. The id collision is real too: with 3 machine hotspots, add -> 'user_04'; then delete a machine hotspot (len back to 3); then add -> 'user_04' again, overwriting the first pathologist-added ROI. An 'add' whose op carries an existing id likewise overwrites that hotspot outright.

*Also reported at:* `frontend/components/viewer/TriageViewer.tsx:164` (Pathologist-added ROI is given fabricated model probabilities (88% / 95%) that are displayed as tumor confidence); `backend/worker/grading.py:155` (Grading worker ranks hotspots by prob_mean, so pathologist-added hotspots (fabricated prob_mean=1.0 at confirm) are always force-selected as the 'worst area')

#### 568. GET/confirm fall back to the case-level output.json whenever output_ref is empty, so a freshly re-queued attempt displays and confirms the previous attempt's hotspots

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Data integrity · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/triage.py:123`

get_triage_data selects the latest attempt but, when that attempt has no output_ref yet (status queued/running/failed after retryStage), it reads cases/{case_id}/triage/output.json — which is the previous attempt's artifact because the worker keys all artifacts by case_id. The response therefore reports the new attempt's stage_execution_id/status alongside the old attempt's machine_hotspots, and confirm_triage (lines 504-506) does the same, so a confirm on a queued attempt persists stale hotspots under the new stage_execution_id.

```
else:
            out_bytes = download_blob_as_bytes(settings.GCS_ARTIFACTS_BUCKET, f"cases/{case_id}/triage/output.json")
            machine_output = json.loads(out_bytes.decode("utf-8"))
```
**Impact:** Reviewer sees and can confirm results that do not belong to the attempt they are reviewing; hotspots rows carry a stage_execution_id whose output_ref is NULL.

**Fix:** Only load machine output from stage_exec.output_ref; when it is NULL return machine_hotspots=[] with the real status (or 409 for confirm).

*Verifier note:* Confirmed; the quoted else-branch is :122-124 (download at :123) in get_triage_data and :504-506 in confirm_triage. Both select the latest attempt (:105, :488) but fall back to the case-keyed blob whenever output_ref is empty. Worker artifact keying verified: worker/triage.py:515-520 writes `cases/{case_id}/triage/output.json` with no attempt in the path, so the blob is the previous attempt's content until the new attempt finishes. Result is exactly as claimed: the response pairs the new attempt's stage_execution_id/status (:146-147) with the old attempt's machine_hotspots (:152), and confirm_triage persists those into hotspots rows carrying `stage_execution_id=str(stage_exec.id)` (:521) for a row whose output_ref is NULL. One nuance the finder missed, which makes the proposed fix necessary but not sufficient: because artifacts are case-keyed, attempt N's output_ref points at the same path attempt N+1 will overwrite, so 'read only from output_ref' fixes the queued/failed case but not the already-overwritten case — a per-attempt artifact path is the real fix. Medium holds. Distinct from 535 (stale read vs. history mutation), not a duplicate.

#### 89. Thumbnail endpoint: unvalidated mag/stain become GCS object keys; full-WSI download per unauthenticated request

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Security · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/triage.py:280`

`mag` and `stain` are free-form query strings interpolated into `patch_blob` and later uploaded (434-439) — any value creates a new object in the artifacts bucket; `stain` is also passed as the pyramid `layer` prefix. When the cached patch is missing the endpoint downloads the entire raw WSI (multi-GB) into a temp dir on every request (384) with no size cap or rate limit, then deletes it. Non-matching `mag` values fall through to `field_um = 512` while the synthetic generator's `else` treats them as 40x.

```

...
download_blob_to_filename(raw_bucket_name, blob_name, local_slide_path)
```
**Impact:** Unbounded bucket writes and trivial DoS (each request pulls a full slide); inconsistent behaviour for bad params.

**Fix:** `mag: Literal['10x','20x','40x']`, `stain: Literal['norm','orig']`; return 404 instead of downloading the WSI on the API path (pre-generate patches in the worker, which already does).

*Verifier note:* Every sub-claim checks out. mag/stain are plain str query params (270-271) interpolated into the cache key at 280 and written back with upload_blob_from_bytes at 433-439, so any value mints a new object in the artifacts bucket. stain is also forwarded as `layer=stain` at 367 into pipeline/tiles.py:205 f"{slide_id}/{layer}/{z}/{c}_{r}{ext}"; an unknown layer finds no tiles, hits `if not found_any: return None` (tiles.py:221), and drops the request into the OpenSlide branch at 375-384, which downloads the full raw WSI to a temp dir per request with no size cap, rate limit or concurrency guard - and serializes on OPENSLIDE_GLOBAL_LOCK (389), so a handful of such requests also stall every other thumbnail. Because the cache key varies with the attacker-chosen params, the download is not amortized. The mag inconsistency is real too: 344-348 leaves field_um=512 for any unrecognised mag while generate_synthetic_microscopic_patch's else branch (line 229) renders it as 40x. Medium is the right level - it is resource exhaustion and bucket litter, not data disclosure (the cross-patient disclosure is index 77).

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/triage.py:270` (Unauthenticated, unvalidated mag/stain query params drive unbounded GCS writes (cache poisoning / storage DoS))

#### 285. Attempt-selection drift: confirm re-queues attempt 1 while retry/approve create attempt N+1, and mitosis/grading confirm pick an arbitrary attempt

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/triage.py:548`

Three different conventions coexist: confirm_triage looks up next stage with `attempt == 1` (triage.py:544-558), cases.approve creates `existing_next.attempt + 1` (cases.py:272), and mitosis/grading confirm select `.first()` with no ORDER BY (mitosis.py:626-628 and 654-659; grading.py:694-696 and 762-767), so which attempt gets flipped to confirmed/queued depends on DB row order.

```
select(StageExecution).where(
    StageExecution.case_id == case_uid,
    StageExecution.stage == next_stage_name,
    StageExecution.attempt == 1
)
```
**Impact:** Scenario: mitosis attempt 1 failed, user retries -> attempt 2 runs and reaches awaiting_review. Pathologist re-confirms triage (e.g., after adjusting a polygon): attempt 1 (failed) is reset to queued and re-executes, deleting attempt 2's reviewed detections. Then confirm_mitosis may mark attempt 1 'confirmed' while attempt 2 remains awaiting_review.

**Fix:** Always resolve 'the current execution' as ORDER BY attempt DESC LIMIT 1 through one shared helper, and only ever create a new attempt rather than resetting old rows.

*Verifier note:* Every quoted convention exists, and they really do disagree. (a) triage.py:544-558 pins `StageExecution.attempt == 1` for the next stage (twice: 548 and 556 for the uuid/str fallback) and creates attempt=1 at 564. (b) cases.py:272 `next_attempt = (existing_next.attempt + 1) if existing_next else 1` in approve, and cases.py:186-194 does the same in the retry endpoint (`/{case_id}/stages/{stage_name}/retry`, cases.py:167), so attempt 2+ rows genuinely get created. (c) routers/mitosis.py:626-628 selects the mitosis stage exec with no ORDER BY and takes .first(), and 654-659 does the same for 'grading'; routers/grading.py:694-696 (grading) and 762-767 (report) likewise have no ORDER BY. By contrast triage.py:105/455/488 and cases.py:186/239/250/269 all use `.order_by(StageExecution.attempt.desc())`. So which attempt a confirm mutates is DB-row-order dependent. The described scenario is reachable: retry creates mitosis attempt 2, then a triage re-confirm resets the *failed* attempt 1 to queued and the worker re-runs it, wiping attempt 2's reviewed detections (case-scoped delete, worker/mitosis.py:412). Distinct from index 279: 279 is the missing status guard on the reset, this is the attempt-selection convention drift — same code region, different root cause. Medium is right: it is a latent inconsistency that needs a retry/approve to have happened first, and the destructive half is already counted under 279.

#### 215. Audit pagination orders only by created_at with no tiebreak, so pages can repeat/skip events created in the same transaction

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/audit.py:28`

Events written in one request share created_at to microsecond granularity (e.g. triage.py:529-542 writes model_invocation and stage_output back-to-back; cases.py:149 writes slide_uploaded in the same commit as the stage row). ORDER BY created_at DESC with OFFSET/LIMIT is not a stable sort in Postgres for equal keys, so a page boundary that falls between tied rows can return the same event on two pages and drop another. There is also no filtering by event_type/stage, which the PRD 00 section 7 DoD ('new audit events ... visible via GET /cases/{id}/audit') implies reviewers will need.

```
stmt = select(AuditEvent).where(AuditEvent.case_id == str(case_id)).order_by(AuditEvent.created_at.desc())
total = db.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(stmt.subquery())) or 0
events = db.scalars(stmt.offset(offset).limit(page_size)).all()
```
**Impact:** Audit review UI can show duplicated or missing events across pages — unacceptable for an append-only ledger.

**Fix:** order_by(AuditEvent.created_at.desc(), AuditEvent.id.desc()) (or cursor on id) and add optional event_type/stage query filters.

*Verifier note:* Code is as quoted: audit.py:28 orders by created_at DESC only, and audit.py:31 pages with .offset(offset).limit(page_size). created_at is not unique (models/audit.py:20-24), so ORDER BY + OFFSET is genuinely an unstable sort and a page boundary landing inside a tie group can repeat/drop a row. Downgraded from medium because the stated premise is overstated: created_at uses `default=lambda: datetime.now(timezone.utc)` evaluated per-row at flush, so the two writes at worker/triage.py:529 and :542 (and cases.py:149) get distinct microsecond values in practice on Linux/macOS -- no writer sets created_at explicitly (grep for created_at across routers/workers hits only audit.py:28). Ties are therefore possible (coarse clock, bulk inserts) but not the routine case, and audit volumes per case are small enough that pages past the first are rare. The second half of the finding (no event_type/stage filters) is a missing feature, not a defect, and should not carry severity. Fix as proposed -- adding `AuditEvent.id.desc()` as a tiebreak is a one-token change on a bigserial PK.

#### 708. Audit events are keyed by an unnormalized client-supplied case_id string while the audit endpoint matches exactly

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Data integrity · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/audit.py:28`

AuditEvent.case_id is a plain String with no FK and no normalization (backend/app/models/audit.py:15). The stage routers write it straight from the request body: `case_id=payload.case_id` (backend/app/routers/triage.py:467 and 577, mitosis.py:379, grading.py:420, report.py:638). The audit query filters on str(case_id) of the parsed uuid.UUID path parameter, i.e. canonical lowercase hyphenated form.

```
stmt = select(AuditEvent).where(AuditEvent.case_id == str(case_id)).order_by(AuditEvent.created_at.desc())
```
**Impact:** Any client that posts the case id in a non-canonical form (uppercase hex, braced, or 32-char unhyphenated -- all accepted by to_uuid() and by the JSON body) writes audit rows that never appear in GET /cases/{id}/audit. Review edits, confirmations and sign-off events silently vanish from the append-only trail that PRD 00-overview s5.6 and s7.3 require to be visible.

**Fix:** Normalize on write (store str(to_uuid(payload.case_id))) or type the column as GUID with an FK to cases.id.

*Verifier note:* Verified end to end. models/audit.py:15 declares `case_id: Mapped[str|None] = mapped_column(String, nullable=True)` -- plain varchar, no FK -- and the schema is built from the ORM (Base.metadata.create_all, backend/app/main.py:23), so the deployed column really is text, deviating from PRD 00-overview:122 which specifies `case_id uuid`. Writers fed by a request body store the raw client string: triage.py:467 and :577 use `case_id=payload.case_id` with `case_id: str` fields (triage.py:47, :52), mitosis.py:379 uses `case_id=case_id` from `case_id = payload.case_id` (mitosis.py:357), and grading.py:420/:498 and report.py:638 wrap an already-str field in str() (no-op). The reader at audit.py:28 compares that varchar to `str(case_id)` of the parsed uuid.UUID path param, i.e. canonical lowercase-hyphenated. The escape path is real on Postgres: the stage-execution lookups those endpoints perform first bind through models/base.py GUID into a `uuid` column, and PG's uuid input is case-insensitive and accepts the unhyphenated form, so a non-canonical id passes the lookup and is then persisted verbatim into the varchar audit column, where the exact string compare will never find it. Downgraded from medium to low because every writer not driven by a request body already writes canonical form (cases.py:47 `str(case_obj.id)`, cases.py:149 `str(case_id)` from the uuid path param, and all worker sites e.g. worker/triage.py:529/:542 `str(case_id)` off the GUID-typed column), and the shipped frontend passes ids it received from the API, so triggering needs a client that introduces a non-canonical id. Note the SQLite test path behaves differently -- CHAR(36) compares exactly, so the stage lookup 404s and no orphan row is written; the divergence is Postgres-only.

#### 647. create_case commits the case and its audit row in two separate transactions

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Data integrity · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/cases.py:43`

The Case is committed at line 43, then the AuditEvent is added and committed again at line 53. If the second commit fails (DB hiccup, audit table constraint), the response is a 500 but the case already exists with no case_created event, violating the PRD minimum audit set. Every other endpoint in the file correctly adds the audit row before a single commit.

```
app/routers/cases.py:43  db.commit()
app/routers/cases.py:52  db.add(audit)
app/routers/cases.py:53  db.commit()
```
**Impact:** Cases can exist without their creation audit event; the client sees an error and may retry, producing duplicate cases.

**Fix:** Use `db.flush()` after `db.add(case_obj)` to obtain the id, add the audit row, then commit once.

*Verifier note:* Verified at cases.py:41-53: db.add(case_obj); db.commit() (43); db.refresh; then AuditEvent add (52) and a second db.commit() (53). The Case is durable before the audit row is attempted, so a failure of the second commit leaves a case with no case_created event and a 500 to the client. Every other write path in the file does it correctly with db.flush() + one commit (upload_slide_file 131-158, retry 198-208, approve 281-293, finalize 341-362), so the proposed fix is exactly the existing house pattern. Low is right: single-writer dev system, failure window is narrow, no clinical data lost.

#### 711. Case deleted mid-run: the worker's failure handler silently drops the error and orphans GCS artifacts

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Concurrency · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/cases.py:91`

Case.stage_executions is cascade='all, delete-orphan' (backend/app/models/case.py:22), so DELETE /cases/{id} removes the row a worker is currently executing. When the handler finishes, the commit at line 84 issues an UPDATE that matches zero rows and SQLAlchemy raises StaleDataError; the except block rolls back and then db.get(StageExecution, stage_exec.id) returns None, so the `if stage_exec_curr:` guard skips everything and the loop moves on. The handler has by then already uploaded output.json, pyramids, crops and PDFs to GCS.

```
stage_exec_curr = db.get(StageExecution, stage_exec.id)
                if stage_exec_curr:
                    stage_exec_curr.status = "failed"
                    stage_exec_curr.error = err_msg
```
**Impact:** PHI-bearing artifacts (crops, patches, heatmaps, the raw pyramid, the CAP PDF) are written to GCS for a case that has been deleted and are never cleaned up -- no code path deletes GCS objects on case delete. The operator sees no error at all, only a print line. On Postgres the handler's own commit can instead fail with an FK violation while inserting detections/hpf_sites for the vanished case.

**Fix:** Re-check the stage row still exists before doing any external write (or take a row lock for the duration), and delete the case's GCS prefixes when the case is deleted.

*Verifier note:* Half confirmed, half refuted; location corrected. Confirmed: cases.py:80-93 DELETE /cases/{id} does `db.delete(case_obj); db.commit()` with Case.stage_executions cascade='all, delete-orphan' (models/case.py:22), a worker's handler runs for minutes against a separate session, and nothing anywhere deletes GCS objects on case delete — app/core/gcs.py:87 defines delete_blob() but cases.py never calls it, so pyramids/crops/output.json/PDFs written by the in-flight handler are orphaned PHI. That is the real defect, and it lives at the delete endpoint, not at worker/main.py:92. Refuted: the characterisation of main.py:91-97 as 'silently drops the error'. `db.get(StageExecution, id)` returning None and the `if stage_exec_curr:` guard skipping is the correct behaviour — there is no row left to mark failed, and the exception is printed at main.py:90. Adding a 'recheck before every external write' guard, as proposed, only narrows an unclosable race. Also note the orphaned-artifact exposure is not specific to the mid-run race: a case deleted at any time after ingest leaves its GCS prefixes behind. Downgraded medium->low: it needs an operator to delete a case (and the FK sub-claim only bites on Postgres, where detections/hotspots/hpf_sites carry ForeignKey('cases.id') with no cascade and no relationship on Case, so such a delete would more likely fail outright than race).

#### 218. Upload endpoint derives the blob extension from an unvalidated filename and accepts any size/type

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Security · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/cases.py:108`

ext is whatever follows the last '.' in the client filename, unbounded and unvalidated; a filename like 'a.b/../c' yields ext 'b/../c' and blob_name 'cases/{case_id}/{uuid}.b/../c', which GCS stores as a literal key with slashes, so the client controls part of the object path. The PRD 01 section 2.2 whitelist (.svs,.ndpi,.mrxs,.tif,.tiff,.dcm) and 20 GB limit are not applied here or in get_slide_upload_url (line 314, same code).

```
ext = file.filename.rsplit(".", 1)[-1].lower() if file.filename and "." in file.filename else "svs"

blob_name = f"cases/{case_id}/{file_uuid}.{ext}"
```
**Impact:** Arbitrary object key suffixes under the case prefix and non-WSI uploads that fail only later in the worker.

**Fix:** Validate the extension against the whitelist with a regex on the extension token and enforce a size limit; factor the shared logic out of the two copy-pasted endpoints.

*Verifier note:* Evidence exists verbatim at cases.py:108 and the copy at :314. ext is the raw tail after the last dot of a client-supplied multipart filename (Starlette does not sanitise UploadFile.filename), lowercased only, so 'a.b/../c' does yield blob_name 'cases/{case_id}/{uuid}.b/../c'. GCS object names are opaque flat strings, so this is stored literally. No extension whitelist and no size check exist in either endpoint, while prd/01-stage-v4.0-walking-skeleton.md:33 explicitly requires 'extension in {.svs,.ndpi,.mrxs,.tif,.tiff,.dcm}, size <= 20 GB' before issuing the URL. Frontend only sets an accept= hint (frontend/app/cases/page.tsx:118), which is not enforcement. Low is right: the 'cases/{case_id}/' prefix is still a literal prefix of the key so nothing escapes the case namespace, and the one place blob_name is reused for a local path (cases.py:390, os.path.splitext -> tempfile suffix) takes only the basename extension, which is empty for such names and falls back to '.svs'. Real defect is the missing PRD validation, not traversal.

#### 650. Three different input_ref shapes are written for the same stages; blob_name and gcs_uri_original keys are dead

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Improvement · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/cases.py:143`

upload_slide_file writes {gcs_uri_original, slide_id, blob_name}; finalize_slide_upload writes {gcs_uri_original, slide_id}; retry/approve write {gcs_uri_original, slide_id}; worker chaining writes {slide_id, ingest_output_ref} / {slide_id, preprocess_output_ref}. Every handler only reads input_ref['slide_id'] (ingest also reads gcs_uri_original; grep of worker/*.py shows no other keys consumed), so blob_name and the *_output_ref keys are never used, and the PRD idempotency rule ('handlers derive all inputs from input_ref + DB') is only nominally followed.

```
app/routers/cases.py:143  "blob_name": blob_name
app/routers/cases.py:196  input_ref={"gcs_uri_original": slide_obj.gcs_uri_original, "slide_id": str(slide_obj.id)}
worker/preprocess.py:245  input_ref={"slide_id": str(slide_id), "preprocess_output_ref": output_ref}
```
**Impact:** Copy-paste drift makes it impossible to tell from a stage row which upstream output it consumed; retries and approvals silently point at 'latest' state rather than a pinned upstream execution.

**Fix:** Define one helper `make_stage_input(slide, upstream_exec=None)` used by routers and workers, and have handlers read the upstream output_ref from it so re-runs are reproducible.

*Verifier note:* Factually verified. Producers: cases.py:140-144 {gcs_uri_original, slide_id, blob_name}, cases.py:196 and 349 {gcs_uri_original, slide_id}, cases.py:279 {slide_id, gcs_uri_original}, worker/ingest.py:326 {slide_id, ingest_output_ref}, worker/preprocess.py:245 {slide_id, preprocess_output_ref}, plus a fourth shape from app/routers/triage.py:566/571 (input_ref=input_data). Consumers: only ingest.py:227-228 (gcs_uri_original + slide_id), qc.py:34, triage.py:205, preprocess.py:108 - all slide_id only; worker/mitosis.py:52-80 and worker/grading.py:131-144 ignore input_ref entirely and re-query Slide by case_id. Grep confirms no read of blob_name, ingest_output_ref or preprocess_output_ref anywhere. So the dead keys and the drift are real; the PRD idempotency rule (00-overview.md:5.4, 'handlers derive all inputs from input_ref + DB') is only nominally met. Low/improvement is the right weight - nothing breaks today.

#### 214. Naive datetimes from SQLite fallback are serialized without timezone for slides, stages and audit events

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/cases.py:453`

CaseResponse/CaseDetailResponse.created_at have a field_serializer that stamps UTC on naive datetimes (schemas/case.py:14-18), but label_stripped_at (line 453), started_at/completed_at (lines 466-467) call .isoformat() directly and AuditEventResponse.created_at (schemas/audit.py:11) has no serializer. SQLite (the silent fallback in core/db.py:27-32 and the test DB) returns naive datetimes, so these come out as '2026-09-03T10:00:00' with no offset while created_at comes out as '...+00:00'.

```
"label_stripped_at": s.label_stripped_at.isoformat() if s.label_stripped_at else None
...
"started_at": st.started_at.isoformat() if st.started_at else None,
"completed_at": st.completed_at.isoformat() if st.completed_at else None
```
**Impact:** JavaScript's Date parser treats offset-less ISO strings as local time, so stage timings and audit timestamps display shifted by the user's UTC offset — a wrong time on a clinical audit record.

**Fix:** Apply one shared UTC-normalizing serializer (or make slides/stages typed Pydantic models sharing it) and use it for AuditEventResponse.created_at as well.

*Verifier note:* Factually confirmed, but medium overstates it. The asymmetry is real: schemas/case.py:14-18 and :45-49 give CaseResponse/CaseDetailResponse.created_at a field_serializer that stamps timezone.utc on naive values, while cases.py:453 (label_stripped_at) and cases.py:466-467 (started_at/completed_at) call .isoformat() on raw ORM datetimes inside plain dicts typed `list[dict]` (schemas/case.py:40-41), which bypasses Pydantic entirely; schemas/audit.py:11 declares created_at: datetime with no serializer and is used by routers/audit.py:34. core/db.py:12-32 does fall back to SQLite silently when Postgres is unreachable, and SQLAlchemy's SQLite dialect returns naive datetimes even for DateTime(timezone=True), so on that path created_at serializes with '+00:00' while the sibling timestamps do not — JS Date() then reads the offset-less ones as local time. Downgraded to low because the blast radius is narrower than claimed: on the intended Postgres deployment DateTime(timezone=True) returns aware datetimes and .isoformat() emits the offset, so the defect is confined to the SQLite dev/test fallback, and the consequence is a display shift with no persisted-data corruption. Worth fixing as an inconsistency, not a clinical-record defect.

```
            "tubule_percent": grading_record.tubule_percent,

```

After sign-off GET returns machine == current, so the delta is not derivable from the API response. Fix as proposed (read machine['aggregate']) is correct and one line.

#### 159. Patch review 'update' with status=approved wipes previously modified values, unlike approve_all which preserves them

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/grading.py:405`

For action 'update' the override dict is replaced wholesale with the request's fields; SinglePatchReview defaults tubule_percent/tumor_present/pleomorphism_score to None. A pathologist who modified p_003 to tubule 60% and later clicks approve on it sends status='approved' with None values, silently reverting to the machine value. approve_all (lines 391-400) spreads **existing and keeps them. patch_id is also never validated against machine patch ids.

```
                "status": r.status,
                "tubule_percent": r.tubule_percent,
                "tumor_present": r.tumor_present,
```
**Impact:** Pathologist corrections can be lost without feedback; aggregate silently changes back.

*Verifier note:* The code asymmetry is real: action 'update' assigns patch_overrides[p_id] wholesale at lines 405-413 from SinglePatchReview fields that default to None (56-58), whereas approve_all spreads **existing (394-399), so a partial update drops previously stored tubule_percent / tumor_present / pleomorphism_score. The patch_id sub-claim is harmless: the merge loop at 166-187 iterates machine patches only, so an unknown id in overrides is inert (it cannot inflate approved_patches or all_patches_reviewed, which are computed from merged_patches at 189-191). **Severity:** low · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/grading.py:405`

review_grading_patches 'update' writes patch_overrides[r.patch_id] without checking that the id exists in machine_patches; review_grading_hpfs does the same for seq. #### 611. Synthetic patch RNG seeded with Python hash(), so the 'deterministic' fallback image differs per process

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/grading.py:602`

hash() of a str is randomised per interpreter process via PYTHONHASHSEED, so the seed changes on every API restart/worker process; the same case/patch renders a different synthetic image across requests served by different uvicorn workers, contradicting the intent of a deterministic fallback and making cached copies inconsistent.

```
rng = np.random.RandomState(hash(f"{case_id}_{patch_id}") % (2**32))
```
**Impact:** Non-reproducible output from a path that is already serving fabricated evidence; harder to notice in tests.

**Fix:** Remove the synthetic fallback (return 404); if a placeholder is kept, seed from hashlib.sha256 like sample_stratified_patches does.

*Verifier note:* Confirmed verbatim at grading.py:602: np.random.RandomState(hash(f"{case_id}_{patch_id}") % (2**32)). str.__hash__ is salted per interpreter (PYTHONHASHSEED is not pinned anywhere in the repo — grep found no setting in code, Dockerfiles or ops config), so each uvicorn worker/restart renders different synthetic glands (612-628) for the same case/patch. Contrast worker/grading.py:117, which seeds with int(hashlib.md5(seed_str).hexdigest(),16) % 2**32 (md5, not sha256 as the finder wrote — cosmetic error). Worth noting the fallback is not rare: the on-demand extraction block above it cannot succeed at all, because Hotspot (line 553) and OPENSLIDE_GLOBAL_LOCK (line 572) are never imported in this file (imports at 24-45; cases.py:21 and mitosis.py:27 import the lock, grading.py does not), so any request that misses GCS raises NameError, is swallowed at 596-597, and lands on the synthetic path. Low is right for the seeding defect itself.


**Fix:** Pass cfg to both functions and have validate_grading_invariants take cfg (or make the DB CHECK the single hard-coded authority and delete the YAML keys); catch ValueError -> 400; coalesce None scores to 400.

*Verifier note:* Partly confirmed, materially over-stated. Real: line 648 calls calculate_nottingham_grade(t,p,m) with no cfg, so it falls back to DEFAULT_GRADE1/2_MAX_SUM (pipeline/grading.py:151-156) while the GET path at line 282 does pass scoring_cfg — an inconsistency, though currently invisible because configs/scoring.yaml sets grade1_max_sum: 5 / grade2_max_sum: 7, identical to the defaults. Real: validate_grading_invariants hard-codes `<= 5` / `<= 7` at pipeline/grading.py:187 with no cfg parameter, and aggregate_grading_findings computes the grade WITH cfg at line 289 then validates it at line 299, so changing the YAML cutoffs would make every worker run raise — and gradings' CHECK constraint (app/models/grading.py:44-50) hard-codes 5/7 as well. The config knob is genuinely a trap. Refuted sub-claim: the NULL-score 500. No production writer can create a Grading row with NULL sub-scores — worker/grading.py:414-436 is the only creator/updater and always sets all six values from aggregate_res; only test fixtures build rows, and they populate them too. And if it did happen the failure would be TypeError (None + int) inside calculate_nottingham_grade at line 648, not the ValueError at 649. Net: a latent config/maintenance hazard, not a live crash — low.

*Also reported at:* `backend/app/routers/grading.py:648` (recompute_grade_preview ignores the scoring config that the aggregate path uses); `backend/app/routers/grading.py:648` (/recompute endpoint never loads configs/scoring.yaml despite importing load_scoring_config)

#### 490. score_override audit event payload uses non-spec field names (from_score/to_score) instead of PRD's {component, from, to, justification}

**Severity:** low · **Category:** PRD deviation · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/grading.py:809`

PRD section 5 (and 00-overview.md §5.6) specify score_override audit events as '{component, from, to, justification}'. The confirm endpoint instead writes from_score/to_score keys.

```
payload={
    "component": comp,
    "from_score": o_info.get("original_score"),
    "to_score": o_info.get("score"),
    "justification": o_info.get("justification")
}
```
**Impact:** Cosmetic/schema-drift only within this stage, but any downstream analytics or audit-log consumer written against the PRD's documented shape (from/to) would fail to find the expected keys.

**Fix:** Rename to from/to to match the documented audit event contract.

*Verifier note:* Verified. prd/05-stage-v4.4-grading.md:77 reads: 'Overrides -> review_edits diff + score_override audit events {component, from, to, justification}'; 00-overview.md:153 lists score_override in the minimum audit set. The code at grading.py:802-813 emits event_type='score_override' with payload keys component / from_score / to_score / justification (the mismatched keys are on lines 809-810; 807 is the opening `payload={`). Purely a key-name deviation within this stage — no consumer in this repo reads these keys (grep for from_score/to_score finds no reader), so 'low' is right. Worth noting the PRD's `from` cannot be a Python kwarg but is fine as a dict key, so the fix is trivial.

#### 604. score_override audit 'from' value is client-supplied instead of the server's machine score

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Data integrity · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/grading.py:809`

The client can send any 'from' value, so the audit trail does not prove what the model actually proposed. The frontend (GradingReviewWorkspace.tsx:355) happens to send data.machine.tubule_score, but the server does not verify it.

```
"to_score": o_info.get("score"),
```
**Impact:** Override audit rows can misstate the machine score; delta analytics (PRD 05 section 6 'machine values for delta analytics') are unreliable.

*Verifier note:* Evidence exists verbatim at grading.py:809-810 inside the score_override audit loop (799-814), and the handler does hold server-side machine values: grading_record is loaded at 689 and its columns are only overwritten later at 740-746, plus worker/grading.py:378/422 persists aggregate_res into grading_record.machine['aggregate'], which survives confirm. So the proposed server-side fix is implementable and the claim 'from_score is unverified client input' is factually correct (frontend GradingReviewWorkspace.tsx:355/363 sends data.machine.tubule_score / pleo_score). Downgraded to low: the entire ConfirmGradingPayload is client-supplied and trusted (tubule_score, pleo_score, grade, reviewed_by at 98-103, 740-748), so from_score is no weaker than the values it annotates and no privilege boundary is crossed; and the PRD-05:91 'machine values for delta analytics' impact is overstated because machine['aggregate'] retains the true machine scores independently of the audit row.

#### 591. GET /stages/mitosis/{case_id} returns every detection with no pagination, and immutable crops are served no-cache, so the gallery re-downloads thousands of PNGs

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Performance · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/mitosis.py:99`

The stage payload materialises all Detection rows into JSON on every fetch (and bulk_action/re_place_hpfs re-invoke it). With the heuristic detector returning up to 6 candidates per tile and ~800 tiles per case, the payload is thousands of rows, the frontend recompute sends the full label map every 300 ms toggle, and MitosisGallery renders an <img> per candidate whose crop response is 'Cache-Control: no-cache, must-revalidate' (line 192) without an ETag, so each re-render re-fetches full PNGs through FastAPI to GCS.

```
det_rows = db.scalars(
    select(Detection).where((Detection.case_id == case_uid) | (Detection.case_id == str(case_id))).order_by(Detection.det_conf.desc().nulls_last())
).all()
```
**Impact:** Review UI latency and API load scale with candidate count; the PRD's 'recompute p95 < 1 s for 300 candidates' target is not achievable for the candidate volumes this detector produces.

**Fix:** Add limit/offset (or cursor by det_conf,id) and label filters to the GET, return summary separately; send only changed labels in recompute; mark crop responses immutable (Cache-Control: private, max-age=31536000, immutable) since crop ids never change content.

*Verifier note:* Both code-level claims hold. (a) mitosis.py:99-101 materialises every Detection row for the case with no limit/offset/label filter, and bulk_reject_unreviewed (line 570) and re_place_hpfs (line 612) both re-invoke get_mitosis_stage_data, so the full payload is re-sent after each bulk action; nothing in worker/mitosis.py caps candidate count — apply_global_nms (line 226) is the only reducer and there is no top-N. (b) mitosis.py:192 and 203 return crops with 'Cache-Control: no-cache, must-revalidate' and no ETag/Last-Modified, so any revalidation is a full re-GET through FastAPI to GCS even though crop bytes never change; MitosisGallery.tsx:150,170 builds one <img> per candidate from that endpoint. The frontend full-label-map claim is also verified (MitosisViewer.tsx:196-213 sends labelsMap over ALL candidates on a 300 ms debounce). Severity lowered because the volume premise is a projection, not evidence: '6 per tile x ~800 tiles' assumes the OpenCV heuristic fallback (pipeline/detect.py:118-119 caps at 6/tile) fires and that hotspot tiling yields ~800 tiles; at the PRD's own stated envelope (prd/04 line 82: 50-300 candidates; line 113: p95 < 1 s at 300) the payload is a few hundred rows and the p95 target is not obviously missed. Performance-only, no correctness impact.

#### 373. scoring.py masks n_hpf=0 with a 0.001 mm2 floor and router substitutes n_hpf=10 when there are no fields

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Bug · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/mitosis.py:150`

With zero HPFs area is clamped to 0.001 mm2 so any count >= 1 yields density >= 1000/mm2 (score 3); app/routers/mitosis.py:150 instead passes n_hpf=10 when hpfs is empty, giving area 2.157 for fields that do not exist. Both hide an invalid state rather than surfacing it.

```
area_mm2 = max(0.001, float(n_hpf * single_hpf_area_mm2))
```
**Impact:** Inconsistent, silently wrong summaries when hpf_sites is empty (e.g. mid-re-placement or after a failed worker run).

**Fix:** Raise ValueError for n_hpf <= 0 and let callers return a 'no fields placed' state.

*Verifier note:* Half confirmed, half unreachable — net still a real (minor) defect, so confirmed at low with the location moved to the surviving half. REFUTED part: the quoted failure at scoring.py:78 cannot occur. count_total is always produced by calculate_hpf_mitosis_counts over the SAME hpf list (worker/mitosis.py:402->405, routers/mitosis.py:147->148, :422->423), and with an empty hpf list that function returns total_count=0 (scoring.py:23-47), so the 0.001 floor is only ever divided into 0 -> density 0 -> score 1, never 'count>=1 -> >=1000/mm2 -> score 3'. Worker additionally can't reach n_hpf=0: hpf.py's pass-3 `while len(placed_hpfs) < count` loop (lines 232-252) always fabricates the full count. CONFIRMED part: routers/mitosis.py:150 and :425 substitute n_hpf=10 (and radius 262.0 at :151/:426) when no HPFs exist, so the API returns area_mm2=2.157 and n_hpf=10 for fields that do not exist, e.g. mid-re-placement or after a failed worker run. Wrong displayed denominator/field count, not a wrong score. Low is correct.

#### 127. Concurrent recomputes race on hpf_sites delete+insert; a failed request silently drops the label changes in it

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Concurrency · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/mitosis.py:392`

The frontend sends the full hpfs array on every debounced toggle (MitosisViewer.tsx:203), so every recompute deletes and re-inserts all ten HpfSite rows. Two overlapping requests (a second tab, or the 300 ms timer firing while approve-field's sync is in flight) both delete then both insert (case_id, seq) -> IntegrityError -> 500. get_db (app/core/db.py:39-44) closes without rollback so the label updates staged in that session are lost, and the UI's optimistic state now disagrees with the server with only a console.error (MitosisViewer.tsx:210-212).

```
if payload.hpfs:
    # Update HPFs in DB
    db.execute(delete(HpfSite).where(HpfSite.case_id == case_id))
    for h in payload.hpfs:
        hpf_row = HpfSite(
```
**Impact:** Lost pathologist toggles under normal double-click/keyboard usage; 500s in the review loop.

**Fix:** Only accept hpfs when the user actually moved one (frontend) and upsert rows by (case_id, seq) instead of delete+insert; wrap in a SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the case or a retry.

*Verifier note:* Mechanism confirmed: lines 392-405 unconditionally `delete(HpfSite).where(case_id == case_id)` then re-insert every row, and the frontend sends the full hpfs array on every debounced sync (frontend/components/viewer/MitosisViewer.tsx:200-204, called from both handleToggleCandidate:237 and handleApproveFieldAndNext:290). HpfSite PK is (case_id, seq) (backend/app/models/hpf_site.py:18-19) so two interleaved requests can collide on insert -> IntegrityError -> 500, and get_db (backend/app/core/db.py:38-44) has no except/rollback branch, so nothing in the request is committed. Two downgrades from the claimed severity: (a) the debounce timer is a single ref cleared on every call (MitosisViewer.tsx:191-195), so two overlapping requests need a round-trip slower than 300 ms or a second tab - not 'normal double-click usage'; (b) the payload is a full label map of every candidate, so a dropped request is repaired by the next toggle - only the last toggle before the reviewer leaves the screen is truly lost. The delete+insert-instead-of-upsert and the missing rollback are still real defects, hence confirmed at low rather than medium. Note this is the same delete-then-reinsert pattern as re_place_hpfs (line 601), which shares the window.

#### 128. add_candidate derives the detection id from a row count — concurrent adds collide on the composite PK

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Concurrency · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/mitosis.py:455`

new_id = f"m_user_{count_dets + 1:03d}" where count_dets is the total number of detections. Two simultaneous 'add missed mitosis' clicks (or two reviewers) compute the same id and the second insert violates PRIMARY KEY (id, case_id) -> IntegrityError -> 500, after the (slow) crop has already been uploaded to GCS. The count is also loaded as full ORM rows just to len() them.

```
count_dets = len(db.scalars(select(Detection).where(Detection.case_id == case_id)).all())
new_id = f"m_user_{count_dets + 1:03d}"
```
**Impact:** Sporadic 500s and orphaned crop blobs under concurrent review.

**Fix:** Use f"m_user_{uuid4().hex[:8]}" (or a DB sequence) and select count() instead of materialising rows.

*Verifier note:* Evidence exists verbatim at mitosis.py:455-456. Detection's PK really is composite: backend/app/models/detection.py:17-18 declares id=Column(String, primary_key=True) and case_id=Column(GUID, ..., primary_key=True), so a duplicate m_user_NNN for the same case is an IntegrityError. Sequential adds are safe (count grows by one each time), so the only failure path is two overlapping requests reading the same count — genuine but narrow, and the GCS uploads at 497-498 happen before db.add/commit at 512-525, so a failed insert does leave two orphan crop blobs. Low is correct; the wasteful len(...all()) instead of select(count()) is a real but cosmetic side note.

#### 593. add_candidate performs no de-duplication against existing detections, so clicking near an existing candidate creates a second mitosis a few um away

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Data integrity · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/mitosis.py:455`

The endpoint counts rows for an id, cuts a crop and inserts a new Detection with label 'mitosis' unconditionally. It never checks whether a detection already exists within the 7.5 um NMS radius (e.g. a rejected 'not_mitosis' candidate the pathologist meant to re-accept, or an accidental double click). The frontend 'add missed mitosis' click lands on the same figure the model already found in a large fraction of cases.

```
count_dets = len(db.scalars(select(Detection).where(Detection.case_id == case_id)).all())
new_id = f"m_user_{count_dets + 1:03d}"
```
**Impact:** Two rows at the same coordinates both count toward HPF counts and count_total, inflating mitoses/mm2; the audit trail records an 'added' figure rather than a label flip, corrupting the v4.6 FP/FN analytics.

**Fix:** Before inserting, query detections for the case and if any lies within nms_radius_um of the click, flip that row's label to 'mitosis' (logging review_edit from/to) and return it instead of inserting; otherwise insert.

*Verifier note:* The absence is real: add_pathologist_mitosis (mitosis.py:446-539) does no proximity query at all — it counts rows (455), cuts a crop, and inserts unconditionally with label='mitosis' (507). Neither side of the wire dedups: MitosisViewer.tsx:239-252 posts on a single click in pinning mode with no radius check. But the impact paragraph is materially overstated, which is why I drop it to low. The headline scenario ('a rejected not_mitosis candidate the pathologist meant to re-accept') does NOT inflate any count: pipeline/scoring.py:31-32 counts only candidates with label == 'mitosis', so the rejected twin contributes nothing to HPF counts or count_total. Double counting requires pinning on top of an already-accepted mitosis, or pinning the same figure twice. And a genuine double-click does not produce two rows — two in-flight requests both compute the same count_dets and thus the same new_id, colliding on the (id, case_id) primary key (app/models/detection.py:17-18) and 500ing; the id-generation scheme itself is broken (deleting or re-adding rows makes m_user_{n+1} collide), which is an adjacent defect this batch does not report.

#### 628. Concurrent first GETs on the same case race in _ensure_report_record and can 500 on the primary key

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Concurrency · **Location:** `backend/app/routers/report.py:117`

_ensure_report_record does select-then-insert with no locking or ON CONFLICT and is called by GET /report/{case_id}, /pdf, /json, PUT, sign and amend. Two overlapping requests (the ReportWorkspace fetch plus a direct /pdf or /json link, or two browser tabs) both see no row, both db.add(Report(case_id=...)) and one commit raises IntegrityError on the case_id primary key, which is not caught -> HTTP 500. GET endpoints therefore also have a write side effect.

```
report = db.scalars(select(Report).where(Report.case_id == case_uid)).first()
if report:
    return report
...
db.add(report)
db.commit()
```
**Impact:** Intermittent 500 on first open of a report page; a read endpoint that writes.

**Fix:** Create the draft row exactly once (in the worker on stage queue / grading confirm) and make GET 404 if it is missing; if lazy creation stays, catch IntegrityError, rollback and re-select.

*Verifier note:* Verified. _ensure_report_record (117-153) is select-then-insert with no SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, no ON CONFLICT, and no IntegrityError handling; case_id is the sole primary key of reports (backend/app/models/report.py:17-19), so a losing racer's commit at line 151 raises IntegrityError and escapes to a 500. It is called from GET /{case_id} (334 -> 254), GET /pdf (539), GET /json (571 -> 254), PUT/POST update (345), resynthesize (415), regenerate (491), sign (584) and amend (672), so read endpoints do write. The race is real because all those handlers are sync `def` and run concurrently in the threadpool. Low is the right severity: it only fires on the very first touch of a case, on a narrow window, and self-heals on retry. Note the worker has the same lazy-create (backend/worker/report.py:68-91), so a stage run overlapping a first GET is another way in.
