#### 266. Nested <button> in StageRail (retry inside stage button) is invalid DOM

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Frontend / UX · **Location:** `frontend/components/viewer/StageRail.tsx:161`

The retry `<button>` (line 161) is rendered inside the stage-select `<button>` (line 130). Interactive content inside a button is invalid HTML; React logs `validateDOMNesting` and browsers may hoist the inner button out of the outer one, so the `e.stopPropagation()` in `handleRetry` does not reliably prevent stage selection and keyboard activation is ambiguous.

```
<button onClick={() => onSelectStage(st.name)} ...>
  ...
  {!collapsed && isFailed && (
    <button onClick={(e) => handleRetry(e, st.name)}
```
**Impact:** Retry click can also switch stages or not fire; screen readers announce one control.

**Fix:** Make the stage row a `<div role="button">` or render the retry control as a sibling outside the button.

*Verifier note:* The structural claim is accurate: the stage-select <button> opens at StageRail.tsx:130 (`onClick={() => onSelectStage(st.name)}`) and closes at line 172; the retry <button onClick={(e) => handleRetry(e, st.name)}> at lines 161-168 sits inside it (inside the status-badge div at 159-171). That is invalid HTML per the button content model, and React logs `validateDOMNesting: <button> cannot appear as a descendant of <button>` in dev. Line numbers as cited are correct.

Severity lowered medium -> low because both stated failure modes are refuted:
(1) "browsers may hoist the inner button out" - hoisting is an HTML *parser* behaviour, so it only bites for server-rendered markup. This subtree only renders when `isFailed` (line 126), which requires `stages` to contain a failed entry; the parent at frontend/app/cases/[id]/page.tsx:265-267 passes `stages={caseDetail?.stages || []}` and `caseDetail` is populated only by the client-side `loadData()` in a useEffect (page.tsx:47-61), so on the server pass stages is always empty and the nested button is never in the SSR HTML. It is created client-side via React's DOM node APIs, which bypass the parser and preserve the nesting - no hoisting, no hydration mismatch.
(2) "stopPropagation does not reliably prevent stage selection / retry may not fire" - both handlers are React synthetic handlers on the same delegated root listener, and `e.stopPropagation()` at line 44 halts propagation through the React tree, so onSelectStage(st.name) does not run on a retry click. Keyboard activation is likewise unambiguous: the inner button is separately focusable and Enter/Space fires its own onClick, which stops propagation the same way.

What remains genuinely wrong is the spec violation and the a11y consequence: a nested interactive control inside a button is not guaranteed to be exposed as its own control in the accessibility tree, and the outer button's accessible name absorbs the inner content. Worth fixing, but it is a correctness-of-markup/a11y nit, not a broken retry. The proposed fix (render the retry as a sibling outside the button, e.g. wrap the row in the existing flex div at line 129 and drop the outer <button> to a div/row with the label as its own button) is the right shape; the sibling variant is preferable to role="button" since it avoids reimplementing keyboard semantics.

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Data integrity · **Location:** `frontend/components/viewer/TriageViewer.tsx:179`

The edit mapper checks `h.excluded` before `h.source === 'pathologist_added'`. For a user_XX ROI that was excluded, only `{op:'exclude', id:'user_01'}` is sent; apply_edit_ops ignores exclude for ids not in the machine set (backend/app/routers/triage.py:86-88), so the ROI is neither added nor recorded. Likewise a hotspot the model already flagged `excluded: true` is re-sent as an exclude op with the pathologist's reason, overwriting provenance.

```

  if (h.excluded) {
    return { op: "exclude", id: h.id, reason: h.exclude_reason };
  } else if (h.source === "pathologist_added") {
```
**Impact:** UI shows the user ROI as 'Excluded (Restore)' but after reload/confirm it does not exist; audit trail cannot distinguish model exclusions from pathologist exclusions.

**Fix:** Emit ops from a diff against `data.machine_hotspots`: add (+exclude) for user ROIs, exclude only when excluded changed, modify only when polygon changed, delete for missing ids.

*Verifier note:* First half confirmed, second half refuted. In handleSaveDraftEdits (lines 179-186) the `if (h.excluded)` branch precedes the `pathologist_added` branch, so an added-then-excluded ROI is serialised only as {op:'exclude', id:'user_01'}; apply_edit_ops (routers/triage.py:86-88) guards `elif action == 'exclude' and hid in hotspots_dict`, and user_01 is not in the machine set, so the op is a no-op and the ROI is silently lost on the next fetch/confirm. The second claim does not hold: extract_hotspots always emits excluded=False (pipeline/hotspots.py:96,134), so a machine hotspot is never excluded:true in the machine output; the only way h.excluded is true for an hs_XX id is that a pathologist excluded it earlier, and re-emitting that exclude with the same stored reason is idempotent, not a provenance overwrite. Severity lowered to low: the loss needs the odd add-then-exclude sequence (deleting the ROI is the natural action, and Delete does remove it from local state). Worth noting a nearby, larger defect the finder only hints at in the fix: no `delete` op is ever emitted, so a deleted machine hotspot reappears after reload, and every untouched machine hotspot is sent as `modify`, which flips its source to 'pathologist_modified' (routers/triage.py:72-74).

*Verifier note:* Line 9 is correct: `async rewrites()` starts there and the quoted destination http://localhost:8000/api/:path* is verbatim (lines 12-13). The claim that the rewrite is dead holds: a grep for relative '/api/' string literals across app/, components/, lib/, types/ returns zero hits, while all 7 files that build request URLs use the absolute API_BASE (lib/api.ts uses `${API_BASE}/api/v1/...` for every fetch/XHR; OpenSeadragonViewer.tsx:278 builds tile URLs as `${API_BASE}/api/v1/cases/${caseId}/tiles/...`). The secondary remark about lib/api.ts:1-3 is also factually true (the server branch is hardcoded to http://localhost:8000 and ignores NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL), but it is latent only: all 9 modules importing @/lib/api are "use client" and no fetch runs at module scope, so no request is ever issued from the server branch today. (Also noted: no .env* file exists in frontend/, so the client branch falls back to localhost too, which is why the dead rewrite went unnoticed.)

#### 268. next-shim.d.ts shadows real type definitions; ignoreBuildErrors hides the rest

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Dependencies / environment · **Location:** `frontend/types/next-shim.d.ts:1`

Shorthand ambient modules take precedence over resolved packages. Verified empirically: with this shim, `const a: number = Link; <Link nonsense={1}/>` type-checks (exit 0); without it, tsc reports 3 errors. So `next/link`, `next/image`, `lucide-react` and `openseadragon` are `any` everywhere despite real `.d.ts` files being installed, which is why `tsc --noEmit` 'passes'. `next.config.mjs:3-8` then sets `typescript.ignoreBuildErrors: true` and `eslint.ignoreDuringBuilds: true`, and there is no ESLint config, so `next lint` prompts interactively and cannot run in CI. `@types/openseadragon ^3.0.10` is also paired with `openseadragon ^5.0.0` (package.json:14,20).

```
declare module "next/link";
declare module "next/image";
declare module "lucide-react";
declare module "openseadragon";
```
**Impact:** Prop typos on Link/Image/icons/OSD and any future type error ship silently to production.

**Fix:** Delete the shim, fix the resulting real errors, set `ignoreBuildErrors: false`, add an `.eslintrc.json` with `next/core-web-vitals`, and update `@types/openseadragon` (or rely on OSD 5's bundled types).

*Verifier note:* Mechanism and evidence both hold. The four lines at next-shim.d.ts:1-4 are quoted verbatim, and TypeScript does consult ambient module declarations before node_modules resolution, so next/link, next/image, lucide-react and openseadragon all resolve to `any`. Reproduced the finder's experiment in a scratch copy with node_modules symlinked from frontend/: a probe with `const a: number = Link; const b: number = Upload; <Link nonsenseProp={1}/>` gives exit 0 with the shim present and 3 TS2322 errors with it removed. The rest of the description checks out too: next.config.mjs:3-8 really sets typescript.ignoreBuildErrors:true and eslint.ignoreDuringBuilds:true; no .eslintrc*/eslint.config.* exists outside node_modules and neither eslint nor eslint-config-next is installed, so `next lint` hits the interactive setup prompt; and openseadragon 5.0.1 ships no `types`/`typings` field in its package.json, so the ^3.0.10 @types pairing is a real version mismatch (and the finder's suggested 'rely on OSD 5 bundled types' alternative does not exist). Downgraded medium -> low on impact: I ran tsc over the actual app/, components/ and lib/ with the shim deleted and got 0 errors, exit 0 — the shim is currently hiding nothing, so this is preventive hygiene (a 4-line deletion, one of which, next/image, is dead since the app never imports it) rather than a live defect. The compounding risk from ignoreBuildErrors:true belongs to next.config.mjs, not this file.

#### 48. QC thresholds contradict the PRD and the 'calibration' comment is placeholder text; 3 of 5 checks and their config sections are dead

**Severity:** high · **Category:** Clinical correctness · **Location:** `configs/qc.yaml:15`

PRD 02 §3.1 defaults: blurry if VoL < 45, slide fail if > 30% blurry, warn if > 10%. qc.yaml ships vol_threshold 5.0, fail 0.70, warn 0.30 — an order of magnitude more permissive. The header claims calibration on 'ARCHIVE-BAD-001..020 / ARCHIVE-GOOD-001..050' with 'sensitivity >= 90%' — these are template ids, not a recorded calibration. The pen_marks, folds and stain_sanity sections are never read: pipeline/qc_checks.py implements only tissue_coverage and focus (run_all_qc_checks lines 149-155).

```
focus:
  vol_threshold: 5.0    # Variance of Laplacian (VoL) threshold below which a 512x512 tile is considered blurry
  ...
  fail_blurry_ratio: 0.70  # > 70% blurry tissue tiles triggers hard fail
  warn_blurry_ratio: 0.30  # > 30% blurry tissue tiles triggers warning
```
**Impact:** Even if the focus sampler were fixed, a slide with 69% blurry tissue passes as 'warn', and pen marks / folds / faded stain are never flagged. The fabricated calibration comment gives false assurance to reviewers.

**Fix:** Restore PRD defaults (45 / 0.30 / 0.10), delete the fake calibration block until a real run is recorded, and either implement pen/fold/stain-sanity checks or remove their config so the file reflects what runs.

*Verifier note:* Every sub-claim checks out. (1) PRD 02 line 56 locks 'tile blurry if VoL < 45; slide fail if > 30% blurry; warn if > 10%'; qc.yaml:15,18,19 ship 5.0 / 0.70 / 0.30 — 9x more permissive on VoL and 2.3x/3x on the ratios. The same lax numbers are also baked in as code defaults (qc_checks.py:27,81-83), so there is no fallback to PRD values. (2) The header calibration block (qc.yaml:3-8) is placeholder text: grep for ARCHIVE-BAD/ARCHIVE-GOOD across the whole repo returns only qc.yaml itself — no fixtures, no calibration run, no recorded metrics; the '>= 90% sensitivity / <= 2.0% false-fail' figures are unsupported. (3) Dead config confirmed: run_all_qc_checks (qc_checks.py:147-155) builds checks=[cov_res, focus_res] only; pen_marks (:21), folds (:42) and stain_sanity (:47) are read by nothing in the repo, so 3 of the PRD's 5 checks (PRD lines 57-59) do not exist. This also breaks PRD acceptance item line 95 ('a deliberately blurred copy of a fixture slide -> QC fail with focus message') and unit-test requirement line 89 (drawn green rectangle triggers pen detector) — test_qc_checks.py has no pen/fold/stain test at all. Severity high is right: it is a config/coverage gap on a human-reviewed gate, not silent patient-facing output, so not critical.

**Impact:** The acceptance checklist item (PRD §9) appears satisfied while the shipped pipeline is unvalidated; downstream readers (clinical sign-off, regulators) are misled.

(Minor correction to the finder: verify.py:29's own default parameter IS 0.50, so EVAL.md matches the dead default rather than the live config — it does not rescue the claim, the worker always overrides.)

(4) PRD conflict confirmed. prd/00-overview.md:26 decision 2: "Mitosis verifier = dedicated classifier, published weights first; HoVer-Net deferred (morphometry is optional evidence, v4.6+)", and prd/04-stage-v4.3-mitosis.md:12 lists HoVer-Net under "Out". EVAL.md nonetheless designates it the shipped Primary Verifier and sources the headline F1 from it.

(5) Severity raised medium -> high. This file is not incidental documentation, it IS the ship gate: prd/04-stage-v4.3-mitosis.md:117 requires "MIDOG++ held-out eval ... documented (F1, precision, recall, threshold) in models/detector/EVAL.md; F1 >= 0.70 floor to ship ... below floor -> escalate, don't ship silently". #### 177. Narrative prompt asks for margin, nodal and mitotic-count statements the payload does not contain

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** Clinical correctness · **Location:** `configs/prompts/cap_report@v1.md:9`

The prompt demands 'mitotic activity per 10 HPFs (2.157 mm²)', 'surgical margin clearance, nodal status' but case_summary_payload (worker/report.py:115-133, router 504-515) contains only mitotic_score, no count/density, no margins, no lymph_nodes, no dcis. Rule 1 ('rely SOLELY on the JSON') therefore forces the model to invent them. The unit itself contradicts PRD 00 locked decision 1 (mitoses/mm² through CAP table) and configs/scoring.yaml:4 (basis: per_mm2).

```
- **MICROSCOPIC_DESCRIPTION**: ... mitotic activity per 10 HPFs (2.157 mm²), lymphovascular invasion status ...
- **CLINICAL_CORRELATION**: ... surgical margin clearance, nodal status ...
```
**Impact:** Systematic fabrication of margin/node/mitotic statements in the narrative.

**Fix:** Include margins, lymph_nodes, dcis_present, mitoses_per_mm2 and count in the payload; change unit text to mitoses/mm²; instruct the model to write 'not assessed' for absent keys.

*Verifier note:* Payload omission is real. configs/prompts/cap_report@v1.md:9-10 demands 'mitotic activity per 10 HPFs (2.157 mm²)' and 'surgical margin clearance, nodal status', while both callers build a payload without those keys: backend/worker/report.py:115-133 sends only case_id, procedure, laterality, tumor_site, histologic_type, tumor_size_mm, lvi_status, nottingham_grade{grade,tubule_score,tubule_percent,pleo_score,mitotic_score,nottingham_sum}, staging, biomarkers; backend/app/routers/report.py:505-516 (regenerate-narrative) builds the identical set. report_record.margins, .lymph_nodes and .dcis_present exist on the record and are passed to the PDF renderer (worker/report.py:190-192) but are deliberately absent from the LLM payload. There is no mitotic count or density anywhere: Grading (backend/app/models/grading.py:20-25) stores only mitotic_score 1-3, no mitoses_per_mm2 and no raw count, so 'per 10 HPFs' cannot be grounded even in principle. Nothing downstream catches an invented statement: validate_narrative_consistency (backend/pipeline/staging.py:181-207) only compares Nottingham grade tokens, and the worker path never calls it at all (worker/report.py:141-144 assigns the narrative directly). Severity lowered from high to medium for three reasons. (1) Nodal status is partly grounded after all — staging IS in the payload and carries pn_stage/pt_stage/stage_group computed at worker/report.py:99-109, so the model can legitimately write 'pN0'; the ungrounded parts are margins, DCIS and the mitotic count. (2) Rule 2 on line 6 explicitly forbids altering or inventing numeric values including 'mitotic count, lymph node counts, margins', which directly counteracts Rule 1's pressure; the likely output is a hedged 'correlation with margin status is recommended' (exactly what the deterministic fallback at backend/pipeline/medgemma.py:312-315 writes) rather than a fabricated margin measurement, so fabrication is model-dependent, not guaranteed — the deterministic part of the defect is the prompt asking for content the JSON cannot supply. (3) The unit sub-claim is refuted: 2.157 mm² is not a contradiction of the repo's own config — configs/scoring.yaml:35-37 sets hpf.radius_um 262.0 with the comment 'area ≈ 0.2157 mm²' and count 10, i.e. exactly 2.157 mm² for 10 fields, and line 9 of scoring.yaml sets display_classic_equivalent: true while PRD 00 locked decision 1 says 'Classic per-10-HPF count also displayed'. So expressing mitoses per 10 HPF alongside a mm² figure is what the locked decision asks for, not a violation. The only genuine unit nit is that PRD 06 line 31 uses 0.274 mm²/HPF (2.74 mm² per 10) for the classic equivalent while the prompt and scoring.yaml hpf block use 0.2157 mm²/HPF — a repo-internal inconsistency worth a separate low-severity finding, not evidence for this one. Real fix is the payload, not the unit string: add margins, lymph_nodes, dcis_present and a mitoses count/density to both builders (worker/report.py:115 and routers/report.py:505) and add an explicit 'write "not assessed" for any key absent from the JSON' instruction.

#### 633. cap_elements.yaml histologic_types value set drifts from the HistologicTypeResponse Literal used by grading

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Docs · **Location:** `configs/cap_elements.yaml:70`

The YAML lists 10 histologic type ids (adds micropapillary, apocrine, medullary_features vs the PRD/Pydantic set), while pipeline/medgemma.py:36 HistologicTypeResponse.type only allows IDC-NST, ILC, mucinous, tubular, papillary, metaplastic, other, and the PRD 06 section 2 value_set is the 7-item list. specimen_types likewise lists re_excision / total_mastectomy / modified_radical_mastectomy against the PRD's [core_biopsy, excision, mastectomy, other]. Because the YAML is never loaded (already noted) nothing breaks today, but the moment it is wired up the two sources disagree.

```
histologic_types:
  - id: IDC-NST
  ...
  - id: micropapillary
  - id: apocrine
  - id: medullary_features
```
**Impact:** Two competing value sets for the same clinical element; wiring the YAML in will either reject grading outputs or accept types the grader can never produce.

**Fix:** Make the YAML the single source and derive the Pydantic Literal from it (or generate both from one list); keep the PRD value set or explicitly extend it.

*Verifier note:* Verified line by line. cap_elements.yaml:70-90 lists 10 histologic ids — IDC-NST, ILC, mucinous, tubular, papillary, micropapillary, metaplastic, apocrine, medullary_features, other. backend/pipeline/medgemma.py:36 HistologicTypeResponse.type is Literal['IDC-NST','ILC','mucinous','tubular','papillary','metaplastic','other'] — 7 values — and PRD 06 §2's value_set for histologic_type is that same 7-item list, so the YAML's micropapillary, apocrine and medullary_features exist in no other source. specimen_types drift is real too: YAML:4-22 has core_biopsy, excision, re_excision, total_mastectomy, modified_radical_mastectomy, other against the PRD's [core_biopsy, excision, mastectomy, other]. The finder's own caveat is accurate — nothing breaks today because the YAML is never read (index 191), so the pydantic Literal is the only enforced set and the grader can never emit the three extra types. Low is the right severity: latent, docs/consistency-grade, and it becomes real only when 191 is fixed. Overlaps index 191's 'histologic_types, lvi_statuses, margin_statuses duplicate Literal lists in code' but is not a duplicate — 191 asserts duplication, this asserts the duplicates already disagree in membership, which is a separately verifiable fact and a separate line item in the fix. Worth adding: the drift is three-way, since frontend/components/viewer/ReportWorkspace.tsx:401-404 offers procedure as free-text display strings ('Core Needle Biopsy', 'Excision / Lumpectomy', 'Total Mastectomy', 'Modified Radical Mastectomy') that match neither the YAML ids nor the PRD set.

#### 518. Shadow-mode model scaffold is entirely absent, including its config file location

**Severity:** low · **Category:** PRD deviation · **Location:** `configs/mitosis.yaml:3`

PRD section 4 item 3 requires `configs/models.yaml` to gain a `shadow: {detector: <weights_uri>}` key, with the mitosis worker running both models when set, persisting shadow outputs to a parallel GCS prefix (never shown in UI), and a nightly diff job. configs/models.yaml does not exist at all; the actual detector config lives in configs/mitosis.yaml with no shadow key, and worker/mitosis.py runs a single fixed detector from configs/mitosis.yaml's `detector.weights_path`.

**Impact:** PRD calls this scaffold 'how any future model swap (probe v2, own detector) gets validated without touching patients' — without it, any future detector/probe swap has no safe validation path and must be tested live against pathologists instead.

**Fix:** Add configs/models.yaml with the shadow key, thread a second detector invocation through worker/mitosis.py behind that config flag, and write a nightly diff job.

*Verifier note:* Facts verified: `find`/`ls configs/` shows no models.yaml (configs/ holds only cap_elements.yaml, mitosis.yaml, pricing.yaml, qc.yaml, scoring.yaml, triage.yaml, stain_reference.png, prompts/); grep for 'shadow' across .py/.yaml returns nothing outside Tailwind class names in frontend/*.tsx; configs/mitosis.yaml:3-15 defines one detector block with no shadow variant; worker/mitosis.py:156 constructs exactly one detector. The PRD requirement is real — prd/07-stage-v4.6-validation.md:71 item 3 verbatim requires configs/models.yaml with `shadow: {detector: <weights_uri>}`, dual-model runs, a parallel GCS prefix and a nightly diff job. Severity cut high -> low. Two reasons. (1) Scope: this is a v4.6 item, and v4.6 is the last stage in prd/00-overview.md:21's stage map; the repo implements v4.0-v4.5 only (backend/worker has ingest, preprocess, qc, triage, mitosis, grading, report — no validation worker, no batch harness, no override analytics, no cost dashboards, no DICOM export, i.e. NONE of prd/07's deliverables exist). This is one line item of a stage that was never started, not a localized defect in shipped code, and the 'without it any future swap must be tested live against pathologists' impact is hypothetical future-work risk with no current patient exposure. (2) The location anchor is misleading: the finding is 'a file does not exist', pinned to configs/mitosis.yaml:3, which is merely where the single detector block happens to live. Note also the proposed fix is partly redundant with index 130 — a shadow key in a second models.yaml would be dead on arrival while worker/mitosis.py:156 ignores detector.weights_path entirely; wiring weights_path (130/472) is a prerequisite.

#### 562. qc.yaml focus.tile_size_px is never read; 512 um patch size and 2x stride are hard-coded

**Severity:** low · **Category:** PRD deviation · **Location:** `configs/qc.yaml:16`

The 'live' focus section declares tile_size_px: 512, but check_focus_sharpness hard-codes patch_size_um = 512.0 and step_um = patch_size_um * 2 (qc_checks.py:88,96), so editing the config has no effect and the sampling stride (which halves coverage) is undocumented.

```
focus:
  vol_threshold: 5.0    # Variance of Laplacian (VoL) threshold below which a 512x512 tile is considered blurry
  tile_size_px: 512
```
**Impact:** Config discipline violated for the one QC check that is implemented; calibration edits to tile size are silently ignored.

**Fix:** Read tile_size_px (and add stride) from cfg in check_focus_sharpness; delete unread keys.

*Verifier note:* Confirmed. check_focus_sharpness reads only vol_threshold, fail_blurry_ratio, warn_blurry_ratio and sample_max_tiles from cfg (qc_checks.py:81-84); tile_size_px is never read anywhere in the repo (the tile_size_px hits in detect.py:177 and mitosis.py:93 come from configs/mitosis.yaml, not qc.yaml). Tile geometry is hard-coded three times: patch_size_um = 512.0 (:88), step_um = patch_size_um * 2 (:96), and out_px=512 in the read_region_srgb call (:109). Minor correction to the finder's wording: patch_size_um is a micrometre field-of-view, not a pixel size — the pixel dimension the config key actually names is the hard-coded out_px=512 at line 109 — but either way editing qc.yaml:16 has zero effect. The 2x stride is real and undocumented: it samples one tile per 1024um x 1024um cell, covering ~25% of tissue area, which is consistent with the <=400-tile cap but is not stated in the PRD or the config. Low severity is right: the stride still yields a representative sample and the cap bounds cost; the harm is config-discipline/false-configurability, not a wrong verdict.

#### 550. configs/stain_reference.png is a synthetic 3-colour image, not a TCGA H&E patch

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Clinical correctness · **Location:** `configs/stain_reference.png:1`

PRD 02 §2.2 requires 'one well-stained TCGA patch' as the Macenko target. The checked-in 512x512 PNG contains exactly 3 unique RGB values (verified with PIL/numpy: mean [194,147,185], 3 unique colours, 15 KB). Macenko's SVD/angle-percentile fit on a 3-colour image is degenerate: the 1st/99th percentile angles collapse, triggering the `abs(max_angle-min_angle) < 0.25` fallback in _get_stain_params, so 'fitted' target params are just the hard-coded vectors.

```
(binary) 512x512 RGB PNG, 3 unique colours — see stain.py:62-64 fallback:
        if np.abs(max_angle - min_angle) < 0.25:
            v_min = np.array([0.65, 0.70, 0.29])
            v_max = np.array([0.07, 0.99, 0.11])
```
**Impact:** stain_params.json records a target that was never derived from real tissue; any future fix that makes transform() honour the fitted target would normalise every slide toward a cartoon palette.

**Fix:** Replace with a real well-stained H&E patch (e.g. a TCGA 512x512 crop) and add a test asserting the reference has > N unique colours and produces a non-fallback stain matrix.

*Verifier note:* Core claim holds, quoted mechanism does not. Verified with PIL/numpy: the checked-in file is 512x512 RGB with exactly 3 unique colours ([65,45,115] x45600, [215,145,185] x160218, [240,235,240] x56326), mean [194.3,146.9,184.6], 15135 bytes - a synthetic flat-colour image, not the 'one well-stained TCGA patch' that prd/02-stage-v4.1-preprocess-qc.md:31 requires. That spec violation is real. The stated failure path is REFUTED: running backend/pipeline/stain.py:41-77 on the actual file gives 205818/262144 px past the od>=0.15 mask, min_angle=-3.0618, max_angle=2.8487, |diff|=5.91 - two orders of magnitude above the 0.25 threshold at stain.py:62, so the hard-coded-vector fallback is NOT triggered and the fitted target is [[0.5822,0.7389,0.3392],[0.2541,0.8408,0.4780]] with max_conc [1.0196,0.2916], not the fallback constants. The real weakness is different: those two vectors have dot product ~0.93 (near-collinear, a degenerate deconvolution basis) and an E max-concentration of 0.29 that is implausibly low for real tissue. Severity lowered from medium to low because there is no runtime effect at all today: transform() hard-codes W_target (stain.py:144-147) and maxC_target (stain.py:179) and refits W_src from the source image, so every consumer that loads stain_params.json into stain_matrix_target/max_conc_target (worker/triage.py:395-396, worker/mitosis.py:332-333, app/routers/tiles.py:97-99, app/routers/triage.py:413-415, app/routers/mitosis.py:316-318) has those values silently ignored. The defect is provenance/spec-compliance in a persisted audit artifact plus a latent trap for a future fix, not a live clinical-correctness bug, and the proposed test assertion ('produces a non-fallback stain matrix') would pass on the current bad file.

(4) calculate_mitotic_score_from_hpfs (backend/pipeline/grading.py:192, called from backend/app/routers/grading.py:251) genuinely has zero tests — grep for the symbol across backend/tests returns nothing — and it uses a wholly different rule (raw-count cutoffs 8/16, grading.py:210-211) from scoring.py's density rule, so the divergence is untested. (5) test_hpf.py:90-112 is exactly as described: its only assertion is `assert len(hpfs) == 10` (line 112), and on that input (40x40 grid = 640x640 um, min_sep 524) placement falls through Pass 1 and Pass 2 into the Pass 3 geometry fallback (hpf.py:232-249), which places fields at radius_um*0.75*(1+seq//4) ~= 196 um from the first center — far under the 524 um non-overlap requirement — so the test would and does pass with overlapping fields. The strict-path test at test_hpf.py:50-87 does assert the invariant, but the relaxation test does not. (6) test_cap_reporting.py: test_ajcc_pn_staging_cutoffs (lines 112-134) never passes largest_meta_mm <= 0.2 (pN0(i+)/ITC, documented at staging.py:67), test_ajcc_pt_staging_cutoffs (74-108) never asserts pT0, no test asserts pN1b/pN1c/pN2b/pN3b/pN3c (all in valid_pn, staging.py:176), and the stage-group default fallback (staging.py:141-149, which silently returns 'IA' for any unmatched pT/pN pair such as pT2+pN1b) is never exercised. Two of the PRD items the finder lists in passing ARE covered and should not count against the suite: '< 10 HPFs' (test_scoring_with_fewer_hpfs, lines 51-58) and 'zero mitoses' (the (0, 10, 1) case, line 34). That trims the finding slightly but does not change it — medium is the right severity: this is not itself a clinical bug, but it is a documented-PRD test requirement that is unmet and that demonstrably lets the Pass-3 overlap defect and the two-implementation mitotic-score divergence ship under a green suite.

#### 459. The 'embedding cache' test never wires in the mock client and only asserts a trivially-true equality — doesn't test PRD 5's caching requirement

**Severity:** medium · **Category:** PRD deviation · **Location:** `backend/tests/test_triage_worker.py:58`

PRD §5 requires 'Embedding cache: second run makes zero endpoint calls (assert via injected fake client)'. The test creates a `MagicMock` with `side_effect=Exception(...)` on `get_embeddings` but never passes it into `run_triage` (which has no such injection point at all), then only asserts `output_ref_2 == output_ref` — which is trivially true regardless of caching since the output path is deterministically derived from `case_id` alone.

```
mock_client = MagicMock()
mock_client.get_embeddings.side_effect = Exception("Should not be called when cached!")

stage_exec.status = "running"
db_session.commit()

output_ref_2, _ = run_triage(stage_exec, db_session)
assert output_ref_2 == output_ref
```
**Impact:** The test suite gives false confidence that embedding caching (which does not exist — see prior finding) is verified; CI would pass this test even with zero caching behavior, masking the missing PRD requirement.

**Fix:** Once real caching is implemented, inject a fake Vertex client/counter into `run_triage` and assert it recorded zero calls on the second invocation.

*Verifier note:* Both halves hold. The MagicMock at lines 59-60 is never passed anywhere; run_triage's signature is (stage_execution, session) (worker/triage.py:193) and it constructs its own VertexPathFoundationClient internally at :269-274, so there is no injection point — the mock is dead code and its side_effect can never fire. The assertion at line 66 is vacuous: output_ref is built at worker/triage.py:515 as f"gs://{settings.GCS_ARTIFACTS_BUCKET}/cases/{case_id}/triage/output.json", derived from constants and case_id alone, so output_ref_2 == output_ref regardless of whether any caching, embedding, or endpoint call happened. The premise that no cache exists is also verified: pyarrow.parquet is imported at triage.py:18, parquet_path is computed at :240, and neither is referenced again anywhere in the file — nothing is ever written to or read from parquet. That directly contradicts the test's own comment on line 58 and PRD 03 §5 line 93 ('second run makes zero endpoint calls (assert via injected fake client)'). Medium is fair: a PRD-mandated test exists in name only and would pass against zero caching. Note the test cannot actually reach line 66 today anyway — it dies at the GCS upload per index 101 — but that is a separate defect.

#### 405. No conftest.py — every API test file duplicates identical in-memory-SQLite/dependency-override boilerplate, and DB state is shared across all tests within a file

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Tests · **Location:** `backend/tests/test_cap_reporting.py:45`

There is no conftest.py anywhere in backend/tests/. Seven of the fifteen test files (test_api_auth, test_cap_reporting, test_grading_api, test_mitosis_api, test_triage_api, test_triage_worker, test_scoring uses no DB but others do) each hand-roll the same `create_engine("sqlite:///:memory:", poolclass=StaticPool)` + `override_get_db` + autouse fixture pattern. Within a file, the engine/session factory is a module-level singleton reused for every test function in that module — Base.metadata.create_all() is idempotent (doesn't truncate), so rows inserted by one test function persist for the rest of the module's test run.

```
engine = create_engine(
    SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URL,
    connect_args={"check_same_thread": False},
    poolclass=StaticPool,
)
TestingSessionLocal = sessionmaker(autocommit=False, autoflush=False, bind=engine)
Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)
```
**Impact:** Test isolation within a file relies entirely on each test using a fresh random uuid.uuid4() as case_id; any test that reuses a fixed id, or a future test that queries across all rows of a table (e.g. `select(Case)` without filtering), will observe leftover rows from earlier tests in the same module and get non-deterministic results depending on test execution order.

**Fix:** Extract the SQLite engine/session/override fixture into a shared backend/tests/conftest.py, and either use a fresh in-memory engine per test function or explicitly clear all tables in a fixture teardown.

*Verifier note:* Facts check out. `find . -name conftest.py` over the repo returns nothing, so there is no shared fixture module. The quoted block is at lines 45-51 (finding cites 41): module-level create_engine(sqlite:///:memory:, StaticPool) + TestingSessionLocal + Base.metadata.create_all, with the autouse fixture at 62-67 only re-running create_all (idempotent, no truncate) and setting/popping app.dependency_overrides[get_db] — there is no drop_all or row cleanup in teardown, so rows do persist for the module's whole run. Duplication confirmed in test_api_auth.py:13-32, test_grading_api.py:18-38, test_mitosis_api.py:20-40 (module-level, identical shape); test_triage_api.py:19-34 builds the same thing inside a fixture and test_triage_worker.py:16 / test_grading.py:148 build ad-hoc engines in-function, so 'seven files hand-roll it' is right in spirit though only four use the module-level singleton form. Severity lowered medium->low: the failure scenario is entirely prospective. This module contains exactly one DB-touching test (test_stage_6_full_workflow), it uses a fresh uuid.uuid4() at line 258, and no test in the file issues an unfiltered select(), so no test is currently non-deterministic or order-dependent. This is duplication/latent-isolation hygiene, not a live defect, and it is a distinct issue from index 197 (coverage gaps), not a duplicate of it.

#### 461. hotspots.py unit tests assert the deviant fixed-square/local-maxima behavior instead of PRD 2.4's component-based spec

**Severity:** low · **Category:** PRD deviation · **Location:** `backend/tests/test_hotspots.py:37`

PRD §5 requires hotspot tests to verify 'expected component count, polygon area within 5%, margin applied' from `scipy.ndimage.label` connected components. `test_extract_hotspots_standardized_candidates` instead asserts the implementation's actual (deviant) local-maxima/fixed-square behavior: exactly `len(hotspots) == 8` (== `max_hotspots`, regardless of how many real blobs exist) and `hotspots[0]["area_mm2"] == 0.36` ('Standard 600 µm x 600 µm HPF candidate' — a fixed constant, not a measured component area).

```
assert len(hotspots) == 8
assert hotspots[0]["id"] == "hs_01"
...
assert hotspots[0]["area_mm2"] == 0.36  # Standard 600 µm x 600 µm HPF candidate
```
**Impact:** The test suite locks in and green-lights the algorithmic deviation rather than catching it — passing tests give false assurance that hotspot extraction matches the PRD.

**Fix:** Rewrite tests against the PRD-specified component-based algorithm once implemented: assert component count matches the number of synthetic blobs above threshold, polygon area is within 5% of the blob's true area, and margin dilation is reflected in the returned polygon.

*Verifier note:* Evidence exists verbatim at test_hotspots.py:37-42 (len==8, id hs_01/hs_02, area_mm2==0.36, polygon len==5). I executed pipeline/hotspots.py against this exact fixture (shapely/skimage stubbed, both absent from the env): the grid contains 2 blobs and only 2 local maxima clear prob_threshold, yet 8 hotspots are returned - 6 are fabricated by the top-up loop at hotspots.py:101-136. Every hotspot has area_mm2 == 0.36 and a 5-point axis-aligned square from box() at hotspots.py:78-85, i.e. a constant, not a measured component area. PRD 03 s2.4 specifies scipy.ndimage.label components, min_area_mm2 drop, find_contours polygons, and margin_um dilation; s5 requires tests for 'expected component count, polygon area within 5%, margin applied'. cfg keys min_area_mm2 and margin_um are never read by the implementation (hotspots.py:27-30) and never asserted by any test. The test therefore green-lights the deviation. Severity low is right: this is a test-quality/false-assurance issue; the algorithmic deviation itself is a separate, higher-severity finding, and double-counting it here would inflate this one.

#### 460. PRD §5's edit-application idempotency property test and probe-eval CI guard are both absent from the test suite

**Severity:** low · **Category:** PRD deviation · **Location:** `backend/tests/test_triage_api.py:43`

PRD §5 lists two additional explicit test requirements for this stage that are not present anywhere in the repo: (1) 'Edit application: property test — apply(diff, machine_output) idempotent, order-stable' for `apply_edit_ops`, and (2) 'Probe eval numbers asserted in CI against the committed artifact metadata (guard against silently swapped weights)'. `test_triage_api.py` only covers a single happy-path exclude+add+confirm sequence, and no test file references `probe_v1.json`'s AUC/metadata at all.

```
def test_triage_api_workflow(client_and_db):
    ... # single sequential exclude+add+confirm run, no idempotency/order-stability assertions, no probe-metadata assertions anywhere in the repo
```
**Impact:** Without an idempotency/order-stability test, a future refactor of `apply_edit_ops` could silently break replay-safety of the edit diff (relevant given the confirmed delete-op bug found above); without a probe-metadata CI guard, a swapped or corrupted probe artifact would go undetected exactly as PRD 5 warns against.

**Fix:** Add a property-based test applying edit ops in varying orders / repeated application and asserting a fixed-point result, and a CI assertion comparing `probe_v1.json`'s recorded AUC/hash against the actual artifact.

*Verifier note:* Both PRD requirements exist verbatim at prd/03-stage-v4.2-hotspot-triage.md:94-95 and both are genuinely absent from the repo. test_triage_api.py contains exactly one test (def test_triage_api_workflow at line 43, not 42 - line 42 is blank): a single sequential exclude+add+confirm asserting edits_count==2 and len(db_hotspots)==2, with no repeated or reordered application and no fixed-point assertion. Repo-wide grep for apply_edit_ops (--include=*.py) returns only the definition at backend/app/routers/triage.py:57 and call sites :130 and :511 - zero test references. grep -rn 'auc|probe' -i over backend/tests/ returns nothing; grep -rln probe_v1 hits only backend/worker/triage.py, configs/triage.yaml, backend/pipeline/probe.py, backend/pipeline/diagnose_system.py and models/probe/probe_v1.json, no test or CI file. There is no .github/ directory at the repo root at all (the only workflow YAMLs are under frontend/node_modules/), so the 'asserted in CI' guard has no host. models/probe/probe_v1.json does carry the assertable metadata (train_auc 0.965, pf_model_version path-foundation-v1, embedding_dim 384) and nothing verifies it. Impact is if anything understated: apply_edit_ops's own docstring (triage.py:56-59) claims 'Idempotent and order-stable' while the add branch at line 72 computes new_id = hid or f"user_{len(hotspots_dict)+1:02d}" from mutable dict size - a preceding delete in the same batch shrinks the dict, so an id-less add can regenerate an existing id (silently overwriting it) or yield a different id on replay. The missing property test therefore masks a live contract violation rather than guarding a hypothetical one. Severity kept low: this is absent coverage plus a missing CI guard, not a runtime defect by itself, and the id-less-add path needs a client that omits 'id' (the existing test always supplies one). Note hypothesis is not in backend requirements, so a minimal parametrized-permutation test is the appropriate fix rather than a new dependency.

*Verifier note:* All four sub-claims verified against the 61-line .gitignore. (1) Weights: configs/mitosis.yaml:5 and :20 point weights_path at models/detector/yolov8_midog.pt and models/verifier/hovernet_mitosis.pt; `git check-ignore -v models/detector/yolov8_midog.pt` returns nothing (not ignored), and no *.pt/*.pth/*.onnx/models rule exists anywhere in the file — .gitignore is the only ignore file in the repo (find turned up no nested ones). (4) *.pdf at line 55 is a blanket rule; no PDF is currently tracked, and the generated CAP reports go to GCS/tmp (backend/app/routers/report.py:160,542; backend/worker/report.py:150), so the rule protects nothing in-tree while silently swallowing any future docs PDF. #### 377. README documents mitotic scoring as fixed per-10-HPF counts and misstates the HPF calibration

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Docs · **Location:** `README.md:96`

README.md:96 and :128 present the score as '<8 / 8-15 / >=16 per 2.157 mm2'. These integers happen to equal ceil(3.65*2.157)=8 and ceil(7.30*2.157)=16, i.e. the per-mm2 thresholds of PRD 00 decision 1 evaluated at exactly 10 fields, but the README never states the per-mm2 basis, the configurable CAP table, the classic 0-9/10-19/>=20 per 2.74 mm2 reference, or that fewer than 10 fields are area-normalised. README.md:93 claims 'FN = 22 mm at 40x' which gives diameter 0.55 mm / area 0.238 mm2, not the 0.2157 mm2 (diameter 0.524 mm) used in code. README.md:8 and :236-244 claim 58/58 tests incl. test_staging.py, test_report.py, test_mitosis.py, test_tiles.py which do not exist (actual files: test_cap_reporting.py, test_mitosis_api.py, test_scoring.py, test_hpf.py, ...).

```
* Instantaneous Nottingham Mitotic Score calculation ($<8 -> 1$, $8--15 -> 2$, $>= 16 -> 3$).
```
**Impact:** Clinicians reading the README will assume a count-based rule and will not understand why a 5-field case with 8 mitoses scores 3.

**Fix:** Rewrite the Stage 4 section around mitoses/mm2 with the configurable table, state FN ~21 mm / 0.524 mm diameter, and list the real test files.

*Verifier note:* Primary claim verified. backend/pipeline/scoring.py:53-95 computes `density = count_total / (n_hpf * pi*(radius_um/1000)^2)` and scores `density >= 7.30 -> 3`, `>= 3.65 -> 2`, else 1, with both thresholds overridable from config (configs/scoring.yaml:7-8, configs/mitosis.yaml:35-36 — the PRD 00 decision 1 'configurable CAP table'). README.md:96 and :128 state fixed integer counts (<8 / 8-15 / >=16 per 2.157 mm2); those integers are only the density rule evaluated at exactly n_hpf=10 (3.65*2.157=7.87 -> 8; 7.30*2.157=15.7 -> 16). The finder's exact failure case is already pinned as a test: backend/tests/test_scoring.py:53 asserts count_total=8 with n_hpf=5 (area 1.078 mm2) yields score 3, which the README's '8-15 -> 2' contradicts. The FN sub-claim also holds: FN 22 mm at 40x gives a 0.55 mm field (r=275 um, 0.2376 mm2), not the r=262.0 um / 0.2157 mm2 hardcoded throughout (scoring.py:53, hpf.py:27, models/hpf_site.py:20); consistent FN for r=262 um is ~21 mm. Severity low is right — the README is not a code path and the code itself is correct and config-driven; the harm is reader misunderstanding only. NOTE: the trailing part of this description (58/58 tests and the four missing test files) is the same defect as index 386 and should be scored only there.

*Also reported at:* `README.md:93` (README's HPF calibration is internally inconsistent: FN = 22 mm at 40x implies a 275 um radius / 0.2376 mm2, not the 262 um / 0.2157 mm2 stated in the same sentence)

#### 547. run_server supervisor restarts every second forever on permanent startup errors (e.g. ImportError in app.main)

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Improvement · **Location:** `backend/run_server.py:27`

uvicorn.run('app.main:app') raises from Config.load() when the app module fails to import (missing scipy/cv2 etc. as already established for requirements.txt). The generic except Exception branch prints the traceback and retries after 1 s with no backoff or attempt cap, so a permanent error produces an infinite tight loop of tracebacks. Port-in-use is a SystemExit and exits, but import/config errors are not.

```
except Exception as e:
    print(f"[Server Supervisor] Server crashed with: {e}. Auto-restarting in 1s...")
    traceback.print_exc()
    time.sleep(1.0)
```
**Impact:** Log flooding and a process that looks alive while never serving; masks the underlying error in container logs.

**Fix:** Delete the supervisor (Cloud Run / compose restart policies already do this) or add exponential backoff with a max-attempt exit.

*Verifier note:* Line number is correct (`except Exception as e:` at 27, print at 28, traceback at 29, time.sleep(1.0) at 30, inside `while True:` at 15). The propagation analysis holds, and I verified it against the installed uvicorn rather than assuming: uvicorn/main.py:618 calls `config.load_app()` OUTSIDE the surrounding try, and load_app (config.py:412-418) catches only ImportFromStringError. importer.py:21-24 does `except ModuleNotFoundError as exc: if exc.name != module_str: raise exc from None` — so only a missing `app.main` itself becomes ImportFromStringError/sys.exit; a missing TRANSITIVE dependency re-raises the raw ModuleNotFoundError, as does any other exception raised at module-import time (e.g. a pydantic-settings failure in app/core/config.py). app.main reaches numpy, PIL, google.cloud.storage, sqlalchemy and the openslide/pyvips paths via app/routers/tiles.py:10-20 and app/routers/__init__.py, so this class of failure is reachable, not hypothetical. Such an exception hits run_server.py:27 and retries every 1 s forever with no backoff and no attempt cap. The finder's carve-out is also correct and worth crediting: port-in-use (config.bind_socket -> sys.exit(1)) and lifespan/startup failure (main.py:627 `if not server.started ... sys.exit(STARTUP_FAILURE)`, which is how a dead DB in main.py's `Base.metadata.create_all` exits) both raise SystemExit and are caught by line 24, breaking the loop cleanly. Severity low is right — consequence is log flooding and a never-serving process that looks alive. Partial overlap with index 30, whose impact line mentions the restart loop in passing, but not a duplicate: different location (line 27 vs 19), different defect, different fix. One nit the finder missed that strengthens the case: uvicorn returns normally (no exception) on a clean shutdown, so the loop also restarts with ZERO delay in that path — the sleep(1.0) is not even a floor on the tightest loop.

#### 34. Default DATABASE_URL embeds a password and compose publishes Postgres on all interfaces

**Severity:** low · **Category:** Security · **Location:** `ops/docker-compose.yml:13`

The dev password appears in config.py:48 as the DATABASE_URL default and in compose; ports '5432:5432' binds 0.0.0.0, exposing the PHI dev DB with a known password to the LAN. Because the SQLite fallback exists, a prod deployment that forgets DATABASE_URL does not fail — it silently uses this default and then SQLite.

```
docker-compose.yml:10  POSTGRES_PASSWORD: oncogemma_dev_password
docker-compose.yml:13  - "5432:5432"
config.py:48  "postgresql://oncogemma:oncogemma_dev_password@localhost:5432/oncogemma_db"
```
**Impact:** Credential in source plus network-exposed dev database.

**Fix:** Bind '127.0.0.1:5432:5432', read POSTGRES_PASSWORD from .env, and make DATABASE_URL required (no default).

*Verifier note:* All quoted evidence is exact: compose:10 POSTGRES_PASSWORD: oncogemma_dev_password, compose:12-13 ports short syntax "5432:5432" (Docker publishes on 0.0.0.0 by default, so LAN-reachable), config.py:46-49 DATABASE_URL default embeds the same credential. The silent-degradation chain is also real: db.py:10-32 takes the non-sqlite branch, tries engine.connect(), and on any exception prints a warning and rebinds to sqlite:///<repo>/oncogemma_local.db, so a deployment that forgets DATABASE_URL gets the dev default, fails to reach that Postgres, and silently runs on a local SQLite file rather than crashing. Severity stays low for the compose half: a well-known dev-only password in a dev-only compose file is conventional, and the practical exposure is a LAN-reachable empty dev DB with no PHI in it yet. Note the genuinely sharper part of this finding is the db.py:27-32 silent fallback, which belongs to db.py, not ops/docker-compose.yml; if filed separately it should carry a higher severity. Not a duplicate of index 17 (that one is about the unwired GCS emulator and missing dev tooling).

#### 515. Weekly pilot-review ritual and its runbook are entirely undocumented

**Severity:** low · **Category:** PRD deviation · **Location:** `prd/07-stage-v4.6-validation.md:62`

PRD section 3 requires the weekly ritual to be documented in `docs/pilot-runbook.md` (read the three override views; Stage-4 toggle rate rising -> detector/threshold problem; Stage-3 edits ~0 for 3 weeks -> make triage confirm opt-in). No `docs/` directory exists in the repo at all.

**Impact:** Without this doc there is no process artifact for the pilot pathologists or team to follow the interpretation heuristics the PRD specifies, even if the underlying views existed.

**Fix:** Author docs/pilot-runbook.md per PRD section 5 alongside the analytics views.

*Verifier note:* Absence verified. `find . -iname 'docs*'` in OncoGemma-v5 returns nothing; repo root is .gitignore, README.md, backend/, configs/, frontend/, models/, ops/ (ops/ contains only docker-compose.yml). No file anywhere matches 'runbook' (grep over *.py/*.ts/*.tsx/*.yml/*.tf/*.sql excluding node_modules returns zero hits), and README.md has no runbook/pilot-review content. The PRD requirement is real and quoted accurately: prd/07-stage-v4.6-validation.md:62 'Weekly pilot review ritual (document in `docs/pilot-runbook.md`): read these three views; Stage-4 toggle rate rising -> detector/threshold problem; Stage-3 edits ~ 0 for 3 weeks -> make triage confirm opt-in', and line 79 lists docs/pilot-runbook.md as a pilot onboarding asset. Severity lowered medium->low: this is a documentation artifact for an entirely unstarted stage, not a defect in shipped code. The three override SQL views the ritual is supposed to read also do not exist (grep 'CREATE VIEW|v_score_overrides' returns nothing), and git log shows the newest commit covers 'v4.0 through v4.5' only — so v4.6 as a whole is unimplemented. The runbook's absence has no runtime impact and is strictly downstream of the missing views. Location `docs/:0` is not a real path; the checkable anchor is the PRD line cited.

#### 528. Backup/restore drill and its documentation are absent

**Severity:** low · **Category:** PRD deviation · **Location:** `prd/07-stage-v4.6-validation.md:73`

PRD section 4 item 5 and the acceptance checklist require Cloud SQL PITR, GCS versioning on artifacts+pyramids, and a documented one-page restore drill actually executed once (DB + one slide's artifacts recovered to a scratch project). No such documentation or infra-as-code exists in the repo.

```

```
**Impact:** Acceptance checklist item 'Restore drill executed once' cannot be checked off, and there is no evidence the pilot's data-loss recovery path has ever been exercised before real patient-adjacent pilot data starts flowing.

**Fix:** Document and execute the restore drill, then commit the one-page runbook to docs/.

*Verifier note:* Not a duplicate of 515 — different PRD item (section 4 item 5 / checklist line 92, backup+restore), though both share the same root absence of docs/. Evidence verified: prd/07-stage-v4.6-validation.md:73 '5. **Backup/restore:** Cloud SQL PITR on; GCS versioning on `artifacts` + `pyramids`; restore drill documented (1 page).' and :92 '[ ] Restore drill executed once (DB + one slide's artifacts recovered to a scratch project).' In the repo: no docs/ directory, `find` for *.tf/*.tfvars/*.tf.json/cloudbuild* returns nothing, ops/ contains only docker-compose.yml, and grep for 'restore drill|backup|PITR|versioning' across the repo (README.md included, node_modules excluded) returns zero hits. So the documented one-page drill genuinely does not exist. One correction to the finder's framing: the PITR-on and GCS-versioning-on halves cannot be judged from this repo at all — it contains no infrastructure-as-code whatsoever, so those are GCP console/gcloud settings that may or may not be enabled; absence from the repo is not evidence they are off. Severity lowered medium->low on the same basis as 515: the confirmed defect is a missing document for a stage (v4.6) that git log shows has not been started, not a demonstrated data-loss exposure. `docs/:0` is not a real path; anchor is the PRD line cited.

Second loop creation costs microseconds. Nothing here threatens the 4-minute budget. |

| 394 | `backend/worker/triage.py:293` | models/probe/probe_v1.joblib auto-regeneration path has no .gitignore coverage for generated artifacts | refuted | The code path is real (triage.py:289-293 -> pipeline/probe.py:52 train_default_probe, which joblib.dump's probe_v1.joblib and writes probe_v1.json into models/probe/), but the described failure cannot occur and the proposed fix would not fix it if it could. (1) models/probe/probe_v1.joblib and probe_v1.json are TRACKED in git (`git ls-files models/` lists both; the blob is 2395 bytes of ordinary git object, and there is no .gitattributes and no git-lfs in this repo), so the 'clean checkout missing the committed joblib / LFS not pulled' premise is false — a shallow clone still checks out the full tree. When the file is present, line 292's os.path.exists guard short-circuits and train_default_probe never runs. (2) Even in the hypothetical where someone deletes the file and a Stage 3 run regenerates it, the result is a MODIFIED tracked file, and .gitignore has no effect on tracked files — so adding `*.joblib` would change nothing about that `git status` line. (3) A regenerated model binary showing up as modified is the desired signal, not pollution: silently ignoring a changed model weight in a clinical pipeline would be worse. There is a defensible (unclaimed) smell here — train_default_probe writing synthetic-data weights into the repo at runtime rather than failing loudly — but that is not the gitignore gap this finding asserts. |

| 666 | `frontend/components/viewer/MitosisViewer.tsx:416` | Keyboard effect depends on hpfs.length instead of hpfs, so hotkey toggles run computeClientScore/syncWithServer with stale HPF data | refuted | The quoted dep array at line 416 is real, and `hpfs` / the two handlers are indeed absent from it. But the stated failure cannot occur, because `activeFieldCandidates` IS in the dep array and its identity changes on every `hpfs` replacement. Chain: `activeHpf` (line 250, useMemo deps [hpfs, activeHpfSeq]) = `hpfs.find(...) // hpfs[0] // null` — any `setHpfs` call passes a freshly built array (`syncWithServer` line 203 `setHpfs(res.hpfs)` from JSON; `computeClientScore` line 145 returns `currentHpfs.map(hpf => ({...hpf, count}))`), so the found element is a new object reference. `activeFieldCandidates` (line 256, useMemo deps [candidates, activeHpf]) therefore recomputes and returns a new `candidates.filter(...)` array. That new reference re-runs the keydown effect, which rebinds `handleKeyDown` closing over the CURRENT render's `handleToggleCandidate` / `handleApproveFieldAndNext`, which close over the current `hpfs`. The effect re-subscribes at commit, before any subsequent keypress, so a hotkey toggle never sees a stale `hpfs`. The 'becomes a real bug once drag-to-move is wired in' impact fails for the same reason: moving an HPF center replaces the hpfs array → new activeHpf identity → new activeFieldCandidates → rebind. The only case where `activeFieldCandidates` keeps identity is `activeHpf === null` (empty hpfs), where there is no HPF data to be stale. Genuinely sloppy deps (an eslint exhaustive-deps violation, and `hpfs.length` is misleading), but not a defect — style at most, not `low` severity bug. Separate real staleness exists in `syncWithServer`'s 300ms window (server response overwrites hpfs with counts computed from the payload sent 300ms ago), but that is not the claimed defect. |

| 702 | `backend/worker/qc.py:111` | A QC clinical rejection is recorded as an execution failure, so retry re-runs the same doomed slide forever | refuted | The PRD prescribes exactly the behaviour the finding calls a deviation. prd/02-stage-v4.1-preprocess-qc.md §3: 'Stage `qc`, ends in `awaiting_review` (warn) or `failed` (hard fail) or `done` (clean pass)'; §3.3: 'fail -> case blocked; UI shows reason + "Request re-scan" (sets case status `needs_rescan`)'. qc.py:110-114 does precisely this (status='failed', reason into error, case.status='needs_rescan'). The proposed fix ('record it as done or rejected') would itself be the deviation. §5.2's `rejected` is the review outcome of a pathologist rejecting an awaiting_review stage — it was never meant for a machine hard-fail verdict, so 'no code path writes rejected' is not evidence about qc.py. The residual observations are real but belong elsewhere and do not support the stated finding: (1) retry_case_stage (app/routers/cases.py:167-214) accepts any status and queues attempt N+1 — user-initiated, not a loop, and by §3.3 re-scan is the intended human remedy; (2) approve_case_stage sets `case_obj.status = "open"` unconditionally at app/routers/cases.py:284 and queues triage even when the latest qc row is 'failed' (it only skips flipping the qc row to confirmed, cases.py:249-254) — that is a genuine QC-gate bypass, but it is a defect in cases.py:284, not in qc.py:111, and it is unrelated to which status string QC writes. Worth filing separately against cases.py. Severity dropped to low as filed; the qc.py behaviour is spec-conformant. |

| 715 | `backend/app/models/stage_execution.py:40` | stage_executions has no index on case_id and its poll index is not the partial index the PRD specifies | refuted | The headline claim and the stated impact are both wrong. Line 39 -- quoted in the finder's own evidence -- is `UniqueConstraint('case_id', 'stage', 'attempt', name='uq_stage_execution_attempt')`. Both backends this app uses (db.py:12-32: Postgres, falling back to SQLite) implement a UNIQUE constraint as a btree/auto index, here on (case_id, stage, attempt) with **case_id as the leading column**. So there IS an index usable for case_id, and every query the finder lists is served by it: cases.py:438 `WHERE case_id = X` uses the leading column; triage.py:101, mitosis.py:90, grading.py:356 and report.py:255 all filter `case_id = X AND stage = '<literal>'`, matching the first two columns exactly. No sequential scan occurs, and the proposed `Index('ix_stage_case','case_id','stage')` would be a strict prefix of the existing unique index -- pure redundancy. The mitosis.py:90 OR (`case_id == case_uid / case_id == str(case_id)`) is indeed not index-friendly, but that is a defect of the redundant OR (the GUID TypeDecorator normalizes both sides to the same bind value anyway), not evidence of a missing index; fixing it by adding an index would not help. Only one sub-claim survives: ix_stage_poll (line 40) is a full index where PRD 00-overview.md:118 specifies `WHERE status = 'queued'`. That is a real one-line deviation but its stated cost -- extra entries for done/confirmed rows on a table growing ~7-15 rows per case -- is negligible at any realistic size and is not what this finding argues. Not worth a finding as written. |

(3) The specific '6 of 24 pleomorphism calls failed' premise is wrong about how schema-retry exhaustion is handled: worker/grading.py:294-300 catches SchemaRetryExhaustedError per patch and returns a substitute `PleoResponse(pleomorphism_score=2, rationale='Moderate variation (fallback)', confidence='low')` (the tubule path does the same at 287-292), so a failed call yields a placeholder element, never a dropped one — the gather results are always len(extracted_patches). A partial-evidence signal for those low-confidence fallbacks may be worth having, but that is a different defect from the length mismatch alleged here, and the reported total_patch_count is never wrong. |
